  the second while `mesh_bodies_removed` is 0. Example, the ladle (3.25 mm, 80 passes, objective mass, three stress rows): 13 bodies at the cut 0.5 and 1 in `final.stl`; twelve of the 13 hold 1 to 12 voxels each.
- `solver`: the solver of the run, copied from `run.json` (added in version 1.6). Old runs have `null` (`post.finish` writes `"solver": null` if `run.json` has no solver).
- `filter`: the dict `derived.filter` of `run.json` (section 22a): filter radius, where it came from, the
  solid rule, the requested `min_member_mm` and the radius that the rule gives, `min_feature_mm`, `min_feature_note`,
  and the facts.
  `null` for a run from before A3a.
- `robust` (added with A3b, section 22b): `{"on": false}` for a default run. In robust mode: the
  thresholds, the nominal and the eroded compliance (`compliance_nominal`, `compliance_eroded`, and for each case),
  `stiffness_cases_eroded`, a `note`, the seconds spent in the robust part and the total run time. A run from before
  A3b has no key.
- In robust mode `compliance_final` and `stiffness_cases` are the **nominal design**, the part that the user prints
  (`final.stl` is the nominal design): `compliance_final` is `robust.compliance_nominal` and `stiffness_cases` is
  `|F|^2 / c` of the nominal compliance of each case. The eroded values are in the `robust` block: the eroded compliance is an upper bound of the nominal compliance, and
  the eroded stiffness is a lower bound of the nominal stiffness. In a default run
  both keys come from the last history line, as before (bit for bit). `compliance_initial` is the first history line
  in every mode, so in robust mode it is the eroded design at pass 0 (there is no nominal solve at pass 0). The history
  curve is the eroded design in robust mode. If a robust run ends before the nominal solve (`robust.complete` false),
  `compliance_final` and `stiffness_cases` come from the last history line and are eroded values; the `note` says so.
- `verdict`: the convergence verdict, the last key that `post.finish` writes (section 24.2); `buckling` is added after it (section 33). The one that the run wrote to `verdict.json`; for a folder with no `verdict.json`, one from the history (`source: "history"`).
- `buckling`: only when the buckling check is on, and always the last key (section 33, added with A6a).

### Mesh binary format (`preview.bin` and `/api/mesh/<it>`)

Little-endian: `uint32 n_vertices`, `uint32 n_triangles`, then
`float32[3 * n_vertices]` (x, y, z in mm, world coordinates), then
`uint32[3 * n_triangles]`. Triangles wind counter-clockwise when seen from
outside (outward normals).

## 6. Code panel step markers (E writes, D reads)

The code panel shows the real optimizer source. E puts one marker comment on
its own line before each step block in `topopt/optimize.py`:

```python
# [step:assemble]
K = assembler.K(E_e)
# [step:solve]
...
# [end]
```

A block goes from its marker to the next marker or `# [end]`. The step names
are the `step` values of `status.json`. The dashboard removes the marker lines
from the shown text and marks the block of the current `step`. D tests this
with a stand-in file `topopt/dashboard/fake_optimize.py` that uses the same markers.

## 7. Dashboard server (D)

`topopt dashboard <run_dir> [--port 8765] [--replay [--speed 1.0]]`. Server:
Python standard library only (`http.server`, threaded). It also serves the
static files in `topopt/dashboard/` (package data: a wheel ships them). Port default 8765. It binds to `127.0.0.1`.

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /` | `topopt/dashboard/index.html` |
| `GET /api/run` | `run.json` |
| `GET /api/status` | `status.json`; for a run in the state `running` with a live time estimate, also the key `time_left` (E1-P2, section 24.5) |
| `GET /api/history` | JSON array of all `history.jsonl` lines |
| `GET /api/labels` | `labels.bin` |
| `GET /api/density/<it>` | `snapshots/it_XXXX.bin` |
| `GET /api/mesh/<it>` | Preview mesh: marching cubes at 0.5 on the padded density of that iteration (server side, `skimage`), mesh format of section 5. Cache it. |
| `GET /api/mesh/latest` | Mesh of the newest snapshot. |
| `GET /api/final` | `result/preview.bin` (404 before it exists) |
| `GET /api/metrics` | `result/metrics.json` (404 before it exists) |
| `GET /api/log` | Last 30 lines of `run.log`, `text/plain`. (Added in version 1.1.) |
| `GET /api/part_file` | `{"file": "result/final.stl", "run_dir": "<absolute run folder>", "run_name": "<folder name>", "exists": bool}`. The result panel shows `<run_name>/result/final.stl` under "Part file", with the full path as a tooltip, when `exists` is true (in replay mode: when the clock has shown the file). (Added in P9-8.) |
| `GET /api/source` | `{"path": "...", "lines": [...], "steps": {"solve": [start, end], ...}}` for `topopt/optimize.py`. Line numbers are 1-based, marker lines removed. |

Replay (`topopt/replay.py`): the same endpoints, but the server shows only
the data with `elapsed_s` less than or equal to the replay clock. Before the
clock starts, `/api/run` and `/api/status` return 404 (the waiting screen).
Enter in the server terminal, or `GET /api/replay/start`, starts or restarts
the clock. A restart gives `run.json` a new `started_at`. In replay mode
`/api/status` has `"mode": "replay"` and the page shows a small REPLAY label
(`--no-badge` leaves the field out). (Version 1.4.)

All JavaScript libraries are copied into the package: `topopt/dashboard/vendor/` for the
dashboard, `topopt/refine/vendor/` for the refine page (the refine step puts them into
`result/refine.html`). The dashboard and the refine page must work with no internet
(`tests/test_pages_offline.py`).

**Talk screen (P9-8).** The code panel (`#codepanel`: the source of `topopt/optimize.py`, with the active step marked) and the result row
"Pull-off stiffness per gram" (`#m-perg`) are the screen that the first demo used. They show only when the run has a load case named
`pull_off` (`run.json` `load_cases[].name`; the recorded hook run has one), or when the page address has `?demo=1`
(`topopt/dashboard/js/talk.js`, `talkScreen(search, run)`). The server does not know the rule and has no setting for it. Otherwise the side
panel shows the log (the tail of `run.log`, 30 lines, header "run.log"), and on the done screen the result rows with a short log strip
under them. `/api/source` is then not asked for. The replay of the recorded hook run keeps the demo screen.

The dashboard does not put a fake terminal on screen. It can show a small `run.log` tail.

## 8. CLI (E)

```
topopt run <file.yaml> --out <dir> [--dashboard] [--port 8765] [--quiet] [--solver VALUE] [--override-lock]
                    [--resume [--allow-changed-inputs]] [--stop-rules | --no-stop-rules]   # section 24.2
                    [--continue-from <parent_dir> --more-iterations N [--allow-changed-inputs]]   # section 24.3
                    [--fine-from <parent_dir> [--fine-voxel H] [--fine-passes N] [--fine-tol T] [--allow-changed-inputs] | --fine-pass [--fine-voxel H] [--fine-passes N] [--fine-tol T]]   # section 24.6
topopt stop <run_dir>               # ask the run in the folder to stop at the end of its pass (section 24.2, "Stop on request")
topopt dashboard <run_dir> [--port 8765] [--replay] [--speed 1.0]
topopt check <file.yaml> [--json] [--solver VALUE] [--fine-from <parent_dir> [--fine-voxel H] [--fine-passes N] [--fine-tol T] [--allow-changed-inputs]]   # load + voxelize + guards + summary, no optimizer run (with `auto` the short self-test of gpu-mg runs in a child process, at most 60 s: seconds the first time on a device and driver, then the cached pass); the plan of a fine pass (section 24.6)
topopt doctor [file.yaml] [--json] [--timeout-s S]   # read-only facts about this install, offers, next commands (8.1)
topopt levers [key or word ...]       # the lever cards of every YAML key and engine tool; with words, the matching cards (section 41)
topopt levers --run <run_dir>       # the facts of that run that the engine flags, each with the cards that name them, cheapest layer first (section 41.10)
topopt report <run_dir>             # write result/report.md, the one-page part card, again with the facts the folder has now (section 9.2)
topopt gpu-check [--out DIR] [--device D] [--skip-tests] [--skip-bench] [--step-timeout-s S]   # gpu-mg on this machine (section 20)
topopt step <run_dir> [--part-only] [--out FILE] [--tolerance-mm X] [--no-merge-planes] [--schema AP214|AP242] [--estimate-only] [--json]   # faceted STEP file of a finished run (section 42; extra `step`)
topopt --version                    # topopt.__version__ (from the package metadata)
```

- `--dashboard` starts the dashboard server in the same process (a thread) and opens the browser.
  After the run, the `job.DONE` marker is written. Then the process stays alive and serves the result until Ctrl+C or `kill <pid>`.
  `--no-wait` ends the process at the marker instead. The process prints one line with the URL, the pid and how to stop it.
  This is by design: the dashboard shows the final screen and the refine page.
  - The optimizer process holds its Python heap, the compiled numba code and the libraries of the run. That is 587 MB for
    `examples/hook/hook_short.yaml`, and 1.7 MB of it are arrays (measured with `/proc/<pid>/smaps`). The server needs none of it.
  - So, when `topopt` runs as a command (`main` got no argument list), the process replaces its program at the wait (`os.execve`, POSIX only).
    The new program is `python -P -m topopt dashboard <run folder> --listen-fd <fd> --no-open`.
    It keeps the pid, the process group and the terminal.
    `-P` keeps the current folder off the path, so a `topopt.py` there cannot run instead of the package.
    PYTHONPATH names the folder of the running package first, and an older PYTHONPATH stays after it.
    So the new program is the same package (P4 review, L1).
    It uses 25 MB at rest and 43 MB after the pages and the meshes were served (measured).
    The pages are the same. Ctrl+C ends it with the exit code 0.
  - The listening socket stays open across the exec (`--listen-fd` is a hidden option).
    The port is never closed. A request that comes during the exec waits in the backlog, and the new program answers it.
    A request that is in progress at the exec can be reset. The page then asks again.
    The page clears its view only when `/api/run` answers HTTP 404, not on a network error (P4 review, M1).
  - Before the exec, the Python streams and the C stdio buffers are flushed.
    Every open file descriptor above 2, except the socket, is marked close-on-exec.
    (`import numba` opens a handle on the Python program with no such mark. The new program kept it.)
    Only the standard streams and the socket pass to the new program (P4 review, L8).
    This is POSIX only.
    The new program checks that the fd is a listening socket. macOS does not answer `SO_ACCEPTCONN` (`ENOPROTOOPT`), so there the
    check is: a stream socket that is bound is taken, and `listen()` is called on it again. An fd that is not a socket, a socket
    that is not bound and a datagram socket give the same errors as on Linux. A socket for which `listen()` fails (`OSError`) gives
    the "does not listen" error too. The end-to-end exec tests need /proc and do not run on macOS.
  - The old program stops accepting before the exec.
    If the exec call fails (`OSError`, `ValueError` or `TypeError`), the server stays in the optimizer process and serves again, as before.
    The model, the solver tables and the stress cache are dropped first.
    The same holds when a program calls `main` with an argument list (a test, a notebook).
    If the new program fails after the exec (for example an import error), the process ends and the port closes.
    That case has no fallback.
  - The MCP server's `run_topopt` stops the old process group of a finished run in all these cases, as before.
- `--solver VALUE` (`run` and `check`, since G1d) replaces `settings.solver` for that command. Values: `auto`,
  `cholesky`, `pardiso`, `amg`, `gpu-mg` (section 20).
- Exit code 0 on success, 1 on a user error (bad YAML, guard, a solver that
  this platform cannot run, a piece of active voxels with no support: section 3), 2 on an internal error. User errors print one clear
  line, no traceback.
- Exit code 5 (`topopt run` only, since P4b-4): a request to stop ended the run (`topopt stop`, MCP `stop_run`; section 24.2). It is not
  an error and not a success: the run did not finish, its checkpoint is kept, and `--resume` continues it. The job marker is
  `job.STOPPED` (section 24.1), the status `stopped`. With `--dashboard` the process still serves the dashboard after the stop (like
  after a finished run) unless `--no-wait` is given.
- `topopt stop <run_dir>` writes `<run_dir>/job.stop` and returns at once: no signal, no wait. It prints the message of the reply of
  section 24.2 (the pid, the pass, what happens next), one `option:` line for each option, and the note (`runjob.STOP_NOTE`) that a topopt build
  from before this change ignores the request. Exit code 0: a request is in the folder (written now, or there already).
  Exit code 1: nothing was written. The run is in its post step, it has ended, it is gone, the folder holds no run, or the live job lock in
  the folder belongs to a job that is not a topopt run. Exit code 1 is also given when the argument is not a folder.
- `check` prints a `solver:` line with the solver that the run will use. On Linux
  x86_64 without `pypardiso`, with `settings.solver: auto`, it also prints a text line
  `recommendation: <reason> Command (<action>, extra '<extra>'): <install_command> (about <speedup_factor> times faster for this problem). <license_note>`.
  The data has the fields `action`, `extra`, `install_command`,
  `reason`, `speedup_factor` (the ratio of the two estimates, depends on the
  problem), `estimate_s` (`without_pardiso`, `with_pardiso`) and `license_note`; `--json` and the MCP tools (`check_problem`, `environment`) give them as keys.
  `action` is `install_pypardiso` if pypardiso is not installed. It is
  `fix_pypardiso_load` if pypardiso is installed but does not load (for example,
  the MKL library is not found). In that case the field `error` has the text of
  the exception. `--json` prints one JSON object instead of the text lines. Its
  fields are `name`, `grid_shape`, `voxel_size_mm`, `active_voxels`, `free_dofs`,
  `iterations`, `solver` (`setting`, `resolved`, `platform`, `error`),
  `time_estimate` (`solver`, `s_per_iteration`, `total_s`, `limit_s`,
  `amg_total_s`; `limit_s` is the time budget of the user, `settings.stop_rules.time_budget_s`, or `null` when the YAML sets none: the
  engine has no budget of its own since P9-8; the budget is a stop rule, see section 11), `recommendation` (`null` if there is no offer), `hint` (a line
  for an x86_64 Python on a Mac, else `null`), `warnings`, `assumptions`, `derived`
  (the same as in `run.json`), `lost_force` and `mirror` (the facts of section 26.1, or `null`). The JSON also has the other facts of `check_data`
  (the fields of MCP `check_problem`: `grid`, `voxel_counts`, `backends` with a `pardiso` entry,
  `memory_estimate` and more). For each backend, `time_estimate` is the model value (the AMG time
  per iteration is `AMG_TIME_FACTOR` times larger).
  (Added in version 1.6.)
- `check` prints one line when the buckling check and the buckling row are both off (the default): `buckling: off (check and row). A part with
  members in compression can buckle: buckling.check true gives the load factors (memory estimate about N GB; the time budget of each eigen
  solve is S s; the tool has no estimate of the time).` It adds a sentence when the check would skip now (for example with the solver `amg`:
  it needs a direct solver). The facts are in the key `buckling_off` of `--json` (section 33). With `check: true` or `min_factor` set the line
  does not appear. With interfaces, `check` also prints the facts of what each cut takes from the frozen regions (section 23).
- If the solver cannot run, `check` prints the grid, the dofs and the time
  estimate first (`solver: none`). Then it reports the solver error (with the
  other solvers) and exits with 1. With `--json`, the JSON has `solver.resolved`
  `null` and the text in `solver.error`.
- With `--json`, `solver` has these keys: `setting` (the value of `settings.solver`, or of `--solver`), `resolved` (the solver that a run uses first:
  with `auto` it can be `gpu-mg`), `cpu_solver` (the CPU rule for `setting`: with `auto` the matrix solver of the platform, which is the solver of the
  fallback when `resolved` is `gpu-mg`; with another value the solver itself; `null` when the solver cannot start), `platform`, `error` and, when the
  solver can start, `choice` (the facts of the pick: `solver`, `cpu_solver`, `fallback`, `device`, `case`, `self_test`, `reason`, `line`; section 20).
  Use `cpu_solver` to compare a machine with an expected CPU solver: `resolved` depends on the GPU that the machine shows.
- `run` with `auto` that ends in `amg` on Linux x86_64 prints one `warning:` line
  with the same hint, and goes on.
- On Linux, `main()` sets `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS` to `min(4, usable CPUs)`
  (`len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))`) before numpy loads. It does nothing if the
  user set any of `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, `GOTO_NUM_THREADS` or
  `OMP_NUM_THREADS`. `python -m topopt` (the MCP server uses
  it) and the `topopt` script both call `main()`. macOS: no change.
- `run` calls post-process (F) at the end: `topopt.post.finish(run_dir)`.
- Live flow (added in 1.3): the person who shows the dashboard starts
  `topopt dashboard runs/live` before the demo. Then a run goes into the same folder. So:
  - `run --out <dir>` on a folder with an old run deletes only the files of
    section 5 (run.json, labels.bin, status.json, history.jsonl, run.log,
    snapshots/, result/) and the folder verify/ (section 16, added with B2)
    and then starts. Other files stay. If a live process
    holds the job lock of the folder, the command stops first and deletes
    nothing (exit 1; `--override-lock` runs anyway; section 24.1). A run that an input check refuses (a voxel guard, a region
    error) deletes nothing either: section 24.1, "A refused run keeps the earlier run". The same holds for a run that the optimizer
    stops before it saved its first pass: the files move into the hidden folder `.earlier-run/` and go back (F4-47). The run deletes
    that folder when its first pass is saved.
  - A run without `--resume` in a folder that holds the checkpoint of a run that did not finish deletes it with the other files. The run log says so
    in a `warning:` line at the start, and the MCP reply of `run_topopt` has `earlier_checkpoint` (section 24.2). The run goes on.
  - `run --out <dir> --resume` deletes nothing: it continues the run from `checkpoint.npz` (section 24.2).
  - `run --out <new_dir> --continue-from <parent_dir> --more-iterations N` starts a NEW run in `--out` from the last checkpoint of another run folder.
    The parent is only read (section 24.3). `--out` as the parent or inside it is an error and writes nothing.
  - `run --out <new_dir> --fine-from <parent_dir>` starts a NEW run in `--out` on a finer voxel from the design of a finished run folder (a fine pass, section 24.6).
    `run --out <dir> --fine-pass` makes the run in `<dir>`, then the fine pass in `<dir>-fine`. The parent is only read. A fine pass starts only with one of these two options.
  - `--dashboard` when the port is already in use: use the next free port (`Dashboard port N is busy. Port M is used.`), print the URL and go on.
    If no port of the range is free, print "No dashboard" and go on. Do not fail. A dashboard that is already open on the same run
    folder follows the new run (below), so its page shows the run too. The MCP tool `run_topopt` picks the free port first and gives it in `dashboard_url`.
  - `topopt dashboard <run_dir> --port N` when port N is busy: `error: dashboard port N is busy ...` that names `--port`, exit code 1 (a user error), no traceback.
  - The dashboard detects a new run (`started_at` in `run.json` changes) and
    resets its view with no page reload.

### 8.1 `topopt doctor` and `topopt gpu-check` (added with L1b)

**`topopt doctor [file.yaml] [--json] [--timeout-s S]`** (`topopt/doctor.py`). It changes nothing: it installs, builds,
fetches and deletes nothing, and the git commands it runs only read (`rev-parse`, `log`, `symbolic-ref`, `status`,
`rev-list`, `worktree list`; `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, so `git status` does not write the index). On macOS, when `git` is
`/usr/bin/git`, it runs `xcode-select -p` first: without the Command Line Tools that `git` is a stub that opens an install dialog, so
no git command runs and a note gives the install command. `import topopt.cli` and `import topopt.doctor`
load only PyYAML and the standard library, so the command starts in an environment with a broken numpy or scipy; every part
that can fail is a line in the report, not a crash. The text report has short sections, facts first: Checkout, Machine,
Packages, Environments, Problems (only if there are any), Offers, Next commands. `--json` prints one object with the keys:

- `topopt_version`, `time_utc`, `ok` (true when `problems` is empty), `problems` (a list of lines), `next_commands` (a list
  of `why` and `command`; a command has no trailing comment, because zsh does not read `#` in an interactive shell).
- `checkout`: the same object as `environment_data()["checkout"]` (section 10), made by `doctor.checkout_facts()`. `ahead` and
  `behind` count against `origin/<default branch>` AS OF THE LAST FETCH; the text report shows the age of the newest
  `FETCH_HEAD` file next to them (git writes one in the git folder of each worktree where `git fetch` ran). Doctor never fetches: the fetch command is in the next commands.
- `environment`: `environment_data(file.yaml)` (section 10), or `null` with the text in `environment_error` when it raised.
- `imports`: one row for each package, each tested in its own child Python (the way of `tools/platform_probe.py`; up to four at
  a time): `name`, `import` (the statement), `package`, `use` (`core`, or `extra <name>`), `version` (from the package metadata,
  else `null`), `status`, `detail`, `seconds`. `status` is `ok`; `not installed` (the module is missing and the metadata has no
  such package); `cut` (the module is missing but the metadata lists the package: an install that was cut); `failed` (the import
  raised another error, for example a library that does not load); `crashed` (a signal); `timeout` (`--timeout-s`, default 90).
  The module that is missing can be the package of the row and not a name in its statement: the row `MCP server`
  (`topopt_mcp.server`) is `not installed` when `mcp` is, so a venv without the `mcp` extra is a valid install (exit code 0). A
  `not installed` row of an extra has `install_command` (`uv pip install --python <python> -e '<checkout>[<extra>]'`, for a
  checkout; the `pardiso` extra only on Linux x86_64) and the text report prints it under Packages. The rows are the
  dependencies of `pyproject.toml` (`core`), `mcp`, `MCP server` (no version of its own) with `topopt_mcp.server`, `pyopencl`,
  `pypardiso`, `gmsh`, `cholespy` and `scikit-fem`.
- `known`: `environments` (this Python, the `.venv` of a source checkout, the environment of `scripts/topopt-env.sh`: its folder
  is `$TOPOPT_ENV_DIR`, else `$EVAL_TOPOPT_ENV_DIR`, else `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, else `<repo>/.plugin-env`, as in the script; and the folders found under
  `~/.claude/plugins/data`). Each has `role`, `name`, `dir`, `python`, `exists`, `is_this`, `runs` (a child Python started it),
  `python_version`, `topopt_from` (the folder its `topopt` is imported from), `error`, `used_by`. `clients`: for each of
  `.mcp.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json` and `.codex/config.toml` that exists, which environment its
  `topopt` server starts: `.venv`, `launcher` (it names `scripts/topopt-env.sh`), `other`, `unreadable` or `no topopt server`.
  Only the command and its arguments are read, never the `env` or the headers of a config.
- `offers`: `environment["recommendations"]`, the same list as in section 10, with their commands.

**Progress of `doctor`.** The command takes a few seconds on a machine with no GPU device (measured: about 2.5 to 3.5 s on Linux x86_64). The
limits are: the self-test of gpu-mg, up to `PROBE_TIMEOUT_S` = 60 s on a GPU, until a self-test has passed once on the device and
driver; 19 import checks, up to `--timeout-s` each (4 at a time). So it writes progress lines to **stderr**, flushed at each line,
and nothing new to stdout: one line before the machine facts, one line when the import checks start, and one line when each import
check ends (`[k/N] name: status (seconds s)`, in the order of the ends; a row of an optional package names its extra:
`[15/19] pypardiso (extra pardiso): not installed (0.1 s)`; the rows of `imports` keep the order of the list). `--json`
has the same lines on stderr; its stdout is still one JSON object. A stderr that is closed, or a pipe with no reader, changes
neither stdout nor the exit code: the printer stops at the first failed write and never writes to stdout. `doctor.collect(progress=None)` and
`doctor.import_checks(progress=None)` take a callable for one line of text; with `None` (the default, for `environment_data`, the MCP
server and tests) nothing is printed. Only `doctor.run()` (the command) passes a printer. Tests: `test_import_checks_call_progress_*`,
`test_run_writes_progress_to_stderr_*`.

**Exit code of `doctor`.** 0 when `problems` is empty; 1 when it has a line. A problem is: `environment_data()` raised; a `core`
package whose status is not `ok`; an optional package that is installed (the metadata lists it) and does not import. A package that
is not installed and is optional, a checkout that is behind origin, uncommitted changes and an offer are facts, not problems. An
internal error is exit code 2, as for every command. `scripts/topopt-env.sh doctor` calls `python -m topopt doctor` and prints it;
a version of topopt without the command answers with a usage error ("invalid choice"), which the script reports as "older code".

**Next commands.** For a core package that does not import, in the `.venv` of a checkout: `uv pip install [--reinstall] --python
<python> -e '<checkout>[dev,mcp]'` (`--reinstall` for `cut`, `failed` and `crashed`, because uv skips a package whose `.dist-info`
folder is there); in the launcher environment: `touch <env dir>/venv/.topopt-step2 && sh <script> sync` (the same command as
`scripts/topopt-env.sh doctor`: the marker file makes `sync` install the packages again. This needs the network, also with a warm
uv cache, because `uv --reinstall` also refreshes; with `UV_OFFLINE=1` in front, uv works offline when its cache has every wheel;
`TOPOPT_ENV_DIR=<dir> sh <script> sync` when the folder is not the default). When the checkout is behind origin: the
update command (`git pull` fetches first, so there is no separate fetch), then the refresh of the packages. For a git checkout that is
level with origin as of the last fetch: the fetch command. Then the `command` of each offer.

**`topopt gpu-check [--out DIR] [--device D] [--skip-tests] [--skip-bench] [--step-timeout-s S]`** (`topopt/gpu_check.py`; the
gpu-mg steps are in section 20). Four steps; the report folder (default `runs/gpu-check`) gets `gpu-check.md`, `gpu-check.json`,
one log for each child step (`parity.log`, `tests.log`, `bench.log`) and `bench/` (the files of `tools/bench_gpu_mg.py`). The
markdown is printed at the end: it is one block to paste in a chat.

1. facts: `environment_data()`. It is "not run" (with the reason and the commands) when `tools/gpu_mg_parity.py` or
   `tools/bench_gpu_mg.py` is not in the code folder (a wheel install: the text gives the `git clone` and the install line); when
   pyopencl is not usable (the command is the `install_command` of the `opencl` facts); when pyopencl loads and no OpenCL device is visible; when no device that is not a CPU is visible and `--device`
   is not given (the text says so and names `--device N` for a smoke test on a CPU device); or when `--device` fits no device.
   `--device` takes a number or a part of a name, as `settings.gpu_device` does, and any device, a CPU device too.
2. parity: a child `python tools/gpu_mg_parity.py --device N` (the tested device). Passed when it exits with 0.
3. tests: a child `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` on `tests/test_gpu_mg.py`, `tests/test_gpu_mg_device.py`,
   `tests/test_gpu_mg_x_merge.py` and `tests/test_bench_gpu_mg.py`, with `TOPOPT_TEST_REAL_GPU=1` (only this child gets it). The
   tests take the device that `auto` takes, so the step is "skipped" with the reason when `--device` names another device. It is
   "not run" when pytest or the test files are missing (the command is `uv pip install --python <python> -e '<code folder>[dev]'`).
4. bench: a child `python tools/bench_gpu_mg.py --out <out>/bench --sizes 1.2,1.0 --iterations 20 --device N`. Its markdown table is
   in the report; the summary line gives the median seconds per iteration and the speed-up of each size. When the bench passes, the
   step also saves the constants of the device for the time model of `topopt check` (the paragraph "Calibration" below).

A step that runs and fails has the state `failed`, stops the flow (the later steps depend on it, so they are "not run"), and the
report lists the command to run next. A step that cannot run because a tool is missing is "not run" with the command that fixes it;
it does not stop the flow (a missing pytest does not stop the bench). A step skipped by an option (`--skip-tests`, `--skip-bench`)
or by its rule is "skipped". `--step-timeout-s` stops a step that runs longer than S seconds (default: no limit). Exit code: 0 when
no step is `failed` or "not run" (a skipped step does not count); 1 otherwise. The report has the result line (`PASS`,
`PASS (skipped: ...)`, `FAIL at step ...` or `NOT RUN: ...`), a table of the steps, the output of each step and the commands to run
next. It holds folder names and no secret. For a CPU device
the facts step prints that the times are not GPU times. Each child runs in its own process group: `--step-timeout-s` and Ctrl-C stop the child and
every process it started (the bench starts `topopt run`), and Ctrl-C still writes the report ("stopped by the user"). The bench step
deletes the `bench_gpu_mg.json` and `.md` of an earlier run in the same report folder before it starts, so the report never shows the
table of an old run. The commands of the report start with `cd <code folder> &&` when they use relative paths.

**Calibration (P2a).** The bench step turns the `bench_gpu_mg.json` of the bench run into the constants of the tested device and saves them in the
per-user state folder: `$TOPOPT_STATE_DIR` when the variable is set, else `~/.topopt` (`gpu_mg.check.state_dir()`). The file is
`<state folder>/gpu-constants.json`. It is NOT the report file `gpu-check.json` of the report folder (another name, so that the two cannot be mixed). It is `{"schema": 1, "calibrations":
[...]}`, with one record for each device and precision case: a new record for the same device and case replaces the old one (a smoke
test on a CPU device or a second GPU does not remove another record). A record has `time_utc`, `topopt_version`, `device`
(`platform`, `name`, `vendor`, `kind`, `fp64`), `case`, `columns_per_launch`, `c_s_per_dof_iteration`, `host_s_per_dof`, `points` (one for
each size of the bench: `voxel_mm`, `free_dofs`, `n_load_cases`, `c_s`, `host_s_per_dof`) and `source`. `c` is, for each gpu-mg run of
the bench, the median over the optimizer iterations of `solve_s / (device iterations * free dofs)`, the seconds of the device for one PCG
iteration of one block of load cases and one free dof; `host_s_per_dof` is `(median seconds of an optimizer iteration - median solve_s) /
free dofs`. The sizes are combined with their free dofs as weights. The columns for each launch (`columns_per_launch`) are 2 when the
problem has more than one load case (the hook has two), else 1; the bench report has `n_load_cases` for each run (a bench file of an earlier
version has not, and then there is no calibration and the report says so). The report JSON of `gpu-check` has `calibration` (the record, or
`null`) and `calibration_file` (the path, or `null`). A folder that cannot be written is not an error: the text says "Not saved" and
`check` does not use the constants. `topopt check` reads the file for the device that it would use (section 20, "Time model"). A file
that cannot be read, is not JSON (or not UTF-8 text), has another `schema` or has no list `calibrations` is ignored as a whole. A record with a bad field is
dropped and the other records are used. A good record has: `device` (an object with the texts `platform` and `name`), `case` (a text),
`columns_per_launch` (1 or 2), `c_s_per_dof_iteration` (a finite number above 0) and `host_s_per_dof` (a finite number, 0 or more)
(`gpu_mg.check.record_problem`). In both cases the text of `check` (the `Note:` after the constants, `time_estimate.note`) names the file and, for a
record, its number and the field. A bad file never stops `check`, `check_problem`, `build_regions` or `topopt run`: `constants_for` has a second
guard that falls back to the table row or the reference row, with the problem in the note. The next `gpu-check` writes the file again without the bad records.
The file is written like `checkpoint.npz` (section 24.2): a temporary file with a name of its own in the same folder, flushed to the drive, then renamed, then the folder is flushed. There is no lock (as for
the checkpoint), so two `gpu-check` runs at the same time can lose the record of the one that wrote first.

## 9. Post-process (F)

`topopt.post.finish(run_dir: Path) -> dict`. It reads the last snapshot and
`labels.bin`, makes a smooth watertight mesh (marching cubes on the padded
density field, island removal, Taubin smoothing), writes `result/final.stl`,
`result/preview.bin`, `result/metrics.json`, and returns the metrics dict.
With `blur`, fixed and load voxels are always solid in the mesh (the voxel labels give their shape). Time budget: 15 s or less.
The mesh step has two methods: `sdf` (default) and `blur` (the method that this section describes).
Section 19 describes `sdf`. With `sdf` the fixed, load and keep-out regions have their STL shape, so the mass of the final
mesh changes by a few percent against `blur`, with either sign (hook -4.9 % at 1.2 mm voxels (`examples/hook/hook.yaml`) and -8.8 % at 2 mm voxels
(`examples/hook/hook_short.yaml`), ladle +2.1 %; the size depends on the voxel size).
`stiffness_cases[i].N_per_mm` is `null` with a `reason` for a case that has a moment, a remote force or a
pressure (section 5, `metrics.json`; section 26.2). A per-axis support changes nothing here.
With `interfaces` (section 23) the post step also makes the exact union and cut of the interface shapes after the smoothing,
in both methods. `final.stl` is then the as-printed mesh, and `nominal.stl` (only with stock) is the finished mesh.
The post step writes no STEP file. `topopt step <run_dir>` (section 42, extra `step`) wraps `result/final.stl` (or `part_only.stl`) as a faceted STEP solid in
`result/final.step` (`part_only.step`) with the report `result/final.step.json` (`part_only.step.json`); it reads the finished run and changes none of its files.

### 9.1 Bodies that are not printed: `regions.not_printed` and `result/part_only.stl` (added with P4b-2)

A problem can hold bodies that the optimizer needs but that are not in the print: the plate that the part is bolted to, the axle that
a hub sits on, a load block. They are `fixed`, `load`, `solid` or `keep_out` regions, so `final.stl` holds them (a keep-out region
as a void). The key `regions.not_printed` (section 2) lists them. When it is set, the post step writes `result/part_only.stl`
next to `final.stl`. Without the key nothing changes: the files, `metrics.json` and `run.json` are the same bytes as before this
section, except for the time fields (a test compares them with the base).

**The file.** `part_only.stl` is the mesh of `final.stl` with the listed bodies cut out by an exact boolean (manifold3d). It is cut
from the mesh that `final.stl` holds (with machining stock, section 23, that is the as-printed mesh; there is no `nominal`
variant of `part_only.stl`). `final.stl`, `preview.bin` and `nominal.stl` do not change. The cut uses the primitives of the exact
interface step (section 23): the STL of each listed body is loaded as a manifold (`smooth_sdf._load_manifold`), the union of the
bodies is subtracted, and the result gets the same float32 rounding and clean-up as `final.stl` (`interfaces.CLEAN_TOL_MM`). No new
number is introduced. The contact face of the part with a removed body is the surface of that body, not a voxel step. With the `sdf`
mesh method (section 19) a fixed, load or solid STL is already united exactly with the smooth mesh, so the cut leaves exact planes
and cylinders there. Measured on a plate whose face is at x = 0.37 mm with voxels of 1 mm: every vertex of the contact face has
x equal to float32(0.37).

**Loose pieces.** The volume step of the `sdf` method (section 19, step 7) shifts the whole surface by one level. So the mesh
stands a little off the exact surface of a frozen body: it leaves a thin skin around the body. The cut leaves the skin of a removed
body as thin loose pieces, and a piece that touches the part along one edge makes the STL file non-manifold after the float32
reload. (Measured on the hook, voxel 2 mm: 5 loose pieces of 0.0002 to 0.043 mm3, 0.1 to 9 micrometres thick, before the drop.) So the step splits the cut into connected pieces and drops each piece that holds no material of the density field. A
piece "holds material" when it contains the centre of at least one voxel with label design, fixed or load whose density is above 0.5
(the threshold of the sharp field of the mesh step). A piece that only a removed body held together (two members joined by the
plate) holds material, so it stays: it is part of the print, and `bodies` counts it. The rule of the interface step that drops a
body which no frozen shape touches is NOT used here. The wall of a cavity (a closed void of the design that the mesh step keeps, section
19, step 6) is not a piece: it goes with the innermost piece around it, so a kept piece keeps its cavity, and a dropped piece counts
its material. `leftovers_dropped` says how many pieces and how much volume were dropped. A skin
that is joined to the part by a face stays: it is a thin film on the contact face. The step measures it (`contact`, below) and
cuts it off if the user sets `settings.part_only_min_film_mm` (the next part of this section).
`shortest_edge_mm` is the fact about slivers. `topopt verify` reads `part_only.stl` only with `--part-only` (below, and section 16).

**The thin film at the contact faces (added with P4b-6).** The skin that stays is a wall behind the contact face of a removed body. A
stress check of the file (`topopt verify`) lets such a wall carry the load as a membrane, and a mesher gets slivers from it. *The areas and
walls in this part of the section were measured on the mesh without the snap to the region faces (section 19, step 6): that film comes in
part from the smooth surface of the `sdf` mesher, which lies a little off the exact region face. With the snap, the contact area of the
plate of the bar with a wall under the voxel size is 27.9 mm2, against 100 mm2 and more without it, and the thinnest wall is 0.017 mm
against 0.0005 mm (measured at `c080f62`, one Linux x86_64 host; `tests/test_part_only_film.py` runs the old mesh on purpose, and has one test of the effect). The numbers of the hook
were not measured again; the rule below is for the film that stays.* Measured on
the bar of `tests/test_part_only.py` (voxel 1 mm), the contact area of the plate is 122.3 mm2; the plate face itself is 95.3 mm2, and the
rest is film around the plate. A wall under 0.05 mm covers 22.3 mm2 of it (centre of each triangle), a wall under 0.2 mm covers 77.4 mm2.
Measured on the hook (`examples/hook/hook_short.yaml` with `not_printed`, voxel 2 mm): the contact area of the removed tip is 485.5 mm2,
and a wall under 0.05 mm covers 31.0 mm2 of it, a wall under 0.25 mm covers 182.3 mm2; at the plate 0.2 and 5.4 mm2 of 275.7 mm2.
- *Contact triangle.* A triangle of the result that comes from the mesh of a removed body. The step gives each input of the boolean its own
  original id (`Manifold.reserve_ids`, `Mesh.run_original_id`), and manifold3d keeps the id of the source on every output triangle. The
  test is exact. There is no distance test. The ids change nothing in the arrays of the boolean (a test compares them with the base). A face
  that two removed bodies share (two bodies with the same mesh) belongs to one of them: the union keeps one source, the first in the list.
  The other body has area 0, 0 triangles and `thinnest_wall_mm` `null`.
- *Wall.* A ray from the centre of the contact triangle, against its outward normal (into the part). The first hit with a triangle other
  than the start triangle is the wall. The start triangle is excluded by its index, not by an offset. The next hit, if there is one,
  ends the air gap behind the wall (`gap`). A triangle with no hit has no wall (`unmeasured_triangles` counts them; none in the measured
  runs). The ray needs `rtree` through `trimesh`; there is no embree. The ray search of `trimesh` has its own tolerances (a barycentric
  test, a forward distance, and a merge of hits at the same location, about 1e-8 mm); the step adds none. A wall below the merge step can
  merge with the start hit and be lost; the tests measure a film of 1e-5 mm.
- *Facts, always* (also with the setting off), in `contact`: for each removed body the contact area, the number of contact triangles,
  `thinnest_wall_mm`, the smallest wall (`null` for a body with no contact face), and `area_below_voxel_mm2`, the contact area with a wall
  below the voxel size of the run (the existing scale of the run; the note uses it too). A fact has no limit.
- *Choosing the value.* The step recommends none. The value is the wall thickness that the user wants to cut off, a decision about the print
  or the look. `thinnest_wall_mm` is the lower end of the film, not a value to use: the hook tip has 0.000033 mm, and a value just above it
  removes almost nothing (0.001 mm cuts 2.0 of its 485.5 mm2). `area_below_voxel_mm2` is the scale of the whole film (hook, tip: 292.6 of
  485.5 mm2 below 2 mm). A way to find a value: write one, resume the run (below), read `thin_area_mm2`, `cut_area_mm2` and
  `thin_area_after_mm2` for each body, and change the value if the film that the user wants gone is still there. Measured on the hook (tip,
  voxel 2 mm): the thin area is 47.1, 182.3, 233.4, 242.2, 282.6 and 292.6 mm2 for 0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 mm (at 2.0 mm it is
  `area_below_voxel_mm2`). With the `verify` of P4b-3 on a scratch merge (not in this branch), the file of 0.25 mm has a stiffness of 559 N/mm
  (hang) and 1131 N/mm (pull-off), the file of 0.5 mm 488 and 411 N/mm, and the file without the setting 0 and 0 N/mm (the film carries the
  load). At 2.0 mm, the voxel size, the written file has one non-manifold edge after the float32 reload: `watertight` is `false`, `pinches_left`
  is 2, and the log line and a note say so.
- *The rule, with the setting* `t` (`settings.part_only_min_film_mm`, mm). A contact triangle is thin if its wall is thinner than `t`.
  Each thin triangle gets a prism: the triangle and its copy moved along the inward normal by the depth `min(t, wall + gap / 2)`
  (`t` when the ray has no second hit). The depth comes from the centre ray of the triangle: on that ray the prism stops in the middle of
  the air gap behind the film. Off the centre ray the prism cuts any material of the part under the triangle, up to its depth (see *Edge
  of a film*). Measured: a rib 0.3 mm wide that stands 0.1 mm behind a film of 0.1 mm, off every centre ray, loses 0.135 mm3 at a value of
  0.3 mm and 1.08 mm3 at 1.0 mm (the film itself is 0.675 mm3). The prisms are joined and subtracted from the part. Then the loose-piece rule runs again, and the same float32 clean-up as
  before. A contact triangle with a thicker wall keeps the exact face of the removed body.
- *Pinch vertices.* The cut can leave two vertices with the same float32 position that no edge joins (the thin triangles alternate
  with thicker ones around a vertex, or a thin triangle touches the rim of a film). `topopt.tet` refuses such a surface. The step finds
  these positions exactly (equal float32 coordinates, no distance) and adds a prism for each contact triangle that has a corner there
  (the same depth rule). It repeats until no new pinch is left. The set only grows, so the loop ends (2 or 3 passes in the measured runs,
  0.1 to 0.4 s). A pinch that the part had before the cut is not touched. The repair is on purpose: it makes a file that the mesher of
  `topopt.tet` accepts, and no contact triangle with a thin centre wall stays. The price is that the cut area can be larger than the thin
  area. If no contact triangle with a wall has a corner at a pinch, the loop cannot fix it. The block then has `pinches_left` above 0 and
  a note with the options. It is 0 in the measured runs, except the hook at a value equal to the voxel size (2.0 mm), where it is 2. The facts give both areas for each body: `thin_area_mm2` and `thin_triangles` (the triangles that are thin by the rule), and
  `cut_area_mm2` and `cut_triangles` (the triangles that got a prism). Measured: bar, plate, 0.1 mm: thin 54.65 mm2, cut 84.08 mm2; hook, tip,
  0.05 mm: thin 30.95 mm2, cut 90.66 mm2 (film removed 3.49 mm3 against 0.58 mm3 for the thin triangles alone); bar, plate, 0.05 mm: thin
  22.28 mm2, cut 22.66 mm2. A variant that drops the prisms at a pinch instead (the set only shrinks) was measured: it leaves 3 to 63 % of the
  thin area in place, so it is not used.
- *Edge of a film.* Where a thin wall meets a thick wall the prism of a triangle cuts a notch into the thick wall as deep as the depth of
  the prism, with the footprint of the whole triangle. So `film_removed_mm3` is all the material that the cut removes: the film and, at an
  edge or off the centre ray, other material. Measured with the prisms of the thin triangles alone: 12 % (t 0.05) to 22 % (t 0.5)
  of the removed volume is notch, not film.
- *Limits of the rule* (facts, not errors). The wall is measured at the centre of a triangle. A wedge of film inside a triangle whose
  centre wall is above `t` can stay. Measured on the bar, plate, with 8 sample points on each triangle of the written file: the area with a
  wall under `t` is 33.3, 54.5 and 72.8 mm2 without the setting and 12.0, 6.1 and 4.2 mm2 with it, for `t` 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 mm. The cut
  also makes new triangles. The step measures the walls again on the result, at the centre of each contact triangle that stays
  (`thin_area_after_mm2`, `thinnest_wall_after_mm`). That is the thin area that stays after the rule, as a fact. It is 0 in
  the bar at 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 and in the hook at 0.05 and 0.25; in the hook at 0.5 one new wedge triangle of the keep-out body stays
  (0.135 mm2, wall 0.44 mm). A fact at the centre does not see a wedge inside a larger triangle.
- *The mesher.* The file passes the input check of the mesher (`topopt.tet.surface.surface_report`: one closed manifold, no non-manifold
  edge or vertex) at every measured value. The mesher itself (`mesh_stl`, section 14) was run on the written files, and it is not always
  satisfied (facts, not limits of this step). Bar, mesh sizes 1.0, 1.2, 1.5 and 2.0 mm: without the setting 0 of 4 sizes give a mesh; with 0.05 mm
  4 of 4; with 0.1 mm 0 of 4 (the surface that the mesher prepares has non-manifold edges); with 0.2 mm 4 of 4. Hook: with 0.05 mm the default
  size fails (the prepared surface crosses itself at 6 places) and 3.0 mm gives a mesh; with 0.25 and 0.5 mm both sizes give a mesh.
- *A value that removes everything.* If the cut leaves no material of the field, the step is a fault (below), and the error text gives
  the value and the option (a smaller value, or remove the key).
- *A fault in the measure or the rule.* With the setting on, a fault in the measure of the walls or in the rule is a fault of the step too
  (below). The error names the fault and the option: `the film rule failed (<Type>: <message>). Option: remove
  settings.part_only_min_film_mm to get the exact cut`. A fault of the files (a region file that is gone) does not get this option, because
  removing the key would not help. With the setting off, a fault in the measure of the contact faces is not a fault of the step (`contact`
  is `{}`, and a note says so).

**`metrics.json` key `part_only`** (a run with the key; after `interfaces`, before `verdict`):

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `applied` | `true` when the file was written. |
| `file` | `"part_only.stl"`, or `null` when `applied` is false. |
| `removed` | the labels `role:name` in the order of the YAML. `role` is `fixed`, `load`, `solid` or `keep_out`. `name` is the file name, or the region name for `load`. |
| `volume_before_mm3` | volume of `final.stl` as a slicer reloads it (`mesh.stl_roundtrip.volume_mm3`). |
| `volume_after_mm3` | volume of `part_only.stl` as reloaded. |
| `removed_mm3` | `volume_before_mm3 - volume_after_mm3`: the bodies, and the dropped pieces. |
| `overlap_mm3` | for each label, the volume of the mesh of `final.stl` that lies inside that body (0.0 for a keep-out region: it is a void in `final.stl`). Two bodies that overlap share volume, so the sum can be above the volume that the cut removes. |
| `leftovers_dropped` | `{"bodies": n, "volume_mm3": v}`: the loose pieces that hold no material of the field. With the film setting the number counts the pieces of both passes of the rule. |
| `contact` | (added with P4b-6) for each label: `area_mm2` (the area of the contact triangles of that body), `triangles`, `thinnest_wall_mm` (`null` if there is no contact triangle) and `area_below_voxel_mm2` (the contact area with a wall below the voxel size). Always there, also with the setting off. With the setting each record also has `thin_area_mm2` and `thin_triangles` (wall below the value), `cut_area_mm2` and `cut_triangles` (the triangles that got a prism), `film_removed_mm3` (the volume of the part inside the prisms of that body: the film and any other material that a prism cuts), and for the contact faces that stay: `area_after_mm2`, `thinnest_wall_after_mm` and `thin_area_after_mm2`. A record has `unmeasured_triangles` (and `unmeasured_triangles_after`) if some ray had no hit. With the setting off, a fault in the measure gives `contact` `{}` and a note, and the file is still the exact cut; with the setting the fault is a fault of the step (below). |
| `min_film_mm` | only with `settings.part_only_min_film_mm`: the value in mm. |
| `pinches_left` | only with the setting: the number of positions where the cut surface touches itself at a vertex (two vertices with the same float32 position that no edge joins), measured on the part that is written, not counting the positions that the part had before the cut. It is 0 when the repair of pinch vertices finished (the measured runs, except the hook at 2.0 mm, where it is 2). If it is above 0 a note gives the options (another value, or remove the key). |
| `film_removed_mm3` | only with the setting: the volume that the join of all prisms removed from the part. It is all the material that the cut removes: the film and, at the edge of a film or off the centre ray of a triangle, other material of the part. |
| `bodies` | the number of connected bodies of the reloaded file. A hook has 1. More than 1 is a fact, not a fault: the removed body may have joined members. |
| `mass_g`, `triangles` | of the reloaded file (`material.density`). |
| `watertight` | the reload check: watertight, consistent winding, volume above 0 (`stl_roundtrip.ok`). |
| `shortest_edge_mm` | the shortest edge of the reloaded mesh (a fact about slivers, no limit). |
| `stl_roundtrip` | the same record as `mesh.stl_roundtrip` (section 19) for this file. |
| `mesh_method` | the method that made the mesh that was cut (`sdf` or `blur`). |
| `notes` | optional list of texts. A note says that the cut leaves pinch vertices (`pinches_left` above 0), that no removed body shares volume with the mesh, and that the `blur` method holds a removed body as a voxel shape (so the cut leaves voxel steps; the option is `settings.mesh_method: sdf`). With the film setting off, a note also says that the contact faces of some bodies have a wall thinner than the voxel size. It gives, for each such body, the thinnest wall and `area_below_voxel_mm2`. It says that the thinnest wall is the lower end of the film and not a value to use, and it gives the option: write `settings.part_only_min_film_mm: <the wall thickness that you want to cut off, in mm>` in a new YAML file in the folder of the old one, resume the finished run, and read `thin_area_mm2`, `cut_area_mm2` and `thin_area_after_mm2`. The voxel size is the existing scale of the run; no value is recommended. |
| `t_s` | seconds spent in this step. |

**Fault.** A fault in the step (a region file that is gone, a cut that leaves no material, any error of the geometry code) gives
`{"applied": false, "file": null, "removed": [...], "error": "<Type>: <message>", "t_s": ...}`, no `part_only.stl` (a file of an older
post-process of the folder is deleted before the cut), and a warning in the log. The run is finished and `final.stl` is valid. A post-process
of a folder whose `run.json` has no `part_only` key deletes an old `part_only.stl` too. A resource error (a memory error, a failed thread start) is
not a fault of the step: the post step stops with `PostResourceError`, the status is `error` and `topopt run` ends with exit code 2 (section 19,
"Resource errors"; #447).

**Apply the film setting to a run that has finished.** The setting acts in the post step only, so the optimization does not run again.
Write the YAML with the value as a NEW file in the folder of the old YAML (the region STL paths are relative to the YAML folder).
`topopt run <the new yaml> --out <the run folder> --resume --allow-changed-inputs` (MCP: `run_topopt` with `resume=true` and
`allow_changed_inputs=true`) repeats the post step. It deletes `result/` first and makes it again, and it cuts `history.jsonl` and the
snapshots to the last checkpoint pass (the same pass for a finished run). No optimizer pass runs: measured on the bar and the hook, the
sha256 of `history.jsonl`, every snapshot, `labels.bin`, `result/final.stl` and `result/preview.bin` is the same before and after, and the
arrays of `checkpoint.npz` are equal. Only `result/part_only.stl`, `metrics.json`, `refine.html`, `run.json`, `run.log`, `status.json`,
`verdict.json` and `job.json` change. The wall time (Linux x86_64, 2 threads) is 5.5 s (bar) and 7.8 s (hook) on a quiet host, 8.4 s and
12.0 s on a loaded host (load average 30 on 22 cores); a fresh run takes 6 s and 16 s. A resume without the override stops at once and writes
nothing. To keep the old run, copy the run folder first and resume the copy, or run the YAML in a new `out_dir`. `compare_runs` shows
the key in `setup.yaml_diff` when the two YAML files differ, and `part_only.*` in the keys of `run.json` that differ. It has no metrics
row for `part_only`: read `metrics.part_only` of each run (`run_result`).

**`run.json` key `part_only`.** See section 5. The post step writes the keys of the block above into it and keeps `entries`. The log
(`run.log`, the screen) gets a line `part_only: N body(ies) cut out (...); volume A -> B mm3, K body(ies) in result/part_only.stl`, a
line for the dropped pieces when there are some, with the film setting one line `part_only: film rule (settings.part_only_min_film_mm
<t> mm): thin <a> mm2 (<n> triangle(s)); cut <c> mm2 (<m> triangle(s), with the repair of pinch vertices); <volume> mm3 of material removed;
the thinnest wall that stays is <w> mm`, and one line for each note. `thin` is the contact area with a wall below the value, `cut` is the area that the
cut takes from the contact faces. The two numbers differ when the repair of pinch vertices adds triangles (hook, tip, 0.25 mm: thin 187.740 mm2
and 173 triangles, cut 286.890 mm2 and 207 triangles, summed over the three bodies).

**Verify (added with P4b-3).** `topopt verify` meshes `nominal.stl` or `final.stl` as before. With `--part-only` (MCP
`verify_run(part_only=true)`) it meshes `result/part_only.stl`, and the removed bodies become boundary conditions at their contact faces
(section 16, "Region rule with `--part-only`"). A run without the file gives a `UserError` with the fact and the options. Without the
option, a run that has the file gets one fact line that names the option, and `verify.json` is the same as before. Machining stock (section 23):
`part_only.stl` is cut from the as-printed `final.stl`, so it keeps the stock. Verify states this as a fact and makes no second cut.
Known limit: the thin film around a removed body (above) is part of the mesh that verify gets. On the hook (voxel 2 mm, mesh size 3 mm) the
load goes into the film around the removed tip (the top-stress elements lie in it): the stiffness of that tet model is 0.47 to 0.58 N/mm against 1295 to 1317 N/mm of the optimizer (measured, 2026-10-23). The
boundary-condition facts of verify are right for that mesh, but its stiffness is not the stiffness of the part without the film. No film rule
is decided.

**Platforms.** The step needs `manifold3d` and `trimesh`, the same packages as the `sdf` method. It runs on macOS (Apple silicon)
and on Linux x86_64. It uses no solver and no GPU.

### 9.2 The part card: `result/report.md` (added with P9-7a)

A run has many result files (`metrics.json`, `run.json`, `verdict.json`, `run.log`, the case file, the verify output, the images). The user has no
one file to keep or to share. The part card is that file: one page of Markdown, plain words first, numbers with units (mm, N, MPa, g). Code:
`topopt/part_card.py` (standard library only; it imports `topopt.runinfo` and, for the brief, `topopt.case`).

**Rules.**
- The card reads files that the run folder already has. It computes no new result and sets no threshold. The only arithmetic is a change of unit
  (`overhang_fraction` to a percent). A fact that no file holds is written as `not known`, or as `not run` with the step that gives it.
- Every key is read with `.get()`: a key that a later build adds shows when it is there, and a run folder from an older build gives `not known` and no error.
  A file that is missing or does not parse is named in the section Sources.
- The same run folder gives the same bytes. The card has no time of writing: the date is `started_at` of `run.json`. A path is never absolute: a link starts at
  the folder of the card (`result/`), the problem YAML is shown by its file name only.
- A section that fails to build is one line that names the error. The other sections stay.

**Sections** (the headings are `part_card.SECTIONS`; the text before the first heading says what the card is and how to write it again):

| Heading | Content | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| The part | name, problem file name, `started_at`, run time, voxel size, solver, mesh method, and the verdict in plain words (`iteration_limit`: "The run stopped at its pass limit (pass N of M)", with whether the objective settled and every constraint row is met) and the verdict text of the run | `run.json`, `metrics.json` (`verdict`, else `verdict.json`) |
| Fine pass | only for a fine run (`run.json` `fine_from`: the parent folder name, its pass and voxel, the voxel, the start source and points, the volume shift, the tolerance and the maximum, and how the fine pass ended, from `verdict.json`), or for a run whose part needs a finer voxel (`part_voxel.recommend`: the fact line). The heading is not in the card of any other run | `run.json` (`fine_from`, `part_voxel`) |
| Mass and volume | the design space and its other active regions (fixed, load, solid), all solid (before); the part in `final.stl` (after); mass saved; the asked-mass fact line (`volume_basis.mass_asked_line`) for a run with `settings.target_mass_g`; density; triangles, watertight, mesh method; `part_only` mass and volume when the key is there | `metrics.json`, `run.json` (`derived`) |
| Stiffness | for each load case: the force, the stiffness (N/mm) and the compliance at the end (N mm); the weighted compliance at the start and at the end. A null stiffness shows its `reason` | `run.json` (`load_cases`, `derived`), `metrics.json`, `history.jsonl` (the last row; robust mode: `robust.compliance_cases_nominal`) |
| The brief | the requirement, the assumptions and criteria with their origin (`user`, `inferred`, `default`), and a note when the run started with another brief or with none. Without a brief: "No brief" and the assumptions of the YAML (no origin) | `<yaml stem>.case.json` beside the problem YAML |
| Print facts | printer settings and what was assumed, bed fit, overhang area, plate contact, support volume estimate, thinnest member (estimates) | `metrics.json` `print` |
| Verify (independent check) | file checked, mesh size, SHA-256 match with the mesh now in `result/`, and for each load case the p99.9 stress by volume, the peak, the largest motion, the stiffness against the optimizer, and with an allowable the margin | `verify/verify.json` |
| Other checks that ran | the stress row summaries and the buckling result, the interface warnings | `metrics.json` (`stress`, `buckling`, `interfaces`) |
| Lost force | the force that sits on nodes shared by a load and a fixed region (case, N, percent), or "None" | `run.json` `lost_force` |
| Images | the PNG files of `renders/` (and of `result/`) in name order; a `_montage.png` is shown as an image. A PNG file that is older than `result/final.stl` (modification times, no threshold) has the note "may be from an earlier result". Else one line that names `render_part` | the files |
| Files | `result/final.stl`, `nominal.stl`, `part_only.stl`, `final.step`, `part_only.step`, `metrics.json`, `verify/verify.json` and `run.log`, those that exist | the files |
| Not checked | stress (unless a stress row or verify ran), buckling, fatigue (unless verify ran the Goodman check), the printed part, print limits, and the verify check; each with what gives it | the sections above |
| Sources | the files that were read, not found, or not readable | |

**When it is written.** The run body of `topopt run` (`cmd_run`) calls `topopt.cli.write_part_card` once, after the post step and after the buckling check, and before
it writes the status `done` (`part_card.write_logged`, in its own `try`). So every `topopt run` that has a result has the card with no agent call, with the buckling
result of a run with `buckling.check`, and including a resume that repeats the post step. The log gets `part card: result/report.md`, or one line
`warning: part card not written: <error>` and the run goes on (exit code and status do not change).
Why there: the check runs after `cli.finish` and adds `buckling` to `metrics.json`, so a card written inside `finish` would say "not run" for a check that ran (review M1).
`post.finish` is also called by tests and tools, and other branches change it and `finish`; the lines around `post_finish` are unchanged.
`part_card.write(run_dir)` raises `NoResult` (no `result/metrics.json`) or `OSError`; `write_logged` never raises.

**Write it again.** A fact file can come after the post step: `verify/verify.json`, the buckling result of `topopt buckling` run later, PNG files of `render_part`, a STEP file. There is one way to write the card again, and it adds no MCP tool:
`topopt report <run_dir>` (prints the path; exit code 1 for a folder with no result or a file that cannot be written), and the MCP tool `run_result`, which writes
the card again before it answers (section 10: `report_md`, `report_md_rel`). The file is written (`runinfo.write_atomic`) only when its bytes change.

**Not in this version.** HTML or PDF, the preference card, images made in the post step (a render costs time on each run), and a translation. The images are the PNG files in `renders/` now: `renders/` is not removed when a new
run goes into the same folder, so render again after it. Tests: `tests/test_part_card.py` (the sections, with and without data, the numbers, the refresh,
determinism, a recording of an older build) and `tests/test_part_card_wiring.py` (the run, a write error, `topopt report`, `run_result`, the description).

## 10. MCP server (G)

`topopt_mcp/server.py`, stdio transport.

**The tool set and the core set (#174).** The server has 32 tools (`TOOL_SURFACE` in `topopt_mcp/server.py`; `topopt_mcp/README.md`
"Tools" names all of them). Older clients (Claude Code before v2.1.296) cut the text `INSTRUCTIONS` at 2048 characters
(`OLD_CLIENT_CUT`, #380), so it cannot name all 32 tools. It names a core set first and keeps the rule of one tool in the description of
that tool. The members are chosen from facts, with no target size: a tool is core when the flow of `skills/start-here/SKILL.md`
(with `.claude/skills/part-to-topopt/SKILL.md`) calls it AND an eval case under `evals/` or its mock calls it (the intersection of the two
sources). The core set has 10 tools, in the order of the flow:

Core tools: `environment`, `find_features`, `build_regions`, `record_brief`, `check_problem`, `render_part`, `run_topopt`, `run_status`, `run_result`, `print_check`.

The line "Core tools" of `INSTRUCTIONS` keeps the two routes of the flow line that it replaced: `build_regions` for a part description,
and `check_problem` for own or edited STLs and YAML.
The other tools are named in the flow lines of `INSTRUCTIONS` (`stop_run`) or in its last line ("Descriptions say when to use: ..."), except these 11, which it does not
name (no room under the cut; the client lists every tool anyway):

Not named in INSTRUCTIONS: `verify_status`, `ratchet_status`, `ratchet_approve`, `save_preferences`, `find_printer`, `save_printer`, `find_material`, `save_material`, `printer_materials`, `export_step`, `show_problem`.

A change of the core set changes the line "Core tools" of `INSTRUCTIONS`, this list and the line "Core tools" of `topopt_mcp/README.md`
together; `tests/test_core_tools.py` pins the three to the same set and checks that no live tool is lost from the texts.

Tools:

- `run_topopt(yaml_path: str, out_dir: str | None) -> {"run_dir", "dashboard_url", "pid"}`.
  Starts `topopt run ... --dashboard` as a background process and returns at
  once. The reply also has `message` (#440). Nothing calls the agent back when the run ends: no MCP client starts a new model turn for a background job,
  and the server sends nothing that could. The agent can call `run_status` again in the same turn until the state is done, error or stopped,
  or `process_alive` is false. Or it can end the turn and tell the user what to ask for the result. A promise of a later report cannot be kept.
  The descriptions of `run_topopt`, `run_status`, `verify_status` and `ratchet_status`, the start messages of `verify_run` and `ratchet_run`,
  and step 5 of the skill `start-here` say the same (`tests/test_no_later_report.py`). The reply also has `brief_stated` and `brief_facts`. A YAML with a case file and no current brief gets
  `{"state": "awaiting_user", ...}` and the override `proceed_without_brief=true` (section 30). A change of a method setting
  only (for example `settings.solver`) after the brief is not a stale brief: the run starts and `brief_facts` names the key.
  Since P9-14 the reply has `other_server_jobs` when another topopt server on this machine has a running job (a fact with options; the run starts; section 43.5).
- `show_problem(yaml_path)` (the problem view, `topopt_mcp/problem_view.py` and `problem_view.html`): the problem as a 3D page of MCP Apps
  (spec 2026-01-26), with the meshes in `_meta` and the facts in `structuredContent` (`yaml_rel` is the path that `run_topopt` takes; `start_run_dir_rel` is the run folder that a start without `out_dir` uses).
  No optimizer run. The button "Start the run" reads `hostCapabilities` of `ui/initialize` and goes one of three ways:
  - `serverTools` offered: the click is the consent of the user, and the page sends no `ui/message`. It first calls `run_status` with `run_dir` = `start_run_dir_rel` of the facts (the folder that `run_topopt` uses without `out_dir`: `_rel(default_out())`, `runs/live`).
    - A folder with state `none` and no checkpoint, and no run that works there (the rule below comes first: a live job lock on a folder with no status file has state `none`): the page calls `run_topopt` at once (`yaml_path` = `yaml_rel`, `out_dir` = `start_run_dir_rel`).
    - A folder that holds a run: the first click shows a warning, and a second click ("Replace and start") makes the same `run_topopt` call (`yaml_path` = `yaml_rel`, `out_dir` = `start_run_dir_rel`). The warning names the folder, the state, the pass (`checkpoint.iteration` of `checkpoint.iterations`, else the status pass) and the YAML of the old run (`checkpoint.yaml_path`, only when set). It says what the start deletes: the result only for a done run, the checkpoints when the reply shows one, else the files.
    - The second click looks at the folder again. It starts only if the job is the one that the warning named; another job gets a new warning.
    - A run that works there gets no start: job state `running` (this also covers a run of the command line), or `process_alive` with state `starting`, `running` or `postprocess`, or `process_alive` with a `fine_run` in state `not started`, `starting`, `running` or `postprocess` (a fine pass still to come: `run_topopt` counts the run as busy). The page shows the summary of `run_status` and "Check again". A done or stopped run whose process only serves the dashboard is not such a run: `run_topopt` stops that process.
    - A pre-check that fails is shown, nothing starts, and the button goes the way below.
    - The facts of the start reply (the run folder, what the start replaced, the note about a deleted checkpoint of `earlier_checkpoint`, the fact of `other_server_jobs`) stay on the screen in their own line, which the poll does not replace.
  - A refusal of `run_topopt` (`error`, or `awaiting_user` with `options`) shows one short line ("The run did not start: ...", the first sentence of the reply), and the page does not retry. The options are for the agent: with `message` offered a button "Ask the agent" sends them in a `ui/message` with the refusal text; else the page shows the line to type.
  - A call that fails (an error of the host, `isError`, an unreadable reply, no run folder in the reply) is shown, and the button then goes the way below (`message`, else the line). A call with no answer in `HOST_ANSWER_WAIT_MS` (30000 ms) is not a failure of the tool: the host may run it later. The page says "No answer from the host: the run may have started." and offers "Check again" (`run_status` of `start_run_dir_rel`). That folder can still hold the old run, so the page keeps the job (`job.started_at` and `job.pid`) of the look before the start: a reply with state `none`, or with the same job, gives "No run has started in <folder> yet. You can start it again.": the button "Start the run" is free again (a new click looks at the folder first, and `run_topopt` refuses a start while a run of this server is busy), and "Check again" stays for a call that runs late; no end note and no "Discuss the result". A reply is a new run (watched, or shown with its summary) when it has `job.earlier_run` true, `job.state` `no_record`, or state `starting` with `process_alive` true (a new process whose job record is not written yet), when the job differs from the one of the look, or when the folder was empty at the look. A run that ends with no status message shows its `summary` as the reason, on screen and in the end note. The route does not change.
  - With `updateModelContext` offered, the page sends `ui/update-model-context` after the start (the run folder, the two start facts, "call run_status") and a second one at the end (the state, the verdict, the pass, the volume, the mass of the part if the verdict has it, the run time), which replaces the first. `structuredContent` goes in only if the host lists `structuredContent` in `updateModelContext` (or lists no type); the text has the facts anyway.
  - The page calls `run_status` through the host every `RUN_STATUS_POLL_MS` (5000 ms, one constant at the top of the page script; one call is one round trip through the host) and shows the pass, the volume and the time.
    The run has ended when `state` is `done`, `error` or `stopped`, or `process_alive` is false. A reply with `earlier_run` (`topopt/earlier_run.py`) is the reply for a job that an input check refused over an earlier run: its `state` is that job's own state (`error`), and only its data keys moved into `earlier_run`; so the same rule applies. Then
    the page stops polling and shows the end numbers. The page also stops when the host tears it down, and after a failed poll (it shows the reason and a button "Check again";
    there is no automatic retry). A page that comes back from the page cache (`pageshow`, `persisted`) shows "Check again" and does not poll by itself; if the run had ended, it shows the end view and sends no second end note. After a start went through, the button "Start the run" stays disabled (also after the end, and when the host sends the tool result again); a refusal or a failed call gives it back.
    At the end, with `message` offered, a button "Discuss the result" sends `ui/message`.
  - `message` offered, no `serverTools`: the button sends `ui/message` ("Start the run of <yaml> (from the problem view)."); the host may only put the text into the chat input. `HOST_ANSWER_WAIT_MS` covers every request of the page, also `ui/message`: a host may hold it while it asks the user, so a `ui/message` with no answer in that time says "No answer from the host: the message may have been sent. Look in the chat before you press the button again." and gives the button back.
  - Neither: the page shows the line "Type in the chat: start the run of <yaml>".
  A details line in the page shows which of `message`, `serverTools` and `updateModelContext` the host offered. The logic is in the block "run button logic" of the page; `tests/test_problem_view.py` runs it in node.
- `record_brief(yaml_path, text, assumptions=None, criteria=None)` and `case_status(yaml_path)` (section 30): the brief of a
  problem YAML, the input hashes, the runs and what is stale.
- `build_regions(spec: dict | str, name: str | None) -> dict` (the part builder, `topopt/regions_builder.py`): writes the region STLs and
  the problem YAML to `<work folder>/runs/<name>/` and returns `ok`, `name`, `run_dir_rel`, `yaml_rel`, `files_rel`, `other_files_rel`,
  `overwrote_existing_folder`, `voxel_size`, `voxel_auto`, `retries`, `builder_ok`, `problems`, `builder_warnings`, `report`, `check`
  (the data of `check_problem`, or `null` with `check_error`), `warnings`, `derived` and `assumptions`. `ok` is true only when
  `builder_ok` is true (since P9-8). A builder problem (a guard stop, a setting that the loader refuses, a piece with no support, a
  memory estimate above the RAM) gives `ok: false` and `builder_ok: false` with the line in `problems`; the files stay and every other key
  is as it was. A spec that cannot be read gives `{"ok": false, "error": <one line>}`. A value of the wrong type or shape (a `radius` that is a list or null, `prism.points` that is not a list, a `load_cases`, `forces`, `pressures`, `springs` or `joints` entry that is not a mapping, a `settings` or `material` block that is not a mapping, a number key with a list, a mapping, null or a bool) is found by one walk over the spec before the build (F4-41, `regions_builder.check_spec_shape`). The line names the key path (`load_cases[0].forces[1]`), what the spec has (the type and a short repr) and what it expects, with an example. The CLI prints it as `SPEC ERROR: ...` with exit code 1. A bool is not a number there: it was read as 1 or 0 before. A spec item `{stl: {path, plug_holes, screw_holes, ring_mm}}` takes the user's own closed STL as a solid (section 45.1; it is not the `stl` interface of section 23). `screw_holes` writes one `tube` interface for each screw hole, with the ring thickness `ring_mm` or the default rule, and the item `{screw_ring: {path, hole}}` is the same ring as a `fixed`, `load` or `solid` region (section 45.2). `settings.stop_rules` of a spec is copied into the
  YAML as given (the loader checks it). A mapping turns the stop rules on, so a `time_budget_s` in it ends the run (section 11).
  The `settings` of a spec (F4-46): the builder copies every key that the YAML takes (`config.SETTINGS_REQUIRED` and `config.SETTINGS_OPTIONAL`), as
  given, and the loader checks the value (`objective: mass` reaches the YAML; so do the `stress_*`, `robust`, `eta_eroded`, `gpu_*` and
  `part_only_min_film_mm` keys, which the builder dropped without a word before). The keys it writes itself are `voxel_size` (the grid it built),
  `iterations` (default 80) and `volume_fraction` (default 0.25) or `target_mass_g` (`regions_builder.BUILDER_OWNED_SETTINGS`); `target_active` and
  `allow_large_grid` are read by the builder and not written (`BUILDER_ONLY_SETTINGS`). Any other key is a `SpecError` before a file is written, with the
  text of the YAML loader for an unknown key (`config.unknown_key_text`: the key, the known keys and the options), for the CLI, the tool and a spec text.
  A key that the config gets later is copied with no change in the builder; `tests/test_builder_settings.py` fails when a run key is neither copied
  nor builder-owned. The order of the keys in the YAML is the old order for the old keys, then the order of `config.SETTINGS_OPTIONAL`.
  The top level of a spec follows the same rule (F4-46, round 2). The builder copies every top-level key that the YAML takes (`config.TOP_REQUIRED` and
  `config.TOP_OPTIONAL`), as given, and the loader checks it: `springs`, `joints`, `assumptions`, `mirror`, `print` and, since round 2, `limits`, `buckling`,
  `interfaces`, `acceptance` and `bore_checks`, which the builder dropped without a word before (a requirement of the user was lost). It writes `name`,
  `regions`, `load_cases`, `settings` and `material` itself (`regions_builder.BUILDER_OWNED_TOP_LEVEL`); `material` takes `E`, `nu` and `density` (written as
  float(), with the defaults; `BUILDER_OWNED_MATERIAL`). `fixed_axes` is read by the builder and not written (`SPEC_ONLY_TOP_LEVEL`). A top-level key in none of
  these, and a `material` key that the YAML does not take, is a `SpecError` before a file is written, with the text of the YAML loader (`unknown key 'k' in
  'top level'. Known keys: ...` or `... in 'material'`). A null is the same as no key; an empty `springs`, `joints`, `assumptions` or `mirror` is not written, as
  before. The old keys keep their order in the YAML, then the new ones follow in the order of `config.TOP_OPTIONAL`. `tests/test_builder_top_level.py` is the
  guard. The spec has no `regions.measure` or `regions.not_printed` role (`build_all` refuses it), so a `limits` row names a load region.
