- *Levels.* With `--levels`, the gate reads the finest level (the reference level). With two or more levels, each check also has `previous_value` and `change_from_previous` ((finer - coarser) / coarser; `null` if the coarser value is 0 or a value is missing) against the level before it, and the key
  `previous_level_mm`. The change is a fact: it does not decide.
- *The key `gate`.* `requested` (true), `passed` (true if at least one check is gated and every one has `met: true`), `mesh_size_mm`, `percentile`, `note`, `checks`, `not_gated`, `failed` (a list `"<check>:<name>"` of every check whose `met` is not true) and `reason` (only when no check was gated). `checks` holds only the checks that are gated:
  `stress` and `buckling` (a dict by case name), `displacement` and `alignment` (a dict by row name, with the `case` in the record). Each record: `value`, `limit`, `source` (the YAML place of the limit, for example `load_cases[hang].stress_limit`, `buckling.min_factor`,
  `limits.alignment[seats].shift_limit_mm`, or `--allowable-mpa (all cases)`), `unit`, `met` (true, false or null), `reason` (when `met` is null), `margin` and, for a stress record, `percentile`, `peak_qp_MPa` and the keys of the replaced limit and percentile (above).
  `margin` is 1 or more when `met` is true: limit / value for a stress and a row, value / limit for a buckling factor; `null` when the check has no value or the value is 0 (nothing to divide). `peak_qp_MPa` is the highest stress at one point of the case; it is information, as in the `limit` block (section 17).
  A buckling record also has three groups of keys for its three numbers (K1-C). `value_source` is the key that the value is read from: `buckling.cases[<case>].load_factors[0]`. `run_lowest_load_factor` (`{case, value}`) is a copy of the headline `buckling.lowest_load_factor`, the lowest over all load cases, so a reader sees the case value and the run value together. When the rigid-body rule of section 33 ran for the case, the record has `projected_value` (`rigid_body.load_factors[0]`, or `null` when the projected solve gave no factor), `projected_source` (`buckling.cases[<case>].rigid_body.load_factors[0]`) and `projected_reason`. The projected value is a fact. The gate and the ratchet do not read it: it is higher than the measured value (it does not see the support), and a higher number in place of the measured one would loosen `buckling.min_factor`, a requirement, which needs the consent of the user (section 41.2). The reason says what the number is and, when there is none, why.
- *What the gate does not check.* It is the static linear stress at one percentile by volume on one mesh, the linear buckling factor and the A5 rows. It does not cover fatigue (use the `bore_checks` block), the peaks at sharp features, printing defects or the print direction.
- *Memory.* The buckling check of the gate has the memory rule of section 16, "Memory of the buckling check": above the limit it is skipped, and then the gate fails with `met: null`. `--force` starts it.
- The text result prints one line `gate: ...` for each check (with the margin and, for a replaced limit, the replaced limit; for a buckling check, the key of the value, the lowest value of the run and, when the rule ran, the projected value as a fact) and each not gated item, then `gate: PASSED` or `gate: FAILED (...)`. The plain lines (`verify_status.plain`) use the gate limit of a case when there is no `--allowable-mpa`,
  say the margin and, when the highest value at one point is above the limit, the peak (as for `--allowable-mpa`), and end with the verdict line `gate: PASSED` or `gate: FAILED (...)` (D-4).

**Region rule.** A point belongs to a region when its signed distance to the region STL (positive inside) is at least `-band`.
A fixed region fixes all 3 dofs of every P2 node (vertex and edge midpoint) in it. A load region is every boundary facet with 3 vertices in it.
Keep-out regions are not used. A measure region (section 31) uses the same rule with the role `measure`; only the A5 rows read it. An empty region is an error with the nearest distance. The report has the counts at 0, 0.5 and 1 band, and for a
load region `normal_check` (`coherence` = |sum(a n)| / sum(a) with outward normals, and `mean_normal`): 1 is one flat side, a low value means
facets of different sides.

**Region rule with `--part-only`** (added with P4b-3). The rule is the same: the same band, no new tolerance and no new number. A removed body is not in the mesh,
so the rule finds the part next to the surface of the body: the contact face, and what the band takes next to it.

- A removed `fixed` region: the P2 nodes that the rule selects are clamped (all 3 dofs), as for a fixed region that is in the mesh. If the rule selects no node, the body clamps
  nothing. This is a fact (`boundary_condition: none`), not `EmptyRegion`. If then no fixed node is left, the part is a body with no fixed node: exit code 1 (see "Bodies and a singular matrix"),
  and the text says how many nodes each removed fixed body selected.
- A removed `load` region: the force is a uniform traction on the boundary facets whose 3 vertices the rule selects. The check of the resultant (`resultant_relative_error`) stays.
  If the rule selects no facet, the error is the one of a load region that no body touches (exit code 1), with the file and the removed bodies in the text.
  A removed load region that no load case uses gives no traction: `boundary_condition: none`, the `note` says why, the summary line says `no traction (no load case uses this region)`, and it is not in `singular_note`.
- A removed `solid` or `keep_out` region: no boundary condition. The report gives the facts of the selection and the fact (`singular_note`) that the matrix is singular when nothing
  else holds a piece of the part. A singular matrix stops the solve with exit code 1, the facts and the options.
- A region that is not removed: the rule as it is.

For each removed body the report gives the role, the file, the nodes, vertices and facets that the rule selects, the area of the selected facets, the counts at the three bands
(0, 0.5 and 1 band) and the contact area of the cut. The contact area is measured on `part_only.stl` and the body with no tolerance: for two solids that touch and do not overlap, it is
(area of the part + area of the body - area of their union) / 2, with the exact boolean of manifold3d. `selected_area_over_contact` compares the area of the selected facets
with it. On exact boxes (`tests/test_verify_part_only.py`) the contact areas equal the face areas of the boxes. On the part_only.stl of an optimizer run the ratio is 1.45 (bar plate), 1.47 (bar boss), 0.96 (hook plate) and 1.20 (hook tip);
it is above 1 where a film stays, and 22.6 for the keep-out hole of the hook, which touches the part along an edge only (measured, 2026-10-23).

**Bodies and a singular matrix.** A body is a set of tets that are linked through shared vertices (`topopt/verify/bodies.py`). After the meshing and
before the solve, the command states the body count (a `bodies:` line, `mesh.bodies` in `verify.json` with the volume, tets, box, fixed nodes and load
facets of each body, largest first). Two bodies share no node, so a body with no fixed node can move as a rigid piece and the matrix is singular.
These cases stop before the solve with exit code 1, and the text holds the facts, the likely causes and the options (no traceback, no "internal error"):
a body with no fixed node (the text names the body, its load facets, and how close it comes to a fixed region); a load region that matches no boundary
facet (no body touches it: the final part has no material at the load); a direct solver that stops on a zero pivot or a matrix that is not positive
definite (`pardiso` error code -4 or -7, `cholespy` "not positive definite" or, when CHOLMOD is silent, the residual of the test solve, `cholesky` SparseFactor status -1 or -2,
a `LinAlgError`), a solution with NaN, or a refined solve of a load case with a relative residual of `FACTOR_TEST_RESIDUAL` (1e-3) or more (see "Linear solver"):
`SingularSystem`, with the solver and its error text. A mesh of several bodies where every body has a fixed node is not an error: the count is a fact.
An empty fixed region is still `EmptyRegion` (exit code 2), except a removed fixed region with `--part-only` (a fact, see above).

**Traction rule.** Uniform traction F/A over the load facets. Each facet gives F a / (3 A) to each of its 3 edge midpoints and 0 to its vertices.
The resultant equals the force (`resultant_relative_error`, 1e-10 or less). Each load case is solved alone. Case weights are not used.

**Equilibrium.** `equilibrium` gives the force and moment residual of the reactions against the load. It tests the stiffness matrix and the
solve. It cannot find a wrong load: the reactions come from the same load vector, so a load twice as large gives the same residual.
The checks on the load are `resultant_relative_error` and `load_centre`.

**Memory model.** `estimate = 7.5e9 x dofs / 1e6 x 1.25` bytes (decimal GB) for `cholesky`, `pardiso` and `cholespy`. For `superlu` the
estimate is the central value of its model, with no margin: `0.50 GB + 1.63 GB x (million dofs) + 65,000 GB x C^2 x (million dofs)^2`. C = V / A^1.5
comes from the STL (dimensionless: 0.016 the hook, 0.027 a plate, 0.040 a bar, 0.068 a cube, 0.094 a sphere), because a compact part has much more fill
than a slender one (`topopt.verify.memory`). The model uses the square of the dofs; the fill measured on the hook grew about as N^1.65. The model
over the measured peak was 0.94 to 1.3 on the hook, 1.0 to 1.45 on a cube, a sphere and a bar, and 0.60 to 0.87 on a plate (17 meshes, one Linux host).
So the check gives a range with the number: `range_bytes` (`low`, `central`, `high`) is the central value divided by 1.45 and by 0.60; the peak was 0.69 to
1.67 times the central value. This is a fact about those shapes, not a promise. `ranges_by_backend` has it for `superlu` also when another factor runs
(the line "memory estimate with SuperLU instead" is printed only when SuperLU can run), and `memory.estimate_range_after_meshing_bytes` has it for the
real dofs. The guard compares the central value with the limit, and refuses only if the central value is above it. If only the upper end of the range is
above the limit (`upper_end_above_limit`), the run starts, and `notes` (also printed as `note:` lines) says so, with the options. When the modelled fill is
above 15 GB, `notes` also has the fact that scipy SuperLU has 32-bit indices, so near 2^31 factor entries (about 17 GB) more RAM may not help (not
measured). The refusal text and the out-of-memory text of the SuperLU factor have the same fact. The estimate of the factor that runs is the one the check
uses; the report also has `bytes_by_backend` (each factor), `compactness`, and `estimate_model` (the rule in words). Before meshing, `dofs = 6.35 V / h^3 + 17.0 A / h^2`
(V, A of the STL; h the size). The command refuses to start only if the estimate is above the smaller of the available RAM and `--max-gb`,
and `--force` is not given. The check before meshing covers all levels. The check after meshing uses the real dofs. Peak memory is
`ru_maxrss` in bytes (kB x 1024 on Linux): the peak of the process of the job. `children_peak_rss_bytes` is not a measurement of gmsh: on Linux a
child starts with the size of its parent, so the number is an upper bound of the child peak (the larger of its true peak and the size of the
parent at its start).

**Memory of the buckling check (B3).** The guard counts the factor only, as before. With the check on, the estimate also has a separate term (`topopt.verify.memory.buckling_bytes`):
`12 B x (nnz(K)/3 + 2 nnz(Kff)/3) + 8 B x free dofs x (ncv + 8) + 672 B for each tet and load case + 200 MB`, where `ncv` is the ARPACK basis size for `buckling.modes` (verify keeps the stress of every load case until the check starts). Before meshing,
`nnz(K)` is 77 for each dof and the tets are 0.21 for each dof; after meshing the real counts are used. These ratios are a model fit on one host (the hook at 139k, 359k and 662k dofs), not limits.
Each entry of `estimates_before_meshing` then has `buckling_bytes`, `estimate_with_buckling_bytes` and `above_limit_with_buckling`; the estimate lines print the estimate with the term.
The refusal before meshing is not changed by the term. After the factor, if the estimate with the term is above the smaller of the available RAM and `--max-gb`, and `--force` is not given,
the check is skipped (the record `buckling` has `status: skipped`, `reason: memory`, the facts and the options) and `topopt verify` goes on with the stress check. `buckling.max_gb` of the YAML is not used.
The term is above the measured growth of the peak: 1.35 to 4.4 times at the sizes of the fit (0.32, 0.53 and 0.81 GB against growths of 72 to 234, 199 to 389 and 300 MB), 2 load cases, one shape and one host.
On the hook at 1.5 mm (139k dofs) the check added 0.12 to 0.13 GB to the measured peak of the process and the term was 0.32 GB (2.6 to 2.7 times). More load cases and other shapes are not measured.
`memory.measured_over_estimate_with_buckling` compares the peak with the
estimate that has the term (0.75 with pardiso, 0.89 with SuperLU); `memory.measured_over_estimate` compares it with the estimate of the factor only.

**Time model.** Each estimate has `estimated_seconds` (for the solver of the run) and `seconds_by_backend` (`cholesky`: None, there is no
measurement on a P2 system; `pardiso`, `cholespy`, `superlu`), from a fit on 12 hook runs on one Linux x86_64 host (`topopt.verify.memory.estimate_seconds`;
`seconds_note`). It is a fact about that host (mean error about 18 % there, on a busy host), not a promise. The factor time of `superlu` is 20 s for each GB of
modelled fill, so it depends on the compactness of the part like the memory does (on the hook the whole run was within 0.6 to 1.3 of the estimate; on other
shapes the modelled factor time over the measured one was 0.4 to 1.9). The check prints the estimate before meshing and again with the real dofs (`estimate_seconds_after_meshing`).

**Linear solver.** Order for `auto`: `cholesky` (macOS arm64, Accelerate shim), `pardiso` (Linux x86_64, pypardiso), `cholespy` (`verify` extra), `superlu`
(scipy `splu`, BSD-3-Clause, always installed: the last fallback). Each factor is used with 3 steps of iterative refinement and a double-double
residual, so every factor gives the same solution (about 1e-9). The factor that ran is a printed fact, never a silent switch: the estimate lines and
`verify.json` (`backend`: `solver`, `requested`, `order`, `skipped`, `available`) name it, say why `auto` passed the others, and give its time and memory
estimate. A name that cannot run, and `auto` with no factor, give `SolverUnavailable` (exit code 1) with the notes of all factors. A cholespy that
is installed but fails to load gives the error text, not the hint to install the extra (the form of `solver_choice.resolve_solver` for pypardiso).
Every text that gives the install command (gmsh, scikit-fem and cholespy missing) gives the same command, and it installs the whole `verify` extra:
`uv pip install --python <python> -e '<checkout>[verify]'` in a source tree, and the pins of the three packages (`gmsh` only where the extra has a gmsh wheel)
in an installed package with no `pyproject.toml` beside it.
`superlu` runs `splu` with the order `MMD_AT_PLUS_A`, symmetric mode and no pivoting on the diagonally scaled matrix. **Test solve (both `superlu` and `cholespy`;
E3b).** After its factor, each of the two solves one fixed random vector and checks the relative residual of the scaled system: a residual of 1e-3 or more
(or NaN) is a singular matrix (`SingularSystem`, exit code 1). SuperLU does not always stop on a singular matrix, and CHOLMOD is often silent on one too: it stops on a pivot of
zero or below, but roundoff gives a tiny positive pivot (numpy 2.3.5, the floating body of `tests/test_verify_bodies.py`, 1,275 dofs: CHOLMOD factored it, the test solve gave
0.8 and the solution had entries of 1e12; on numpy 2.5.3 CHOLMOD raised for that body, but it was silent on 17 of 17 matrices held at one node or one line). There is one constant, `FACTOR_TEST_RESIDUAL = 1e-3` in `topopt/verify/factor.py`, and one test solve (the
same vector and the same error text, which gives the value and the threshold). `pardiso` and `cholesky` have no test solve; they stop with their own error. Measured on the hook matrix at 2.0 mm
(SuperLU): 4e-13 for a valid matrix, 3 for a floating part, 6 for a part with one fixed node, 3e-6 for a floating part on a spring of 1e-12 times the diagonal (valid, very
ill-conditioned; cholespy factors it too, 1e-5 on a path Laplacian of 400 nodes with the same spring). cholespy on the floating body of the tests: 3e-14 for the valid matrix of the
same mesh. The test solve of cholespy uses the lower triangle that CHOLMOD factored, made symmetric. The cost of the extra solve is 0.13 s at 359,193 dofs (the factor takes
40 s) and 0.02 s at 45,129 dofs (measured on the hook, cholespy, 4 threads). The test solve does not change the solution of a valid matrix (bit for bit). **The test solve finds most singular matrices, not all.** A fixed vector can miss a
matrix with one free rotation (a part held at the nodes of one line): the 6 mm cube of `tests/verify_mesh.py` held at the edge x 0, y 0 gives a test residual of 7.7e-4
(cholespy) and 4.2e-4 (SuperLU), and a valid bar with a soft middle third (E x 1e-9) gives 7.2e-4, so no threshold separates them (a valid matrix is refused from a spring of
3e-15 times the diagonal or a stiffness contrast of 1e10). **The residual of a real load case stops it** (E3b, fix round 1). After the refinement, `verify_run` computes the
relative residual `|b - A x| / |b|` of each load case (`linear_solve.relative_residual`, double-double residual). If it is `FACTOR_TEST_RESIDUAL` or more (or NaN), the run stops
with `SingularSystem` (exit code 1, the mesh facts and the options). It is for every factor (`cholesky`, `pardiso`, `cholespy`, `superlu`), and it uses the same constant. The
detail gives the load case, the value and the threshold, and `facts` has `load_case`, `relative_residual` and `threshold`. On the cube the residual is 0.19 to 0.34 on both numpy
pins (3e-12 on the hook at 1.0 mm). A load case with no force on the free dofs (|b| = 0) has no relative residual: it is not checked, and the report has `relative_residual` and
`backward_error` of `null` and a `note` in `linear_solve` (not NaN), and the summary line says "not defined (the load is zero)". The matrix must be the
full symmetric matrix: SuperLU reads both triangles, and one triangle gives a wrong solution and no error; cholespy reads the lower triangle. `topopt.solver.LinearSolver` is unchanged (it does not know `cholespy` or `superlu`). A cholespy that is gone when the
factor is made is `SolverUnavailable` too (exit code 1). The install hint for cholespy names the Python that runs topopt, as the pypardiso hint does.

**Files** (in `<run_dir>/verify/`).

- One level: `verify.json`, `fields.npz`, `mesh.npz`, `status.json`.
- Several levels: `h<size>/fields.npz` and `h<size>/mesh.npz` for each level, `verify.json` of the reference (finest) level with
  `levels` (`sizes_mm`, `relative_change`, `relative_change_first_to_last`), and `status.json`.
- `files` in `verify.json` (names relative to `verify/`): `verify`, `mesh`, `fields` (the files of the reference level) and, with several
  levels, `levels` (`{"<size>": {"mesh", "fields"}}`). The MCP result also has `files_abs`, `files_rel`, `verify_json`, `verify_json_rel`.
- A real run removes `verify.json`, `fields.npz`, `mesh.npz`, `status.json` and the `h<size>` folders from `verify/` before it starts. Other
  files stay. A new optimizer run in the same folder removes the whole `verify/` folder (`RUN_DIRS` in `snapshot.py`).
  `previous_verify` (`final_stl_sha256`, `same_final_stl`, `removed`) tells if the earlier `verify.json` was for the same mesh file (the file that `run.verified_file` names: `final.stl`, `nominal.stl` or `part_only.stl`; the keys keep their names). The `note:` line says "another mesh file (run.verified_file)".
- `fields.npz`: `p` (3, nodes) and `t` (4, tets, int32) of the P1 mesh in the pipeline layout, `vm_elem_max_<case>` (float32, max von Mises of each tet
  over its quadrature points), `node_xyz` (float32). `mesh.npz`: `TetMesh.save` (its `facts` hold `sha256`).
- `status.json` (written atomically while the job works): `format`, `pid`, `started_at`, `updated_at`, `state` (`starting`, `meshing`, `solving`,
  `writing`, `done`, `error`), `level`, `levels`, `size_mm`, `sizes_mm`, `solver`, `message`, `estimated_seconds_total`, `estimates`, and at the
  end `exit_code` and `error`.

**`verify.json`** (`format` 1). Keys: `kind`, `partial` and `coverage` (which sub-checks ran, failed or were not run: section 44), `run` (name, yaml_path, final_stl, voxel_size_mm, final_stl_sha256, verified_file), `yaml_vs_run` (`matches`,
`differences`), with `--part-only` the block `part_only` (below), `material` (E_MPa, nu), `stl` (volume, area, default mesh size), `band_mm`, `band_is_default`, `near_region_mm`, `load_sensitivity`,
`backend` (solver, requested, available, problem, refinement_steps), `extras`, `platform`, `memory_limit`, `estimates_before_meshing`
(`size_mm`, `estimated_dofs`, `estimate_bytes`, `estimated_seconds`, `seconds_by_backend`), `ok`, `estimate_only`, `reference_level_mm`, `mesh`
(the facts of `TetMesh`, and `bodies`, `p2_nodes`, `edges`, `dofs`, `free_dofs`, `fixed_dofs`, `p2_volume_mm3`, `p2_volume_over_stl`), `regions` (per region: band,
nodes, facets, area, centroid, `counts_by_band`, `normal_check` for a load region; `keep_out_used`, `near_region_mm`, `moment_reference_mm`),
`memory` (`estimate_before_meshing_bytes`, `estimate_after_meshing_bytes`, `rule_bytes`, `peak_rss_bytes`, `measured_over_estimate`,
`children_peak_rss_bytes`, `note`), `timing_s`, `cases`, `load_band_sensitivity`, `files`, `previous_verify`, `limit` (with `--allowable-mpa`), `no_allowable` (without it and without `--gate`; section 25.7), `gate` (only with `--gate`; "The gate" above),
`levels` (several levels), `exit_code`, and with B3, when the YAML or a flag asks for them, `buckling_check`, `buckling` and `motion`; with B4, when the YAML has the block `bore_checks` and the flag does not
turn it off, `bore_checks`, `bore_facts`, `goodman` and (with a `press_fit` block) `pressfit` (section 40).
These keys are absent when the check is off (with both off the file has the keys of the version before B3), a reader ignores unknown keys, and `format` stays 1.
`part_only` (added with P4b-3; only with `--part-only`; a file without the option has no such key): `on` (true), `file` (`part_only.stl`), `sha256` (of the file that was meshed), `run_record` (the keys of the block
`part_only` of `run.json` that describe the cut: `applied`, `removed`, `volume_before_mm3`, `volume_after_mm3`, `removed_mm3`, `leftovers_dropped`, `bodies`, `watertight`, `shortest_edge_mm`,
`mesh_method`, `notes`), `yaml_vs_run` (`matches`, `differences`, `note`), `notes` (with machining stock: the stock fact), `removed` and `singular_note` (when a removed body gives no condition).
`removed` has one entry for each body of `regions.not_printed`, in the order of the YAML: `label` (`role:name`), `role`, `name`, `file`, `boundary_condition` (`clamp`, `traction` or `none`), `band_mm`, `nodes`, `vertices`,
`facets`, `area_mm2` and `centroid_mm` (of the selected facets; a body that selects nothing has `empty: true` and no `vertices` and no `centroid_mm`), `counts_by_band` (`0`, `0.5x`, `1x`: nodes and facets), `normal_check` (a load body), `note` and `contact` (`area_mm2`,
`selected_area_over_contact`; `area_mm2` is null with an `error` when the contact area cannot be measured: it is a fact, never a reason to stop). The text summary has the line `removed body <label>: ...` for each entry.
An error of the part (a body with no fixed node, a load that no body touches, a singular matrix) has `facts.part_only` (`file`, `removed`, `fixed_selected_nodes`: a list with one `{label, file, nodes}` for each removed fixed body, in the order of the YAML; two bodies can have one label, so the list is by body). The text of a report names a body by its label, and adds the file when another body has the same label.
`buckling_check`: `on`, `source` (`the flag --buckling`, `the gate (buckling.min_factor in the YAML of the run)` or `buckling.check in the YAML of the run`), `modes`, `max_seconds`. `buckling` is the record of section 33,
"In `topopt verify`". `motion` is the record of section 31, "In `topopt verify`". With the check on, `timing_s` has `buckling_s`, with rows `motion_s`; the `levels` block has
`buckling_lowest_load_factor` (for each case) and `motion_tet_value` (for each row) in each row of `rows` and in the relative changes. The check runs on every level.
With the bore checks on, `timing_s` has `bore_s` and `goodman_s`, and the `levels` block has `goodman_n` (for each Goodman row id).
With `--part-only`, `timing_s` has `part_only_contact_s`: the seconds of the contact-area booleans (a measured fact, not a limit; the booleans run once for the run, so every level reports the same time). A run without the option has no such key.
Each entry of `cases`: `weight_of_the_optimizer`, `weight_used` (false), `forces` (force_N, area_mm2, traction_MPa, resultant_N,
`resultant_relative_error`, `load_centre`), `force_on_fixed_nodes_N`, `linear_solve` (`relative_residual`, `backward_error`, `refinement_steps`; for a load case with
no force the two residuals are `null` and there is a `note`),
`equilibrium` (applied and reaction force and moment, `force_relative_residual`, `moment_relative_residual`), `max_displacement_mm`,
`compliance_Nmm` (f.u, as the optimizer), `stiffness_N_per_mm` (|F|^2 / (f.u)), `optimizer_stiffness_N_per_mm`, `stiffness_over_optimizer`, and
`von_mises`: `p50`, `p95`, `p99`, `p99_9` (`_by_volume_MPa`), `peak_qp_MPa`, `peak_vertex_MPa`, `peak_qp_over_p99_9`, the position of each peak,
`percentile_by_volume_MPa`, `top_elements` (with `tet_quality`), `tets_below_quality_cut`, the same values without the tets of quality below 0.05
(`..._excluding_bad_tets`) and `near_regions`. The percentile of the stress is by volume. The peak can move with the mesh at sharp features.

- `load_centre`: `optimizer_center_mm` (the `center` of the force in `run.json`, or None), `p2_traction_centroid_mm`, `distance_mm`,
  `reference_mm` (the area-weighted centroid of the fixed regions), the moments `r x F` of both, and `moment_ratio` = |M_p2| / |M_optimizer|.
- `near_regions`: `distance_mm`, `regions`, `volume_fraction_excluded`, `p99_9_by_volume_MPa_excluding_near_regions`,
  `peak_qp_MPa_excluding_near_regions`, and `top_volume_share_near` (for each region, `any` and `none`: the share by volume of the quadrature points at or above
  the p99.9 of all points that are within `distance_mm` of the region, or inside it). The distance is to a sample of the region surface (spacing at most 0.5 mm).
- `load_band_sensitivity`: `bands` (labels `0` and `2x` of the band; for each: the load regions with `facets`, `area_mm2`, `centroid_mm`, and for each case
  the p99.9, the peaks, the stiffness and their change against the base run; or `empty_load_regions`). Only the load vectors change: the factor is reused.

**Joints and springs (added with K1-A).** `topopt verify` models the `springs` (section 35) and the `joints` (section 38) of the YAML with the physics of the voxel
model (`topopt/verify/supports_p2.py`). `regions.fixed` may be empty. The model of a joint is the bordered matrix
`[[K + Kb, C], [C^T, D_bond + B]]` of section 38 on the P2 dofs, as one CSR matrix with one factor and no Schur step (`K` alone is singular when the YAML has `fixed: []`).

- Regions. A joint or spring region is selected like a load region (the boundary facets of the tet mesh with 3 vertices in the band of the region STL), also when no load case puts
  a force on it. A region with no force is a row of `regions.load` with `role: "joint"` or `"spring"` (a region with a force keeps `role: "load"`), and it is a mask of `near_regions`
  (REVIEW-135 M3); the load-band check keeps its facets at the base band, because its matrix is in the factor, and its `note` says so. The voxel model bonds the exposed faces of the region voxels: a face toward empty space or a keep-out region, and no face toward design, fixed or other load voxels. The
  tet rule does the same (REVIEW-135 M1): of the boundary facets in the band it drops a facet when the point `neighbour_step_mm` along its outward normal lies in the design, a fixed or a load
  region and not in a keep-out region (the label KEEP_OUT wins, as in `voxelize`). `neighbour_step_mm` is 0.5 times the voxel size of the run (`run.BOND_STEP_FACTOR`, the value of
  `DEFAULT_BAND_FACTOR`): the centre of the neighbour voxel of a voxel face. The rule reads the regions of the YAML, not the density of the run, so a face next to a hole that the optimizer cut
  later is not bonded, as in the voxel model. A region with no facet left stops with the fact and the options. The facts of each entry give both sets: `facets` and `area_mm2` (bonded),
  `band_facets` and `band_area_mm2` (the band rule), `facets_toward_design` and `area_toward_design_mm2` (dropped), `voxel_area_mm2` (from `joints.joints[]` and `springs.regions[]` of `run.json`; `null` when
  the run has none) and `area_over_voxel_area`. The two sets of faces are not the same (the tet surface is a marching-cubes surface), so `area_mm2` and `reference_mm` can differ a little. On the pad bar of
  `tests/test_verify_supports.py` the band rule bonded +20 % of the voxel area (216 to 218 mm2 against 180) and the voxel rule bonds 178 to 181 mm2.
  A body of the mesh that has a facet of a joint or spring region counts as held (`mesh.bodies.bodies[].support_facets`, only with a joint or a spring); a body with no fixed node and no such facet
  is still the error of this section. `moment_reference_mm` is the area-weighted centroid of the joint and spring regions when there is no fixed region.
- Spring. The matrix `k int N^T N dA` is added to `K` on the facets of the region (the stiffness per area on each axis). `stiffness` (N/mm, the total) is divided by the area of the tet
  facets; `stiffness_per_area` (N/mm3) is used as it is.
- Joint. The facets are bonded to a rigid body of 6 dofs `q = (t, w)` with the energy `1/2 k_a int |u - R q|^2 dA` and `R = [I, -skew(x - ref)]`. The penalty is `k_a = c E / h` with
  `c = 30` (`joints.BOND_C`) and `h` the voxel size of the run, or `bond_stiffness_per_area`. The reference point is `origin`, else the area centroid of the facets. The beam matrix `B`
  is `joints.beam_stiffness` (the same function as the voxel model). The displacement for the stress is the first block of the solution, and `q = -D^-1 C^T u`.
- Key `supports` of a level (absent when the YAML has no joint and no spring; the keys of a plain `verify.json` do not change): `kind`, `joints` and `springs` (the facts of each entry:
  `region`, `facets`, `area_mm2`, the reference point, the beam, `bond_stiffness_per_area_n_per_mm3`, `c_equivalent`, `bond_share_max`; for a spring `stiffness_n_per_mm`,
  `stiffness_per_area_n_per_mm3`), `bordered_dofs` (`6 m`), `bond` (`c` and its source), `facets_note`, `voxel_size_mm`, `note` and `cases`. `cases.<case>.joints.<region>`: the 6 resultants of the
  bond on the part, `bond_force_N` (3) and `bond_moment_Nmm` (3, about `about_mm`, the reference point), from the nodal forces of the bond; `beam` (`part` is `-B q`, `ground` the reaction at the far point,
  as `joints.joint_wrenches`), `translation_mm`, `rotation_rad`, `bond_wrench_vs_beam_relative` (the nodal wrench against `-B q`: a check of the model, near 0) and `bond_energy_share`.
  `cases.<case>.springs.<region>`: `force_N` and `moment_Nmm` of the spring on the part. The bond resultants are what a bond check of the adhesive needs.
  The text summary (`report.supports_lines`) prints a head line and, for each case, the 6 numbers of each bond (`bond_force_N`, `bond_moment_Nmm`, `about_mm`; the same line as the log) and the `force_N`, `moment_Nmm` of each spring (REVIEW-135 Q5).
- `cases.<case>.equilibrium` has the keys `support_force_N` and `support_moment_Nmm` (the force of the springs and bonds on the part, `-(Kb u + C q)`); the balance of applied load, reactions at the fixed
  nodes and supports is zero to the residual of the solve.
- Memory (REVIEW-135 L3). A joint adds the bordered copy of `Kff` (`supports_p2.bordered_csr`): 12 bytes for each stored entry (a float64 and an int32 index). The
  estimate after meshing gets this term once `Kff` is known, with a note and the key `memory.estimate_bordered_copy_bytes` (only with a joint; `estimate_after_meshing_bytes`
  and `measured_over_estimate` include it), and the guard compares the sum with the limit (`when` is "after meshing, with the bordered copy of K"). A spring adds no border.
  The estimate before meshing (`preflight`) has no such term: `nnz(Kff)` is not known before the mesh.
- Buckling (section 33) runs with the stiffness `S = K + Kb - C D^-1 C^T` (the same operator as the voxel check, `joints.CondensedStiffness`). The geometric stiffness is that of the tets only; the beam
  has no `Kg`, so the load factors are for buckling of the part and not of the beams. The record has `eigen_solver` of section 38 and the key `supports` (`beams_have_geometric_stiffness: false`), and one fact says so.
  The A5 rows (section 31) use the displacement of the tet nodes as before.
- The press-fit stage of the bore checks (section 40) is skipped with a record when the YAML has a joint (`reason: "supports"`, `facts`, `options`; the estimate before meshing says it in the key `pressfit.skipped_with_joints`): it makes its own factors of `K` and does not take the border of the joints. A part held by springs only keeps the stage: the springs are in `K`, so the stage solves the part that they hold (measured on the hook with a spring on the wall plate: relative residual 3e-17). The record then has one more fact: `solve.clamp_reaction_N` is the reaction of the clamps only and does not balance `net_spring_force_N`, because the springs carry the rest. Goodman uses the stress only.
- Not modelled, still refused with the old text: a moment, a remote force, a pressure and a per-axis support. `--part-only` with a removed joint region uses the same region rule; it is not tested.
- Measured on the pad bar of `tests/test_verify_supports.py` (2026-10-24, Apple silicon): a block on a joint beam, tip load: the deflection is 0.99998 of the beam formula; a block on a spring: 1.0005 of `F / (k A)`;
  two joints and `fixed: []` after `topopt run` (12 passes, voxel 1 mm): the tet stiffness is 0.995 of the voxel stiffness (`stiffness_over_optimizer`).

**MCP tools.**

`verify_run(run_dir, estimate_only=True, mesh_size_mm, levels_mm, region_band_mm, allowable_mpa, percentile, solver, max_gb, force, yaml_path,
near_region_mm, load_sensitivity, part_only=False, gate=False)`.

- `gate=true` is `--gate` (added with K1-B): the key `gate` of the result, and `exit_code` 3 when it fails. The estimate and the preflight apply the same checks as the command (a gate with no limit is `{"ok": false, "exit_code": 1}`). The description of the tool names `gate` in one short sentence and points to the card `verify_run:gate` (and one sentence that `allowable_mpa` replaces the YAML stress limits with `gate`). To stay under 4096 characters the description is shorter in these places, and the card holds the detail:
  the run time sentence ("about 10 s on the hook ...", now in the estimate and the card `verify_run`), the detail of `part_only` (now in the card `verify_run:part_only`), and the parentheses of two result keys (`memory`, `files`). The key names and the explanations that K1-B had shortened are back:
  `peak_qp_over_p99_9`, `counts_by_band`, `near_regions` and `load_centre`. Since K1-FU-C they are in the card `verify_run` (`topopt://levers/verify_run`), together with the whole list of result keys and the keys that YAML blocks add.
  The description keeps `ok`, `exit_code` with its values, the key of the p99.9 value (`cases.<case>.von_mises.p99_9_by_volume_MPa`) and one sentence that points to the card. It has 3258 characters (4094 before). No key was removed, and no text changed: the list moved word for word.

- `part_only=true` is `--part-only` (added with P4b-3). The reply of an estimate and of a real start has the block `part_only` (`on`, `file`, `sha256`, `run_record`, `yaml_vs_run`, `notes` (with machining stock: the stock fact), `removed`: `label`, `role`, `name`, `file`; the
  facts of each body are in the result, `verify_status`). Without the option there is no such key; if the run has `part_only.stl`, the reply has `notes`, a list with the one fact line that names `part_only`. A run without the file
  gives `{"ok": false, "error", "exit_code": 1}`. The description of the tool is at the limit of `tests/test_plugin_manifest.py` (4096 characters), so the added sentence is paid by shorter phrases in the other sentences (no fact was removed).

- The buckling check and the A5 rows have no argument. They follow the YAML of the run (`buckling.check`, `limits`), because the child process is `topopt verify`. The estimate result has
  `buckling_check` and the term in `estimates_before_meshing` when the YAML switches the check on. The card `verify_run` names the keys `buckling`, `buckling_check` and `motion` (the description of the tool points to it).
- The bore checks (section 40) have no argument either. The block `bore_checks` of the YAML decides. The card `verify_run` names the keys `bore_checks`, `bore_facts`, `goodman` and, when the block has `press_fit`, `pressfit` (the description of the tool points to it).

- With `estimate_only` (default) it returns the dict of the estimates (memory and time for each size), the solver, the state of the extras and
  the RAM, and meshes nothing.
- With `estimate_only=false` it checks the inputs (the same code as the command: `preflight`) and starts `topopt verify` as a detached child
  (`start_new_session`, output in `<run_dir>.verify.stdout`), then returns at once with `started`, `pid`, `status_file`, `log_file`, the estimates and
  `estimated_seconds_total`. The env var `TOPOPT_MCP_VERIFY_CMD` replaces the child command (a test hook; the word `{run_dir}` is replaced).
- One job at a time: a lock file `.topopt-verify.lock` in the work folder (pid and run folder) and the Popen handle. `verify_run` refuses while a
  verify job is alive or an optimizer run is busy; `run_topopt` refuses while a verify job is alive. A lock of a dead process, of a process whose
  command line has no `topopt` (Linux) or of a job with the state `done` or `error` is removed. A child that ends within 1 s with an error is reported
  in the same call.
- On an error: `{"ok": false, "error", "exit_code": 1 or 2}` and `facts` when the error has them: a memory refusal, an empty region, a linear solver
  that cannot run (`SolverUnavailable`: `requested` and the note of every factor) and an unsolvable part (`UnsolvableMesh`).

`verify_status(run_dir=None, result=True)`: `state` (`starting`, `meshing`, `solving`, `writing`, `done`, `error`, `failed` = the process ended with no
final status, with `log_tail`; `none`), `summary`, `message`, `level`, `levels`, `size_mm`, `elapsed_s`, `estimated_seconds_total`, `process_alive`, `pid`,
`status`, and for `done`: `exit_code`, `result` (the content of `verify.json`), `result_matches_final_stl` (the sha256 of the file `run.verified_file` now against the one
in the result), `verify_json`, `verify_dir`, `files_abs`, `files_rel` and the `_rel` keys. When `verify.json` has `partial` and `coverage` (section 44), `verify_status` has both as keys
of the reply, before `result`, and also with `result=false`. When `partial` is true, `summary` ends with the line `partial: ...` of section 44.3.

**Plain lines (added with P9-17).** "Will it break?" in one plain line for each load case. `topopt.verify.report.plain_lines(res)` reads a verify result and
returns a list of text lines; it reads keys that the result already has (`cases`, `limit`, `no_allowable`, `buckling`, `goodman`) and adds no number, limit or wait.
`verify_status` adds the key `plain` (the same list, with the option name `allowable_mpa`) when the state is `done` and `result` is true and the list is not empty; with
`result=false`, with another state, or with a result that has no load case, the key is absent. If `result_matches_final_stl` is false, the first line says that the lines belong
to an older mesh file. `topopt verify` prints each line after its summary with the prefix `plain: ` (not for `--estimate-only`; the option name is `--allowable-mpa`).
With TC-2 (section 44), line 2 of the text of `topopt verify` is the `partial:` line, and when the result is partial it is also the first `plain:` line.

- With a `limit` block, a line is: `case <name>: <p> % of the volume has von Mises stress at or below <value> MPa (p<p> by volume, the value that topopt compares). The allowable is <a> MPa, given by the user (<option>); topopt has no default. The value is above | below | equal to the allowable, margin <m> (allowable divided by value).`
  When the compared value is below the allowable but the peak at one point is above it, a clause names the peak and says that the check compares the percentile value only. A case with a stress of 0 says that no load reaches the free part in this case and gives no margin.
- With no allowable, a line is `case <name>: ... at or below <value> MPa (p<p> by volume). No allowable was given, so there is no yes or no for this case.` One more line says that typical data sheet values for
  printed PETG and PLA are in `topopt://materials/reference` (section 25.7), that they are not the values of the user's material, and how to give an allowable.
- The last line is for the whole set: the check is the linear static stress of one mesh, one load case at a time, with one isotropic material, and it does not cover fatigue (unless `goodman` is `done`),
  buckling (unless `buckling` is `done`), printing defects or print direction.
- A case name is put on one line (a run of white space becomes one space). A line does not say that a part is safe or will hold: it states two numbers and their ratio.

## 17. Stress constraint and report (added with A2)

This section holds the A2 additions to sections 2, 5, 8 and 9. The other sections stay as they are.
The code is in `topopt/ks_stress.py` (the row), `topopt/stress_report.py` (the report),
`topopt/formulation.py` (`mass_objective`, the stage notes) and `topopt/optimize.py`
(`formulation_from_config`).
`examples/hook/hook_stress.yaml` is a full example.

### YAML keys

```yaml
load_cases:
  - name: pull_off
    stress_limit: 5.0            # optional. float > 0, MPa. The final limit. The optimizer tries to keep the relaxed von Mises stress of this case at or below it.
    allowable_mpa: 40.0          # optional. float > 0, MPa. The allowable of the material. The user or the agent gives it.
    safety_factor: 8.0           # optional. float > 0. Only with allowable_mpa: limit = allowable_mpa / safety_factor. Not with stress_limit.
    allowable_source: "text"     # optional. Free text: where the allowable comes from. The report shows it.
settings:
  objective: compliance          # optional. compliance (default) | mass
  stress_q: 40.0                 # optional. float > 0. KS sharpness.
  stress_power: 0.5              # optional. float in (0, 1]. Relaxation power s of rho^s.
  stress_scale: auto             # optional. auto | float > 0. The KS scale c of the row.
  stress_step_acceptance: true   # optional. true (default) | false. Check each MMA step against the stress rows (see "Step acceptance").
```

- The tool has no default limit. The filament catalog (section 18.8) gives `E` and `density` for `material.filament`; it gives no allowable.
  No material is refused. The allowable comes from the user or the agent.
  Data sheet ranges of printed PETG and PLA are in the MCP resource `topopt://materials/reference` (section 25.7). The tool does not read them.
- A load case has a stress row if it has `stress_limit` or `allowable_mpa`. There are two ways to write the limit:
  1. `allowable_mpa` + `allowable_source` + `safety_factor`: the limit is `allowable_mpa / safety_factor`
     (the factor is 1 when only `allowable_mpa` is given);
  2. a final `stress_limit`, with no `safety_factor`.
  `stress_limit` is final: the optimizer and the report use it as it is. `safety_factor` applies only to `allowable_mpa`.
  A case with `stress_limit` and `allowable_mpa` (no factor) is allowed: the limit is `stress_limit`, and the report uses the
  allowable only for the achieved safety factor against the allowable (`limit_note`).
  `safety_factor` together with `stress_limit` is a loader error. A `safety_factor` with no `allowable_mpa` is a loader error
  that names `allowable_mpa`. Numbers in text form are read as in section 13 (`"5e-3"`).
- `objective: compliance` is the default and its run does not change (bit-equal to the run before A2). With stress rows the run
  has the volume row, the compliance-limit rows and the stress rows.
- `objective: mass`: MMA minimizes the mass of the whole part (g, with the forced-solid voxels). There is no volume row.
  `settings.volume_fraction` is only the start density. The rows are the stress rows and the compliance-limit rows.
  A mass run with no stress limit and no compliance limit is not refused. `topopt check` and the run log say, as a fact,
  that no row holds material, and the run goes on with a volume row (ceiling) at `volume_fraction`.
  Under `objective: mass`, a displacement or alignment row on a probe region does not hold material: the optimizer can remove the
  material between the load and the probe. Add a `compliance_limit` or a stress limit. A `max` or `min` row is also met when the
  region moves the other way. A row on a load region (section 31) holds material. A run with only rows on probe regions gets the
  same fact, with these words, and no volume ceiling; each `max` or `min` row gets a fact of its own.
  `case_combine: max` has no effect in a mass run (a fact in the log).
- The row is a target that the optimizer tries to meet. It is not a guarantee. The run log, `history.jsonl` (`g` of the row) and
  `result/metrics.json` (`stress.cases.<case>.relaxed.met`, `stress.stage_ends`) say whether it was met. A met row is a
  statement about the relaxed measure, not about the printed part.
- The row assumes the filter rule of the demo: the density filter counts the solid voxels (fixed and load regions) as density 1.
  The pipeline filters over the design elements only, and its filter radius is in mm. The two rules give different stress at the
  same radius, so a limit that was tuned in one tool does not carry over to the other without a new run.
- Move limit: the numbers are from measured runs. At 1.2 mm from a uniform start the design
  collapsed without step acceptance with `move_limit` 0.03, and a move limit of 0.01 only slowed the collapse (measured runs).
  With step acceptance the move limit of the settings is the upper limit of the trial step (see "Step acceptance").
- The loader checks the keys. Messages (one line, with the file name, as in section 2):
  `'load_cases[1].stress_limit' must be > 0.0, got -2.0`,
  `'load_cases[1].safety_factor' needs 'load_cases[1].allowable_mpa' (limit = allowable_mpa / safety_factor); or write a final 'load_cases[1].stress_limit' with no safety_factor`,
  `'load_cases[1]' has both safety_factor and stress_limit: stress_limit is the final limit and takes no safety_factor. Write allowable_mpa + allowable_source + safety_factor, or a final stress_limit with no safety_factor`,
  `'settings.objective' must be compliance or mass, got 'stiff'`,
  `'settings.stress_scale' must be auto or a number > 0, got ...`.
- `topopt check` prints "stress limit:" and "objective:" lines and the facts. `--json` and `run.json` `derived` add, for each load case,
  `stress_limit_mpa`, `stress_limit_from`, `allowable_mpa`, `safety_factor`, `allowable_source` (`null` if none), and the key `objective`.
  `--json` adds the list `facts`.
- `topopt check` adds a line "stress rows:" with the part of the time estimate that the stress rows add (adjoint solves, KS
  aggregate, rejected tries of the step acceptance), labelled as an estimate. `--json` has it under `time_estimate.stress`.
  Model: `per_it * (1 + k * n_rows) + n_rows * 0.5e-6 s * n_design (+ a share of per_it for the rejected tries)`; `k` is 0.2 for a direct
  solver and 1.0 for AMG. The model has no fixed cost per pass (older than A2), so a small problem is under-estimated.
- For a run with stress rows `topopt check` also prints a line "time range:". Low is the
  model above. High is the model times `STRESS_RUN_TIME_FACTOR` (1.6 in `topopt/cli.py`), a fixed factor and not a bound. It was chosen from
  three PARDISO runs on Linux x86_64 (hook at 1.2 mm: 731 s and 845 s against a model total of 509 s; example at 2.4 mm: 44 to 62 s against
  32 s), and the rejected tries of the step acceptance made a pass 50 to 55 % longer than a pass with one try. Experiment E1 (section 5.1)
  measured more: 53 finished PARDISO runs with stress rows in 6 problems on one shared Linux host had a median of 2.23 times the model
  total, and 70 % took more than 1.6 times it (`tshirt_hook_stress`, 36 runs: median 2.63 times; a part with two tube joints, 14 runs: median 0.46 times).
  The line and the warning give this E1 fact. `--json` has `time_estimate.range_s` (`[low, high]`) and `time_estimate.range_factor`; both keys
  are absent without a stress row. The warning about the time budget of the user (`settings.stop_rules.time_budget_s`; there is no warning
  without it) compares the high end with the budget, gives the range, and says what the budget does in this YAML (section 11).

### The stress row

The measure is the one of the pipeline (an earlier pipeline of the same author, d43bcf3), on the centre strain of each hex8 voxel of the design space:

```
sigma_e = max(rho_e, 1e-12)^s * D0 * eps_e(u)      s = stress_power, D0 with the full modulus E
vm_e    = sqrt(max(von Mises(sigma_e)^2, 1e-12))   MPa
z_e     = vm_e / limit
S       = zmax + ln(sum exp(q (z_e - zmax))) / q   KS aggregate, max shift, q = stress_q
row     = c * S - 1  <=  0                          one row for each load case with a limit, name "stress:<case>"
```

- `c` is `stress_scale`. With `auto`, `c = zmax / S` at the first design of each beta stage, so the row is the relaxed peak at that
  moment. `S >= zmax`, so `c <= 1`. A number (for example 1) is kept. With `c = 1` the row is a bound: `S <= 1` gives `zmax <= 1`.
  With `auto` and a stage that starts far below the limit, `c` is small and the relaxed peak can go above the limit while the row is met.
  The log has a fact for a stage start with `c < 0.5`, and an end-of-run fact (`stress peak above the limit`) when the relaxed peak is above the limit
  by more than `ks_stress.PEAK_ABOVE_TOL` (the value of `formulation.NOT_MET`, 5e-3 of the limit), whether the row is met or not. With `c = 1` such a row is
  not met, so a met row with such a peak has `c < 1`. `metrics.stress.cases.<case>.relaxed.peak_above_limit` (below) is the same test.
- A `stress_scale` above 1 is accepted. The row `c * S - 1 <= 0` then asks for `S <= 1/c`, so the relaxed peak is held below the limit
  (stricter than the limit). `topopt check` and the run log say so as a fact.
- A `stress_scale` below 1 is accepted too (F4-28). The row asks for `S <= 1/c`, and `S >= zmax`, so the row allows a relaxed peak up to `1/c` times the
  limit and is met there (looser than the limit). `topopt check` (text, and `facts` of `--json`) and the run log say so as a fact, in the form of the fact
  above 1 (`optimize.stress_scale_facts`): the row, what it holds or allows, that the number tightens or loosens the stress limit of the user, a requirement
  (only the user can allow a looser limit; the tool does not change it), and the options (1, which makes the row a bound of the relaxed peak, or `auto`). The
  fact is for a load case with a stress row. Exactly 1 and `auto` have no fact: 1 is the limit as the user wrote it, and `auto` is the default (the run log has
  the stage-start fact when `c` is far below 1). Measured (E2/SS05, `pull_off` of the hook): 0.5 gave mass x0.761 and a relaxed peak of 0.957 MPa against 0.5 MPa
  with the row met (`relaxed.peak_above_limit`, below).
- The limit never changes during a run.
- The KS set is the design voxels. Forced-solid voxels (fixed and load regions) are not in it. The report counts a solid body that has no clamp
  and no load (a load region that no case uses) in the physical peak (see "Peak scope" below).
- The row has the price 1000 (the default of a custom row: linear form, as the volume row) and asks for `xmin` 0.02. `Formulation(xmin=None)` takes the largest `xmin`
  of its rows, else 0.0. A run with a stress row has x floored at 0.02. The compliance run has 0.0 as before.
- The gradient is exact (adjoint, one solve for each stress row, with the solver of the run): `K lam = dS/du`,
  `dS/drho = c * (explicit - stiffness_derivative(lam, u))`, then the chain rule of section 13 through projection and filter.
- Cost: one adjoint solve for each stress row and each iteration, and one more solve at the end for the report.
- API: `topopt.ks_stress.stress_ks_constraint(case, limit, q=40.0, power=0.5, scale="auto", name=None)` returns a `Constraint`.
  `topopt.formulation.mass_objective()` returns the `Objective`. `Response.info` (a dict) goes into the history entry of the row.
  The plain-array functions `relaxed_von_mises`, `ks_aggregate`, `ks_scale` are the ones that a fixture of the pipeline checks.

### Robust mode (A3b)

`settings.robust: eroded` or `wall` (section 22b) with a stress limit on any load case stops at the start of `run`, before the
first solve, and before the delete of an earlier run in the folder (`cli.check_run_inputs`, section 24.1). The stress row reads `point.rho` (the nominal density) in its explicit term and the adjoint term is a slope to
`rho_stiff` (the eroded density), so the gradient is wrong with no error (measured on the merge: relative error 4e-3 to 1e-1
against 1e-5 for a right gradient). The `UserError` and the `topopt check` warning give the facts and the options: robust
off, or no stress limit. Two ways to support it are not built: the stress of the eroded design, and a second solve of the
nominal design for the stress rows (section 22b, "Objectives and rows"). `StepAcceptance.step` already solves the trial
design with `Model.stiffness_density`, so it needs no change when one of them is built. The mass objective and the
compliance limits work in robust mode as before (the mass is on the nominal design, the limits on the eroded design).

### Step acceptance

MMA keeps a convex model of the KS row. When the stress peak moves to other voxels, the model can predict a fall while the row
goes up. The measured effect (reviewer, 1.2 mm from a uniform start, no step acceptance): the design collapsed. At 2.4 mm the
row swung around the limit for the whole run. A run with a stress row therefore checks each MMA step (`topopt.optimize.StepAcceptance`):

1. MMA gives a trial design. One solve at the trial design gives the `g` of each stress row (`Constraint.measure`, no adjoint).
2. Accept the step if each stress row has `g_new <= max(g_old, 0) + 1e-3` (same beta).
3. Else restore the MMA state (a copy of `MmaState`), halve the move limit, and try again, up to 6 tries in a pass.
   After the last try the step is taken, and the pass records it as a fact.
4. After an accepted step the move limit grows by 1.5, up to `settings.move_limit`. The move limit of the next pass is kept in
   `MmaState.move`, and the stage constant `c` of each row in `MmaState.rows` (`{row name: StressRow state}`), so that a resume
   from an `MmaState` continues the same run (KB `pitfalls/resume-differs-from-straight-run`).
5. The solve of the accepted trial design is the solve of the next pass (when beta is the same).

`settings.stress_step_acceptance: false` turns the rule off (for comparisons). The rule acts only on rows with `stage_aware`
and a `measure` (the stress rows; the displacement and alignment rows of section 31 are stage-aware and have no `measure`, so the rule does not check them). A run with no stress row does not use it and is bit-equal to the run before A2 (hook default path:
`compliance_final` 1.3891411615538347 at 1.2 mm). The rule is a heuristic. GCMMA is the standard alternative (it raises the
convexity terms of the rows that the model under-predicts, and has a proof of convergence); it needs a change of the MMA call
and is not part of A2. An accepted first try costs no extra solve (the next pass reuses its solve). Each rejected try costs one more solve and one more MMA step.

### Fields in the run folder

- `history.jsonl` entry for a stress row (in `constraints`): the keys of section 13 and `stress_limit_MPa`, `ks_MPa`,
  `relaxed_peak_MPa`, `c`, `c_changed`, `q`. The values `ks_MPa` and `relaxed_peak_MPa` are relaxed, not physical.
  The record of the objective is `objective` (`name` "mass", `value` in g).
- `history.jsonl` record key `stage` (only with a stress row): at pass 0 and at each pass where beta changes,
  `{iteration, from_beta, to_beta, row, max_g, feasible, notes}`. `max_g` is the largest linear `g` of the last design of the
  old stage. `feasible` is `max_g <= 5e-3`. The schedule goes by iteration, so a stage can end with a row not met. This is
  recorded as a fact, and the run goes on. At pass 0 `from_beta`, `row`, `max_g` and `feasible` are `null`. A row with no result at that design
  (the buckling row after a failed evaluation, section 39) is named as `row`, `feasible` is false, and the note has the key `no_result` (text).
- `history.jsonl` record key `step_acceptance` (not `step`, which is the dashboard step of `status.json`) (only with a stress row and step acceptance): `{tries, accepted, move, move_next, g_old,
  rejected: [{move, g}], g_taken}`. `tries` is the number of trial steps of the pass (1 to 6), `move` the move limit of the last try,
  `rejected` the tries that failed (move limit and the `g` of the stress rows at the trial design), `g_old` the `g` of the rows at the
  start of the pass, `g_taken` (only when all tries failed) the `g` of the step that was taken.
- The run log has the lines "beta stage ... NOT feasible ...", the facts of the rows, for a non-default run `obj=... max_g=... (row)` (`obj` is the physical value of the objective: it does not
  depend on `settings.objective_scale`, section 13),
  one fact line for each pass with a rejected try ("step acceptance, pass N: ... tries rejected ..."), and one summary line
  at the end ("step acceptance (stress rows): N tries rejected in M of K passes ...").
- The stage lines say "all rows met (a stress row is the relaxed measure of the optimizer, not the stress of the part)".
  A mass run whose old stage ended grey (the `grey` fact of the `stage_end` of the last pass of that stage) adds to the same line, before "the schedule goes by iteration count":
  `; the design of the old stage is grey (grayness 0.748, grayness_max 0.1), so "met" holds for this grey design and not for the thresholded part`. The note in `history.jsonl` has the key
  `grey` (`grayness`, `grayness_max`) then. The words before are as they were (F1-3a).
- After the post-process the run log has one fact line for each load case with a stress row:
  `fact: stress <case>: <summary>`. The text is `stress.cases.<case>.summary` of `metrics.json`. It puts the relaxed result and the
  voxel estimates of the part stress together. Example (the 5 MPa form of the committed example, 2.4 mm, `pull_off`; the example now has 1 MPa, see "Load path" below):
  `the optimizer row is met for the relaxed stress (relaxed peak 4.57 MPa, limit 5 MPa, g +0.0005). Voxel estimate of the part stress,
  peak: 6.19 to 8.01 MPa (thresholded design 8.01, grey design 6.19); limit 5 MPa. Both voxel estimates are above the limit (the limit is
  0.81 times the grey peak; 77 of 171 voxels are above 5 MPa in the grey design). "Met" is about the relaxed measure, not about the part.
  ... options: a lower stress_limit, a finer voxel size, or an independent check of final.stl ...`
- `run.json` key `stress` (only with a stress row): `{q, power, scale, step_acceptance, material: {E, nu, density}, cases: [{name,
  stress_limit_MPa, limit_from, allowable_mpa, allowable_source, safety_factor, explicit_stress_limit_MPa}]}`.

### `result/metrics.json` key `stress`

Only for a run with a stress row. On an error the section is `{"error": ..., "note": ...}` and the post-process goes on, except a resource error
(a memory error, a failed thread start, a native library that cannot be mapped): the post step then stops with `PostResourceError` (section 19, "Resource errors"; #449).

```
stress.note, voxel_size_mm, element, parameters {q, relaxation_power, ks_scale, step_acceptance}, accuracy_data
stress.step_acceptance  {passes, tries_rejected, passes_with_a_rejected_try, passes_that_took_a_step_after_all_tries_were_rejected, smallest_move_limit} | null
stress.stage_ends       [{pass, beta, row, g, feasible}]   the largest g at the last pass of each beta stage, and of the run
stress.input_check      {compared_with_run_json, not_compared, changed} | null
stress.voxel_estimates  {physical, physical_thresholded (labels), thresholded_solve_s, note}
stress.load_paths      {rule, thresholded_design_bodies, thresholded_design_bodies_with_a_fixed_region, regions {<load region>: {used_by,
                        voxels, thresholded_design {connected_to_fixed, bodies_with_the_region}, final_stl {connected_to_fixed,
                        touches_a_body, bodies_with_the_region} | absent}}, final_stl {bodies, bodies_with_a_fixed_region} | {error} | null,
                        final_stl_rule}   or {error}
stress.cases.<case>:
  stress_limit_MPa, limit_from, allowable_mpa, allowable_source, safety_factor, limit_note (only if both keys are given)
  summary   text: the relaxed result and the voxel estimates of the part stress together (the same text as the run log fact)
  load_path {regions {<load region of the case>: {thresholded_design, final_stl (true | false | null)}}, all_connected, not_connected [names]}
  relaxed   {label "relaxed, not physical", ks_MPa, peak_MPa, row_value, row_g, met, met_when_g_at_or_below, met_means, peak_above_limit,
             peak_above_limit_tol, peak_above_limit_means, c, q, iteration}   from the last pass
  physical  {label, design (label of the grey design), peak_MPa, peak_over_limit, p99_9_by_volume_MPa, voxels, p99_9_equals_peak,
             p99_9_rank_from_top, top_0_1_percent_voxels, p99_9_note (if equal), peak_incl_forced_solid_MPa, voxels_above_limit,
             volume_above_limit_mm3, above_limit_note, solid_voxels_without_clamp_or_load (only if above 0)}
            the grey design: one solve with the SIMP stiffness of the last snapshot; stress = D0 * strain with the full E;
            voxels with rho >= 0.5 in the peak scope (below); p99.9 is step-wise by volume (the rule of the P2 check of the pipeline)
  physical_thresholded  the same keys as `physical`, for the thresholded design: the same snapshot with rho >= 0.5 solid and the rest
            void (one more factor and solve for all cases). The voxels are the same ones. On an error: {error, label}
  voxel_peak_range_MPa  {low, high, note}   the two peaks of the voxel estimate (grey and thresholded design)
  achieved_safety_factor {against_limit {peak, p99_9}, against_allowable {peak, p99_9} | null, text}
            each entry: {value, range_estimate [low, high] | null, status, member_gate | note}
  member_check {voxels, p10_voxels, median_voxels, min_needed, met}   estimate of the voxels through the member at the top 1 % stress voxels
  verdict   {peak, p99_9}   each {status, pass (null), error_band_pct}
  independent_check {file "verify/verify.json", field, found, p2_p99_9_by_volume_MPa, voxel_p99_9_by_volume_MPa, p2_over_voxel, p2_over_limit, verified_file, note}
            and, only when found and verify.json has `partial` and `coverage` (TC-2, section 44): verify_partial, verify_coverage
  input_changed {fact, differences}   only when the forces or the material of the YAML differ from run.json: then `physical`,
            `achieved_safety_factor`, `member_check` and `verdict` are null for that case
```

- The physical numbers are voxel estimates. The relaxed numbers and the physical numbers are never mixed.
- Peak scope (`topopt.stress_report.peak_scope`): the peak, p99.9, `voxels`, `voxels_above_limit` and the member check count the design
  voxels with rho >= 0.5 and the solid voxels that carry no clamp and no load. Left out: the FIXED voxels, and the voxels of a load region
  that a load case uses (the clamp and the load are spread over whole voxels there, so the stress is not a measure of the part). A load
  region that no load case uses is a kept-solid body without a load (section 2: label LOAD, density 1, no force). Its stress is real, so
  it counts, and the label of the numbers says how many such voxels are in the scope
  (`... and N solid voxels that carry no clamp and no load`; the key `solid_voxels_without_clamp_or_load`). `peak_incl_forced_solid_MPa`
  adds all left-out voxels as before. With no such body the numbers are the same as before this rule.
- Load path (`topopt.stress_report.load_path_facts`, `metrics.load_paths` in every run (I6, section 5), `stress.load_paths` (the same dict), `stress.cases.<case>.load_path`; the same rule is made at the end of each beta stage, section 13): the relaxed rows can be
  met by a design that has no material between the load and the supports. The members that carry the load can be one voxel thin: the
  relaxed stress of such a member is low, the thresholded design (rho >= 0.5) can still join the load and the support through them, and the
  smoothed mesh drops them. So the report gives two facts for each load region, and says if a region is not connected:
  - `thresholded_design`: the solid voxels (design voxels with rho >= 0.5, all fixed voxels, all load voxels) are 6-connected components
    (two voxels are joined when they share a face). The region is connected when one component holds a voxel of the region and a voxel of
    a fixed region.
  - `final_stl` (only when `result/final.stl` exists): the bodies of the mesh (triangles joined by shared vertices). The region is connected
    when one body contains the centre of a voxel of the region and the centre of a fixed voxel (at most 300 centres of each are tested).
    The centres are tested 8 at a time (`topopt.post.CONTAINS_CHUNK`), and the test of a body stops at the first group that has a centre
    inside. The facts are the same as for one call with all centres. The memory is lower: on a body of 206,550 faces the check rose by
    about 0.2 GiB, and one call with 300 centres rose by about 6 GiB (measured with the trimesh `ray_triangle` backend, no embree).
    `final_stl: {error}` when the file cannot be read or has more than 200 bodies. A report error never stops the post-process.
  - `case.load_path.not_connected` lists the regions of the case that fail one of the two tests. Then `summary` says so as a fact, for
    example: "the optimizer row is met for the relaxed stress (...). But the thresholded part has no material between load region 'tip'
    and the fixed regions; this is not a part that carries the load. options: a larger settings.filter_radius (thicker members),
    settings.objective compliance with a volume_fraction and the stress limits as rows (the volume row keeps material between the load and
    the supports), a finer voxel_size, or a lower stress_limit (all of these change the problem or the cost: the tool does not decide)."
    When the thresholded design is connected and `final.stl` is not, the sentence says "the thresholded design joins them, the smoothed
    mesh does not". The report does not change the result, the exit code or the optimizer.
  - A joined region is a necessary condition. It does not say how stiff or strong the joint is. Measured (2.4 mm): the hook with `pull_off`
    1 MPa has one `final.stl` body that joins the tip to the plate through a thin neck; `topopt verify` gives a stiffness of 1 N/mm
    (the voxel model: 517 N/mm) and a p99.9 of 144 MPa. With 0.5 MPa the check gives 667 N/mm. The independent check
    (`independent_check`, section 16) is the test of the joint.
- `relaxed.met` is true when the row `g` of the last pass is at or below 5e-3 (the `NOT_MET` threshold of section 13). `stage_ends` has the
  same test for the end of each beta stage. The optimizer tries to meet the row. The file says whether it did. `relaxed.met_means` says what
  "met" means: the relaxed KS row of the optimizer is at or below the limit. It is not a statement about the part.
- `relaxed.peak_above_limit` (F4-34) is true when `peak_MPa` is above `stress_limit_MPa` by more than `peak_above_limit_tol` of the limit
  (`ks_stress.PEAK_ABOVE_TOL`, equal to `formulation.NOT_MET`): the one comparison (`ks_stress.peak_above_limit`) that the run log line
  `stress peak above the limit` makes, so the flag and the line cannot disagree. It does not look at `met`: with the KS scale `c` below 1 the row
  can be met with the relaxed peak above the limit (measured: `stress_scale` 0.5, peak 0.957 MPa, limit 0.5 MPa, `met` true). It is null for a run whose
  history has no `stress_limit_MPa` in the row. The levers block lists it (41.7).
- The peak of a stress design sits at grey voxels (rho near 0.5). The relaxed row discounts them by `rho^0.5`. The grey estimate gives them
  the full E on the SIMP strain, and the thresholded estimate removes the void ones. Measured on the hook (R1 review): the two peaks differ by
  -34 % to +29 % (2.4 mm: 6.19 grey and 8.01 thresholded; 1.2 mm: 6.18 grey and 4.08 thresholded against a limit of 5 MPa), and can be on
  different sides of the limit. `physical.peak_over_limit` is the grey peak over the limit, `physical_thresholded.peak_over_limit` the other.
  The `summary` gives both peaks and says when they are on different sides.
- p99.9 and the peak: when the top 0.1 % of the volume is fewer than 5 voxels (fewer than 5000 design voxels), p99.9 rests on the top 1 to 4
  voxels. Below 1000 voxels it is the peak. The report says "p99.9 equals the peak at this voxel count" with the voxel count. From
  1000 voxels the rank is 2 or more, so the text adds "(p99.9 is the voxel at rank k from the top: X MPa; peak Y MPa)".
- `achieved_safety_factor`:
  - p99.9: `value` is reference / p99.9. `range_estimate` is `[reference * (1 - 0.59) / p99.9, reference * (1 + 0.57) / p99.9]`, that is
    0.41 to 1.57 times `reference / p99.9`: the factor for a true value between `p99.9 / (1 + 0.57)` and `p99.9 / (1 - 0.59)`. The band is
    the union of the bench and 5 public parts (items under "Verdict rule"). It is an estimate. The `status` gives the band, the source of
    each end (the set, and the row or cell that sets it), the data base (bench: 3 shapes, 1 real part; 5 public parts, 51 cells), "no verdict",
    and that the band is the largest error measured and not a bound for other parts; the public-part fact is in `verdict.p99_9.status`, said
    once for each case. `member_gate` says if the high-stress members are at least about 3.5 voxels thick, and that on public parts this gate
    did not keep the error inside the bench band. The `text` of the case gives the band and the source of each end once.
  - peak: `value` with the status "no accuracy band". The voxel peak was below the reference in every measured case, by 5 % to 87 %: the
    lowest value, -87.14 %, is the ladle `full_scoop` (run type MF, variant S2, voxel 3.25 mm) of the 5 public parts, and the highest,
    -4.82 %, is the beam with 16 voxels through the thickness of the bench. So the true factor can be lower. The same holds for a p99.9
    that equals the peak.
- Verdict rule: a statistic gets a pass or fail only if its entry in `bench/stress_accuracy.json` `verdict_rule` has `verdict: true`
  (`bench/stress_accuracy.py` makes the file; `topopt.stress_report.ACCURACY` is a copy of it). **At this time no statistic has a verdict.**
  `pass` is always null, and `status` gives the measured error range and the reason.
  - Band (F1-8c): the band of an entry is the union of two sets of data, the 11 rows of the bench
    (a beam, a plate with a hole, the hook against P2: `bench/stress_accuracy.json`) and the 51 cells of 5 public parts
    (`bench/stress_public_parts.json`). `under_pct` and `over_pct` are the largest error on each side, rounded up to whole percent
    (`math.ceil`). `measured_min_pct` and `measured_max_pct` are the union, not rounded. The entry keeps the two sets apart in `sources`:
    `bench` and `public` each have `data`, `under_pct`, `over_pct`, `measured_min_pct`, `measured_min_from`, `measured_max_pct` and
    `measured_max_from` (the row or cell that sets the end; `public` also has `parts` and `cells`), and `lower_end` and `upper_end` say which
    set ("bench" or "public") sets that end of the union. `data_base` has the counts of the union (`rows`,
    `rows_where_p99_9_is_a_true_percentile`, `rows_where_p99_9_equals_the_peak`) and, apart, `bench` (shapes, real parts, rows) and `public`
    (parts, cells, `cells_where_p99_9_equals_the_peak`). `verdict.<stat>.error_band_pct` is `{measured_min_pct, measured_max_pct, data,
    sources, data_base}`. Every text that gives a band or a range names the source of each end. The band is the largest error measured,
    not a bound for other parts.
  - `p99_9`: -59 % to +57 % of the reference. Lower end -59 % (measured -58.32 %): the 5 public parts, the hook, `pull_off`, run type MS,
    voxel 2.4 mm. Upper end +57 % (measured +56.91 %): the 5 public parts, the phone stand, `poke`, run type MS, voxel 2.45 mm. The bench
    alone gave -54 % to +13 %: lower end -53.32 % (the hook at 1.2 mm, `pull_off`, against P2), upper end +12.95 % (the plate with a hole, 8
    voxels across the hole, gross scaling of the reference). Each end is set by one row or cell, with no margin. The member gate does not
    predict the error: the hook (1.2 mm) passes the gate and has -53 %, the beam at 4 voxels has -28 %. The data base is 62 rows and
    cells; 35 of them (4 of the 11 bench rows, 31 of the 51 public cells) have fewer than 5000 voxels, so their p99.9 is the peak.
  - Public parts (F1-8, Refs #129; data `bench/stress_public_parts.json`, made by `bench/stress_public_parts.py`): on 5 public parts (the
    hook, the bracket, the ladle, a shelf bracket and a phone stand; 51 cells) the error of the voxel p99.9 against the P2 p99.9 of
    `topopt verify` (voxel / P2 - 1) was -58 % to +57 %, in both directions. The voxel value was above P2 in 23 cells, mostly grey
    mass-objective designs (20 of the 23), and up to 2.4 times below P2 on a coarse part with thin members (the hook, `pull_off`, at its
    example voxel size 2.4 mm: about 1.25 voxels across the thinnest member and fewer than 1400 voxels in the scope). 15 of the 51 cells
    were outside the bench band (4 below it, 11 above it; the band of the report contains all of them by construction). The member gate did
    not select the cells inside the bench band: 18 cells met it (P2 / voxel 0.64 to 1.40), and 6 of them were above +13 %. The voxel peak
    was below the P2 peak in all 51 cells. One host (Linux x86_64), main 74a1e46, 2026-10-25; the run folders are not in the repository.
    The summary in the file counts against the bench band alone (`sources.bench`; `python bench/stress_public_parts.py --resummarize`
    makes it again). `ACCURACY["p99_9"]["reason"]` quotes this fact once, and `["valid_when"]`, the `status` and `text` of
    `achieved_safety_factor`, the member gate text and `stress.note` point to `verdict.p99_9.status`. For the stress of the part, run `topopt verify`.
  - `peak`: -88 % to 0 % of the reference. Lower end -88 % (measured -87.14 %): the 5 public parts, the ladle, `full_scoop`, run type MF,
    variant S2, voxel 3.25 mm. Upper end 0 % (measured -4.82 %): the bench, the beam with 16 voxels through the thickness. The voxel peak
    was below the reference in every measured case. The reference of the public cells is the P2 peak at the quadrature points, and the P2
    peak depends on the mesh of `topopt verify`. On public parts 3 of the 18 cells that met the member gate had a voxel peak more than 72 %
    below the P2 peak (72 % is the lower end of the bench band). The sign for other shapes is not known, and the peak of a corner or a load
    point depends on the voxel size.
  - The data file splits the hook comparison into its effects (`cross_check.split`: grey voxels, thresholded design, the load patch
    left out, the load model like for like). For `pull_off` about 12 points of the -53 % come from the load model (surface traction
    in P2, nodal spread in the voxel model); about -41 % is a voxel error of this part (hex8 at about 4 voxels through the member,
    stair steps). The grey voxels and the load patch do not explain it.
- `independent_check`: if `<run>/verify/verify.json` (B2, `topopt verify`) has `cases.<case>.von_mises.p99_9_by_volume_MPa`,
  the report shows it beside the voxel value (`p2_over_voxel`) and beside the stress limit of the case (`p2_over_limit`, F4-29: the stress of the part against the
  limit, an estimate with no verdict). `topopt.stress_report.update_metrics(run_dir)` writes the section again after B2 made the file.
- "Met" for a stress row (F4-29). The row is the relaxed measure of the optimizer, not the stress of the part, and every text that shows "met" says so: `relaxed.met_means`;
  the sentence ` "Met" is about the relaxed measure, not about the part.` in the `summary` of every case that has a relaxed row (met or not; it was there only for a met row with
  a voxel estimate above the limit); the stage line of the run log; the `detail` of a row that is not met; the `says` of the levers entries. The `summary` (and the run log fact with the
  same text) ends with the stress of the part when `independent_check.found` is true: `The stress of the part from the independent check: P2 p99.9 by volume X MPa, R times the limit L MPa
  (tets of <verified_file>, quadratic elements; source verify/verify.json, <field>).`; when it is false, with one option: `run verify for the stress of the part (...): verify/verify.json has no P2 value for
  this case` (`options: a lower stress_limit, a finer voxel size, or run verify ...` for a met row with a voxel estimate above the limit). The post step writes `metrics.json` before `topopt verify` runs,
  so the file keeps the option. When `independent_check.verify_partial` is true (TC-2, section 44), the `summary` has one more sentence after the P2 value: `That verify result is partial: <the line of section 44.3>.`
  A reader of a finished run reads `verify/verify.json` again (`stress_report.refresh_from_verify`, in memory, no file is written): the MCP tool `run_result` (its `metrics`)
