  * The device. The three kernels run after the V-cycle in each iteration, between the last Chebyshev launch and `p_update`: `z <- z - Z E^-1 (AZ)^T z`, so that `z` is
    A-orthogonal to `Z`; they make the two partial dots of `cheb_dot` again for the projected `z`, so the other launches are unchanged. `GpuMG.pcg` makes the
    coarse correction around the device loop, in 64-bit: `a = E^-1 Z^T b`, the device solves `b - A Z a`, and the result is `x + Z a`. `solve_refined` is unchanged. The
    projection is exact for any `Z` of full column rank: a poor `Z` costs iterations and never gives a wrong answer, and a solve is accepted only by the 64-bit residual
    of the host, as before. The program has the kernels only for case C with joints (`kernels.source(..., defl_dk=DK)` appends them after all other kernels;
    `DK` is the number of columns of `Z`, a macro). They use no 64-bit type and no feature that the other kernels do not use.
  * Buffers. `(2 DK n3 + DK^2 + nr DK G + nr DK)` values of 4 bytes, with `n3` the dofs of level 0 and `G` the groups of the dot kernels: for one body, 12 vectors of the dofs
    (48 bytes for each dof; it grows in a straight line with `DK`). The host keeps `Z` and `AZ` in 64-bit and in 32-bit (24 bytes for each dof and each column), and, for each harmonic column, the
    prescribed motion and the extension in 64-bit (16 bytes for each dof): `host_bytes = DK n3 24 + 2 H n3 8 + DK^2 4` with `H` the harmonic columns (624 bytes for each dof for the 18 columns of one body with two joints). For
    a part with a joint, the gpu-mg memory model of `check` counts the columns in the loop phase of case C (1,000 bytes for each free dof; see "Memory model of `check`" below). Estimate against the measured peak,
    for the two YAMLs of the two-joint part (pocl, one Linux x86_64 host, revision `133e5a1`; `ru_maxrss` of `topopt run`, one run each): the estimate of `check` before F4-36 (610 MB + 1,000 bytes for each free dof) was 0.69 GB at 2.2 mm (75,489 free dofs) and 1.21 GB at 1.0 mm (600,771 free dofs). The measured
    peak in case C is 2.5 GB (2,379 MiB) and 3.5 GB (3,311 MiB); the 1.0 mm run was cut by a timeout of 1,500 s after the first optimizer pass, so its figure is the peak up to the cut. The measured peak in case B (no column; the run ended) is 2.6 GB and 3.7 GB.
    The columns (`Z` and `AZ`; `run.log` prints MB as 2^20 bytes: 10.4 MB on the device and 44.9 MB on the host at 2.2 mm, 82.5 MB and 357.5 MB at 1.0 mm) are 0.06 GB and 0.46 GB, that is 3 and 20 percent of the gap of case C (1.8 GB and 2.3 GB).
    F4-36 measured public parts on pocl (revision `74a1e46`) to find the rest of the gap: the voxels of the grid and the joints are small terms (220 bytes for each grid voxel in the mesh step; the columns are 0.95 to 0.97 kB for each free dof in the loop phase of case C and nothing in case B); the larger causes are
    that the fit of the first model was of a time before the SDF mesh step, and that the mesh step of the post-process (not the optimizer loop) sets the peak of most runs: it grows with the surface of the part (free dofs to the power 2/3) and with the layout of the regions. The new model gives 10.3 GB (4.6 GB for the layout of the hook example) at 1.0 mm for 600,771 free dofs and 6.45 million grid voxels, and at 2.2 mm 2.61 GB for any grid size
    (2.75 GB for about 0.61 million voxels, the count of the 1.0 mm grid divided by 2.2^3) against the measured 2.6 GB; the number of the hook example at 2.2 mm (1.2 to 1.3 GB) is below that peak. The gap of the two-joint part at 2.2 mm is not explained by the free dofs, the grid or the joints; the layout of its regions is not known to this study.
    The run says the real figures of the columns (below).
  * When the device cannot run it. The solve runs without the deflation (the code path of before P2d), and the reason is a fact in `run.log`, in
    `GpuSolver.facts()["deflation"]` (`{"on": false, "why": ...}`), in the record and in the text of a failed solve. The reasons: the program does not build with the kernels
    (it is built again without them); the device allows a work-group size for `defl_apply` that is smaller than the node kernels use; a buffer is larger than the
    largest buffer of the device or cannot be made; all dofs of the part are fixed (`Z` has no column). A design whose `E` is not finite or not positive definite in
    64-bit, or whose extension gave a value that is not finite, runs without the deflation, and the next design tries again. A device error in the V-cycle of the extension is the
    usual device error (a `UserError` with the device, the case and the step: "ran the V-cycle for the harmonic columns of the deflation").
  * Facts. `GpuSolver.facts()["deflation"]` is None (case B, or no joints) or `{on, bodies, columns (= DK), rigid_columns, harmonic_columns, columns_per_body, columns_per_patch, patches,
    active_columns (= k of the last design), topology_s, design_s, work_group, device_bytes, host_bytes, extension_tol, extension, extension_total}`. `extension` is the extension of the last design: `{columns,
    warm, tol, iterations (PCG iterations over all blocks and chunks), iterations_per_block, chunks, rel_max (the largest final relative residual), converged (every column at the tolerance), stopped (one of
    "tol", "stagnation", "breakdown" for each block), seconds}`; `extension_total` has the sums over the designs `{designs, warm, iterations, seconds, above_tol, rel_max}`. The record of a design in
    `gpu_mg.jsonl` has `deflation` (`{on, bodies, columns, rigid_columns, harmonic_columns, active_columns, extension}`, or `{on: false, why}`) and, in `setup_parts_s`, `defl_ext` (the seconds of the extension), `defl`
    (the host seconds of the basis, `AZ` and `E`) and `defl_upload` (the copy of `Z`, `AZ` and `E^-1` to the device); `setup_s` and `upload_s` include them. `run.log` has
    `gpu-mg: deflation of the rigid modes in the inner PCG is on (case C with joints, a method setting): N bodies, K rigid mode column(s) [...] and H harmonic column(s) [...] of P bonded patch(es) (...); K+H columns in all; ...;
    the device holds Y MB for Z and AZ, the host W MB ...` after the line of the support terms; the line of the first design `gpu-mg: deflation of the first design: extension of H harmonic column(s) of P bonded
    patch(es), cold start, N PCG iterations in C chunk(s) of up to M (X s), largest relative residual R against T; host part ...`; one line `gpu-mg: the extension of the harmonic columns stopped above its tolerance in the design
    of optimizer iteration I: ...` the first time that a design does it (once for a run); and, at the end of the run, `gpu-mg: extension of the harmonic columns over the run: D design(s), W warm, N PCG iterations, X s,
    A above the tolerance T, largest final relative residual R`. When it is off: `... is off (case C with joints): <reason>`, or, for one design, `gpu-mg: deflation of the rigid modes and patches is off for this
    design (optimizer iteration I): <reason>. The inner PCG of this design runs as before; the next design tries the deflation again`. A failed solve says `the inner PCG deflated the rigid modes (N bodies, K columns) and H harmonic
    columns of P bonded patch(es) (the patch motions extended into the part) and the host solved them in FP64` (with `, the extension stopped above its tolerance` when it did) or `the deflation of the rigid modes was not used: <reason>`.

**Per-axis supports (P2c).** `gpu-mg` takes a `fixed` entry with `axes` (a roller or a slider, section 26.2), alone or with springs and joints. The hierarchy keeps
one Dirichlet flag for each dof on every level (`Level.fix`, shape `(nn, 3)`), and the device mask has bit 0, 1 and 2 for x, y and z: every kernel (the operator,
the smoother, the restriction, the prolongation) cuts each dof alone, and the coarsest dense inverse is zero on each fixed dof. Level 0 flags exactly the dofs of
`Problem.fixed_dofs`; a full clamp flags all 3 dofs of its nodes, as before, and a fixed dof on a node that no active element uses is skipped. A dof of a coarse node
is flagged when the same dof of any fine node within one fine step of it (the 27 positions around twice its coordinates) is flagged. The rule is for each dof
because the transfer acts on each dof alone: a fine dof is zero when the same dof of every parent is zero, so every level keeps the supports of the fine level and
the six rigid-body modes stay blocked on every level (a test checks this for each level). Measured on pocl (the cantilever block of `tests/test_gpu_mg_axes.py`, 9,507
free dofs for the roller case: the wall x, the floor y and the floor z, each with one axis; 8,121 for the slider case: the wall y and z, a stop x), case B, PCG iterations
executed, `gpu_tol` 1e-9, one random design: the rule above 26 (roller) and 29 (slider), the same geometry with full clamps 26 and 29; a rule for each node (all 3 dofs
of a coarse node next to a roller) 84 and 80, and at a voxel size of 0.5 mm (70,194 and 59,022 free dofs, 4 levels) 167 and 159 against 28 and 31, so that rule rises with the grid.
A rule that flags a coarse dof only when all its neighbours have it leaves the coarse matrix singular on both cases (the residual stays above 1); a rule that copies the
flag of the coincident fine node gives a NaN on the roller case and 37 iterations (4 levels) on the slider case. Case C (32-bit float on the device; on pocl it is the emulation of the device without 64-bit float): converged in 4 refinement
steps with at most 9 (roller) and 11 (slider) PCG iterations in a step, the full clamps 10. A line or a point roller that the coarse rule spreads to
its coarse neighbours needs about the count of the same support as a full clamp (P2c review probe, a half beam, case B: line 40 vs 43, point 35 vs 37 at 1.0 mm;
39 vs 37 at 0.5 mm), and the count does not grow with the grid.
The reactions (`reaction_facts`) come from the displacement as for the other solvers: a support counts only the force on its fixed dofs, so the force on the dofs of one
axis balances the load along that axis.

**What it does not do.** The voxel guards (`max_grid_voxels`, `max_active_voxels`)
keep their meaning and their default. A hook run at 0.8 mm or finer needs `max_active_voxels` raised in the YAML.
**`topopt check`** with `gpu-mg`: the memory line is the gpu-mg model (the largest of three phases of the peak memory of
`topopt run`, measured on pocl with the device buffers in host memory, see "Memory model of `check`" below; `memory_estimate.model` is `"gpu-mg"` and
`memory_estimate.cholesky_bytes` has the Cholesky number for comparison), and the warning "the memory estimate is ...
above the RAM" uses that number (`memory_estimate.bytes`). The time line is the time model of the paragraph below: `time_estimate.model` is `"gpu-mg"`,
`total_s` and `s_per_iteration` are its mid number, `low_s` and `high_s` its band, `basis` is `calibration`, `table`,
`reference` or `none`, `note` says where the constants come from, and `time_estimate.gpu_mg` has the whole result (the keys of
`GpuEstimate.as_dict()`: `iterations_per_block` with `low`, `mid`, `high`, `contrast_lgk`, `gpu_tol`, `gpu_tol_factor`, `blocks`,
`columns_per_launch`, `other_gpu_runs`, `device`, `case`, `n_cases`, `penal`, `volume_fraction`, `basis`, `label`, `constants`,
`assumptions`). `check` prints the lines `memory model:`, `time model:` and `time constants:`. The first line,
`time estimate:`, ends with the basis in a few words: `(constants of this machine)` for `calibration`, `(Intel Arc iGPU constants)` for
`table` and `(reference: Intel Arc iGPU constants)` for `reference`; for `none` it is the line with no seconds (see below). The same
words are `time_estimate.gpu_mg.label` and `derived.time_model.label`. `derived.time_model` (section 5, `run.json` and `check_problem`;
only for `gpu-mg`) is `{model, basis, label, device, case, penal, volume_fraction, lgK, gpu_tol, n_cases, constants_source}`: it says
whose constants the seconds of `derived.time_estimate_s` are and which inputs the band used (`lgK` is null without a `penal`). The line that gives the model starts `gpu-mg models: ` and is one entry of `warnings` (the text is not repeated); `topopt check` prints it as a fact line, without the prefix `warning: ` (gpu-mg is the main mode, so the line is no warning). The time warning of
`check` ("the gpu-mg time estimate is X s (band a to b s), above your time budget of B s (settings.stop_rules.time_budget_s)") stays, with the words of section 11 about what the budget does;
it is given only when the YAML sets that budget.
`cli.backend_estimates(..., gpu=TimeInputs)` has a `gpu-mg` entry with the same numbers (`low_s`, `high_s`, `gpu_mg`); the JSON key
`backends` still lists the three direct solvers, each with its own `time_estimate`. `check` loads the OpenCL drivers of the
machine to list the devices when pyopencl is installed (no context is made).

**Memory model of `check` (F4-36; `topopt/gpu_mg/check.py`, `estimate_memory`).** The peak resident memory of a whole `topopt run` with `gpu-mg` is the largest of three phases (the build phase and the filter terms came with P9-4d, issue #329).
The first model (2026-10-20: 610 MB + 1,000 bytes for each free dof, 15 hook runs) measured the optimizer loop only; on main the post-process mesh step (`mesh_method` `sdf`,
`snap_into_regions`, whose `trimesh` closest-point queries made one array for all pairs of a vertex and a nearby face) is the larger phase for most runs.
The mesh terms below were fitted before #429. Since #429 the queries of the mesh step take 8,192 points at a time (`smooth_sdf._query`), so the
mesh phase of a mesh with many vertices is lower than the fit (on a generated lattice of 6.2 million fine voxels the step peaked at 3.1 GB instead
of 4.3 GB). The model is then high, not low.

```
build = 860 MB + F_build                         (the filter is set up before the model; F_build = `filter_build_peak_bytes`)
loop  = 860 MB + 730 B * N + F_held              (+ 1,000 B * N in case C when the part has a joint: the columns of the deflation)
mesh  = 500 MB + 220 B * V + 3.2 * 370,000 B * N^(2/3)
bytes         = max(build, loop, mesh)           typical_bytes = max(build, loop, 500 MB + 220 B * V + 370,000 B * N^(2/3))
```

`F_held` and `F_build` are `filter_held_bytes` and `filter_build_peak_bytes` of `memory_estimate` (`members.filter_size`: the same number as the CPU model of
`cli.estimate_memory_bytes`, 56 B for each cell of the padded FFT grid of the filter plus 24 B for each design voxel, #333; section 22a); they are 0 when the filter is not known. The runs that gave the constants of `loop` had a small filter, so the
sum can count a small filter part twice (the number can be higher than a measured peak). Since #333 `F_build` equals `F_held`, so the build phase is never above the loop phase. The mesh phase has no filter term.
A part with a small filter keeps its number when the mesh phase sets the peak (the hook example). Before P9-4d `bytes` had no filter term: a part of 529,287 free dofs with a filter matrix that held 6.53 GiB and needed 14.0 GiB at its build got
a number below the RAM check, and the filter was only in the side keys. Before #333 the run built that sparse matrix (28 B held and 60 B at the build for each entry), and a large radius in voxels could set the peak.

`N` is the free dofs, `V` the voxels of the grid (`grid.voxels` of `check`), and the joint count is `len(extended.joints)`; `check` has all of them, and no config key is new. The names are
`GPU_MG_BASE_BYTES`, `GPU_MG_BYTES_PER_DOF`, `GPU_MG_JOINT_BYTES_PER_DOF`, `GPU_MG_MESH_BASE_BYTES`, `GPU_MG_MESH_BYTES_PER_DOF23`, `GPU_MG_MESH_BYTES_PER_GRID_VOXEL` and `GPU_MG_LAYOUT_FACTOR`
(`tests/test_gpu_mg_device.py` pins them; `tests/test_gpu_mg_memory.py` has the table of the measured peaks). The mesh vertices follow `N^(2/3)` (the surface of the part); the hook alone fits `387 MB + 0.365 MB * N^(2/3)` within 3 percent
over 16,434 to 905,010 free dofs. The layout factor 3.2 is a cover for the region shapes: a keep-out shape whose bounding box covers the whole part, or a small one with 320 triangles, gave a mesh phase up to 2.4 times
that of the plain hook at the same `N` and `V` (its surface term up to 2.7 times the typical fit; a fit of all 47 rows alone gives 2.95 times). `check` does not know the region layout, so `bytes` has the factor (the number that was not below any measured peak) and `typical_bytes` has none (a layout like the hook example). It is a measured cover, not a bound.
`check --json` has `memory_estimate.bytes`, `typical_bytes`, `build_bytes`, `loop_bytes`, `mesh_bytes` and `phase` (`"build"`, `"loop"` or `"mesh"`); the text prints the line `memory model:` with the three phases.
When the number is above the RAM, `check` gives the warning "the memory estimate is ..." and, when the filter is the cause, the filter line of the CPU model (`cli.memory_warnings`: "the filter needs about ... Option: a larger voxel_size"). The start of `topopt run` (`cli.run_memory_lines`) gives the same number and the same lines for `gpu-mg`. The estimate is not below any of the measured peaks (47 runs) and
the 15 runs of the old fit are below both numbers.

Measured cases: 47 runs of 2026-10-25 (49 were recorded; a 4-pass harness test and a case-C joint run that stopped early are not in the fit) on one Linux x86_64 host (Intel Core Ultra 9 185H, shared; the load was 20 to 25), the pocl CPU device
(8 compute units), revision `74a1e46` of main, `ru_maxrss` of the whole `topopt run`: the hook at 8 sizes (16,434 to 905,010 free dofs, 13 to 81 passes), a sparse frame at 6 sizes, a block with 0 to 2 joints in case B and C
(51,912 to 189,621 free dofs), the hook with a keep-out shape over the whole part, with dense keep-out shapes (80 and 320 triangles) and with a far keep-out shape (a grid of 0.06 to 6.5 million voxels), 6 load cases, a filter radius of 6 mm, and the `blur` mesh method. The peaks are 0.51 to 4.0 GB. `bytes` is 1.15 to 6.3 times the measured peak (the hook: 2.0 to 3.1 times; the block and the sparse frame at 1.0 mm and finer: up to 6.3 times, because their layout is simple and the factor 3.2 is not needed;
the stress layouts: 1.15 to 2.6 times). `typical_bytes` is 1.05 to 2.5 times the peak for the parts of a simple layout (the hook: 1.08 to 1.44 times) and 0.46 to 1.6 times for the stress layouts (below the peak for 12 of the 16 stress runs).
**Not measured:** a real GPU (the device buffers, about 0.3 kB for each free dof, are then not in the host memory), Apple silicon and macOS, parts of more than 905,010 free dofs, a part with more than 2 joints, case C with joints above 190,000 free dofs,
and the two-joint part. A mesh step that falls back to the `blur` path because the fine SDF grid is over its guard (`MAX_SDF_VOXELS`) was measured for 2 runs (a grid of 5.4 and 6.5 million voxels), and the setting `mesh_method: blur` for 1; the peaks of all 3 are below the estimate. The two-joint part at 2.2 mm is not explained (see the paragraph of the columns above).
`derived.memory_estimate_gib` of `gpu-mg` (the E1 bounds) is still the Cholesky number, not this model. The buckling check and the buckling row use the Cholesky number on purpose: they need a direct solver, and with `gpu-mg` they do not run. The memory check of the region builder (`regions_builder.check_yaml`) also uses the Cholesky number for `gpu-mg`, although it knows the solver. The fine pass (`fine_pass.fine_estimates`) uses this model for `gpu-mg`.

**Time model (P2a; `topopt/gpu_mg/check.py`, light, no pyopencl).** `estimate_seconds_gpu_mg(n_free, n_cases, iterations, ...)`. The
model is linear in the free dofs (power 1.0; the direct solvers use `DOF_POWER` 2.4, and `cli.fit_voxel_size` and
`regions_builder.target_active` take the power of the solver in use):

```
t_total = T0 + (N + 1) * t_pass
t_pass  = B * I * c_NR * n * S + h * n          T0 = 8.1 s + 80 us * n
B = ceil(n_cases / 2) (1 for one case)          c_NR = c1 (one column) or c2 (two columns per launch)
I = mean PCG iterations of a block over a run   S = 1 + 0.65 * k_other  (k_other = other gpu-mg runs on the device; 0 in check)
```

The constants are ONE table, `TIME_CONSTANTS`, with one row for each device class. The row `intel-arc-igpu` (a GPU of an Intel platform
named "Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics", case B) has `c1` 15.3 ns, `c2` 23.3 ns, `h` 2.0 us (each per free dof and, for `c`, per PCG
iteration of one block). It is a fit of 49 finished test runs (170k to 790k free dofs). `I` is a band
(low, mid, high) from the stiffness contrast of the start design, `lgK = -log10(1e-6 + volume_fraction**penal)`: below 2.5: 50, 65, 80;
2.5 to below 5: 100, 145, 200; 5 and above: 150, 200, 300; `penal` or `volume_fraction` not known: 60, 150, 300. The bands hold for
`gpu_tol` 1e-8 to 1e-6 (the default 1e-6 is inside): there is no factor in that range (56 of the 58 runs were at 1e-8; the one real pair of the same
problem at 1e-8 and at 1e-6 gave 0.92 for the mean iterations). Outside the range the count is scaled by a rule of thumb of 15 percent of the count at 1e-6
for each decade (`1 + 0.15 log10(1e-6 / gpu_tol)` looser than 1e-6; the same over its value at 1e-8 tighter than 1e-8), from pocl runs on
synthetic designs, not from real runs; the assumptions of the estimate say so. The estimate
is the mid band; `low_s` and `high_s` are the low and high bands. **The band is the spread of the iteration counts, not a limit:**
of the 49 runs of the fit the time was inside the band for 19 runs, below it for 14 and above it for 16 (15 of those 16 shared the
GPU with another gpu-mg run; `check` assumes none). **The accuracy of `check` is the row of the 18 runs with a recorded `penal`**,
because `check` always has a `penal` (`settings.penal`, default 3.0) and so always takes the band of its stiffness contrast. The mid
number without sharing, ratio of the estimate to the wall time: median 0.75, range 0.46 to 1.29, 8 runs within 25 % (ratio 0.75 to 1.25)
and 12 within 50 % (0.67 to 1.5); the Cholesky number for the same runs: median 17.8, range 3.9 to 47.4. With the other gpu-mg runs on
the device known (`k_other`, which `check` does not know) the 18 runs give median 0.96, 10 within 25 % and 17 within 50 %: the
difference to 0.75 is the sharing. The row of all 49 runs is "penal not recorded for 31 runs: band of all runs" (those 31 had
the band 60 / 150 / 300): median 1.01, range 0.36 to 2.15, 16 within 25 % and 23 within 50 %; the Cholesky number for the same runs:
median 6.08, range 0.81 to 47.4. That row is not the path that `check` takes; it is not the accuracy of `check`. If those 31 runs had the
default `penal` 3, `check` would give median 0.78 over the 49 runs, range 0.23 to 1.34. `run.json` has the `penal` of each run now
(`derived.time_model`), so the next fit has it. Not in the data: stress rows and robust mode (their extra solves are added with the model of the other
solvers), step acceptance, the springs and joints kernels of gpu-mg and the first-pass cap of 1000 iterations (P2b), per-axis supports (P2c), and any device other than
the Intel Arc iGPU.
The basis of the constants, in this order: (1) `calibration`: a record of `gpu-constants.json` in the state folder (section 8.1) for the
chosen device and case: its `c` is measured for the columns of its bench; the other column count is NOT measured: it is `c`
divided or multiplied by the ratio `c2 / c1` = 1.52 of the Intel fit. Its host part replaces `h`: it is measured at the sizes of the
bench only (the free dofs of the record `points`; the hook sizes) and is used for every size. The start and end are those of the table
row. The text says both facts; (2) `table`: the row of
the device class; (3) `reference`: a GPU with no row (an Apple GPU, an Intel Arc card, a GPU that `check` does not know) is
shown with the numbers of the Intel Arc iGPU row, named as a reference, with the text "no constants for this device (<name>, case
<case>); run `topopt gpu-check` to measure them", and the note that this device can be faster or slower. The reference is a choice: a
number that is labelled is more use to the agent and the user than no number, and for the Mac M4 it is on the safe side:
on the three hook rows of `GPU_MG_MEASURED` (2 load cases, mid band, `gpu_tol` 1e-8) it is 1.4, 1.6 and 2.1 times the measured seconds for
each iteration. The reference group is GPUs only. A device that is not known at all (no OpenCL, no device) has the same text and the
reference numbers. (4) `none`: an OpenCL device of kind CPU with no calibration. The Intel numbers are 2.5 to 5 times too low for a CPU device
(two pocl measurements on the hook at 1.2 mm), so the estimate gives **no seconds**: `total_s`, `low_s`, `high_s` and `s_per_iteration` are null, `basis` is
`none`, and the text is "no constants for this device (CPU device); run `topopt gpu-check` to measure them". The iteration band stays.
`check` gives no time warning for it, the YAML builder aims at the iteration cap instead of a time goal, and the doctor prints
"time estimate none (no constants for this device)". A CPU device that has a calibration record has the basis `calibration` and numbers.
`topopt check` never runs the device. `topopt gpu-check` (section 8.1) measures the constants.

**Errors of an explicit `settings.solver: gpu-mg` (a fact and the options; never a fallback to another solver).** With `auto`, a failure during the run is a
fallback ("Fallback during a run" above); a problem found before the run (no device, a device that is not a GPU, a failed self-test) gives the CPU rule
and the reason as a fact.

- pyopencl missing: `solver 'gpu-mg' needs pyopencl, and it is not installed. Install the gpu extra: <command>. Or set
  settings.solver to 'auto', 'cholesky' (Apple silicon), 'pardiso' (Linux x86_64, needs the pardiso extra) or 'amg'`.
- pyopencl that does not load; no OpenCL device; `gpu_device` that fits no device (the text lists the devices);
  a device that lacks a feature (not available, no compiler, local memory below 4096 bytes, constant memory below
  16384 bytes); `gpu_case: B` on a device without 64-bit floats; a coarsest level without a free dof; a dense inverse
  of the coarsest level that is larger than the largest buffer of the device; joints whose kernel `bord_w_*` keeps more bytes in local memory
  (the load case columns of one launch times `6 m` times the 4 or 8 bytes of the outer type) than `CL_DEVICE_LOCAL_MEM_SIZE` (the text gives the
  needed bytes, the device bytes and the joints count); a device that cannot build or allocate.
- The solve is not accepted: it does not reach `gpu_tol` and its backward error is above `gpu_backward_error` (case C: in 12
  refinement steps of 300 iterations, or earlier when the loop stagnates; case B: in the first pass and then the same steps). The
  `UserError` text gives the facts (the target, the relative residual reached, the backward error and its limit, the case, the device,
  the iterations, "the loop stopped early" when it stagnated, "the iteration gave a value that is not finite" when the PCG broke down, and in case C with joints the
  32-bit rounding fact, the ratio of the beam to the bond stiffness and whether the inner PCG used the deflation of the rigid modes and of the bonded patches) and the options, not orders: a larger `settings.gpu_tol`; a larger
  `settings.gpu_backward_error` (or one above 0 when it is 0); `settings.gpu_max_iter` (case B only: a larger cap of the first pass, with its present value in the text); a stiffer start design (a lower `settings.penal` or a higher
  `settings.volume_fraction`); a stiffer beam (a larger section, a shorter beam; case C with joints only); `settings.gpu_case: B` only in case C on a device with 64-bit float (case C is no cure for case B, it
  uses the same loop); another solver. Each is an option of its own in the text. When `eta` was computed, the text adds that, on the designs without joints measured so far, a solve at the FP64 rounding floor has a backward
  error of about 4e-17 to 2e-16, and a larger one means that the iteration did not converge (with the rule off there is no `eta` and no
  such sentence). A run with joints gets other facts in place of that sentence (F1-7): the host check of a part that joints hold has a rounding noise of its own in the relative residual (about
  1.6 unit roundoffs of `|Kb u|`; 5e-8 of the load on the two-joint part), the backward error of that noise is inside the floor of parts without joints, and the answer of a direct solver (pardiso) on the
  two-joint part had a backward error of 6e-16 to 4e-15 (the measured numbers of the two-joint part above). Two design facts follow (#378), each only when it holds: the load case whose
  compliance rose the most in the passes of `history.jsonl` so far, from its lowest value to the last pass (the two values, their passes, the factor and its
  `compliance_limit`; no sentence when no compliance rose, with fewer than two passes, or without a run folder), and the per-axis supports (each `fixed` entry with
  `axes` that are not all three, with its axes). They add options: a lower `compliance_limit` for that load case (when it has one), and full clamps in place of the
  per-axis supports, if the part is held that way in use. The case of #378: a phone dock with a per-axis front support, case C on a GPU; the compliance of the
  load that the support does not take rose 4.5 times in 4 passes before a solve used all 12 refinement steps above the target, and case B solved the same
  passes (a tight limit on that load case only moved the stop from pass 7 to pass 12). The option of another solver
  says that with `auto` a gpu-mg failure does not end the run: it goes on with the CPU solver from the last checkpoint ("Fallback during a run", above).
  The record of the failed solve is in `gpu_mg.jsonl` before the error is raised (below).
- A device error (`pyopencl.Error`) during an upload or a solve: the engine is released, and the `UserError` names the
  device, the case, the optimizer iteration and the OpenCL error text, with the options (`gpu_case: C`, another
  `gpu_device`, another solver). It is not an internal error.

**Run folder.** `gpu_mg.jsonl` (new run, with any solver: `RunWriter.clean()` deletes the old file and its `.tmp` file, `snapshot.RUN_FILES`; a new gpu-mg run then writes a new one. Resume: the solver cuts the file to the checkpoint pass, like
`history.jsonl`, and appends; `line` and `solve` go on after the last kept line, and one `resume:` line in `run.log` says what was kept
and what was dropped): one JSON line for each solve, NOT for each optimizer
iteration. The line has `line` (its number), `kind` (`main`: the design of the loop; `trial`: a trial design in
another step of the loop, for example the step acceptance of A2; `adjoint`: an adjoint solve with the operator of the
last design, with `setup_s` and `upload_s` 0), `iteration` (the optimizer iteration of the run writer), `solve` (the
number of the design that the solve used), `case`, `setup_s` (CPU numbers), `setup_parts_s` (`avg`, `dinv`, `eig`,
`coarse`, `total`, and `defl` in case C with joints; design lines only), `upload_s`, `solves` (blocks of load cases), `solve_s`, `map_s`, `iterations` (a
list with one entry for each block: case C `{inner: [executed PCG iterations of each refinement step], refine_steps}` (with joints the line of the design also has `deflation`, section 20),
case B `{pcg, executed}`, and for a restart also `inner` and `refine_steps`; and since G2 `accepted_by`, `true_rel`, `eta` as below), `total_s`,
`accepted_by` (`"tol"` or `"backward_error"`: `"backward_error"` when the rule accepted any solve of the line), `eta` (the largest backward error that
was computed for the line; absent when none was) and `true_rel` (the largest true relative residual at the end of a solve of the line; absent when it was
not computed: case B with the rule off). An entry of `iterations` has, as far as it applies: `accepted_by`, `true_rel`, `eta`, `check_s` (seconds of the
check of the first pass, case B), `pass1_true_rel` and `pass1_eta` (the check of a first pass that was sent to the restart loop). A solve that fails
writes its line BEFORE the `UserError`, with `failed: true` in the line and in the entry, and in the entry `rel_hist` (the largest relative residual
at each residual check, the first is the start of the loop), `eta_hist` (the same for `eta`; `null` where it was not computed), `inner`, `refine_steps`,
`stagnated`; the entry of the failed solve has no `accepted_by`, and the line has `accepted_by` only when an earlier block of the same line was accepted (3 or more
load cases make more than one block). With step acceptance or adjoint
rows a run has more lines than optimizer iterations; a reader sums the lines of an iteration. `run.log` has one line `gpu-mg: device ..., case ..., N levels, work-group a/b, device buffers X MB,
tolerance 1e-06, backward error 1e-15, PCG cap 1000 in the first pass (settings.gpu_max_iter) and 300 in a restart step` (case C: `PCG cap 300 in a refinement step
(settings.gpu_max_iter does not apply to case C)`). The first time the rule accepts a solve in a run, `run.log` gets one line (the optimizer iteration, the relative
residual reached, the target, `eta`, the limit, and that a solve at the FP64 floor has `eta` of about 4e-17 on the designs without joints measured so far; a run with joints says that the host check of such a part has a noise of its own, so the residual reached can be that noise: facts, no claim about the design); a resume that finds such a record in the kept part does not repeat it. At the end of the run (when the solver is
released, also after an error) one line gives the count: `gpu-mg: N of M solves were accepted by the backward error ...`; it is written only when N > 0 and counts the
kept part of a resumed run. The dashboard and `history.jsonl` are unchanged.

**Environment.** `topopt.environment.environment_data()` has the keys `opencl` (`pyopencl` version or null, `problem`,
`install_command`, `platforms`, `devices` with `index`, `platform`, `name`, `kind`, `fp64`, `version`,
`vendor`, `max_work_group_size`, `max_mem_alloc`, `global_mem`, `local_mem`, `constant_mem`, `compute_units`,
`duplicate_of`: the index of an earlier device with the same platform, name and version, else null; `auto_device`,
`auto_case`, `chosen_device`: the device that `settings.gpu_device` takes), `solver_setting["gpu-mg"]` (`resolved` or `error`), `auto_choice` (the
`SolverChoice` of `auto` as data) and `gpu_solver`. `experimental_solvers` is an empty object. `topopt check` prints the `opencl` lines when
pyopencl is installed, and `check --json` has the same `opencl` object.

**`gpu_solver` (P9-4d).** Facts about the GPU solver on this machine; data, not an offer. Keys: `used` (true when `settings.solver: auto` runs `gpu-mg` here),
`device` and `case` and `self_test` (the facts of the pick, else `null`; the self-test numbers of a failed test are in `why`), `why` (the line
`solver: auto -> ...` of the pick: the device and the self-test, or the reason for the CPU solver), `to_use_the_gpu` (what would make a GPU usable, or `null`
when it is used or when no step is known: a GPU is visible and the reason in `why` says all; the cases are pyopencl not installed with the install command,
pyopencl installed and not loading, no OpenCL device, and only non-GPU devices), `test_command` (`<python> -m topopt gpu-check`) and `measured` (the
constant `environment.GPU_MG_MEASURED`: the figures of the table above as the figures of ONE machine, with `machine`, `what` and the rows). The agent
tells the user the solver and the device, and asks before it runs a command of `to_use_the_gpu`. No grid-size threshold is in the code: the tools give
the facts, the agent and the user decide.

**`topopt gpu-check`** (section 8.1) is the one command that checks gpu-mg on a machine: facts, `tools/gpu_mg_parity.py`, the four
test files on the real device, and a short `tools/bench_gpu_mg.py` run (sizes 1.2 and 1.0 mm, 20 iterations), then one report
(`gpu-check.md`, `gpu-check.json`). It needs a checkout (`tools/` and `tests/` are not in a wheel).

**Install (`pyproject.toml`, P9-4d).** `pyopencl==2026.1.4` (MIT) is a main dependency on an Apple silicon Mac and on Linux x86_64, with the marker
`(platform_system == 'Darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64') or (platform_system == 'Linux' and platform_machine == 'x86_64')`, so `uv pip install -e .`,
the plugin and the Claude Desktop extension (section 25.5) get it without an extra. `requirements.lock` pins it with the three packages it needs (`platformdirs`,
`pytools`, `siphash24`); `requirements-macos-x86_64.lock` has none of the four (pyopencl is not a main dependency on an Intel Mac). The extras stay:
`gpu` = `pyopencl==2026.1.4` with no marker (for a platform outside the marker, and so that old commands work). `gpu-test` = pyopencl and, on Linux x86_64,
`pocl-binary-distribution==3.0` (a CPU OpenCL device for the tests; test extra only; never a runtime dependency). A machine with no OpenCL driver or device runs
`auto` on the CPU rule, as before. Tests: `tests/test_gpu_mg_device.py` (no OpenCL needed), `tests/test_gpu_mg.py`, `tests/test_gpu_mg_fallback.py` and
`tests/test_bench_gpu_mg.py` (skip with `no usable OpenCL device: ...` through the `dev` fixture, or without pyopencl), `tests/test_opencl_guard.py` (no OpenCL needed).
`tests/conftest.py` reads the ICD files (the vendors folder and `PYOPENCL_HOME/.libs`, whatever `OCL_ICD_FILENAMES`
holds) and the device types. If a non-CPU OpenCL device is visible and the environment variable `TOPOPT_TEST_REAL_GPU`
is not `1`: on Linux the pytest session stops (exit code 3); on macOS the tests with the marker `opencl_context` are
skipped with one reason and the rest of pytest runs. With `TOPOPT_TEST_REAL_GPU=1` the tests use the real GPU (case C).
Without it, `tests/conftest.py` also sets `TOPOPT_AUTO_GPU=0` at the start of the session (a value that the user set stays), so a Mac or a CI runner with an OpenCL GPU
runs the `auto` tests on the CPU rule, as a machine without a GPU does. The tests of the `auto` pick (fake devices, or pocl as a GPU) delete the variable with `monkeypatch`.

**Scripts.**

- `tools/gpu_mg_parity.py` (also the second step of `topopt gpu-check`): one solve of a small cantilever with case B and C against the direct solvers of the
  platform and SuperLU. Prints a table. Exit code 1 if the relative difference of the displacements is above 1e-6, if a case
  stops with a `UserError` (a `FAIL` line with the text), or if no case ran.
- `tools/bench_gpu_mg.py --out <dir>`: the hook at 1.2, 1.0, 0.8 and 0.6 mm with the default solver and with `gpu-mg`,
  one job at a time (a child process for each, with its own peak memory). It skips a default-solver run when the memory
  estimate of `topopt check` is above the RAM, and says so as a fact. A run has a time limit (default: 4 times the
  time estimate of `topopt check`, at least 600 s; `--timeout-s 0` for none); a run over the limit is stopped and has the status
  `timed_out`. It writes `bench_gpu_mg.json` and `bench_gpu_mg.md` (machine, macOS, RAM, git revision and `git_dirty`,
  OpenCL device, 64-bit flag, case, setup, upload, solve, map and device iterations summed for each OPTIMIZER iteration,
  total time, peak memory in MB of 10^6 bytes, final compliance, `max_active_voxels` used). The report holds no
  absolute path: `hook` is the path relative to the repo (or the file name). `--dry-run` prints the plan and the memory
  facts.

**Recorded defaults (not user settings).** `GpuParams.tol` 1e-8 (the one-off stress solve and the tools; the loop of a run takes `settings.gpu_tol`); inner tolerance 1e-2; 12 refinement steps; 300 PCG
iterations in a restart step or a refinement step (the first pass of case B takes `settings.gpu_max_iter`, default 1000; the last step of the loop has the margin 0.5 above); 12 power iterations for the Chebyshev bound; coarsening stops at 3000 free dofs (at least 2 levels, at
most 8); 2 load cases for each kernel launch; Chebyshev degree 2 on 3x3 block Jacobi; `sync_every` 0 (no `finish` inside
a solve; a speculative residual check one iteration ahead). Device memory is about 0.3 kB for each free dof.

## 21. Refine by feedback: run history, compare, marks as hints (added with V3)

`topopt/feedback.py` reads run folders and turns the marks of the Refine page into facts and options. It gives facts,
estimates and options. The agent decides. The MCP tools (`topopt_mcp/server.py`) are thin wrappers around it. It has
no CLI command in `topopt/cli.py`: use `python -m topopt.feedback` (below). The module imports numpy and PyYAML at the
top; trimesh, manifold3d and the voxelizer load when a function needs them.

**Boundary.** The three functions are read-only and advisory. `run_history` and `compare_runs` write nothing.
`make_hints` writes one NEW folder and nothing else. None of them edits a mesh, a run folder, an input YAML or a region
STL of the run. Applying marks to a mesh, geometric cleanup and the mesh edits are not part of this section. V3
adds no write path for a history file: the history is what a scan of the run folders finds (`run.json`, `status.json`,
`history.jsonl`, `result/metrics.json`). The optimizer, `post.py` and the snapshot files do not change.

### 21.1 `run_history(root, depth=2, limit=20, detail=False)`

- Search: `root` itself if it holds `run.json` or `status.json`; else the folders under it, up to `depth` levels
  (default 2: `runs/<name>` under a work folder; at most 5, and a note says when the value was cut). A run folder is not
  searched inside. Symbolic links and folders that start with a dot are not followed. The scan stops after 5000 folders
  (a note says so). Newest first (the latest modification time of `status.json`, `run.json`, `history.jsonl`,
  `result/metrics.json`).
- `limit` (default 20): the newest runs only; 0 or `null` gives all. `count` is the number of runs found, `listed` the
  number in `runs`, and a note says when older runs are left out. The facts are read for the listed runs only.
- Returns `{ok, root, depth, count, listed, detail, runs, notes}`. On a wrong folder: `{ok: false, error}`.
- Each run (short form): `name`, `dir_name`, `run_dir`, `state` (`done`, `error`, `running`, `starting`, `postprocess`,
  `unknown`, or `unreadable`), `iteration`, `iterations`, `message`, `started_at`, `modified`, `mtime`, `yaml_path`
  (from `run.json`), `yaml_exists`, `yaml_newer_than_run` (the YAML file is more than 2 s newer than `started_at`),
  `settings` (`voxel_size_mm`, `volume_fraction`, `iterations`, `solver` (the solver that ran), `filter_radius_mm`,
  `n_active`, `load_cases` as names), `metrics` (`compliance_initial`, `compliance_final`, `mass_design_space_g`,
  `mass_final_g`, `mass_saved_pct`, `volume_final_mm3`, `volume_fraction_final`, `run_time_s`), `metrics_source` and
  `problems`. `detail: true` adds the full `settings` (grid shape, free dofs, load cases with forces, regions as file
  names), all metrics (`stiffness_cases`, `watertight`, `triangles`), `last_history`, `files` (which files exist, the number
  of snapshots) and `yaml.newer_region_files`.
- A missing or partial file is a fact in `problems`, not an error: a missing `run.json`, `status.json`, `history.jsonl`,
  `result/metrics.json` or `result/final.stl` (the last two only for a run that is done or unknown); a status file that is
  not JSON (`state: unreadable`); a history line that cannot be read (skipped; a partial last line is the usual cause).
  Without `metrics.json`, `metrics` holds `compliance_last` and `volume_fraction_final` from the last history row, and
  `metrics_source` says so.
- The MCP tool adds `root_rel`, and for each run `path` (relative to the work folder) and `process_alive`.
- A folder where an input check refused a fresh run over an earlier run (section 24.1, P9-19) has a row with the key `earlier_run`, after `state`.
  `earlier_run` holds `note` and the keys of the row that come from `run.json`, `result/` and `history.jsonl`, which are the earlier run's: `name`,
  `iterations`, `started_at`, `yaml_path`, `yaml_exists`, `yaml_newer_than_run`, `settings`, `metrics` and `metrics_source` (with `detail`: `name`,
  `iterations`, `started_at`, `yaml`, `settings`, `metrics`, `metrics_source`, `last_history` and `files`). At the top of the row they are `null`.
  `state`, `iteration`, `message` (and `step` with `detail`), `modified`, `mtime` and `problems` stay: they are the folder's or the refused job's.
  Any other folder has the row as before.

### 21.2 `compare_runs(run_a, run_b=None, check_labels=None, variants=None)`

Two forms. Give one: `(run_a, run_b)` is the two-run form below; `(run_a, variants=[...])` is the table form at the end of this section.

A is the base, B the change. `delta` is B - A, `delta_pct` is relative to A. Every value names its source. `run.json`
holds the YAML path and the region file names but no hash (section 5), so the YAML and the STL files on disk can be newer
than the run or can differ from it. `compare_runs` says so as facts. They are evidence, not proof.

- Returns `{ok, a, b, setup, metrics, inputs, notes, summary, problems}`. `a` and `b`: `name`, `dir_name`, `run_dir`,
  `state`, `iteration`, `iterations`, `started_at`, `modified`, `yaml_path` (the tool adds `run_dir_rel`).
- A side that is a folder of a refused job over an earlier run (section 24.1, P9-19) has `earlier_run` in `a` or `b`, after `state`: `note`, and
  `name`, `iterations`, `started_at` and `yaml_path`, which are `null` at the top. The first entry of `notes` and the first line of `summary` say
  that the setup, the metrics and the inputs of that side are of the earlier run (they are read from `run.json`, `labels.bin` and
  `result/metrics.json`, as for any run, and they are not changed). A side that is not this case is as before.
- `setup.run_json_diff`: the keys of `run.json` with another value, `{key, a, b, source}`; `missing_in` is `"a"` or `"b"` for a key
  on one side only. Source: `run.json of each run (recorded at the start)`. Left out: `format`, `started_at`,
  `yaml_path`, `lost_force` and the `derived` block (forces, volumes, estimates; these keys stay:
  `filter_radius_mm`, `min_feature_mm`, `case_combine`, `density_g_cm3`, `volume.target_volume_mm3`,
  `volume.target_mass_g`, and every `derived` key whose name starts with `filter`, so a new filter key shows without a code
  change; for example `derived.filter.radius_mm`, `.radius_source`, `.solid_neighbours`, `.min_member_mm` of section 22a.
  A list of sentences, size estimates and notes inside a filter block are not copied: `feedback.FILTER_SKIP`).
  A relative `yaml_path` starts at the run folder.
- `setup.yaml_diff`: `{same_file, diff, source}`. `diff` lists the flat keys of the two YAML files on disk that differ;
  it is `null` if both runs name the same file or a file is missing. The source text says the files are read now.
- `setup.region_files`: `{diff, same_count}`. Each region file under `regions` of the YAMLs on disk (every key) has a key
  (`design`, `fixed:<file>`, `keep_out:<file>`, `load:<region name>`; `<key>:<file or name>` for another key) and a SHA-256. `diff` lists `{key, status, a, b, source}` with status `changed`,
  `only_in_a`, `only_in_b` or `unknown`. If the YAML of a run is missing, `diff` and `same_count` are `null` and a note says so.
- `setup.labels_diff`: the voxel classes of the two runs (`labels.bin` of each run, so what ran), when the grids (shape,
  voxel size, origin) are equal: `{comparable: true, voxels, transitions: {"design->keep_out": n, ...}, bbox_mm: {min,
  max}, source}`. Otherwise `{comparable: false, reason}`.
- `metrics.rows`: `{key, a, b, delta, delta_pct}` for the numbers of `metrics.json` (`compliance_initial`,
  `compliance_final`, masses, `volume_final_mm3`, `run_time_s`, `iterations`, `triangles`), `volume_fraction_final` and
  `stiffness[<case>] N/mm`. `metrics.other` lists a `solver` or `watertight` that differs. `metrics.filter` (only when
  a run has one): `{a, b, differs, source}`, the flat keys of every top-level `filter*` block of `metrics.json`
  (`filter.radius_mm`, ...; same skip as above), side by side, and `differs` as `{key, a, b[, missing_in]}`. `source_a` and
  `source_b` name the file (or `history.jsonl` for a run without `metrics.json`).
- `inputs.a` and `inputs.b`: `yaml` (path, exists, mtime, `newer_than_run`, `newer_region_files`), `yaml_vs_run_json`
  (`differs`: `{key, yaml, run_json}` for the values that the YAML on disk has with another value than `run.json`;
  `compared`: the names of the values that were compared; `not_compared`: `{key, run_json_key, run_json, reason}` for
  a value that the engine derives and the YAML does not hold (`settings.filter_radius` without that key: "derived by the
  engine; not compared"); `not_recorded`: the values that `run.json` does not record),
  `labels_vs_disk` (the YAML on disk is voxelized and compared with `labels.bin`:
  `{checked, grid_same, labels_same, voxels_differ}` or `{checked: false, reason}`), `facts` (all sentences),
  `warnings` (the sentences that say the files on disk may not be the ones that ran) and `line` (one sentence for the run).
- What is compared with `run.json` (`compared`): `settings.voxel_size`, `volume_fraction`, `iterations`, `solver` (when
  not `auto`), `name`, the load cases (names, weights, forces), the region file names of every key under `regions`, and
  from `derived`: `settings.filter_radius` (only when the YAML has that key: without it the engine derives the radius
  from `voxel_size` or `min_member_mm`, so the value is listed in `not_compared` with the `run.json` value),
  `settings.case_combine` and `material.density`. `run.json` does not record `material.E`, `material.nu`,
  `settings.penal`, `settings.beta_schedule` and `settings.move_limit` (`feedback.NOT_IN_RUN_JSON`), so a change of them
  in the YAML cannot be seen here. A fact in `inputs.*.facts` and a note of the result say so. Follow-up: after A2 (PR #22)
  `run.json` has a `stress` key with E, nu and density: compare them then.
- `check_labels`: `null` voxelizes the YAML on disk when the grid has at most 10 million voxels; `true` does it for any
  size; `false` skips it. The voxelizer keeps the guards of the YAML (`max_grid_voxels`).
- `notes`: the load cases, the voxel size, the volume fraction, the iteration counts or the target volumes differ (the
  compliance of another load, grid or target is not comparable), both runs name the same YAML file, and what `run.json`
  does not record. `summary`: short sentences (a line "filter differs: ..." when a filter fact differs); the files on disk give one sentence for each run (what says that they may not
  be the files that ran, and what still matches). `problems`: files missing in a run.

**Table form (#209).** `compare_runs(run_a, variants=[...])`: `run_a` is the base, `variants` is a list of run folders (one or more; the code sets no upper
bound, the agent chooses how many). It gives one table of the runs, and it writes nothing (no image, no file).

- Returns `{ok, base, runs, vs_base, notes, summary, problems}`. `base` is the brief of the base run, as `a` above. `runs` has one row for each run: the base
  first, then the variants in call order. A row has `name`, `dir_name`, `run_dir`, `state`, `mass_final_g`, `mass_saved_pct` (`result/metrics.json`),
  `stiffness` ({load case: N/mm}, the value of the optimizer, the voxel model, from `stiffness_cases` of `result/metrics.json`; a case with no value is `null`
  and has an entry in `problems` with its `reason`) with `stiffness_source`,
  `verdict` (the state word of the verdict, from `result/metrics.json` or `verdict.json`), `verify`, `print`, `render` and `problems`. The tool adds
  `run_dir_rel` to `base`, to each row and to each `vs_base` entry.
- `verify` has `status`: `not run` (no `verify/verify.json`), `no result` (the file is not readable, or `ok` is not true, or `estimate_only` is true; the rule
  of the part card, section 9.2) or `done`. With `done`: `cases` ({case: `stiffness_N_per_mm` of the tet model, `p99_9_MPa`}), `limit_exceeded` when the
  file has a limit, `same_mesh` and `source`. `same_mesh` is `true` when the SHA-256 that `verify.json` records for its mesh file is that of the file now in
  `result/` (the rule of `part_card._same_mesh`), `false` with an entry in `problems` ("run verify again") when it is not, and `null` when the file
  records no hash or the mesh is not there. The stiffness of `verify` is of the tet model and the stiffness of `stiffness` is of the optimizer: the two differ.
- `print` has `ok`, `support_needed`, `bed_fit`, `overhang_area_mm2`, `support_volume_mm3` and `thinnest_member_mm` from the `print` block of
  `result/metrics.json`; when that block says `ok: false` it has `ok` and `error`. A run with no `print` block (an older build) has `print: null`.
- `render` is `{montage_rel, newer_than_final, section}` for the newest `renders/*_montage.png` of the run folder that is not a section view (a cut view is
  named `<stem>_section-x10_montage.png`; `section` is `true` only when the run has no other montage) (the name rule of section 15; `montage_rel`
  starts at the run folder; `newer_than_final` compares the file times with `result/final.stl`, `null` when that file is not there), or `null`. Only
  `render_part` makes the images; `compare_runs` returns paths and does not make them. A `null` has an entry in `problems` that names `render_part` with
  this run folder.
- A fact that no file holds is `null` and one entry in `problems` (as in `run_facts`); it is never a guess. A row of a refused job over an earlier run
  (section 24.1) keeps `earlier_run` after `state`: `name`, the mass, `stiffness`, `verdict`, `verify`, `print` and `render` are in it, and `null` at the top.
- `vs_base` has one entry for each variant, in call order, built by the function of the two-run form with the base as A: `ok`, `run_dir`, `setup`
  (as above), `labels_vs_disk` ({base, variant}), `summary` and `notes` of the pair. A user who wants the whole pair (the metrics rows, the
  `inputs`) calls the two-run form. `check_labels` applies to each pair.
- `summary`: one line for each variant (state, `mass_final_g` and the stiffness of each load case that both runs have, with the change in %).
  `notes`: the order of the rows, the optimizer stiffness against the tet stiffness, runs that do not share the load cases, and a refused-job row.
  `problems`: the table-level problems only (a pair that failed to compare); the problems of a row are in the row.
- Refused with `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` that names both forms, with nothing changed: `run_b` and `variants` together; neither; an empty
  `variants`; a blank `run_a`, `run_b` or entry (no folder is read); two entries, or an entry and the base, that are one folder; a folder that is not
  there (the error names it). `variants` that is not a list (a string) and an entry that is not a text get `{"ok": false, ...}` from the library
  (`feedback.compare_runs`) only. Through MCP the schema check of the SDK refuses them first, before the tool runs: the reply is an error result
  (`isError` true) with a validation message that names `variants`, and it is not the `{"ok": false}` reply (section 10). A JSON list written as a text
  (`'["runs/b"]'`) is read as a list.
- Measured (finished runs of the hook and ladle examples, a base and two variants, read only, 3 calls each, host load average 9.4): with the label check
  0.44 s, 0.11 s and 0.13 s (hook) and 0.21 to 0.22 s (ladle); with `check_labels` false 0.03 s; the reply is 7.9 KB and 8.2 KB of JSON. The lever card
  `compare_runs` has the same numbers. Tests: `tests/test_compare_variants.py`.

### 21.3 Marks and the hint mapping

Input: the file of the Refine page (`topopt/refine/README.md`): `version: 1`, `units: "mm"`, `source_sha256` (of
`final.stl`), `marks[]` with `id`, `type` (`add`, `remove`, `smooth`), `points` (mm, the frame of `result/final.stl`, which is
the frame of the region STL files), `radius_mm`, `mirror` (plane y = 0), and `normals`, `amount_mm`, `strength`, `note`.
`read_marks` accepts the path, the JSON text or the dict. A file that is not JSON, has no `marks` list or another version is
an error. A mark with a wrong field (type, points, radius) is `unreadable` in the report and the others go on.

The marks are points of emphasis, not absolutes. The YAML format of this version has no key for a place: every region is an
STL. So:

| Mark | Option the proposed YAML uses | Other options (not used by the YAML, in the report) |
|---|---|---|
| `remove` | `keep_out`: a keep-out STL | `skip`; a smaller radius (`radius_scale`); lower `settings.volume_fraction` (global) |
| `add` | `solid`: a forced-solid region (a load region that no load case uses, as the `solid` role of `build_regions`) | `skip`; a smaller radius; raise `settings.volume_fraction` (global); a bigger design space |
| `smooth` | none: facts and options only (the YAML has no key that smooths one place) | `settings.filter_radius` (global); a mesh edit (not in this section) |

- Shape: a sphere of radius `radius_mm x radius_scale` for one point; for a stroke, a chain of capsules of that radius along the
  points (`regions_builder.make_primitive`). With `mirror`, the same shape at y -> -y. Used from a mark: `points`,
  `radius_mm`, `mirror`. Not used: `normals`, `amount_mm`, `strength`, `note`, and the keys of 29.1 `smooth_mode`, `remove_mode` and
  `cleanup` (a keep-out or solid region has no depth and no strength); the report keeps them as given.
- The region is cut to the box of all input regions, so the grid (origin, shape) does not move; the report gives the cut share
  (`outside_grid_box_pct`). A `remove` region is cut by the fixed and load regions (`protect_regions`, default true). An `add`
  region is cut to the design space (`clip_to_design`, default true). `cut_to` names a cut only when it removed volume.
- The marks are read in file order and the first mark wins an overlap, as the first load region wins in the engine: a hint
  region (keep-out or solid) is cut by the hint regions of the marks before it. The report gives the overlap
  (`overlap_earlier_hints`: the mark ids, the voxels and the volume that was cut). The effect of a mark (`design_voxels`) is
  counted on the labels that already hold the earlier hints. A mark whose region is empty after the cut is `no_effect`, with
  the reason.
- A region with no free design voxel (the mark is outside the part, already solid, or inside the region of an earlier mark)
  is `no_effect`: it is not put in the YAML, because a region without a voxel stops the loader.
- If the proposed YAML still does not load, the loader error is in `problems` and `summary.proposed_yaml`, `ok` is false
  (the folder and `hints.json` are written), and a mark that the error names gets status `invalid` with the error.
- A solid hint that touches no material of `final.stl` can be removed by post-process: it drops every solid island that does
  not touch the fixed region. The fact `final_material_in_region_mm3` (`touches_final_material`) says if the region
  touches the material of `final.stl`. Follow-up: when A3a adds `regions.solid`, `add` maps to it instead of a load region.
- Keep-out STLs must sit next to the YAML for the exact cut of `post.py` (it looks in the YAML folder), so the
  proposed YAML names every region file by its file name, in the new folder.

### 21.4 `make_hints(run_dir, marks, out_dir=None, options=None, overwrite=False, check=True, yaml_path=None)`

Writes the new folder (default `<run folder>-hints` beside the run folder; `-2`, `-3` when it exists):

```
<out>/<name of the input YAML>.yaml   the YAML of the run, with the hint regions; one line added to `assumptions`
<out>/<copies of the region STLs>     flat; a file name that two regions share gets _2, _3
<out>/hint_remove_<id>.stl            the keep-out regions (binary STL)
<out>/hint_add_<id>.stl               the solid regions; the YAML load region is named hint_add_<id>
<out>/hints.json                      the full report (paths relative to <out>, or file names)
```

- Needs `run.json` and the YAML it names (a relative path starts at the run folder), or `yaml_path`: the YAML of the run at
  its new place (a moved run). The labels check (`grid.labels_match_run`) says if that YAML and its STL files give the labels
  of the run. Reads `labels.bin` and `result/final.stl` when they exist (the surface distance and the hash of the marks are
  facts; a missing file is a fact in `problems`). Comments of the input YAML are not copied (PyYAML writes the file). Every
  file under `regions` (all keys) is copied and renamed in the new YAML. New load regions come last in `regions.load`, so
  a real load region wins an overlap.
- The tool writes only into the new folder. It stops before the voxelization, with `{ok: false, error, refused: {reason,
  path, options}}`, when: the folder is a run folder or inside one (`run.json` or `status.json` in it or in a parent folder:
  `run_folder`); the folder holds an input file of the run, that is, it is the folder of the YAML or of a region STL
  (`input_folder`); the folder, or a file that will be written, is a symbolic link (`symbolic_link`: it is not followed and not
  removed); a file that will be written is not a plain file (`not_a_file`) or the folder is a file (`not_a_folder`); the
  folder holds files and `overwrite` is false (`not_empty`); `overwrite` is true and the folder holds files but no `hints.json`
  of format 1, that is, it is not an earlier hints folder (`not_a_hints_folder`). With `overwrite`, files of an earlier call
  that the new YAML does not use stay (a note names them). The files that will be written are checked again before the
  first write. A write error (for example `SameFileError`) is an error with the cause, not an internal error.
- Other stops, with `{ok: false, error}`: the run folder or `run.json` or the YAML is missing (the message offers `yaml_path`);
  the marks file cannot be read.
- `options`: `remove` (`keep_out`, `skip`), `add` (`solid`, `skip`), `radius_scale` (number above 0, default 1.0),
  `protect_regions`, `clip_to_design`, `per_mark` ({mark id: option}). A wrong option is a fact in `problems`; the default is used.

Report (the return value of `make_hints`; `hints.json` holds the same data with relative paths: `run_dir` relative to the
folder, `out_dir` ".", `marks_file` and `source.yaml_path` as file names, and `marks_sha256` for the provenance): `ok` (false
when the proposed YAML does not load, with `error`), `format` (1), `run_dir`, `run_name`, `marks_file`, `marks_sha256`,
`marks_count`, `marks_match_final_stl` (null when a hash is missing), `source` (`yaml_path`, `yaml_sha256`, `final_stl_sha256`), `out_dir`,
`proposed_yaml` (`path`, `loads`: it loads through `load_config` and the voxelizer, `error`), `grid` (`origin`, `h`, `shape`,
`same_as_run`, `labels_match_run`, `design_symmetric_about_y0`, `bounds_mm`), `options` (the effective ones), `option_catalog`
(for each mark type: `id`, `implemented`, `text`; for a run whose `run.json` has `derived.target_mass_asked_g` (I7) the text of the option `volume_fraction` names `settings.target_mass_g`, and the ids are the same), `marks`, `summary` (counts of `<type>:<status>`), `files`,
`labels_changed` (`grid_unchanged`, `voxels`, `transitions`, `bbox_mm`: the voxel labels that differ from the input YAML),
`volume_target` (`before` from `run.json`, `after` from the check of the proposed YAML: `target_volume_mm3` and
`target_mass_g`; the volume fraction applies to the free design voxels, so keep-out and solid hints change the target),
`check` (the `check_data` of the proposed YAML, as in `topopt check`) and `check_error`, `values_used`, `values_not_used`,
`problems`, `notes`, `elapsed_s`.

`short_report(report)` gives the short reply of the MCP tool: `ok`, `run_dir`, `out_dir`, `proposed_yaml`, `summary`, one line
for each mark (`id`, `type`, `status`, `option_used`, `radius_used_mm`, `mirror`, `voxels_touched`, `design_voxels`,
`region_file`, `touches_final_material`, `overlaps_earlier_marks`, `mirror_copy_outside_grid_box`, `reason`),
`labels_changed`, `volume_target`, a short `check` (voxels, components, time estimate, `max_lost_percent`, `warnings`),
`grid`, `files`, `problems`, `detail: false`, `report_file` and `more`. Size on the small test case: 3 marks 2.3 KB (the full
report 12.7 KB); 40 marks 13.3 KB (76 KB).

Each entry of `marks`: `id`, `index`, `type`, `status` (`applied`, `skipped_by_option`, `no_effect`, `facts_only`,
`invalid`, `unreadable`), `option_used` (the option the YAML uses: `keep_out`, `solid`, `skip`, or `none`), `reason`, `options`
(`id`, `implemented`, `used`), `facts`, and for an applied mark `region_file` and `region` (`kind`, `centres_mm`, `radius_mm`,
`mirror`, `bbox_mm`). `facts`: `position_mm`, `points`, `path_mm`, `path_length_mm`, `radius_mm`, `radius_used_mm`, `mirror`,
`amount_mm`, `strength`, `note`, `surface_distance_mm` (from each point to `final.stl`; `surface_note` when more than two voxels),
`outside_grid_box_pct`, `voxels_touched` (voxel centres inside the mark shape on the grid of the run),
`voxels_by_label` (`empty`, `design`, `fixed`, `load`, `keep_out`, as the engine labels them), `overlap_regions` (the voxels
inside each input region: `design`, and `fixed`, `load`, `keep_out` by file or region name), `design_voxels_share_pct`,
`mirror_copy` (`outside_grid_box`, `voxels_touched`, `design_voxels`; `outside_grid_box: true` when the copy lies outside the
bounds of the input regions), `applied_region` (`cut_to`, `voxels`, `design_voxels`, `volume_mm3`, `cut_volume_pct`),
`overlap_earlier_hints` (`marks`, `voxels`, `volume_mm3`), `final_material_in_region_mm3` and `touches_final_material` (null
when `final.stl` is missing or not a closed solid), `loader_error` (status `invalid`) and `load_region_name` for a solid hint.

The report and the notes say what they cannot show: whether the marks suit the part is the judgment of the owner; the
mirror plane is y = 0 and the design space may not be symmetric about it (`design_symmetric_about_y0`);
the YAML on disk may differ from the run (`labels_match_run`).

### 21.5 MCP tools and the script

- `run_history(root=None, depth=2, limit=20, detail=False)` (default root: the work folder), `compare_runs(run_a, run_b=None,
  check_labels=None, variants=None)` and `marks_to_hints(marks, run_dir=None, out_dir=None, options=None, overwrite=False, detail=False,
  yaml_path=None)` (default run: the last run of the server; the reply is `short_report` unless `detail` is true, and
  `hints.json` always holds the full report). They sit in one block next to `list_runs`. `list_runs` stays the cheap list
  and reads no metrics (its one change is the mark of a refused run, section 24.1, P9-19). Relative paths start at the work folder. The tools add `*_rel` keys (`root_rel`, `run_dir_rel`,
  `out_dir_rel`, `yaml_rel`, `report_rel`). A wrong input gives `{"ok": false, "error": ...}`. The text of the tools gives facts and
  options; it has no habitual must or never.
- After the hint, the agent starts the rerun with `run_topopt(yaml_rel, out_dir=...)`, then `compare_runs`.
- Script: `python -m topopt.feedback history ROOT [--depth N] [--limit N] [--detail]`,
  `compare RUN_A RUN_B [--check-labels auto|yes|no]`, `hints RUN_DIR MARKS [--out DIR] [--overwrite] [--no-check] [--remove
  keep_out|skip] [--add solid|skip] [--radius-scale F] [--no-protect] [--no-clip]`. It prints the JSON and exits 0, or prints
  `error: ...` and exits 1. `history` has `--limit N` (default 20; 0 = all); `hints` has `--yaml PATH` and `--detail` (the
  short reply is the default).
- `tools/check_hints.py RUN_DIR MARKS.json HINTS_DIR [--make]` checks a hints folder from the files on disk (the YAML loads,
  the STLs are closed, centres and radii, labels, hashes of the inputs before and after).

## 22. Solid regions, the filter rule and the minimum member size (added with A3a)

Section 22a is A3a: `regions.solid`, `settings.filter_solid_neighbours` and `settings.min_member_mm`
(backlog B-088, B-049 and the mapping of B-090). Section 22b is A3b (the eroded projection, B-044). Sections 16 to 21 are in this file. Do not renumber.

### 22a. Keys, labels, facts and outputs

**`regions.solid`** (optional list of STL files, like `fixed`). A voxel of a solid region is frozen at
density 1. It has the label `LOAD` (3) and the load id -1: it is a load region that no load case uses.
Every code that reads the labels `FIXED` or `LOAD` works as before (the model, the filter, the post-process of
this branch). The nodes of a solid voxel are free (no clamp) and carry no force.

The mesh step treats a solid region as a frozen body. `run.json` `region_files.solid` lists the solid STL files, and
`post.region_paths` returns them with the load regions, after them, as the old form lists them (the key is
`solid:<file>`). So the SDF smoothing of C1 (`mesh_method: sdf`) keeps the exact shape of a solid body, the exact
interface step of C2 (section 23, `_drop_floating`) does not remove a piece of a solid body that its cuts split off,
and `region_checks` reports the solid region like a load region (`load:solid:<file>`). Without these two lines the
final volume of the test case was 368.7 mm3 instead of 518.5 mm3, and a solid body that touches no fixed or load
region was removed (merge patch `a3a-x-c1c2`).

- Priority when regions overlap: keep_out > fixed > load > solid > design. A voxel in a load region and in a
  solid region keeps the load. A voxel in a fixed region and in a solid region is `FIXED`.
- The grid is the bounding box of all STLs, solid STLs included.
- A solid STL that has no voxel at this voxel size is an error (the same rule as every region). A solid STL
  that a region of higher priority covers completely is not an error: its count of voxels that stay solid is 0.
- An old YAML (a load region that no load case uses) gives the same labels, forces, fixed dofs, filter and run
  as the same body in `regions.solid`. `tools/solid_vs_load.py YAML` shows this for one problem.
- `regions_builder.py` and the `part-to-topopt` skill write a `solid` body as `regions.solid`. `run.json`
  `regions.solid` lists the file names (a missing key is an empty list).

**Facts about solid regions** (never an error). `voxelize(config, facts)` fills `facts["solid"]` and
`Problem.region_facts["solid"]` holds it (`null` or missing without `regions.solid`):

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stl_voxels` | Voxels of all solid STLs together. |
| `voxels` | Solid voxels that stay solid (label `LOAD`, load id -1). |
| `inside_design_stl`, `outside_design_stl` | Of `voxels`: in the design STL, and not in it (they add material to the part). |
| `in_fixed`, `in_load`, `in_keep_out` | Voxels of the solid STLs that take the label of a region of higher priority (`in_keep_out`: removed). Each voxel counts once, for the region that wins, so `stl_voxels = voxels + in_fixed + in_load + in_keep_out`. The counts are read from the final labels, so a cut that only the labels hold (an interface cutter of section 23) is in `in_keep_out` too. |
| `in_two_solid_stls` | Voxels that two solid STLs share. |
| `regions` | For each solid STL: `name` (file stem), `stl_voxels`, `voxels`, `thickness_voxels`. |

`topopt check` prints one line `solid regions: ...` and, with `--json`, the dict as `solid_regions`. A solid
region with fewer than 30 voxels, or less than about 3 voxels across, gives the same warning as a load region.
`topopt run` writes the same line to `run.log`. `voxel_counts["load"]` of `check` counts the solid voxels too (they
have the label `LOAD`): `solid_regions.voxels` is the solid part of it, and `load_regions` lists the real load regions.

**`settings.filter_solid_neighbours`** (`density_one` default, or `ignore`). The rule of the density filter
for the voxels with the labels `FIXED` and `LOAD` (solid regions included):

- `density_one` (the rule of all earlier versions): a solid voxel in the filter radius counts as a neighbour with
  density 1. `rho_tilde = F @ x + b`, where `b` holds the weight share of the solid neighbours.
- `ignore` (the rule of the pipeline): a solid voxel leaves both the numerator and the denominator. Each row of
  `F` is renormalised over design voxels, so `b = 0` and every row of `F` sums to 1. A design voxel next to a
  solid region is not pulled to solid.

`topopt check` (`solid_pull` in `--json`) and `topopt run` (`run.log`) show what the default rule does: one line
`solid pull: N of M design voxels (p percent) have a filtered density above 0.1 from solid neighbours alone (rule
density_one); the largest is X. settings.filter_solid_neighbours: ignore removes this pull`. The numbers are `b`
of the filter, computed without a matrix (a convolution with the hat kernel). `solid_pull` is
`{"rule", "design_voxels", "threshold": 0.1, "voxels_above", "share_above", "b_max", "solid_voxels"}`; with `ignore`
the line says `solid pull: none (rule ignore: ...)`. It is a fact; the run goes on.

The rule changes only `build_filter(labels, h, radius, solid_neighbours, pad_void=False)` and `make_filter` with the same arguments. The projection, the volume and the
sensitivities are as before (the chain rule uses `F^T` only). With the default value the filter is bit-equal
to the filter before A3a (commit 7555b19).

**The filter of the run is an FFT convolution (#333).** The optimizer, the perimeter term, the fine pass and the robust modes get
`F`, `F^T` and `b` from `filter.make_filter`: `F @ x` is the hat-kernel convolution of the design densities (zero outside the design
voxels) divided by the weight sum of each design voxel, and `F^T @ y` is the convolution of `y` divided by the weight sum. Both run on
a grid padded by `ceil(R)` voxels on each side and rounded up to a fast FFT length (`filter.fft_shape`), so the convolution is linear,
not circular. `F` and `F^T` are `scipy.sparse.linalg.LinearOperator` objects: `@` takes a vector or a block of columns, and `.T` works.
No matrix is stored. A value of the convolution below half of the smallest kernel weight is set to 0, so the zeros of `b` are the
zeros of the matrix (a design voxel with no solid voxel inside the radius has `b = 0` exactly). One exception: when R is within
rounding of a lattice distance (for example 2.1 mm / 0.3 mm = 7.000000000000001 voxels), the smallest weight is about 1e-15, below
the FFT rounding; then `b` can be about 1e-16 where the matrix has 0, and the other way. The results do not change. The weight sums and `b` agree with
`build_filter` (the matrix, kept as the reference) to rounding: `tests/test_fft_filter.py` compares `F @ x`, `F^T @ y`, blocks, `.T`
and `b` to 1e-12 for both solid rules, with and without `pad_void`, on six grids (radii 0.6 to 7.3 voxels). `filter.filtered_density`
gives `max(F @ x + b, 0)`: the FFT rounding can give -1e-16 where the matrix gives 0, and `rho**penal` of a negative number is NaN
for a non-integer `penal`. A problem with no design voxel gets the empty matrix of `build_filter`. `pad_void` is on only with `settings.robust: wall` (section 22b); with it
off the arrays are those of the code before #328. The default does not change in A3a. A change of the default is its own
small PR with a new baseline number.

**`settings.min_member_mm`** (optional number > 0, mm). The smallest member that the author wants. It derives the
filter radius by one rule (`topopt/members.py`): `filter_radius = RADIUS_PER_MEMBER * min_member_mm`, with the
constant and the reason in section 22a "The rule" below. It is an estimate, not a guarantee.

- An explicit `settings.filter_radius` wins. `Settings.filter_radius_source` is `default`, `settings`,
  `min_member_mm` or `wall` (`settings.robust: wall`, section 22b: the wall rule sets the radius and `min_member_mm`
  is only reported). The value in `Settings.filter_radius` is always the radius that the run uses.
- Facts with options (they are in `warnings` of `check_data`, in `run.log` with the prefix `warning:`, and in
  `derived.filter.facts`). None of them stops a run:
  - both keys are set and differ by more than 1 percent: the explicit radius is used; the options are to remove
    one key or to keep both;
  - `min_member_mm` is less than 2 voxels: the options are a smaller voxel size, a larger request, or to accept
    the grid limit;
  - the derived radius is not above one voxel: the filter has no neighbour to average with.
- The filter is an FFT convolution (#333, above), so its memory follows the padded grid of the FFT (each side `n + 2 ceil(R)`,
  rounded up to a fast length), not the stencil of about `4/3 pi R^3` weights (R in voxels). `check` adds `derived.filter.size`:
  `radius_voxels`, `entries_per_row` (the weights of the kernel), `method` (`"fft"`), `design_voxels`, `fft_shape`, `fft_cells`,
  and the estimated memory of the setup and of the run, each in bytes and GiB (`build_peak_bytes_estimate`, `held_bytes_estimate`;
  one model, so the two are equal). The model is `members.FILTER_BYTES_PER_PADDED_CELL` = 56 bytes for each cell of the padded grid
  (the kernel transform that stays, and the field, its transform and its inverse of the setup or of one apply) plus
  `members.FILTER_BYTES_PER_DESIGN_VOXEL` = 24 bytes for each design voxel (the weight sums and `b`, and the copies of the design
  values in an apply). Measured on Linux on 2026-10-27 (peak RSS above the process, six grids of 0.18 to 8 million cells, R 3 to 12
  voxels): 33 to 50 bytes a padded cell at the peak of the setup or of an apply, 12 to 23 bytes held between applies. A grid that is
  almost all design, with a small R, measured up to 61.4 bytes a padded cell (100 x 400 x 100, R 1.5, 96 % design), and at the same
  padded grid each design voxel added 14 bytes to the peak; the model is above every measured peak. `tests/test_fft_filter.py` checks
  that the numpy arrays stay under the model. The drone arm at 0.4 mm (395 x 150 x 48 voxels, 273,885 design voxels, R 9.4 voxels, a
  padded grid of 432 x 180 x 72) gets 0.30 GiB from the model (measured peak 0.20 GiB on a grid of the same shape with random labels),
  where the model of the matrix gave 24.5 GiB held and 52.5 GiB at its build. The filter is part of the memory estimate of `check` (`memory_estimate`, with
  `filter_build_peak_bytes` and `filter_held_bytes`) and of the voxel guard of `regions_builder.check_yaml`:
  the estimate is grid arrays + sparse factor + the filter.
  One warning with an option (a larger voxel size) appears when the filter alone is above the RAM of the machine, or when it
  makes the estimate go above it. `topopt run` writes the filter size and the memory estimate (and the warning)
  to `run.log` before the first iteration; the run goes on. It is a fact, not a block.

**Outputs** (all from `topopt.members.filter_report`, so they agree):

`derived.filter` in `check_data`, `topopt check --json`, the MCP `check_problem` and `run.json`, and the same dict
as `filter` in `result/metrics.json`:

```json
"filter": {"radius_mm": 7.508, "radius_source": "min_member_mm", "solid_neighbours": "density_one",
           "min_member_mm": 4.0, "min_member_radius_mm": 7.508, "min_feature_mm": 7.508,
           "min_feature_note": "walls of about 4 mm survive; rods need about 7.03 mm (1.76 x min_member_mm) (continuum values, interior of the design space; thinner ones vanish). The grid sets a floor of about one voxel (1 mm). A skin at a free face of the design space can be about half as thin (2 mm for a wall)",
```
