```json
           "min_member_rule": "filter_radius = 1.877 * min_member_mm",
           "min_member_note": "estimate, not a guarantee: a filter and a projection do not set a minimum member size. It sets the interior members: a skin at a free face of the design space can be about 1 voxel. Measure the thickness of the final part",
           "size": {"radius_voxels": 7.508, "entries_per_row": 1791, "method": "fft", "design_voxels": 1828,
                    "fft_shape": [60, 48, 36], "fft_cells": 103680,
                    "build_peak_bytes_estimate": 5849952, "build_peak_gib_estimate": 0.01,
                    "held_bytes_estimate": 5849952, "held_gib_estimate": 0.01},
           "facts": []}
```

`min_member_mm`, `min_member_radius_mm`, `min_member_rule` and `min_member_note` are `null` or missing when the key
is not set. `min_feature_mm` is `max(voxel_size, radius_mm)`, the same number as `derived.min_feature_mm`. It is the
size of the filter, kept for old readers. It is not the size of the smallest member: a hat filter at projection level
0.5 keeps a wall from 0.5328 R and a rod from 0.936 R. `min_feature_note` says what that means, in mm, for the radius of
the run (the same text is `derived.min_feature_note`, the `min feature:` line of `check` and the line in `run.log`). With
`min_member_mm` it says what the request gets ("walls of about 4 mm survive; rods need about 7.03 mm (1.76 x
min_member_mm)"); without it, from what size walls and rods survive. The values are for the interior of the design
space; a skin at a free face can be about half as thin (not with `settings.robust: wall`, section 22b: the filter is padded
there, the text says that a wall at a face is as thick as an inner wall, and `min_member_rule` and `min_member_note` are
left out). With `settings.robust: wall` the dict has one more key, `wall_rule` (section 22b), and `radius_source` is `wall`.
`size` is in `derived` when the grid is known. `topopt check` prints a line `filter: ...` after `min feature:`,
and the facts as `warning:` lines.

**The rule** (`topopt/members.py`, `RADIUS_PER_MEMBER = 1.877`):

    filter_radius = 1.877 * min_member_mm

- Reason. At projection level 0.5 a hat filter keeps a thin wall of thickness t only when t > 0.5328 R (a
  continuum value: the centre value of a plate). So a wall of the requested thickness just survives at
  R = t / 0.5328 = 1.877 t. A rod survives only when its diameter is above 0.936 R, so the rule removes a thin
  rod of the request size (it needs 1.76 t). The other option, the rod rule R = 1.068 t, is cheaper (R is 43
  percent smaller, the filter matrix is 5 to 8 times smaller) but its measured 5th percentile is 38 to 48
  percent below the request. The pipeline used a grid search (R = 3.75 mm for a 4 mm gate at its own eta_e 0.55)
  and gives no formula. That value is context only.
- It is an estimate, not a guarantee. A filter and a projection do not set a minimum member size. The eroded
  projection (B-044, section 22b) is the tool for that.
- Measured error (`docs/a3a-min-member-calibration.json`, `tools/calibrate_min_member.py`). One case: a bracket of
  48 x 24 x 16 voxels at 1 mm, volume fraction 0.3, two load cases, 150 iterations, requests of 2, 2.5 and 3 mm
  through `settings.min_member_mm`. Local thickness of the density 0.5 material (voxel level, bias about 0.25
  voxel: a wall of n voxels measures n - 0.25). Interior = at least 2 voxels from the free faces of the design
  space.

  | Request | R (voxels) | Interior p5 | Interior p1 | Interior median | Interior share below request |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 2 mm | 3.75 | 1.75 mm (-12 %) | 1.75 mm | 2.88 mm | 12 % |
  | 2.5 mm | 4.69 | 1.94 mm (-22 %) | 1.75 mm | 3.25 mm | 9 % |
  | 3 mm | 5.63 | 2.75 mm (-8 %) | 2.17 mm | 3.75 mm | 12 % |

  In the interior the 5th percentile is 8 to 22 percent below the request (a part of this is the bias and the
  grid: one voxel is 33 to 50 percent of the request). The median is 25 to 44 percent above it. A sensitivity
  check at 2.5 mm gives the interior p5 of -15 percent (volume fraction 0.2) and +10 percent (0.45).
- Free faces. The filter has one side at a free face of the design space (no padding; `settings.robust: wall` pads it, section 22b), so a wall there survives
  from 0.2664 R, half of the interior value. In the calibration 70 to 74 percent of the design material lies in
  the 2 voxels next to a free face, its 1st and 5th percentile are 1 voxel, and 41 to 45 percent of all design
  material is thinner than the request. `min_member_mm` sets the interior member size, not a skin at a free face.
- Memory. The radius is large: the stencil has `4/3 pi R^3` weights (R in voxels), 251, 461 and 739
  in the calibration. Since #333 the filter is an FFT convolution and its memory follows the padded grid, not the
  stencil. `check` prints the size and the estimated memory (see above).
- A user who wants a smaller radius sets `filter_radius` (it wins over `min_member_mm`).

### 22b. Robust erosion projection, low-cost form (added with A3b)

**`settings.robust`** (`off` default, `eroded`, or `wall`: see "The wall rule" below) turns on the low-cost robust form, in the form of the pipeline:
one eroded and one nominal design, with the volume on the nominal design (`pp_core_final.py`: the module text at
lines 1-8, `densities` at 341-347, the mass on the nominal design and K on the eroded design at 495-503). The form
in the literature (Wang, Lazarov and Sigmund, 2011) puts the volume on the dilated design, to our knowledge. The
YAML words `true` and `false` also work (YAML 1.1 loads `on` and `off` as booleans). Any other value is an error.

One filtered field `rho_tilde = F x + b` (section 22a: the filter and its solid rule do not change) is projected
twice with the same tanh Heaviside function (`filter.heaviside_project`):

    nominal  rho_n = P(rho_tilde; beta, eta_n)    eta_n = 0.5
    eroded   rho_e = P(rho_tilde; beta, eta_e)    eta_e > eta_n

| Quantity | Design |
|---|---|
| Volume fraction, mass, the volume row | nominal |
| Snapshots (`it_NNNN.bin`), `preview.bin`, `final.stl`, the grayness | nominal |
| Stiffness `K`, the displacements `U`, the compliance of each case and its weighted sum (the objective) | eroded |
| The history curve (`history.jsonl` `compliance`), `compliance_initial`, the `unmet` lines of compliance limits | eroded |
| Compliance limits of the load cases (section 13) | eroded |
| Displacement, shift and tilt rows (section 31): the gradient and the value that the optimizer sees | eroded |
| `metrics.json` `rows[].value_end`, `g_end`, `met` (section 31) | nominal (from the solve after the last pass) |
| `metrics.json` `rows[].value_start`, `rows[].value_end_eroded` | eroded |
| `metrics.json` `compliance_final` and `stiffness_cases`, the dashboard final screen, the `verify` stiffness ratio, the run compare | nominal (from the solve after the last pass) |
| `metrics.json` `robust.compliance_eroded`, `robust.stiffness_cases_eroded` | eroded |
| `refine` stress (section 12) | nominal (it reads the snapshot) |

The curve and the final values are two designs. The curve shows what the optimizer minimised (the eroded design), and
`compliance_final` is the printed part (the nominal design). The nominal compliance is lower than the eroded one
(`c_e >= c_n`, see "The 3-design worst case" below), so the last point of the curve is above `compliance_final`. The
run log says this in its robust summary line. A script that calls `optimize.minimize` has no `finish_run`, so it gets
the eroded history and no nominal compliance; it can call `Model.solve(Model.stiffness(rho))` on the nominal `rho`.

Each pass has one solve (the eroded design), as in the default run. There is no dilated design: the form is the
"low-cost" one. Two things are new: the second projection (one array operation) and one solve of the nominal
design after the last pass, which gives the nominal compliance. The 3-design worst case (eroded, nominal and
dilated, one solve each, the maximum over them) is a later option and is not in this version. Its estimate: three solves for each pass, about 3 times the time of a default run (an estimate from the measured time of one pass; the 2-solve form without the nominal design is about 2 times).
For a compliance row the low-cost form is already the worst case of the three designs: the eroded density is never
above the nominal one, which is never above the dilated one, and the SIMP stiffness grows with the density, so
`c_e >= c_n >= c_d` (measured on 80 random designs at beta 1, 4, 8 and 16: the largest of `c_d - c_n` and `c_n - c_e`
is -0.0069, below 0). The maximum over the three compliances is always the eroded one, and the 3-solve
form gives the same objective and slope. A 3-design mode is useful only for rows that are not monotone in the
density: a stress, the displacement of a point, buckling.

**`settings.eta_eroded`** (optional number, `0.5 < eta_e < 1`). The default is `robust.ETA_ERODED_DEFAULT` =
**0.55** for `eroded`, from the calibration below. The key has an effect only with `settings.robust: eroded` or `wall` (default 0.7 with `wall`, item 2 of "The wall rule"). With
`robust: off` it gives a fact (`derived.robust.facts`), not an error.

**The wall rule: `settings.robust: wall`** (#328 step 2). The robust eroded form (everything above, the same loop, the same
solves, the same outputs) aimed at the wall of the print check, with three additions and one change of the filter. The mode is
never on by itself: the YAML names it.

1. The wall `w` is `print.min_wall_mm` (mm, section 32). The YAML must give it. Without it the loader raises a `UserError`:
   `'settings.robust' is wall, and 'print.min_wall_mm' is not set`, with the options "set print.min_wall_mm" and "set
   settings.robust to eroded". `Settings.wall_mm` holds the value (a record; it is not in the effective settings of a checkpoint:
   the radius and `eta_e` that it gave are).
2. `eta_e` is `settings.eta_eroded` when the YAML gives it, else **0.7** (`robust.WALL_ETA_DEFAULT`). `robust: eroded` keeps its
   default 0.55. `eta_e_source` is `settings`, `wall_rule` (the default of this mode) or `default` (eroded).
3. The filter radius is `R = max(w / L(eta_e), 1.5 voxels)`, with `L(eta_e)` the width of the nominal design (filtered value 0.5 or
   more) of the thinnest wall that survives the eroded design, in radii, for the 3D hat kernel. `members.nominal_width_per_radius`
   computes it, with no table: the thinnest design wall `a` whose centre reaches `eta_e` is `robust.plate_limit_per_radius`
   (`2u - 2u^3 + u^4 = eta_e`, `u = a / 2R`), and the filtered value at the distance `x` from its centre is `Q(x + u) - Q(x - u)`,
   `Q(t) = t - t^3 + t^4 / 2` for `0 <= t <= 1` (odd in `t`, `Q = 1/2` from 1); `L = 2x` where that value is 0.5. Values:
   0.4061, 0.5665, 0.6868, 0.7885, 0.8819, 0.9754 at `eta_e` 0.55, 0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75, 0.8 (the step 1 theory script gives
   0.406, 0.566, 0.687, 0.789, 0.882, 0.976 on a grid of 3e-4 R; `tests/test_wall_rule.py` checks both). So `R = 1.2 / 0.7885 =
   1.522 mm` at `w` 1.2 mm and the default `eta_e`; 1.5 voxels is the existing default radius, and it is the floor (`floor_wins`
   in the record, with a fact that names the voxel size at which the rule would set the radius). An explicit
   `settings.filter_radius` wins, as it wins over `min_member_mm` (`radius_source` is `settings`, a fact gives the radius that the rule
   would have set and the nominal wall that survives with the radius in use). `settings.min_member_mm` is only reported
   in this mode (a fact; `min_member_rule` and `min_member_note` are left out of `derived.filter`). The radius follows the grid of the run
   (`members.radius_for_grid`): a fine pass computes `max(w / L, 1.5 voxels)` again for its voxel (section 24.6), so the record of the
   fine run states the radius that it uses. An explicit `settings.filter_radius` stays in mm.
4. The density filter is **padded with void** (`build_filter(..., pad_void=True)`, `make_filter(..., pad_void=True)`), in this mode only. Every neighbour that is not
   a design voxel or a solid voxel counts as void in the weights: outside the design space, outside the grid, a keep-out region.
   The entries of `F` are the same voxels as without the padding; only the divisor of each row changes (the sum of the whole
   kernel, so a row near a face or a keep-out region sums to less than 1). Solid voxels (`FIXED`, `LOAD`, `regions.solid`) keep their rule
   of section 22a and are never void: `density_one` counts them with density 1 (through `b`), `ignore` leaves them out of the sum
   and out of the weights. Without the padding the filter renormalises over the design space, a face acts as a mirror, and a wall on
   a face survives the erosion at half of the inner thickness (step 1: the share of the surface area under 1.2 mm was 4.145 percent
   with the default settings, and 0.000 percent with the wall rule). With the padding a wall at a face is as thick as an inner wall
   (`tests/test_wall_rule.py`: the profile of a face wall equals the profile of the same inner wall to 1e-12). The memory of the filter
   does not change: the FFT filter gets the weight sum as the sum of the whole kernel minus the convolution of the dropped
   neighbours, on the same padded grid, and `members.FILTER_BYTES_PER_PADDED_CELL` stays as it is. `solid_pull` (section 22a) reads the same
   divisor (`solid_pull(..., pad_void=True)`), so the check line agrees with the filter that runs.

The mode inherits the stops and facts of `eroded`: a stress limit or `buckling.min_factor` stops the run at the start (the texts
say `settings.robust is wall`), and the solver and beta facts apply. `topopt check` and the run log print the wall rule: the
`filter:` line gives the radius, where it came from (`w / L` and 1.5 voxels), `eta_e`, the padding and the filter size line (entries, build
peak and held memory); the `min feature:` line says that a wall at a face is as thick as an inner wall and does not print that a skin
at a free face can be about half as thin (with the padding it is not true); the `robust:` line says `wall rule`. The measured price on
the hook example (voxel 0.5 mm, 564,298 active voxels, `w` 1.2 mm, 80 passes, solver `gpu-mg` on one Intel Arc iGPU of a shared Linux
x86_64 host; step 1 was a research prototype of the padding that is not in main; issue #328, comment 6431145811). Default settings (robust
off, R 0.75 mm = 1.5 voxels): area of walls under 1.2 mm 4.145 percent, compliance 1.253, 636 s, peak memory 5.51 GiB. Wall rule (eroded,
eta_e 0.7, R 1.521 mm, padded filter): 0 percent, compliance 1.352 (+7.9 percent), 679 s (1.07 times), peak 4.86 GiB; 1 body; mass 27.13 g in
both. The cause of the lower memory was not measured. Reproduced with the code of this section (`robust: wall`, the same hook, `gpu-mg`, Intel
Arc): 0 percent, compliance 1.3524, 1 body, 27.13 g, peak 5.18 GiB (1,187 s, on a busier host).

*Known effect of the padding.* With the padding less of the part lies on the faces of the design space. On that hook the share of the
part surface within 0.75 mm of a design-space face went from 31.0 percent (default) to 24.9 percent (wall rule); nothing came loose (1 body,
the load path joined). A mounting face on the envelope can then sit lower: check the result at that face, or make that face a solid region.

*Fact when the mode is not used.* `print.min_wall_mm` is set in the YAML and `settings.robust` is `off` or `eroded`: `derived.robust.facts`
(and `warnings`) has one fact: the optimizer does not aim at this wall, the print check measures it after the run, and `settings.robust: wall`
would aim at it (the radius it derives, the padding, the step 1 numbers above). Options: set `settings.robust` to `wall`, or keep the
setting and read the wall check after the run. It is a fact: nothing stops and nothing changes.

**What a member needs.** A member survives the eroded design when its filtered value reaches `eta_e` at its
centre. For a hat filter `w = R - d` (continuum values, `robust.plate_limit_per_radius`): a wall needs a
thickness above `0.5328 R` for `eta` 0.5, `0.5948 R` for 0.55 and `0.66 R` for 0.6 (`2u - 2u^3 + u^4 = eta`, `u = t/2R`); a flat face moves in by
`0.0501 R` at `eta` 0.55. The eroded density at `rho_tilde` 0.5 is 0.31 at beta 8 and 0.49 at beta 1 for `eta_e`
0.55: the effect grows with beta, so a run that stops at a low beta has little erosion (a fact is given).

**Solvers.** The loop passes the eroded density to `Model.stiffness`, so every model that builds its element
stiffness from the density it is given works by construction. `robust.ROBUST_SOLVERS` lists the solvers that a parity
test covers (`tests/test_robust.py`: the compliance and the slope of a fixture equal those of a
`scipy.sparse.linalg.spsolve` of the same eroded system, on every platform, for the solvers that the platform has):
`cholesky`, `pardiso`, `amg`, and `gpu-mg` (G1e: `tests/test_gpu_mg_robust.py`, on an OpenCL device; the bounds are the 1e-8 of
`tests/test_gpu_mg.py`; measured on pocl with the fixture of the test, beta 1 and 8: the compliance differs by 2.9e-10 at most
and the slope by 6.3e-10 at most relative to its largest entry, both in case C; source: the docstring of that test). For any other solver robust mode gives a **warning fact** (`derived.robust.facts`,
`topopt check` text and JSON, `run.json`, the run log with the prefix `warning:`) and the run goes on. The fact says
which solvers the test covers, that the step works by construction for this solver but has no parity test, and the
options: use a tested solver; run `topopt verify` after the run (when your version has it); or add the solver to
`ROBUST_SOLVERS` together with a parity test. It is not a refusal: the step can work. A new solver adds its name to
the list in the PR that adds its parity test. `gpu-mg` got robust mode with no code change for the form;
the parity test and the name in the list came with G1e. A robust `gpu-mg` run has one more line in `gpu_mg.jsonl` than passes: kind
`trial`, the solve of the nominal design at the end (`robust.finish_run`), with the iteration of the last pass. This holds for a resume
that runs no pass too (the checkpoint of the last pass is `complete`): the run writer gets that pass and step first, and the resume drops
the old line of this solve, so the file equals the file of a run that was not stopped.

**Objectives and rows.** Every objective and row that a YAML can reach on this base is a compliance row, a volume row
or (A5, section 31) a displacement, shift or tilt row. The compliance rows and the A5 rows read `U`, so they use
`rho_stiff` (the eroded density in robust mode, `rho` in a default run). The volume row uses `rho` (the nominal
density), as above. The A5 rows are linear in `U`: they are the displacement of the eroded design, as the alignment rows of
the pipeline. A row that is written in Python (section 13) sees both: `DesignPoint.rho` is the nominal
density, `DesignPoint.rho_stiff` is the density that `U` belongs to. `Response.wrt` has a new value `"rho_stiff"`:
the slope is with respect to `rho_stiff`, and the chain rule uses the slope of the eroded projection. In a default
run `"rho_stiff"` is the same as `"rho"`, bit for bit. `DesignPoint.stiffness_derivative` is the slope with respect
to `rho_stiff` (it equals the slope to `rho` in a default run). A row that uses `U` (an adjoint) therefore returns
`wrt="rho_stiff"` and reads `point.rho_stiff`; a row that mixes an explicit `rho` term and an adjoint term (the KS
stress row of PR #22) has two slopes to two densities and one `wrt` cannot give both. The pipeline moved its stress
rows from the eroded to the nominal design, with their own solve, because the KS value chased grey voxels of the
eroded design (KB `methods/robust-erosion-projection`). So a stress row in robust mode needs one of: (a)
`wrt="rho_stiff"` on the stress `Response` and `point.rho_stiff` in both terms (the stress of the eroded design, one
solve per pass); (b) a second solve of the nominal design for the stress rows, with its own nominal stiffness
derivative (about twice the time for each pass). Neither is built. Robust mode with a stress limit therefore stops at
the start of `run` with a `UserError` that gives the facts and the options (robust off, or remove the stress limits);
`topopt check` gives the same text as a warning and exits with 0 (`robust.stress_stop_text`; section 17). It is the one
hard stop of robust mode: the step cannot work, because the gradient of the stress row would be wrong with no error.

**Facts with options** (in `check_data` `warnings`, `derived.robust.facts`, `run.log` with the prefix `warning:`;
none of them stops a run):

- `min_member_mm` is less than 2 voxels: the eroded threshold cannot tell members of that size apart, the grid
  sets the member size. Options: a smaller voxel size, a larger request, or to accept the grid limit.
- the wall that the eroded design keeps (`derived.robust.wall_limit_mm`) is below 2 voxels: the options are
  `min_member_mm`, a larger `filter_radius`, or a smaller voxel size.
- the highest beta of `beta_schedule` leaves the eroded density at `rho_tilde` 0.5 above 0.4 (so little erosion).
- `settings.eta_eroded` is set and `settings.robust` is off.
- the solver has no parity test (see "Solvers"): a warning fact, the run goes on.
- `settings.min_member_mm` sets the radius (no explicit `filter_radius`): the radius rule `1.877 x min_member_mm` is for
  the threshold 0.5. The fact gives the wall that the eroded design keeps (`0.5948 R` for eta_e 0.55, about 1.12 times
  the request, continuum estimate) against the request, and the option `settings.filter_radius = x min_member_mm` with
  `x = 1 / plate_limit_per_radius(eta_e)` (1.681 for 0.55), which makes the wall limit equal to the request. No
  constant is changed in robust mode: the value 1.681 is a continuum estimate, and a run has not calibrated it.

**`derived.robust`** (`check_data`, `topopt check --json`, the MCP `check_problem`, `run.json`):
`{"mode": "off", "on": false, "facts": []}` for a default run. In robust mode also `eta_n`, `eta_e`,
`eta_e_source` (`default`, `settings`, or `wall_rule`), `solves_per_step` (1), `extra_solves` (1), `note`, `wall_limit_mm`,
`wall_limit_voxels`, `wall_limit_nominal_mm` (the continuum estimates for the plate), `beta_max`,
`eroded_at_nominal_threshold`, `time_factor`, `solver` and `solver_tested` (true, false, or null when the solver is
not known), and `radius_for_request_mm` when the radius rule fact applies. With `settings.robust: wall`: `mode` is `wall`,
`padded_filter` is true and `nominal_wall_mm` is `L(eta_e) * R` (the width of the nominal design of the thinnest wall that
survives); the numbers of the rule (`wall_mm`, `wall_source`, `eta_e`, `nominal_width_per_radius`, `radius_from_wall_mm`,
`voxel_floor_mm`, `radius_rule_mm`, `floor_wins`, `rule`, `padded`) are the block `wall_rule` of `derived.filter` (section 22a) and
of `filter` in `metrics.json`. Those keys are absent in every other mode, so the records of the other runs keep their keys. `topopt check` prints the `robust:` lines
and the facts (`warning: ...`); the run log has the same.

**Time estimate** (`cli.estimate_seconds(..., robust_mode)`). The time per pass is the same as in a default run
(the second projection is an array operation; measured, plan section 7). The nominal solve at the end is one
more solve: `time_factor = (PASS_TIME_FACTOR * (iterations + 1) + EXTRA_SOLVES) / (iterations + 1)` with
`PASS_TIME_FACTOR = 1.0` and `EXTRA_SOLVES = 1` (`robust.py`, from the hook runs in
`docs/a3b-hook-comparison.json`). `derived.time_estimate_s` includes it. It is an estimate.

**Outputs.**

- `robust.json` in the run folder (robust mode only, written once after the last pass): `on`, `mode`, `eta_n`,
  `eta_e`, `eta_e_source`, `compliance_eroded`, `compliance_nominal` (weighted sums over the cases),
  `compliance_cases_eroded`, `compliance_cases_nominal`, `robust_s`, `robust_parts_s` (`projection`,
  `nominal_solve`), `run_s`. `robust_s` is the measured time of the work that only robust mode does: the second
  projection with its slope (all passes) and the solve of the nominal design. It is a part of `run_s`, not an
  addition. `RunWriter.write_robust`.
- `result/metrics.json` `robust` (section 5): `{"on": false}` for a default run. In robust mode: `on`, `mode`,
  `eta_n`, `eta_e`, `eta_e_source`, `compliance_nominal`, `compliance_eroded`, `compliance_cases_*`, `robust_s`,
  `robust_parts_s`, `stiffness_cases_eroded` (N/mm of each case for the eroded design), `note`, `run_time_s` (the
  total run time of the metrics), `padded_filter` (true; only with `wall`) and `complete` (false when the run ended before `robust.json`). In robust mode the
  keys `compliance_final` and `stiffness_cases` of section 5 are the **nominal design** (the part that you print);
  the `note` says so. The eroded values are `compliance_eroded` and `stiffness_cases_eroded`; the history curve, the
  `unmet` lines of compliance limits and `compliance_initial` are eroded values. Readers of `compliance_final` and
  `stiffness_cases` (the dashboard final screen, the `verify` stiffness ratio of PR #21, the run compare of PR #28)
  therefore get the printed part, with no change in those branches.
- The run log and the CLI output: after the last pass `robust: eta_n 0.5, eta_e ...; compliance nominal ..., eroded
  ...` and `robust: ... s in the robust part ... of ... s run time`; the first line also says that the curve (history)
  is the eroded design and that `compliance_final` and the stiffness are the nominal design. After `done in ...`
  one line with all records: `robust: summary: on, eta_n ..., eta_e ...; compliance nominal ..., eroded ...; ... s in
  the robust part; total run time ... s; compliance_final is the nominal design, the history curve the eroded design`
  (the total run time of `metrics.json`, post-process included).

**Default path.** The wall rule changes nothing outside its mode. `robust: off` and `robust: eroded` build the filter with
`pad_void=False`, the code path of the unpadded filter (the arrays equal those of main b274485 bit for bit: `tests/test_wall_rule.py`
pins the sha256 of the arrays of a small case), and the golden test of section 27.4 passes unchanged. A short hook run with
`robust: eroded` and `min_member_mm` 4 (voxel 2 mm, 12 passes, pardiso, 1 thread) on main b274485 and on the branch gave the same
sha256 for `final.stl`, `labels.bin`, `history.jsonl` without its time fields, `robust.json` without its time fields and the filter arrays.
With `robust: off` (or no key) the code path is the same as before A3b: `Model.robust` is
`None`, `stiffness_density` returns `rho` itself, and `"rho_stiff"` collapses to `"rho"`. The hook at 1.2 mm and 1
thread gives `compliance_final = 1.3891411615538347`, and every snapshot, `final.stl`, `preview.bin` and the golden
values of `tests/test_multirow_mma.py` are bit-equal to the base (`72a9b73`, PR #30; the default path is the same as at 754fefe). A test and the hook run show it.

**Calibration of eta_e** (the mesh-free voxel fixture `tools/calibrate_eta_voxel.py`, data in
`docs/a3b-eta-voxel-fixture.json`; the run values from `tools/calibrate_min_member.py --robust-eta`, data in
`docs/a3b-eta-calibration.json`). The fixture builds a wall or a round rod as a 0/1 field on a voxel grid,
filters it with the real `build_filter`, and gives the thinnest member (whole voxels) whose centre value reaches
`eta`.

Thinnest whole-voxel member that survives the eroded design (fixture; R in voxels):

| R | eta_e 0.5 (nominal) | 0.55 | 0.6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.75 | wall 3, rod 4 | wall 3, rod 4 | wall 3, rod 5 |
| 4.69 | wall 3, rod 5 | wall 3, rod 5 | wall 4, rod 5 |
| 5.63 | wall 3, rod 6 | wall 4, rod 6 | wall 4, rod 6 |

Runs of the A3a bracket (section 22a: one bracket of 48 x 24 x 16 voxels, 1 mm voxels, volume fraction 0.3, two load
cases, 150 iterations with beta 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 from iteration 0, 40, 70, 100 and 130; requests 2, 2.5 and 3 mm,
`R = 1.877 * request`). Interior 5th percentile of the thickness of the nominal design. The measure gives `n - 0.25 mm`
for a wall of n voxels (bias 0.25 mm, A3a plan), so every row has the measured value and the value with the bias
corrected (+0.25 mm), each against the request. The last number of a cell is the share of the interior material below
the request (it uses the measured value, so it is biased high in every row alike: compare the rows):

| Request | off (A3a) | eta_e 0.55 | eta_e 0.6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 mm | 1.75 mm; 2.0 mm (0 %); 12 % | 2.62 mm; 2.87 mm (+44 %); 1 % | 2.75 mm; 3.0 mm (+50 %); 0 % |
| 2.5 mm | 1.94 mm; 2.19 mm (-12 %); 9 % | 2.75 mm; 3.0 mm (+20 %); 1 % | 2.75 mm; 3.0 mm (+20 %); 1 % |
| 3 mm | 2.75 mm; 3.0 mm (0 %); 12 % | 2.75 mm; 3.0 mm (0 %); 9 % | 3.38 mm; 3.63 mm (+21 %); 3 % |

With the bias on both sides, eta_e 0.55 changes the 5th percentile at 2 mm and 2.5 mm (one voxel more than the
request) and not at 3 mm (the same 3-voxel wall as without robust mode, 2.75 mm measured). At 3 mm the share below the
request is the evidence of the effect (12 to 9 percent). The nominal compliance is 6 percent (0.55) and 11 to 16
percent (0.6) above the A3a design.

The default is 0.55. It is the lower of the two candidates that keeps the request in the interior for all three
requests: the share of material below the request falls from 12, 9 and 12 percent to 1, 1 and 9 percent, at about half
of the compliance cost of 0.6 (0.6: 0, 1 and 3 percent). The pipeline used 0.55 too, but its own gates did not pass
for any pair of radius and eta_e (best margin -0.003, KB `capabilities/robust-erosion`), so that value is context and
not a proof. Scope of the evidence: one bracket, 1 mm voxels, volume fraction 0.3, a schedule that ends at beta 16
after 150 iterations. The default schedule ends at beta 8, where the erosion is weaker (the eroded density at
`rho_tilde` 0.5 is 0.31 at beta 8 and 0.17 at beta 16): on the hook with the default schedule and `min_member_mm` 3.6
the 5th percentile moved from 2.81 mm to 3.03 mm only (request 3.6 mm). `min_member_mm` keeps the A3a rule: under robust
mode the interior is thicker than the request (median +42 to +69 percent at 0.55); the robust-mode fact of
`topopt check` names the option `filter_radius = 1.681 x min_member_mm`. The skin at a free face stays thinner than the
request (16 to 35 percent of all design material is below it). Details: plan section 6.

**Gradient check** (`tests/test_robust.py`, `tools/robust_check.py`). Central finite differences on a small
fixture with solid voxels and the direct solver, at beta 1 and at the highest scheduled beta: the best-step error is
1e-8 to 1e-7 against the bound 1e-6 (measured noise floor, plan section 8). A wrong slope gives more than 1e-2; a test
shows that the check sees it.

**What this is not.** It is not a guarantee of a minimum member size, and not a full robust formulation: there is
no dilated design and no maximum over designs. For the same density field the compliance of the eroded design is not
below that of the nominal design (the eroded density is never above the nominal one). A member that the eroded threshold keeps is not always thicker than the request: free faces of
the design space have a filter on one side only (section 22a, "Free faces"), except in the wall rule, where the filter is padded with void
(see "The wall rule"). The wall rule is a continuum estimate as well: L(eta_e) is for an infinite plate and beta to infinity, and a rod needs more than a wall.

## 23. Exact interfaces and machining stock (added with C2)

A part often has surfaces that the optimizer cannot make: a round bore with an exact radius, a boss around it, a flat
face that a machine cuts later. An `interface` is an exact shape that the post step unites with the final mesh or cuts out of
it, after the smoothing. The shape is built with manifold3d, so a bore has its radius and a face has its position, not the voxel
staircase. With machining stock, the step makes two meshes: the as-printed mesh (`result/final.stl`, with stock left on each machined
surface) and the finished mesh (`result/nominal.stl`).
Code: `topopt/interfaces.py` (shapes, labels, the exact step, the measurement), `topopt/config.py` (the YAML block),
`topopt/voxelize.py` (labels), `topopt/smooth_sdf.py` (pins in the SDFs), `topopt/post.py` (`mesh_step`, `finish`),
`tools/check_final_stl.py`. Example: `examples/interfaces/`.

**YAML key `interfaces`.** Optional top-level list. It follows the block pattern of `settings`: unknown keys are an error, a
missing required key is an error. All lengths are in mm. The order of the list is the order of the boolean steps.

| `kind` | op | required keys | optional |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bore` | cut | `name`, `kind`, `point`, `axis`, `radius_mm`, `length_mm` | `stock_mm`, `full_surface` |
| `boss` | union | `name`, `kind`, `point`, `axis`, `radius_mm`, `length_mm` | `stock_mm`, `full_surface` |
| `tube` | union (ring) and cut (hole) | `name`, `kind`, `point`, `axis`, `radius_mm` (outer), `inner_radius_mm`, `length_mm` | `stock_mm`, `full_surface` |
| `face` | cut | `name`, `kind`, `point`, `normal` | `stock_mm`, `radius_mm`, `full_surface` (only with `radius_mm`) |
| `stl` | `union` or `cut` (key `op`) | `name`, `kind`, `file`, `op` | none |

```yaml
interfaces:
  - name: pin_bore          # unique
    kind: bore              # a cylinder that is cut out
    point: [28.0, 10.0, 20.0]   # the centre of the first end face
    axis: [0.0, 0.0, -1.0]      # the direction from `point` along the cylinder (any length, it is made a unit vector)
    radius_mm: 3.0          # the finished radius
    length_mm: 24.0
    stock_mm: 0.4           # default 0. The as-printed bore has the radius 3.0 - 0.4
  - name: mounting_face     # everything on the side of `normal` is cut away (inside the grid box and a margin)
    kind: face
    point: [2.0, 0.0, 0.0]      # a point on the finished plane
    normal: [-1.0, 0.0, 0.0]    # a unit vector (any length is made a unit vector)
    stock_mm: 0.5
  - name: end_face          # radius_mm (optional): cut only the disc of this radius about the line through `point` along `normal`
    kind: face
    point: [60.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    normal: [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    radius_mm: 35.0
  - name: lug
    kind: stl               # an exact union or cut of a closed STL solid. No stock.
    file: lug.stl           # relative to the YAML file
    op: union
```

- `point` and `axis` and `normal` are lists of 3 numbers. The loader makes `axis` and `normal` a unit vector. A zero `axis` or
  `normal` is an error with the fact (`interface 'x': 'axis' must not be the zero vector, got [0, 0, 0]`). `stock_mm` is 0 or more.
- A cylinder goes from `point` along `axis` for `length_mm`. A `tube` is a boss with a hole: outer radius `radius_mm`,
  inner radius `inner_radius_mm` (it must be less than `radius_mm`). It is two shapes: the ring (outer minus inner cylinder) is
  united, and the inner cylinder is cut with the other cuts. So the hole is free of material, also where the smooth mesh has
  material inside the ring (for example a web that crosses the tube). The two shapes are listed as `<name>` (ring) and
  `<name> (hole)` (the hole) in the labels and in `checks.keep_out`.
- A `face` without `radius_mm` cuts the whole half-space on the side of `normal`, inside the grid box (and the margin). So it cuts every
  region that reaches past the plane, also a fixed or load region (the label `KEEP_OUT` wins). With `radius_mm` (a number above 0) it cuts
  only the disc: the cylinder of that radius about the line through `point` along `normal`, from the plane (moved by the stock) to the
  grid box and the margin. Material outside the disc stays. A YAML without the key gives the same labels, meshes and metrics as before
  (`tests/test_interface_cuts.py`). `radius_mm` of a face is stored in `run.json` like the other keys.
- `full_surface` (true or false, default false) says that the surface of the interface must be complete: a bond socket, a bearing seat, a press fit,
  a sealing face. It is allowed on a `bore`, a `boss`, a `tube`, and a `face` with `radius_mm`. A `face` without `radius_mm` cuts a half-space and has
  no complete surface to measure; an `stl` solid has no surface that the tool measures. `true` on either is a loader error with the fact and the options
  (`'interfaces[0].full_surface' is true on a face with no 'radius_mm': ... Options: add 'radius_mm' ...`); `false` is accepted everywhere. A value that is not
  a bool is a loader error. `run.json` `interfaces` has `"full_surface": true` only for an entry that sets it: a run folder of a YAML without the key is bit-equal to before.
  See "A surface that must be complete" below.
- `stock_mm` of a `bore` must be less than `radius_mm`; of a `tube`, less than `inner_radius_mm`. Else the as-printed hole would not exist.
- An `stl` entry has no `stock_mm`. The loader gives an error that says so.
- A loader error gives the fact: the entry (`interfaces[2]`), the key, the value and the rule. Example:
  `'interfaces[0].stock_mm' is 3.5, not less than radius_mm 3.0: the as-printed bore would have no hole`.

**Shapes.** manifold3d builds each shape as a closed solid in float64, and the mesh is made float32. A cylinder is an inscribed
polygon with the vertices on the radius. The number of segments `n` is the smallest even number, at least 16, for which the chord sag
`r (1 - cos(pi / n))` is at most 0.002 mm (`n = ceil(pi / acos(1 - 0.002 / r))`). So a facet wall lies 0 to 0.002 mm inside the
radius, and the mean radius of the wall vertices is within `sag + 1e-4 mm` of the YAML radius (`sag` is the sag of that cylinder;
the 1e-4 mm is the float32 resolution of the file and the rounding). A `face` is exact to float32 (tolerance 1e-4 mm). The face
cutter is the grid box plus a margin of 2 mm plus the stock, cut at the plane. A face with `radius_mm` has a cylinder as cutter (the same facet rule
as a bore); it reaches 2 mm past the far corner of the grid box. `measure` and the expected area of such a face count only the triangles inside the disc.

**Stock.** The finished (nominal) shape has stock 0. The as-printed shape leaves the stock on the surface that a machine will cut:

| kind | as-printed shape |
|---|---|
| `bore` | radius `radius_mm - stock_mm` (a smaller hole) |
| `boss` | radius `radius_mm + stock_mm` |
| `tube` | outer radius `radius_mm + stock_mm`, inner radius `inner_radius_mm - stock_mm` |
| `face` | the plane moves `stock_mm` along `normal` (into the cut side: more material stays) |

Stock acts only on a surface that the interface makes. On a bore or a face, the stock has an effect only where the smooth mesh has
material there (for example in a boss wall). This is the fact of the method: nothing is added to the lattice.

**The exact step** (`interfaces.apply_step`, called by `post.mesh_step` after the method has made its mesh, in both methods):

1. The smooth mesh of the method (`sdf` or `blur`, section 19 or 9) is the base.
2. For each variant (as-printed; and nominal if any built-in interface has `stock_mm` above 0): the union shapes are united
   in the list order; then the keep-out regions are cut (see "A keep-out region wins"); then the cut shapes are subtracted in the
   list order. The volume change of each step is recorded.
3. A body that no frozen shape touches is removed, with this limit: the rule judges only (a) the pieces that the booleans split off
   the method mesh (a body that has no vertex in common with a body of the method mesh, or a piece of a method body that the
   booleans made two or more bodies) and (b) the bodies of the method mesh that lie within one fine voxel (`h / 4`, `UPSAMPLE`) of a
   union shape (the `sdf` step pins the union shapes, so it keeps an island next to one, and the exact union can leave it
   floating). Any other body of the method mesh stays, as the method left it: the same run with and without an interface gives the
   same bodies away from the interfaces. The frozen shapes are the fixed and load STL files
   (gap under 1e-3 mm) and the union interfaces (shared volume). If no judged body touches one, the largest judged body stays.
   The step logs one warning with the count and the volume, and `interfaces.bodies_removed` has them. This needs all fixed and load
   STL files; without them nothing is removed and the bodies are a fact in `stl_roundtrip.bodies`.
4. Each mesh is made clean for float32 (as section 19, step 8: float32 vertices, `Manifold.simplify(1e-5 mm)`).
5. Each file is loaded again from the bytes. The reload check is `smooth_sdf.stl_facts`: watertight, winding, bodies, open and non-manifold
   edges, zero-area faces. A file that is not one closed manifold with 0 zero-area faces gives one warning, and it is a fact in the record.
6. Any error in the step keeps the mesh of the method unchanged, logs one warning (`interface step failed, ...`), and gives
   `interfaces.applied: false` with the error text. The run does not stop. There is no `nominal.stl` then.

**A keep-out region wins over a union shape.** A boss, a tube ring or a union STL that overlaps a `regions.keep_out` STL does not
fill it: the label rule is `KEEP_OUT` over `LOAD` (section 3), and the exact step follows it. When the union shapes overlap the
keep-out regions by more than 1e-6 mm3, the step cuts the region STL files again after the unions and before the cuts of the
interfaces (in each variant); `interfaces.keep_out_cut` then has `files` and `removed_mm3`. If they do not overlap, nothing is cut
again (the method cut the regions already, and the mesh stays bit-equal). `voxelize` logs one warning with the voxel count when a union
shape overlaps a keep-out region ("the keep-out region wins"). A keep-out STL file that is missing at post time is a fact in the log:
the step cannot cut it, and a union shape can fill it.

Without stock there is one mesh: `final.stl` has the exact shapes (the as-printed and the nominal mesh are the same).
With stock, `final.stl` is the as-printed mesh and `nominal.stl` is the finished mesh. A `nominal.stl` of an older post-process of the
same folder is removed when the run has no stock. The existing keys `mass_final_g`, `volume_final_mm3`, `triangles`, `watertight`, the
`mesh` record and `preview.bin` refer to `final.stl` (as-printed). Consumers: the dashboard (`preview.bin`), `render` and `refine` read the as-printed `final.stl` (the
part that the printer makes), and the MCP `run_result` gives `final_stl` and, when the file exists, `nominal_stl`. `topopt verify`
(B2, section 16) reads `nominal.stl` when that file exists, and `final.stl` otherwise, because the stress check is for the part in
service. It records the file in `verify.json` (`run.verified_file`).

**Labels.** The optimizer sees the interfaces in the voxel labels (`voxelize`, the inside test of section 3, no new label code).
The label of an interface is the part that the as-printed and the nominal mesh have in common:

| interface | label | shape used |
|---|---|---|
| `bore`, `face`, `stl` with `op: cut` | `KEEP_OUT` (wins over `FIXED`, `LOAD`, `DESIGN`) | the as-printed shape (radius `r - stock`; plane moved by the stock) |
| `boss`, `tube`, `stl` with `op: union` | `LOAD` with load id -1: solid, no force (set after `DESIGN`, before the load regions, so a load region wins on overlap) | the nominal shape |

A union shape widens the grid like a region; a cut shape does not. A tube is a union (the ring, nominal shape) and a cut (the hole,
as-printed shape): the label of the hole is `KEEP_OUT`. If a shape holds no voxel at the voxel size, the labels ignore it
(one warning); the exact step still applies it. A union shape must touch the part: if the active voxels around it (6-connected) hold
no fixed voxel, the stiffness matrix is singular and no solver can run. `topopt check` then prints a warning with the fact, and
`topopt run` stops before the solve with a `UserError` that has the fact (the voxel counts) and the options (move the shape so that
it touches a design, fixed or load voxel, or remove it from `interfaces`). A boss or tube is the same as a load region that no load case uses (section 2), and a
bore or face is the same as a keep-out region with the same shape: tests compare the labels (`tests/test_interfaces.py`). When
the `regions.solid` key of A3a (B-088) merges, the boss label may go through it.
In the `sdf` method the same shapes are pinned in the SDFs: union shapes in the frozen SDF `U`, cut shapes in the cut SDF `Cs`
(`make_mesh_sdf(..., extra_frozen=, extra_cut=)`), so the smooth surface joins them. The booleans are not made there. In `blur`, the
labels give the staircase and the exact step cuts the exact shape out; where a boss meets the blurred part, the join lies on the
voxel staircase of the labels (not measured).

**What a cut takes from a frozen region (before the run).** The label `KEEP_OUT` wins over `FIXED` and `LOAD` (section 3), so a cut
takes the voxels of a frozen region that lie inside it. A bore through a bearing seat does this on purpose. A `face` that cuts through
a sleeve does not: it cuts the whole half-space (see above). `voxelize.taken_facts` counts it from the voxel masks that exist
before the labels are made (one boolean sum for each pair, no new voxelization). A cut is the cut step of an interface (a `bore`,
the hole of a `tube`, a `face`, an `stl` with `op: cut`) or a `regions.keep_out` STL. A frozen region is a fixed, load or solid region,
or a union interface (`boss`, the ring of a `tube`, an `stl` union). `problem.region_facts["taken"]`, the key `interface_taken` of
`topopt check --json` and of MCP `check_problem`, and the key `interface_taken` of `run.json` hold one entry for each pair that has
a voxel in both (the key is absent in `run.json`, and the list is empty in the check, if no cut takes a voxel):

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `cut`, `cut_kind` | the name of the cut (the keep-out region: the file name without extension) and its kind: `bore`, `tube hole`, `face`, `stl` or `keep-out region` |
| `region`, `region_role` | the frozen region (the load region name, the file name without extension, or the interface name) and its role: `fixed`, `load`, `solid` or `interface` |
| `voxels`, `region_voxels`, `share` | the voxels in both, the voxels of the region (its STL, or the union shape) and the ratio |
| `depth_mm` | how far the region goes past the cut surface; null for a `bore` and a `tube hole` (a hole exists to remove material) |
| `trim_mm` | the limit `max(stock_mm + voxel_size, 2 mm)` of the interface (a keep-out region has no stock); null with no depth |
| `bounded` | true for a `face` with `radius_mm` |
| `warn` | `depth_mm > trim_mm` |

The depth of a `face` is the largest signed distance of the STL vertices of the region past the plane through `point`
(the stock is part of the allowed trim, so it is not taken off). With `radius_mm` the vertices are not enough (the disc cuts only some
of them), so the depth is that of the centres of the taken voxels. For an `stl` cut and a keep-out region it is the largest depth of a
taken voxel inside the cut shape: the distance from its centre to the nearest voxel outside the shape (a distance transform of the
cut mask), less half a voxel. The limit 2 mm is under review: report the values that the
examples give. A bounded face that still takes a region deeply gets the same warning. The warning is a fact; the run goes on.
`topopt check` prints it as `warning: interface '<name>' (face, cut) takes N of M voxels (P %) of load region '<region>', up to D mm
past the plane (the trim limit is T mm). A face cuts everything on the side of its normal. Options: give the face a 'radius_mm' (a
bounded cut), move the plane, or accept the cut` (an `stl` cut: `... into the cut shape ... Options: move the cut shape or the
region, or accept the cut`; a keep-out region: `warning: keep-out region '<name>' takes ...`). Each pair also has one line
`interface cut:  <name> (<kind>) takes N of M voxels (P %) of <role> region '<region>', up to D mm past the plane` (a bore: `(a hole removes material)`).
`topopt run` writes the same lines at the start of `run.log`. Example (`tests/test_interface_cuts.py`): an unbounded end face of a
collar whose plane also goes through a sleeve on the side of the part cuts the sleeve deep (a warning), and trims the end of the collar by
less than the trim limit (a fact, no warning). A coaxial bore in a boss is a fact only. With `radius_mm` on the face the sleeve warning is gone.

**What stays of a frozen region (after the run; check C).** The exact step and the cuts can take more of a frozen region than the label rule
shows before the run (`taken_facts` counts voxels at the voxel size; this measures the finished mesh). `interfaces.integrity(ctx, V, F)`, called by
`interfaces.write_outputs`, measures it on `nominal.stl` (the finished mesh), or on `final.stl` when the run has no stock. A frozen region is the STL of
a fixed, load or solid region (found through `region_paths`; a missing file is not measured), or the nominal shape of a union interface (a `boss`, the ring
of a `tube`, an `stl` union). For each one:

`kept = volume(mesh and (region minus holes)) / volume(region minus holes)`

The holes are the nominal shapes of the `bore` interfaces and the holes of the `tube` interfaces, so a hole that the YAML asks for is not a loss. The
nominal shape of each `face`, `stl` cut or keep-out region that check A judged as a trim for this region (its `interface_taken` entry has `warn` false) is
taken out too: the YAML asks for that cut. A cut that check A warned about stays in the reference volume, so what it takes is a loss. It is one manifold boolean for each region
(about 0.4 s for four regions and seven interfaces in one measured case). Only a run with interfaces has the record. `metrics.json` key
`interfaces.integrity` is a list with one entry for each region: `region`, `role` (`fixed`, `load`, `solid`, `interface`), `volume_mm3` (region minus holes),
`kept`, `lost_mm3`, `cuts` (the cuts of `interface_taken` in `run.json` that overlap it, each `{name, kind, role}` with `role` `hole` for a bore or tube hole, `trim` for a cut that was taken out, `loss` for a cut that stays counted; empty for a run folder from before check A), `warn`
(`kept < 0.97`) and, if the region could not be measured, `kept: null` and a `note`. The limit 0.97 is under review:
the bracket examples give 1.00 for the clamp plate, because its `mounting_face` is a trim. A warning is a fact; the run goes on.
It is in `interfaces.warnings`, in `run.log` (`warning: ...`), in `run_result` (`interface_warnings`) and in the verdict (below). Text:
`load region 'sleeve' keeps 44.6 % of its volume in nominal.stl (the limit is 97 %): 7693.32 of 13899.9 mm3 are missing. The holes of the bore and tube
interfaces are not counted. The cuts of the check before the run that overlap it: bottom_face (face, loss). A face without 'radius_mm' cuts everything on the side
of its normal. Options: bound the cut (a face takes 'radius_mm'), move the cut or the region, or accept the loss`. `topopt run` writes each warning once to `run.log` and once to the console (not with `--quiet`).

**A surface that must be complete (check D).** `coverage` (below) is the area found divided by the area that has material behind it, so it does not count
a wall that is not there: a socket bore that is cut open on one side has `coverage` near 1. For an interface with `full_surface: true`, `measure` gives two more keys
for each surface: `full_area_mm2` (the complete surface: 2 pi r L for the wall of a cylinder, with r the radius of that mesh and L `length_mm`; pi r^2 for a
bounded face) and `full_coverage` (`area_mm2` divided by it). The item has `"full_surface": true`. The record has `full_surface_tests`: one entry for each such
interface: `interface`, `variant` (`nominal` with stock, else `as_printed`), `full_coverage` (the lowest of its surfaces; a `tube` has two), `threshold` (0.98), `met`, and
`surfaces` (`key`, `area_mm2`, `full_area_mm2`, `full_coverage`). The test is not met if the finished mesh shows less than 0.98 of the complete surface; it is a warning
in the same places as check C: `interface 'socket_bore' has full_surface, and the nominal mesh shows 0.75 of its full area (the limit is 0.98): 4802.5 of 6405.92 mm2.
Options: change the region or the interface so that the surface has material all round, or accept the gap`. `length_mm` must be the length of the surface that
has to be complete: a bore that is longer than the material reaches shows a lower `full_coverage`. An interface without `full_surface` has none of these keys, and its
output is the same as before. The limit 0.98 is under review.

**A stock with no effect (check E).** For an interface with `stock_mm` above 0 (not an `stl`), if the as-printed surface has under 5 % of the area of the finished
surface (`area_mm2` of `measured` in `as_printed` and in `nominal`), the stock has no effect: the region next to the surface starts at the finished size, so the
as-printed surface has no material behind it. This is one warning in `interfaces.warnings` and the places above: `interface 'socket_bore': stock_mm 0.3 has no effect: the
as-printed part has 11.5 mm2 of this surface against 4802 mm2 finished. The region next to it starts at the finished size. Make the region reach the as-printed size, or use a
'tube' interface, which adds the stock` (a boss or a tube ends with `Check that the position of the interface is the position of the surface`; a `tube` with two surfaces
names the surface in brackets). The limit 5 % is under review.

**`run.json`.** The key `interfaces` is there only if the YAML has one. It is a list of the resolved entries: `name`, `kind`, `op`,
and, except for `stl`: `stock_mm`, `point`, `axis` (`normal` for a `face`), `radius_mm`, `inner_radius_mm` (tube), `length_mm`; for
`stl`: `file` (relative to the YAML folder, else absolute). A `face` has `radius_mm` only if the YAML gives it. The post step reads it. A run folder without it has no interfaces. A person or an agent can edit `run.json`: an entry that is not a mapping, or a `kind` that is not one of `bore`, `boss`, `tube`, `face`, `stl` (also a list or a mapping), is a `UserError` (exit code 1 in the CLI) that names `interfaces[<i>].kind`, the value and the allowed kinds. There is no default kind (F4-41).
The key `interface_taken` (above) is there only if a cut takes a voxel of a frozen region.

**`interfaces` key of `metrics.json`.** Only with interfaces. Without them the key is not there, and `run.json`, `metrics.json`,
the snapshots and `final.stl` are bit-equal to the output before section 23.

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `applied`, `error` | the exact step ran, or the error text (see step 6) |
| `count`, `stock`, `sag_mm` | the number of interfaces, whether any built-in has stock, the chord sag of the facets (0.002) |
| `files` | `{"final.stl": "as_printed", "nominal.stl": "nominal" or null}` |
| `as_printed`, `nominal` (null without stock) | `volume_mm3`, `mass_g` (volume times the density of the run), `triangles`, `stl_roundtrip` (the facts of the file as loaded again, as in section 19) |
| `stock_volume_mm3` | with stock: volume of `final.stl` minus volume of `nominal.stl` |
| `clean` | for each variant: the float32 clean-up (`triangles_before`, `triangles_after`, `volume_change_mm3`; when the clean-up failed, the mesh stays as it was and the facts have `error` and `error_type`) |
| `bodies_removed` | for each variant: `bodies` and `volume_mm3` removed (step 3) |
| `keep_out_cut` | only if a union shape overlapped a keep-out region: for each variant `{files, removed_mm3}` (the number of keep-out STL files and the volume that the second cut took) |
| `notes` | only if there are any: facts about the run (for example a union shape that lies partly outside the grid box of the run) |
| `label_volume_error_pct` | the volume error of the label shapes (`sdf` method): the last calibration round (`calibration[-1].error`: the mesh with the label shapes against the target volume), in percent. `mesh.volume_error_pct` compares the as-printed mesh (stock on it) with the thresholded label volume, so it holds the stock; this key does not |
| `items` | one record for each interface (below) |
| `integrity` | one entry for each frozen region: what the finished mesh keeps (check C, above). Only if the run has a frozen region file or a union interface |
| `full_surface_tests` | only if an interface has `full_surface`: its test (check D, above) |
| `warnings` | only if there is one: the warnings of check C, E and D, as text (in this order). Also in `run.log`, and in `run_result` as `interface_warnings` |
| `t_s` | seconds: `base` (manifold of the smooth mesh), `as_printed`, `nominal`, `total` (the exact step), `measure` (reload and measure of the files) |

An item has `name`, `kind`, `op`, `stock_mm`, for `stl` the `file`, `full_surface` (true; only if the YAML sets it), and for each variant (`as_printed`, and `nominal` with stock)
`volume_change_mm3` (the volume change of its boolean step; negative for a cut) and `measured`. `measured` is measured on the mesh as
loaded again, not computed from the YAML: `radius_mm` for a `bore`, `boss` and the outer wall of a `tube`; `inner_radius_mm` for a
`tube`; `position_mm` for a `face` (the signed distance of the plane from the YAML `point` along `normal`; it is the stock in the
as-printed mesh and 0 in the nominal mesh). Its keys: `expected_mm`, `tolerance_mm`, `found`, `measured_mm`, `deviation_mm`,
`within_tolerance`, `area_mm2`, `faces`, `expected_area_mm2`, `coverage` and, for a radius, `max_mm` and `min_mm`. With `full_surface`: `full_area_mm2` and `full_coverage`. The radius or position
is measured on the facets that lie on the surface and face the right way (a hole wall faces the axis, an outer wall faces away
from it, a face cut faces along `normal`). A size alone is not enough: a surface that is mostly filled has a few facets at the right
radius. So `expected_area_mm2` is the area that the exact surface should show in this mesh, and `coverage` is `area_mm2` divided by it.
`expected_area_mm2` is the volume of a thin shell (`SHELL_MM` = 0.0005 mm, the same facet count on both radii) next to the wall,
divided by its thickness: for a hole wall and a face cut, the part of the shell that is in the material of the mesh; for the outer wall
of a boss or tube, the part of the shell that is free space, without the volume that the cuts and the keep-out regions of that variant
take away (a counterbore across a boss wall does not make the wall missing). So it counts only the wall that the mesh has material behind (a bore that
crosses a gap has no wall there). It does not count a wall that is not there: a socket cut open on one side has a `coverage` near 1. Use `full_surface` (above) to
test the complete surface. `within_tolerance` needs `coverage` of at least `COVERAGE_MIN` = 0.8. The limit is a choice: the
measured examples give 0.987 to 1.002, a bore filled to 90 percent gives about 0.1, and the sdf and blur meshes do not follow the
wall to 1e-3 mm everywhere. `coverage` is null if the expected area is under `AREA_MIN_MM2` = 0.01 mm2 (a shape in empty space: there
is no wall to find). A surface that is not in the mesh
(a bore in empty space, a face past the part) has `found: false` and `within_tolerance: false`; the step logs one warning. With
stock, `stock_measured_mm` has the stock that the two files show (nominal minus as-printed for a bore or an inner wall, as-printed minus
nominal for the rest).
The `mesh.checks.keep_out` record of section 19 (`sdf`, with region STL files) has one more entry for each cut interface, with the key
`interface:<name>` (the as-printed cutter; `interface:<name> (hole)` for the hole of a tube): `intersect_mm3` is the volume of
`final.stl` inside it. A union shape over a keep-out region gives `intersect_mm3` of 1e-3 mm3 or less (the region wins, see above).

**Check tool.** `tools/check_final_stl.py <run_dir>` reads `result/final.stl` and `result/nominal.stl` from disk (float32). Each file has
its own reload check (`stl_facts`). For each built-in interface it measures the radius or the face position in each file, gives the
deviation from the YAML value, and gives the stock that the two files show. The cutters (as-printed for `final.stl`, nominal for
`nominal.stl`) count as keep-out shapes. The exit code is 1 also if: a measured size is over its tolerance (the sag plus 1e-4 mm for a radius,
1e-4 mm for a position; `--tol-interface-mm` replaces both), a surface that `metrics.json` found at post time is not in the file, the
stock that the files show differs from the YAML by more than the two tolerances, `nominal.stl` is missing in a run with stock, or it is
there in a run without stock. A surface that is not in the mesh is reported as not found and does not fail the check by itself. A feature with a `coverage`
under `COVERAGE_MIN` or a filled or missing surface (expected area above `AREA_MIN_MM2`, none found) is a problem line and fails. The check prints the coverage of each
feature, and, for each failed check, one reason line (for example `region reach` with the note that `blur` can show a machined
face smaller than the region face).

**`topopt check` (text).** With interfaces, one line for each interface: `interface:      <name> (<kind>, <op>): N voxels, M hold
the label (...)`. `N` is the number of voxels that the interface takes (the shape at the voxel size), `M` how many of them keep the label
after the order of the labels (a keep-out region or a load region can win). The `--json` result has the same facts under `interfaces`
(`name`, `kind`, `op`, `voxels`, `held`, and for a union `piece_voxels`, `has_fixed`), and the facts of "What a cut takes" under
`interface_taken`, with one `interface cut:` line for each pair and one warning for each pair with `warn`. The warning about a floating union shape
(above) and the warning about a union shape over a keep-out region are printed too. If the interfaces take all the free voxels, the
`no free voxel` error names each interface and its voxel count.

**Facts and limits.**
- `mesh.volume_error_pct` (section 19) compares the volume of the as-printed mesh (`final.stl`) with the thresholded label volume
  (`volume_thresholded_mm3`). With stock, the as-printed mesh has the stock on it, so the value holds the stock and the exact shapes;
  it is not the error of the optimizer volume. `interfaces.label_volume_error_pct` is the error of the label shapes alone (the
  `sdf` calibration; absent in `blur`).
- The sag tolerance is a choice, not a limit of the library: a smaller sag gives more facets (n grows with the square root of `r / sag`).
- `Manifold.simplify` and the float32 snap move a vertex by at most 1e-5 mm plus the float32 resolution (7.6e-6 mm at 100 mm).
- Calibration (section 19, step 7) with interfaces: the volume that each round measures is the volume of the mesh with the label shapes
  of the interfaces united and cut (`calibration[].final_mm3` is this volume). The exact union of a
  fixed STL puts back the part of a fixed region that a cut interface removes (for example a face that machines the outer part of a
  plate). Without this correction the shift would count that part as extra material and thin all members to pay for it (measured:
  a shift of -0.24 to -0.36 mm instead of -0.02 to -0.07 mm on the example, and a split into two bodies).
- STEP and general solids from CAD are not in this section. A later item may add them.
- No macOS run was made for this section (the code has no platform branch and no new dependency).

## 24. Run folder facts: history lines, peak memory, the run helper (added with D1a)

### 24.1 History lines, peak memory, the run helper and the job lock (B-054, B-097)

Code: `topopt/runinfo.py` (history reader, peak memory) and `topopt/runjob.py` (the run helper). Both use the
standard library and `topopt.config` only. No new dependency. The Linux x86_64 paths are run and tested. The macOS
arm64 paths (`ps -o lstart=` for the start time, `ru_maxrss` in bytes) are tested with sample text and a faked platform
only. They are not yet run on a Mac.

**What is atomic.** A file is atomic when it is written to `<name>.tmp` in the same folder and then moved with
`os.replace`. `RunWriter`, `post.finish`, the refine step and the run helper do this for every file that `topopt run`
writes in the run folder, except four. `history.jsonl`, `run.log` and `gpu_mg.jsonl` (the solver gpu-mg only) only grow, so they are not atomic as files.
`job.guard` is an empty file that is never replaced. `topopt render` writes its PNG files in place.

**History writer.** `RunWriter.add_history` writes one record as one whole line (JSON, then `\n`) with one write
call, then flushes. A `run.log` line is one write, and the file is closed after each line.

**History reader.** `topopt.runinfo.read_history(path, strict=True)` returns `HistoryRead(rows, facts)`. Every
reader that must not fail on a partial write can use it. It is the shared reader (the post step and the MCP server use it; the
dashboard server and the replay reader still have their own tolerant loops; a later tool can call it).
- A last line that does not parse, or is not a JSON object, is skipped. `facts` has one sentence:
  `history.jsonl: skipped a partial last line (line N, B bytes)`.
- Another line that does not parse: `strict=True` raises `HistoryError` (a `ValueError`) with the line number. This is
  an error. `strict=False` skips such a line and adds one fact that names the line numbers.
- A blank line is ignored. A missing file raises `FileNotFoundError`. The file is decoded with `errors="replace"`: a byte that is not UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD, and the line still parses if the JSON is whole.
- `post.finish` reads with `strict=True`. It writes each fact to `run.log` as `warning: <fact>` and to the logger
  `topopt.post`. The metrics then come from the last row that parses (iteration N-1). The mesh comes from the last snapshot on
  disk, which `optimize` writes before the history row of its iteration, so it can be iteration N. The log line says this.
- `run_status` reads with `strict=False`. It returns the facts as `history_facts` and adds them to `summary`.
- `_last_history` of the MCP server reads with `strict=False` and gives the last row that parses (no fact). The dashboard
  server and the replay reader skip a bad line without a fact. They are not changed.

**Peak memory.** `topopt.runinfo.peak_rss_bytes()` (this process) and `children_peak_rss_bytes()` (the largest child that this
process has waited for; 0 if none) return bytes on macOS and on Linux. `peak_rss_info()` gives the number and its source.
- Linux: `peak_rss_bytes()` reads `VmHWM` of `/proc/self/status` (source `VmHWM`). It belongs to the memory of this process only.
- Else (macOS, or no `/proc`): `ru_maxrss` (source `ru_maxrss`). It is in bytes on macOS and in KiB on Linux;
  `ru_maxrss_to_bytes(value, platform)` is the only place that knows this.
- A number for memory names the process it is for. On Linux `ru_maxrss` of a child that `subprocess` starts (vfork or
  posix_spawn, then exec) starts at the peak of its parent; a child of `os.fork` plus exec starts at the current resident memory of
  the parent; `VmHWM` is not inherited. So `ru_maxrss` of a run that the MCP server started would have the peak of the server as
  a floor, and `children_peak_rss_bytes()` is at least the peak that the parent had when the largest child started. A small child of
  a big process looks big (measured: the `gcc` and `ld` children of `pypardiso` gave 1.70 GB in a run with its own peak of
  1.71 GB). `job.json` does not hold the children value.

**File hash.** `topopt.runinfo.sha256_file(path)` returns the SHA-256 of a file as a hex string; it reads the file in blocks.
It is the one file-hash helper for run inputs: a checkpoint, a case manifest and a run record use it, so that the same file gives
the same value in each record.
`topopt.runinfo.region_files(regions, base_dir, root=None, yaml_path=None)` returns every region file as `{"<role>:<path>": Path}`: `role`
is the field name of `config.regions` (any field, so a later region kind is included), `path` is relative to `base_dir` (the YAML folder)
with `/`. Two files with the same name in different folders get different keys. Records that hash the inputs use these keys: the
checkpoint (section 24.2) and the case (section 30), so the same file has the same key in each record.
- `yaml_path`: the key holds the path as the YAML names it, from the YAML text (`region_names`). A symbolic link keeps its own name; the
  hash (`sha256_file`) is of the content. Without it the paths of `regions` are used (the loader resolves a link). A role whose number
  of names differs from its number of paths keeps the paths of `regions`. With `regions=None` the files are those that the text names.
- `root` (default None: no rule, the keys can hold `..`): a file outside `root` has the key `<role>:<outside>/<12 hex>/<file name>`. The
  12 hex characters are the start of the SHA-256 of the resolved path text (`outside_key`), so the key holds no folder name of the outside
  place (a user name, for example). The case passes the work folder. The checkpoint passes `key_root(yaml_path)`: the work folder
  (the folder of `topopt.workfolder.resolve()`, section 10.1, as the MCP server takes it) if the YAML lies in it, else the folder of the YAML.
  The hook example and every file beside the YAML keep their keys.
- `job.json` holds `peak_rss_start_bytes` (the value at the start of the job), `peak_rss_bytes`, `peak_rss_source` and `peak_rss_reset`. With source
  `ru_maxrss` the summary line says when the start value is a large part (25 % or more) of the peak: `X GB of it was there at the
  start and can come from the parent process`. `GB` in the texts of the helper means 10^9 bytes.
- The reset of the own peak (DL1a, Linux). At the start the job writes `5` to `/proc/self/clear_refs`. That sets `VmHWM` to the memory in use
  now, so `peak_rss_bytes` at the end is the peak of THIS JOB and not of the whole process. Before DL1a a process that did other work first
  (a test, a long session, the parent of a refine) gave its old peak as the peak of the job (E1 found this in a third of the peak labels).
  `peak_rss_reset` is `true` when the write worked. `peak_rss_start_bytes` is still the peak BEFORE the reset, so the old and the new
  number are both in the record. The rule for `peak_rss_bytes` is: the largest of the `VmHWM` read at the end, the floor, and
  `peak_rss_loop_bytes`. The floor is the read right after the reset (reset worked) or the start value (no reset: macOS, source `ru_maxrss`, or a
  `/proc` that refuses the write). `VmHWM` can read about 1.5 MB lower than an earlier read, so the floor stops a peak below the start.
  A command that builds the problem BEFORE the job asks for no reset: `topopt run --resume` and `--continue-from` plan in `cmd_run`, and the voxel build
  of a fine grid can be the peak of the command (a 0.5 mm grid crashed a 16 GB Mac). Then `peak_rss_reset` is `false`, one note in `host.notes`
  (`peak_rss_reset: not done, the plan of this command ...`) says why, and the old rule holds: `peak_rss_bytes` is the largest of the end read and
  the start value, so the build is in it. `run_job(..., keep_peak=<reason>)` is that request. A fresh run builds its problem inside the job
  and resets.
  The other caller of `runinfo.peak_rss_bytes()` in the same process, the judge step of the ratchet (`facts["peak_rss_bytes"]`), reads after
  the reset, so it sees the peak since the start of the job. `buckling_voxel` does not call that function: it reads `ru_maxrss` through
  `topopt.verify.memory.peak_rss_bytes`, which the reset does not lower (in a child of a big parent `ru_maxrss` keeps the parent's peak, while
  `VmHWM` does not), and it uses a difference of two reads, which the reset does not change.
  Nothing reads `VmHWM` before the reset for another purpose. macOS: `ru_maxrss` only grows, there is no reset,
  `peak_rss_reset` is `false` (no note), and `peak_rss_bytes` stays the peak of the process.

**Run helper.** `topopt.runjob.run_job(run_dir, body, success_codes=(0,), override=False, t_start=None, keep_peak=None, record=None)` takes the job lock,
calls `body(job)`, records the end and removes the lock. It returns the exit code of the body. An exception ends the job
with the exit code that `topopt.cli.main` gives (user error 1, Ctrl+C 130, other 2, `SystemExit(n)` n) and goes on. A body that calls
`job.finish(5)` (`STOPPED_EXIT`) ends the job with state `stopped` and the marker `job.STOPPED`; a `SystemExit(5)` from a body is the same. `body` can
call `job.finish(code)` when its work is done and only waits after that. The first call counts. Files in the run folder:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `job.lock` | JSON: `format`, `pid`, `process_start` (epoch seconds, or null), on Linux also `process_start_ticks` (field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`) and `boot_id`, `token`, `started_at`, `run_dir`. It exists while the job runs. |
| `job.json` | JSON: the fields of `job.lock`, and `state` (`running`, `done`, `failed`, `stopped`), `success_codes`, `platform`, `notes` (facts from the start), `peak_rss_start_bytes` (the peak at the start), `peak_rss_source` (`VmHWM` or `ru_maxrss`), `peak_rss_reset`, `host` (the facts of the machine at the start), the keys of the `record` argument (the first run of `--fine-pass` has `fine_pass`: `first_run` true, `fine_run_dir`, and `forced`, true when `--fine-voxel` was given), and at the end `exit_code`, `ended_at`, `wall_s`, `peak_rss_bytes` (this process, since the start of the job where `peak_rss_reset` is true), and the CPU, load and phase keys of "Facts for the data loop" below. |
| `job.DONE` | Text `exit N`. Written only if the exit code is in `success_codes`. |
| `job.FAILED` | Text `exit N`. Written for any other exit code. |
| `job.STOPPED` | Text `exit 5` (`runjob.STOPPED_EXIT`). Written when a request to stop ended the run and the exit code is not in `success_codes`. State `stopped` in `job.json`. |
| `job.stop` | The request to stop (section 24.2, "Stop on request"). It is not part of the job record: a person or a tool writes it, the run removes it. |
| `job.guard` | Empty. An exclusive `flock` on it makes "read the lock, then take it" one step. If the file system gives no `flock`, the helper goes on without it. |

- The default `success_codes` is `{0}`. A command that has more success codes passes them (for example `topopt verify` of PR #21 can pass `{0, 3}`: its exit 3 is a valid result with an allowable exceeded).
- `topopt run` ends with the exit codes of section 8. Its job covers the optimizer, the post step and the refine step. It ends
  before the dashboard wait that follows. So `wall_s` is a few seconds above `done in N s` of `run.log`. A job that is killed by a
  signal that Python does not catch (SIGKILL, SIGTERM) writes no marker. Its lock stays: a stale lock.
- The order at the end: `job.json`, then the marker, then the lock is removed. At the start: `job.json` (state running), then the old
  markers (`job.DONE`, `job.FAILED`, `job.STOPPED`) are removed, then `job.lock` is written. All of it happens under the `flock` of `job.guard`.
- A request to stop in the folder at the start (`job.stop`, section 24.2) is checked under the same `flock`. A request that names this pid
  (`target_pid`) stays: it was written for this run between its spawn and its lock. Any other request (another pid, no pid, a file that does
  not parse) is removed, and a fact says so in `notes` of `job.json` and in `run.log`: it belongs to an earlier run.
- `RunWriter.clean()` does not delete the job files. The helper deletes the old markers at the start of the next job.
- `topopt run` takes the lock after the YAML is read and the folder exists, and before `clean()` and the dashboard. A YAML
  error leaves the folder as it was and writes no job files.

**A refused run keeps the earlier run (F4-43, F4-47).** A fresh run removes the files of an old run (`RunWriter.clean()`). Before it does, it makes
every check of the input that can stop it before its first pass (`cli.check_run_inputs`). The checks run inside the job, after the job lock, so the
job record and its peak memory cover the voxel build. The order is the order of the run: `build_problem` (the voxel guards `max_grid_voxels`
and `max_active_voxels`, the region files, the load regions), the union piece with no fixed voxel (section 23), the piece of active voxels with
no support (section 3), the perimeter bound (section 26.3), the buckling row with its solver (section 39), the platform and the backend of the
solver, the solver that runs, robust mode with a stress row or the buckling row (section 22b; F4-47), and the rows of `limits` that cannot work
(section 31; F4-47; the check needs the voxel grid and the free dofs, not the model). A check writes nothing. The run log lines that follow from the checks (the solver warning, the platform hint, the
memory lines) are written after the delete, in the same order and with the same text as before.
- The folder holds an earlier run when `snapshot.old_run_files` is not empty: a file of `RUN_FILES` other than `status.json` and `run.log`, or a
  folder of `RUN_DIRS` that holds an entry. If a check refuses the run then, the run folder holds:
  - every file of the earlier run with the same bytes: `run.json`, `labels.bin`, `history.jsonl`, `run.log` (no line is added), `verdict.json`,
    `robust.json`, `gpu_mg.jsonl`, the checkpoints, `snapshots/`, `result/`, `verify/`, and every file that is not a file of a run;
  - `status.json`: state `error`, iteration 0, step `setup`, and the text of the error, which is the text that the command prints after `error: `.
    The text ends with one more sentence, `cli.EARLIER_RUN_KEPT`: "The earlier run in this folder is kept: its run files, snapshots/ and result/
    are not changed (status.json and the job files now show this run)." The command prints it on stderr, and so it is in `status.message` and `summary` of `run_status`
    and in `message` of `run_result` of the MCP server. A Ctrl+C or an internal error in these checks gives the same status and the same sentence (`internal error: <text>`,
    `stopped by the user (Ctrl+C)`). The first line of these checks is the import of `topopt.optimize` (the `run` of the run, F4-47), so a Ctrl+C or an
    `ImportError` there gives this status too, before the delete;
  - the job record of the refused job, as for any run that fails: `job.json` (state `failed`, the exit code), the marker `job.FAILED` and `job.guard`. The
    job start removes the marker of the earlier job (`job.DONE` or `job.STOPPED`).
  The earlier files are not changed, but the folder does not describe them as the current run: `status.json` says `error`, so `run_status` has the state
  `error` and `run_result` gives no result for it. The earlier run is read from its files, for example `result/final.stl`.
  `run_status` still reads `history.jsonl`, `verdict.json` and the checkpoint of the folder, but it says that they are of the earlier run (P9-18, "After a
  refused run" below). It does not give them as the result of the refused job.
- A folder with no earlier run (an empty folder, or one that holds only what a run leaves when it stops in its setup: `status.json`, `run.log`, an empty
  `snapshots/`, the job files) behaves as before F4-43: `clean()`, then the status `starting`, then the checks. Nothing is lost there, and `status.json` is
