`frozen_note`, `thickness_near_mm` (`before_min`, `before_median`, `after_min`, `after_median`: the inscribed diameter of the
medial-axis balls that reach the changed nodes; the median is the member, the minimum can be the tip of a wedge), `modes`,
`parent_check`, `nearest_frozen_to_edit_mm`, `bodies_after`, `closed_after`, `dropped_bodies`, `odd_rays_repaired`, `stress_near_mark` (B-094: from `result/stress.npz`, the part before the
edit: `voxels_near`, `near_max_mpa`, `near_mean_mpa`, `near_max_by_case_mpa`, `global_max_mpa`, `global_p99_mpa`) and `route_note`
when the re-run route may fit better. Each entry of `steps`: `label`, `kind`, `status`, `paths_mm`, `mode`, `mode_reason`,
`crop` (`lo_mm`, `hi_mm`, `shape`, `nodes`, `pitch_mm`), `edit`, `frozen`, `volume` (`before_mm3`, `after_mm3`, `change_mm3`,
`change_g`: exact, from the meshes), `thickness_near_mm`, `part` (`triangles`, `closed`, `watertight`, `bodies`, `open_edges`,
`non_manifold_edges`, `zero_area_faces`), `operator` (the numbers of the operator), `parent_check`, `splice_zone_bbox_mm`,
`float32_repair`, `frozen_restored_mm3`, `dropped_bodies`, `odd_rays`, `odd_rays_repaired`, `seam`, `rollback`, `facts`,
`options` (a guard), `seconds`.

`seam` (the facts of the splice of the step): `method` is `sewn` or `boolean`. A sewn seam has `loops` (boundary loops of the cut),
`loops_joined_edge_to_edge`, `loops_joined_by_strip`, `loop_gap_max_mm` (the largest distance between a loop and its partner),
`wall_triangles_dropped`, `ear_triangles_dropped` (triangles of the new surface with two boundary edges, no area worth keeping),
`strip_triangles`, `strip_edges_welded`, `short_edge_mm` (`MIN_EDGE_REJECT_MM`), `volume_vs_boolean_mm3` (the volume of the sewn
part minus the volume of the two pieces: the boolean would have this volume) and, when a loop pair used the strip, `why_strip` (a
list of reasons), `old_vertices_removed` and `old_removed_move_max_mm` (the vertices of the old loop that the weld removed, and the
largest distance that one of them moved), and `weld_stopped_by_guard` (true only when the pass guard `SEAM_WELD_PASSES` ended the
weld while a pass still collapsed edges). A `boolean` seam has `why_not_sewn`. `frozen_undo` holds the same facts for the undo of a
change inside a frozen region, when it ran; a sewn undo adds `region_residual_mm3` (the volume that it changed in the region, below
`FROZEN_TOL_MM3`); at `FROZEN_TOL_MM3` or more the undo is the plain boolean, and `why_not_sewn` gives that volume. These are facts: a `boolean` seam is a part that may have fold edges (read `totals.surface_quality`).

`totals`: `volume_before_mm3`, `volume_after_mm3`, `change_mm3`, `change_pct`, `mass_before_g`, `mass_after_g`, `change_g`,
`density_g_cm3` (from `run.json`), triangles, bodies and `closed` before and after, `marks` (counts by status), `steps`,
`steps_applied`, `crop_nodes_total`, `frozen_exact`, `frozen_by_labels`, `restored_mm3`, `triangles_replaced`, `edit_reach_mm`,
`reload_from_disk` (the facts of `edited.stl` loaded again), `edited_stl_sha256` and `surface_quality` (present when `edited.stl`
is written).

`totals.surface_quality`: `before` (`final.stl`) and `after` (`edited.stl` as written), each with the definitions of `topopt verify`
(`topopt.tet.surface`: the STL is read with its merge of equal vertices on a 1e-6 mm grid): `triangles`, `closed_manifold` (every
edge has two faces, the orientation is consistent, and no vertex pinches the surface), `open_edges`, `non_manifold_edges`,
`non_manifold_vertices` (null when the orientation is not consistent and the count is not made), `bodies`, `fold_edges` (edges
whose two faces point back on each other, cos < -0.999: a fin of no thickness), `edge_min_mm`, `edge_p1_mm` (1st percentile of
the edge lengths) and `edges_under_verify_limit` (edges of the file shorter than `verify_edge_limit_mm`); `{error}` when the file
cannot be read as a surface. Beside them: `verify_edge_limit_mm` (`MIN_EDGE_REJECT_MM`, 0.05) and `note`. `topopt verify` refuses a
surface that is not a closed manifold, and a prepared surface with an edge under the limit; its remesh can remove short edges of
the file, and when an edge under the limit stays it welds the input once and prepares the welded surface (section 14, weld retry;
`mesh.surface_weld_retry` in `verify.json`) or, when that is refused, cleans the refused surface (section 14, clean retry;
`mesh.surface_clean_retry`), so `edges_under_verify_limit` is a hint, not a verdict. The block is a set of facts, not a refusal: the file is written
in each case, and `problems` names an `edited.stl` that is not a closed manifold. A call that changes nothing has no block.

`routes`: `use_edited_stl` (the facts to read first; no FE run), `rerun_with_hints` (`marks_to_hints` for the same marks: a new
run of the optimizer; it fits when a mark was rolled back, clipped by a frozen region, or failed the parent check) and, only
when `topopt.verify` can be imported (item #21), `verify`.

`options` (a wrong option is a fact in `problems`; the default is used): `radius_scale` (1.0), `pitch_mm`, `max_crop_voxels`,
`max_total_voxels`, `frozen_keep_mm`, `frozen_full_mm`, `close_mm`, `neck_min_mm3`, `parent_tol_mm`, `parent_check`
(`report`, `enforce`), `smooth_mode` (`auto`, `tube`, `iso`, `fair`), `remove_mode` (`cut`, `shave`), `mirror_plane`
(`{axis, at_mm}`), `skip` (mark ids), `per_mark` ({id: `radius_mm`, `amount_mm`, `strength`, `mirror`, `smooth_mode`,
`remove_mode`, `skip`}), `check_frozen_exact` (true), `loose_body_mm3` (a sliver limit; default max(10 x pitch^3, 0.001)),
`max_odd_rays` (0). The text of each option is in `option_catalog`.

### 29.2 MCP tool and the script

- `apply_marks(marks, run_dir=None, out_dir=None, options=None, overwrite=False, allow_stale=False, detail=False,
  yaml_path=None)` (default run: the last run of the server). It sits next to `marks_to_hints`. The reply is `short_report`
  unless `detail` is true: `ok`, `run_dir`, `out_dir`, `files`, `summary`, one line for each mark (status, modes, radius,
  volume and mass change, `edit_reach_mm`, `edit_note`, clip, `restored_in_frozen_mm3`, thickness, `parent_check_within_tolerance`,
  bodies, `seam_methods` (the count of steps for each seam method, for example `{"sewn": 2, "boolean": 1}`), `dropped_bodies`, nearest frozen, stress near the mark (a voxel estimate), defaults used, reason, route note), `totals` (volume, mass, bodies, closed, `frozen_exact`, `restored_mm3`, `reload_from_disk`, `surface_quality` (`closed_manifold`, `fold_edges`, `non_manifold_vertices`, `edge_min_mm`, `edges_under_verify_limit` before and after, and `verify_edge_limit_mm`), `triangles_replaced`), `grid`,
  `routes`, `problems`, `detail: false`, `report_file`, `more`. The tool adds `run_dir_rel`, `out_dir_rel`, `report_rel` and
  `edited_rel`. A wrong input gives `{"ok": false, "error": ...}`. The text of the tool gives facts and options; it has no
  habitual must or never. `INSTRUCTIONS` names the tool in one short line.
- Script: `python -m topopt.apply_marks RUN_DIR MARKS [--out DIR] [--overwrite] [--allow-stale] [--yaml PATH] [--pitch MM]
  [--radius-scale F] [--parent-check report|enforce] [--smooth-mode ...] [--remove-mode cut|shave] [--mirror-plane y=0]
  [--skip ID ...] [--max-crop-voxels N] [--detail]`. It prints the short report (the full report with `--detail`) and exits 0,
  or prints `error: ...` and exits 1.
- `tools/check_apply.py RUN_DIR MARKS.json [--out DIR] [--pitch MM] [--allow-stale] [--all-at-once]` applies the marks one kind
  at a time into `DIR/<kind>`, prints the facts and the output paths, and checks each output from the files on disk (hashes of
  the run and the input folder before and after, `edited.stl` reloads as one closed solid, no absolute path in
  `apply_marks.json`, the direction of the volume).
- B-094: the read access to the stress report is `stress_near_mark`. The print report is not on the base of this item: it is a
  follow-up.

### 29.3 Automatic geometric cleanup: a list, not an edit (added with C3b)

Code: `topopt/cleanup.py` (the engine, and the script `python -m topopt.cleanup list`), the MCP tool `cleanup_list`
(`topopt_mcp/server.py`) and two optional keys of a mark (29.1). Tests: `tests/test_cleanup.py` (fast),
`tests/test_cleanup_ratchet.py` (slow: the real ratchet), `tests/test_cleanup_mcp.py`. Each number of the method has its source line in the tables below. The section adds no
dependency (numpy, scipy, scikit-image, trimesh and rtree are core). It was run on Linux x86_64. It was not run on macOS. To check it on a
Mac, run `pytest tests/test_cleanup.py`. The reserved text that this section replaces said "off by default (a YAML key)". There is no
key. Nothing runs unless the script or the tool is called.

**1. What it is, and the boundary.** The list command scans `result/final.stl` of a finished run for loose bodies, dead-end spurs, thin
bumps, uneven struts (SMOOTH) and flat webs (FAIR). It writes one NEW folder with `marks.json` (a marks file, format of section 29) and
`cleanup.json` (the full report), and nothing else. It applies no edit and gives no verdict. The run folder, `final.stl`, the YAML and
the region STL files stay as they are. The ratchet judges the list: `python -m topopt.ratchet run RUN_DIR --source marks:FILE` (36.7)
applies each mark with `apply_marks` and judges it with the rules of the YAML `acceptance` block. The agent reads the facts first and
decides what to spend judge runs on. No C3b code is on the path of `topopt run`, `post.py` or the optimizer: only the script and the tool
import `topopt.cleanup` (the tool inside the function; a test checks both), and the module loads no VTK, gmsh or OpenCL package. So a
run with no list is bit-equal to a run before C3b.

**2. The call.**
- Python: `cleanup_list(run_dir, *, out_dir=None, options=None, overwrite=False, estimate_only=False, yaml_path=None, root=None) -> dict`
  gives the full report, or `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` for a wrong input (no exception). `short_report(report)` gives the short form.
- Script: `python -m topopt.cleanup list RUN_DIR [--out DIR] [--overwrite] [--yaml PATH] [--pitch MM] [--max-candidates N | --all]
  [--order pipeline|stress] [--kinds body,spur,bump,member] [--max-voxels N] [--max-gb G] [--root RATCHET_ROOT] [--set NAME=VALUE ...]
  [--estimate] [--detail]`. It prints the short report (the full report with `--detail`) and exits 0, or prints `error: ...` and exits 1.
  `topopt` has no subcommand for it (`python -m topopt.apply_marks` and `python -m topopt.ratchet` are the precedent).
- MCP tool `cleanup_list(run_dir=None, out_dir=None, options=None, overwrite=False, estimate_only=False, detail=False, yaml_path=None,
  root=None)`. The default run is the last run of the server. The tool runs in the server process. The reply is the short report plus
  `run_dir_rel`, `out_dir_rel`, `marks_rel` and `report_rel`; `detail` gives the full report. If the client stops waiting, the call
  still ends and writes the folder: read `cleanup.json`, or call again with `overwrite`. The tool text is under 4096 characters.
- `RUN_DIR` is a finished run, or an `acc_NN` folder of a ratchet root (it has `run.json`, `labels.bin`, `result/final.stl`, and
  `verify/` when the judge ran). The output folder is new. The default is `<run folder>-cleanup` beside the run folder (a number is added
  when it exists). For an `acc_NN` folder of a ratchet root the default is `<root>-cleanup-acc_NN` beside the root, so the root holds
  no file that is not its own. Refused, each with the fact and the options (`refused.reason`): `run_folder` (a run folder, or a folder
  inside one), `ratchet_root` (a root, or a folder inside one: the next `ratchet run` on that root would stop), `input_folder` (the
  folder of the YAML or of a region STL), `symbolic_link`, `not_a_folder`, `not_empty` (a folder with files, with no `overwrite`) and
  `not_a_cleanup_folder` (`overwrite` is for an earlier cleanup folder only: it has a `cleanup.json` of format 1).

**3. Inputs.**

| Input | Gives | When it is missing |
|---|---|---|
| `run.json` | grid (shape, `h`, origin), name, `mirror`, density, YAML name | `{"ok": false}`: the grid is not known |
| `result/final.stl` | the part | `{"ok": false}`: there is no finished part |
| `labels.bin` | fixed, load and keep-out voxels (the distance to a frozen region; the bodies that hold a fixed or load voxel) | `{"ok": false}`: `topopt run` writes it at the start |
| the problem YAML (`run.json`, or `yaml_path`) | the `acceptance` rules and the input folders, for the estimate and the folder check | the list is written; `estimate.judge` has `available: false` with the reason |
| `verify/fields.npz` (and `verify/verify.json`) | the stress facts of each candidate (`vm_elem_max_<case>` and the mesh) | `stress: null` and a note with the option. A `final_stl_sha256` in `verify.json` that differs gives no stress facts and a note |
| `result/metrics.json` | the density, when `run.json` has none | not needed |
| `root` (a ratchet root) | the measured judge time of its log, for the estimate | not needed |

**4. Detectors, options and tables.** One pass in memory (no work folder), deterministic: no random number, stable sort keys, ids by
position, so a second call with `overwrite` gives a byte-equal `marks.json` (a test). The steps follow the pipeline stages
`s1h_half` to `s6_final` of the research (named in the `anchor` column): the lattice; the solid mask (`inside_mask` on the whole part,
no VTK and no half mesh); the distance transform; the skeleton (`skimage skeletonize`); junctions and branches; the member table with the
junction zones trimmed; the section profile of each member (area, CV, largest over smallest radius, flatness); the opening residue (a ball
of `opening_radius_mm`); the rules for spur, bump, SMOOTH and FAIR; the frozen filter; the stress facts; the mirror merge; the order. The
differences from the pipeline are these: the frozen regions are the voxel labels of the run, not CAD annuli; the lattice is anchored; a
candidate is not listed (`counts.frozen_excluded`) when a voxel of it lies inside a frozen region, or when more than `frozen_max_share`
of its voxels are within `frozen_near_mm` of one; a candidate within `near_frozen_mm` of a frozen region stays with `confidence: low`; the old-mark exemption of a small bump, the absolute stress limits and the VTK renders are not
ported; the stress comes from `verify/fields.npz` and the case names come from its keys.

*Options (`THRESHOLDS`).* The call can set each one (`options` of the tool, `--set NAME=VALUE`, or the matching flag). Each has its
pipeline anchor. The mass limits of the pipeline are volumes at the pipeline density 0.0078 g/mm3 (`0.4 / 0.0078` and so on): geometric
sizes, so a part gives the same list in any material. The facts also show the mass at the density of the run.

| Option | Default | Unit | Source (pipeline file:line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pitch_mm` | 0.5 | mm | s1h_half.py:13, s2h_analyse.py:11, s3_sections.py:9, s4_bumps.py:7, s5_candidates.py:11: the voxel size H of the pipeline |
| `opening_radius_mm` | 1.5 | mm | s5_candidates.py:15 and :45: the ball of the opening residue (s4_bumps.py:10 has 1.0 as its own default) |
| `spur_min_length_mm` | 5 | mm | s5_candidates.py:38: remove_skeleton min_len_mm |
| `spur_min_volume_mm3` | 51.2821 | mm3 | s5_candidates.py:38: min_mass_g 0.4 at 0.0078 g/mm3 |
| `bump_min_volume_mm3` | 7.69231 | mm3 | s5_candidates.py:50: a residue below 0.06 g is not a bump |
| `bump_min_final_volume_mm3` | 25.641 | mm3 | s6_final.py:18: a bump below 0.2 g is dropped (the old-mark exemption is not ported) |
| `bump_extent_min_mm` | 5 | mm | s5_candidates.py:53: the longest side of the box of a bump, at least |
| `bump_extent_max_mm` | 30 | mm | s5_candidates.py:53: the longest side of the box of a bump, at most |
| `member_min_length_mm` | 9 | mm | s5_candidates.py:41: smooth min_len_mm |
| `member_min_volume_mm3` | 102.564 | mm3 | s5_candidates.py:41: min_mass_g 0.8 at 0.0078 g/mm3 |
| `member_min_radius_mm` | 1.2 | mm | s5_candidates.py:41: min_rmean_mm |
| `member_min_cv` | 0.15 | ratio | s5_candidates.py:41: min_cv |
| `member_min_ratio` | 1.7 | ratio | s5_candidates.py:41: min_ratio (largest over smallest section radius) |
| `mild_min_length_mm` | 20 | mm | s5_candidates.py:41: the mild tier, length |
| `mild_min_volume_mm3` | 384.615 | mm3 | s5_candidates.py:41: the mild tier, 3 g at 0.0078 g/mm3 |
| `mild_min_cv` | 0.1 | ratio | s5_candidates.py:41: the mild tier, CV |
| `mild_min_ratio` | 1.4 | ratio | s5_candidates.py:41: the mild tier, max/min |
| `web_flatness` | 1.75 | ratio | s5_candidates.py:17 and :42 (read from apply_marks.DEFAULTS): FAIR at this flatness or more |
| `frozen_near_mm` | 3 | mm | s5_candidates.py:36: a voxel closer than this to a frozen region counts as near |
| `frozen_max_share` | 0.05 | share | s5_candidates.py:36: at most this share of the voxels of a candidate is near a frozen region |
| `near_frozen_mm` | 6 | mm | s5_candidates.py:40 and s6_final.py:27: a candidate closer than this to a frozen region has confidence low |
| `max_candidates` | 10 | count | none in the pipeline; a choice of this tool: about 5 to 6 minutes of judge time on the hook |

Other options: `order` (`pipeline` or `stress`), `kinds` (a list of `body`, `spur`, `bump`, `member`), `max_voxels` (the default is
`apply_marks.OPTION_DEFAULTS["max_total_voxels"]`, 60,000,000) and `max_gb` (the default is none; `verify.memory.limits`). A name that is
not known, a value that is not valid and a name of `METHOD` give a line in `problems`; the default is used and the call goes on.

*Constants of the method (`METHOD`).* They are not settable. `cleanup.json` lists them. Every entry has its anchor, and a test checks
that every number of both tables has one. `path_step_mm` (1.0, `lib2.py:176`), the voxel guard and the density come from `apply_marks`
(`DEFAULTS`, `OPTION_DEFAULTS`), not from a copy. No other number is new.

| Constant | Default | Unit | Source (pipeline file:line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grid_pad_mm` | 4 | mm | s1h_half.py:15: the grid reaches 4 mm beyond the box of the part |
| `pair_radius_pitches` | 1.8 | x pitch | s2h_analyse.py:27 and s3_sections.py:17: skeleton points closer than this are neighbours |
| `pair_tolerance_mm` | 1e-06 | mm | s2h_analyse.py:27 and s3_sections.py:17 |
| `junction_trim_min_mm` | 1.5 | mm | s2h_analyse.py:23: the junction zone is max(radius, this) + 0.5 mm |
| `junction_trim_add_mm` | 0.5 | mm | s2h_analyse.py:23 |
| `member_min_skeleton_points` | 2 | count | s2h_analyse.py:40 |
| `member_min_voxels` | 4 | count | s2h_analyse.py:41-42 |
| `path_min_points` | 4 | count | s3_sections.py:15 and :23 |
| `station_window_mm` | 3 | mm | s3_sections.py:31: the section area is smoothed over this length |
| `station_floor_mm` | 0.3 | mm | s3_sections.py:29 and :31 |
| `end_zone_min_mm` | 1.5 | mm | s3_sections.py:36: the end zones of a member are left out of the section statistics |
| `end_zone_radius_factor` | 1.5 | x radius | s3_sections.py:36 |
| `inner_stations_min` | 4 | count | s3_sections.py:37 |
| `flatness_stations` | 12 | count | s3_sections.py:42: about this many stations carry a flatness value |
| `flatness_min_voxels` | 12 | count | s3_sections.py:44: a station needs this many voxels |
| `section_ratio_floor_mm` | 0.05 | mm | s3_sections.py:47: the smallest radius in max/min |
| `bump_spur_overlap_mm` | 1 | mm | s5_candidates.py:57: a bump voxel this close to a spur candidate overlaps it |
| `bump_spur_overlap_share` | 0.3 | share | s5_candidates.py:57: a bump with more than this share overlapping a spur is dropped |
| `stress_radius_mm` | 1 | mm | s5_candidates.py:25-26: the elements within this distance of the candidate voxels |
| `stress_percentile` | 99.9 | percent | s5_candidates.py:23-28: the stress fact is this percentile of the element stress (the keys p999_* keep the pipeline name) |
| `fair_zone_mm` | 5 | mm | it_geom_fair.py:4: Rinf, the radius of the fairing zone of a FAIR mark |

*Units, lattice and pitch.* Lengths and radii are mm, volumes are mm3, in the frame of `final.stl`. The lattice is anchored: its origin
on each axis is a multiple of `pitch_mm`, and a mirror plane of the run is a lattice plane. So the list stays the same when the part moves
by whole pitches, and when `grid_pad_mm` changes (tests). It changes with the pitch and with a shift of a fraction of a pitch (limit 4).
There is no floor and no clamp for the pitch: each candidate shows `length_in_voxels` and `mean_radius_in_voxels`, so the agent sees when a
rule works on a few voxels. Distances for neighbours, trims and ties are computed in voxel index units.

*Guard.* Before any array is made, the command counts the voxels (`voxels x 200 bytes + 300 MB`, the model of `apply_marks`) and compares
them with `max_voxels` and with the smaller of the available RAM and `max_gb`. A refusal is a reply with the facts and the options
(`pitch_that_fits_mm`, a larger `max_voxels`, a larger `max_gb`), not a crash, and nothing was computed. The model is 2.1 to 2.8 times above
the measured peak (hook 2.24 M voxels: model 0.75 GB, measured 0.35 GB; ladle 9.29 M voxels: 2.16 and 0.84 GB at 0.5 mm; hook 10.19 M voxels: 2.34 and 0.85 GB at 0.3 mm).

*Budget, order and kinds.* `max_candidates` (default 10; `null` or `--all` for all) is the number of candidates written (a candidate has more than one mark only
when its voxel set has more than one 26-component, see the walk below). The rest go to
`cleanup.json` `not_listed` with the facts and the reason. The order is the order of judging: bodies, then REMOVE (spurs and bumps) by
volume, then SMOOTH by CV, then FAIR by CV, each group with the largest first, and ties by the centre coordinates. With `order: stress`
the candidate with the lowest stress ratio comes first in its group (unknown last). `confidence` and the stress ratio are columns, not
sort keys; nothing is cut by stress. With no `kinds`, the file holds the body marks only when a removable body exists (part 7), else the
spur, bump and member candidates. A given `kinds` is used as it is; a file that mixes bodies and features has `mixed_kinds_note` in the
header. The candidates of the kinds that are not in the file go to `not_listed` with the reason.

**5. The marks file.** `marks.json` is a marks file of format 1 (`version`, `units: "mm"`, `source_sha256` = the hash of `final.stl` of
the folder that was scanned, `marks`). `apply_marks`, the Refine page and the `marks:` source of the ratchet read it; a reader that does
not know the keys `cleanup`, `smooth_mode` and `remove_mode` ignores them. The Refine page is such a reader: an import followed by an
export on the page drops these three keys (the import keeps only the known keys), so a FAIR or tube mark becomes a plain smooth mark with
the call default of `apply_marks`. The page draws one sphere for each point, and a list can have many points (the ladle list at 0.5 mm: 68,937
points in 10 marks; the hook list at 0.6 mm: 2,098 points in 4 marks), so a long list draws slowly. The file has no time, no host name, no absolute path and no
timing: it is a function of the part, the options and the code. `cleanup.json` has the full report (`header`, `options`, `method`,
`marks`, `bodies`, `not_listed`, `counts`, `estimate`, `routes`, `problems`, `notes`, `timings_s`, `elapsed_s`, `peak_rss_mb`,
`load_avg`); its paths are relative to its own folder.
- The header `cleanup` of `marks.json`: `format`, `tool`, `run` (name, `final_stl_sha256`, `h_mm`, `density_g_cm3`), `pitch_mm`,
  `pitch_is_default`, `grid` (shape, voxels, origin), `thresholds` (value, unit, anchor and `overridden` of each), `kinds`, `mirror`,
  `applicability`, `bodies`, `stress`, `real_change`, `counts` (`found`, `after_twin_merge`, `listed` = candidates written, `marks` = marks written, `not_listed`, `by_operator`,
  `twins_merged`, `frozen_excluded`, `outside_run_grid`) and `order`.
- Each mark: `id` (the position, 1 to N), `type`, `points`, `radius_mm`, `mirror`, `remove_mode` or `smooth_mode`, `note` (one
  sentence: what and why) and `cleanup`, the facts of the candidate:

| Detector | Type and mode | `points` | `radius_mm` |
|---|---|---|---|
| body, spur, bump | `remove`, `remove_mode: "cut"` | a walk over the voxel centres of the detected set (below) | half the voxel diagonal, `pitch x sqrt(3) / 2`, rounded up to 1e-4 (0.4331 at 0.5 mm) |
| SMOOTH member | `smooth`, `smooth_mode: "tube"` | the ordered skeleton path, one point for each `path_step_mm` | the mean section radius |
| FAIR member (flat web) | `smooth`, `smooth_mode: "fair"` | the same path | `fair_zone_mm` (5.0, the radius of the fairing zone) |

*The walk.* `apply_marks` reads the points of a mark as one polyline. In raster order the chords between two voxel centres leave the
detected set and cut into the parent. So the points of a remove mark are a depth-first walk over the 26-neighbour graph of the voxel set
(the first voxel in index order is the start; a fixed offset order; the way back is written out). Two consecutive points are at most
`pitch x sqrt(3)` apart. A set with more than one 26-component gets one mark for each component (the review found that a segment
between two components can cross material, and `apply_marks` cuts along every segment; so no segment joins two components). The marks
of one candidate have the same facts and the fact `component` (`index`, `of`, `voxels`, `detected_volume_mm3`) with a note "Part k of
n"; the ids go on in the order of the file. Each mark is judged alone by the ratchet, so one part can be accepted and the other
rejected. A set with one component (every candidate on the committed runs) has one mark and no `component`. A body with no voxel
centre inside uses the vertices of its mesh in a walk over the edges (one walk for each group of vertices that its edges connect). `iso` is never
written. A `tube` mark can fall back to `iso` (a stroke under 6 mm, or no strut axis); the step of `apply_marks.json` says `mode iso`
and gives `mode_reason`.

*Facts of a candidate (`cleanup`).* `detector`, `operator` (`remove cut`, `smooth tube`, `smooth fair`), `source` (the pipeline anchor),
`confidence` (`high`, or `low` near a frozen region), `reason`; `location` (`centre_mm`, `bbox_mm`, `nearest_frozen_mm`, `near_frozen`);
`thresholds_used` (each rule that the candidate passed, with its limit and the measured value); `measured` (`detected_volume_mm3`,
`removal_reach_mm`, `mass_g_at_run_density`, `volume_basis`, `length_mm`, `mean_radius_mm`, `length_in_voxels`, `mean_radius_in_voxels`,
`voxels`, `points`, `cv`, `max_over_min`, `flatness`, `dead_ends`, `frozen_share`, `components`); `stress` and
`mirror`. The detected volume is NOT the volume that the operator removes: the cut reaches `removal_reach_mm` around the points and is
larger than the detected set (limit 5). `real_change` in the header says where the real change is: `ratchet.jsonl`
`source.facts.change_mm3` (under `source.ref = marks.json#<id>`) and `cand_NNN/apply_marks.json` (`marks[0].edit.part_volume_change_mm3`).
`stress` (when `verify/fields.npz` is there): `p999_mpa` and `max_mpa` of the elements within `stress_radius_mm` of the candidate voxels,
the case, `elements`, `part_p999_mpa` and `ratio` = `p999_mpa / part_p999_mpa`. The relative ratio is a fact. The absolute 300 MPa limit
of the pipeline is for steel and is not used.

**6. The estimate.** `estimate` has two parts, and the facts name the part that is measured and the part that is a model. `detector`: the
voxels, the memory model, the limits, and the measured figures next to it. `judge` (needs the YAML with an `acceptance` block): the
candidates (the number of marks of this list), the judge calls (the candidates, and one more for the baseline when the root has none),
`printcheck_seconds` (measured on the start part by `ratchet.check_report`; the
list call includes it), `verify_seconds_each` and `verify_memory_gb` (the model of `topopt verify` at the mesh size of the rules),
`apply_seconds_each` (not included: 3 to 13 s for each mark on the hook), `seconds_total_model` and the rules that are not ready. With
`root`, `measured_from_root` is the mean `judge.timing_s.total` of the candidates in the log of that root, and the count of the new list
is multiplied by it. The log of the root gives only its baseline state (the judge calls are the marks, plus 0 when the root holds
its baseline): `ratchet.check_report` subtracts the candidates that the log holds, of any source, and that count is not used. A model that is 2.1 times below
the real judge time was measured on the hook (the apply and the remesh are not in it). With no `acceptance` block, the judge estimate
is `available: false` and the list is still written. `estimate_only` stops after the guard and the estimates and writes no file.

**7. Bodies, mirror and applicability.**
- *Bodies.* The bodies are the connected components of the triangles of `final.stl`. `header.bodies` and `bodies.list` give, for each
  body: `volume_mm3`, `triangles`, `cavity` (an inward shell: a void, never a candidate), `holds_fixed_or_load` (by volume, from the
  labels), `removable`, `outside_run_grid` (the box of the body has no common point with the box of the run grid), `bbox_mm` and
  `centre_mm`; and `non_manifold_vertices` of the file. A body is a removal candidate when it is not a
  cavity, holds no fixed and no load voxel, and another body holds one. There is no keep-largest and no volume limit: the judge decides.
  If no body holds a fixed or load voxel, the block says so (the labels may not match `final.stl`) and no body is a candidate. When a
  removable body exists, the file holds the bodies only (`kinds` asks for another set): a root with printcheck-only rules would judge a
  feature cut with no stress and no stiffness rule. `topopt verify` stops on a body with no fixed node (section 16), so the part with
  such a body has `errors.verify` at the baseline of the ratchet. The workflow is two roots. First: the body marks with rules that need
  `printcheck` only (`watertight`, `bodies`, `loose_island`, `mass`); then a list on the `acc_01` of that root (the default folder is
  beside the root), and a new root for the features. `tests/test_cleanup_ratchet.py` runs both steps. A part from `topopt run` rarely has
  such a body; the step is for STL files from other tools. A removable body that lies outside the grid of the run gets no mark: it is a
  fact (`outside_run_grid`, below and limit 7).
- *Mirror.* The detection is on the full part. The planes come from `run.json` `mirror` (section 26.1; axis-aligned, distinct axes);
  each is a lattice plane. A candidate B is a twin of A (same detector and operator) when a mirror image of the voxel set of A, for any
  element of the group of the reflections (2 or 3 planes give 4 or 8 images), shares a voxel with B. There is no tolerance. The solid
  mask is symmetric on the lattice up to the small shift of the rays of the inside test (`topopt/voxelize.py` `_JITTER`, 0.000731 and
  0.000419 of a pitch); the measurement on the E5 pair is 0 differing voxels. The skeleton is not symmetric (130 points differ). A set of twins is one mark, with the points of the largest candidate
  (ties by the position) and `mirror: true`; `apply_marks` edits the images. `cleanup.mirror.twins` lists the other candidates
  (`detector`, `centre_mm`, `detected_volume_mm3`, `twin_overlap_voxels`, `twin_iou`), and `header.mirror.pairs_merged` counts them.
  A candidate on a plane with no twin is one mark with `mirror: false` and `cleanup.mirror.on_mirror_plane_voxels` above 0. With no
  plane, every `mirror` is `false` and `header.mirror` is `null`.
- *Applicability.* The spur, SMOOTH and FAIR detectors assume a lattice of struts. On a shell or a plate (the ladle) the skeleton gives
  sheet fragments as members. `header.applicability` always has these facts: `members_in_table`, `members_with_profile`, `branches`,
  `skeleton_points`, `dead_end_member_share` (by count), `dead_end_member_volume_share`, `member_volume_share` (the members over the
  solid), `flat_member_volume_share`. `note` is a fixed sentence, present when a spur, SMOOTH or FAIR candidate is listed. There is no
  trigger number: two parts cannot prove one. Reference values (this code, anchored lattice, the committed demo parts):

| Part, pitch | Members | With profile | Dead-end share by count | Dead-end share by volume | Members over solid | Flat share by volume |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hook (full), 0.3 mm | 57 | 46 | 0.304 | 0.171 | 0.858 | 0.823 |
| Hook (full), 0.5 mm | 21 | 18 | 0.111 | 0.061 | 0.925 | 0.826 |
| Hook (full), 0.6 mm | 21 | 20 | 0.150 | 0.071 | 0.916 | 0.809 |
| Ladle, 0.5 mm | 165 | 140 | 0.529 | 0.296 | 0.697 | 0.298 |
| Ladle, 1.0 mm | 59 | 54 | 0.463 | 0.323 | 0.739 | 0.214 |

  The dead-end share by volume separates the two parts in these five rows (hook 0.171 or less, ladle 0.296 or more). That is a
  measurement on two parts, not a limit.

**8. Limits (facts; each has its evidence).**
1. The judge runs the buckling check only when a rule `buckling` is listed (36.1; K1-B): without that rule a thinner strut can pass and lose its buckling margin. The rules `displacement` and
   `alignment` read the rows of `limits` on the tets since K1-B (36.1).
2. The stress of a remesh moves by about 0.2 % at a mesh of 1.75 mm and about 2 % at 3.27 mm for a harmless cut (36.10). With
   `not_worse` and no tolerance a harmless cut can be rejected by noise. The stiffness of the committed test fixture (`posts_part`, mesh
   1 mm, limit 5 %) does not scatter from run to run: 7 runs (1 and 4 threads) gave a drop of 7.401 % for the rejected mark and 2.990 % for
   the accepted one, equal to 5 decimals. The margins to the limit are 2.4 and 2.0 percentage points. The position of the whole case on
   the lattice changes the drop by 6 to 21 percentage points (limit 5), so the ratchet test asserts one position and does not claim a
   margin in multiples of the noise.
3. The detectors are weak on the demo parts. The full hook (`hook_full`, mesh 1.5 mm, rules watertight, bodies, stress `not_worse`
   with 5 %, stiffness 10 %, mass must fall): at 0.6 mm the list has 3 bumps and 1 FAIR member; the ratchet gave 2 ACCEPT and 2 REJECT
   (the bump removals 1 and 3 on stress, +16.4 % and +8.6 % on the case `hang`); at 0.5 mm it has 1 bump and the ratchet REJECTED it
   (+11.6 % stress). The volume went from 21362.8 to 21278.0 mm3 (-0.40 %). The ladle gives sheet fragments as members (applicability).
4. The list depends on the pitch and on where the part sits on the lattice. Short hook at 0.5, 0.6 and 1.0 mm: 1, 2 and 1
   candidates. Full hook at 0.3, 0.5 and 0.6 mm: 2, 1 and 4. Ladle at 0.5 and 1.0 mm: 13 found (10 listed) and 6. The anchored lattice gives
   one list for a shift of whole pitches. A shift of a fraction of a pitch can give another list (the test fixtures are asserted at three
   shifts of the whole case). The outcome of a ratchet on a fixture also depends on the position (limit 5).
5. The cut is larger than the detected set. Removed over detected volume was 1.24 to 1.74 on the four bump removals of the hook runs
   (95.0 mm3 detected and 133.4 removed; 137.6 and 170.7; 48.6 and 84.3; 39.3 and 68.5). The cut can reach into the parent when the
   detected set has a collar under the feature. The new surface can have edges under the verify limit (limit 6). The outcome of the same
   two marks depends on the position of the whole case by a fraction of a voxel. Measured on the committed fixture (`posts_part`,
   stiffness limit 5 %, mesh 1 mm), marks c001 and c002:
   - phase 0: c001 -7.401 % stiffness (REJECT), c002 -2.990 % (ACCEPT); the same numbers in 7 of 7 runs;
   - shift (0.13, 0, 0.07): c001 -13.39 % and c002 -23.55 %, both REJECT. For c002 the parent check of `apply_marks` says
     `within_tolerance: false` (skeleton drop 1.5 to 1.8 mm at 4 points over the tolerance, median thickness near the mark 2.25 to 1.75 mm):
     the cut notches the bar;
   - shift (0.31, 0, 0.19): before C3c `verify` refused both outputs (`no_input`, "prepared surface has an edge of 0.0000 mm (limit
     0.05 mm)", limit 6). Since C3c (the weld retry of `prepare_surface`, section 14) both are judged: c001 -28.28 % stiffness (REJECT),
     c002 -3.59 % (ACCEPT). `tests/test_cleanup_ratchet.py` asserts this, and a companion test with the retry off asserts the refusal.

   The change of the drop is 6 to 21 percentage points. It is a systematic effect of the voxel-exact cut, not noise. The ratchet test asserts
   the outcome at phase 0 only; the list tests assert the list at three shifts.
6. The mark geometry is voxel-exact: fold edges and very short edges can appear (facts of `totals.surface_quality`). All 6 applied
   candidates of limit 5 (phase 0 and the two shifts) have 662 to 970 edges under 0.05 mm in `totals.surface_quality.after`
   (`edge_min_mm` 1e-5). They come from marching cubes on the new surface: a flat face that lies on a node of the lattice has a field
   value of about 1e-15 there, and the iso-surface at `EDIT_LEVEL` (1e-5) makes clusters of two to five vertices 1e-5 to 3e-5 mm apart
   (c001 at shift (0.31, 0, 0.19): 460 clusters, 888 short edges; all in the new surface; the old part and the sewn seam have none, or
   5 to 11 at most, which verify removes). The collapse of the prepare step of `topopt verify` removes most of them but not all (a
   hair-thin triangular tube fails the link condition; a flat sliver can fail the normal check), and before C3c `topopt verify`
   refused the surface (36.7: `errors.verify`, the stiffness check `no_input`, REJECT; the candidate was lost). The refusal was not
   limited to the plain-boolean seam: at shift (0.31, 0, 0.19) both refused outputs have `seam.method: sewn`. Since C3c the prepare
   step welds the input once after such a refusal (section 14, weld retry) and `apply_marks` is unchanged (`edited.stl` is the same
   bytes). Measured on the posts case at eight positions of the whole case, 16 candidates: 6 were refused before; with the retry 2
   are refused and 14 are prepared (the 10 that passed before give the same prepared surface). The 2 refused candidates are a known
   limit (C3c does not change `apply_marks`). The weld of the input is not a closed manifold, the refusal
   says so and where ("... the weld retry was tried and did not help: the welded surface is not a closed manifold (...); first pinch
   vertex at (16.3169, -4.0000, 0.3600)"), and the user sees REJECT with `no_input` as before. The cause is in `apply_marks`: marching
   cubes on a flat face that lies on a lattice node makes a hair cluster that joins two sheets of the part which face opposite ways.
   (Measured in the review of C3c.) Shift (0.07, 0, 0.11) mark 2: one cluster of 4 vertices (extent 2.2e-5 mm) whose faces have normals that are nearly opposite
   (cosine -0.969), and no other vertex within 0.2 mm; any weld of the cluster makes a pinch vertex. Shift (0.11, 0.17, 0.23) mark 2:
   a cluster of 5 vertices (extent 2.7e-5 mm) and a group of 3 (extent 0.031 mm) on the plane x = 16.3169 with faces back to back
   (cosine -0.9995), a contact of no thickness; the weld makes a non-manifold edge ("first non-manifold edge at (16.3169, 1.9197,
   0.3571)"). A fix belongs in `apply_marks`, as its own item: it moves the numbers of candidates that pass today. There is no volume or
   thickness limit for the weld (it would be a new number; the weld changes the volume by about 0.003 mm3 of 1180 on the cases
   measured). A rectangular fin
   (plain-boolean seam) and a second candidate on a part that an earlier accept edited gave the refusal before C3c and are not
   re-measured. A deep voxel-exact mark of a thick spur or body can give a `surface_note` in `apply_marks.json` (a point is far from the surface).
7. A body with no fixed node cannot be judged by `verify` (part 7: two roots). A mark for a body that lies outside the grid of the run (a
   body beyond the design box; `final.stl` of the optimizer stays on the grid, so this needs an STL from another tool) has two wrong
   outcomes in `apply_marks`, both a C3a limit. (a) The frozen distance outside the grid is read at the nearest grid voxel, so a 4 mm cube
   at x 30 to 34 (the grid ends at x 24, beyond the load tip) gets `no_effect` with the reason "all of the cut lies within frozen_keep_mm
   (3 mm) of a frozen region", which is not true. (b) A body 2 to 3 mm outside the grid (the same cube at x 27 to 31, or at y 8 to 12 on a
   grid that ends at y 6) gives an internal `ValueError` ("Surface level must be within volume data range") from the marching cubes. So
   the list makes no mark for such a body. `bodies.list` gives `outside_run_grid: true`, `not_listed` has the entry (`outside_run_grid:
   true`, `why_not_listed` starting with `outside_run_grid`, and `options`), `counts.outside_run_grid` counts it, and `notes` says so. The
   test is box against box: the body box has no common point with the box of the grid (`origin` to `origin + shape x h`). It has no
   tolerance, and a body that only crosses the grid edge keeps its mark and `apply_marks` cuts it (measured: a 4 x 4 x 2 mm box at x 23 to
   27 on a grid that ends at x 24: `applied`, -33.35 mm3). The final STL of a real run can reach beyond the grid by a small amount (hook
   0.23 mm, ladle 1.26 mm), so a test of full containment would be wrong. The options in the entry: an STL of the part without the body,
   judged with the `stl:` source of the ratchet (an exact removal that needs no mark); or a design box that holds the body. The test is
   conservative: a body 0.05 mm outside the grid also has no mark.
8. The mass limits of the pipeline are volumes at 0.0078 g/mm3 (geometric sizes), not at the density of the run.
9. Not ported (each needs an input that the demo has not): the old-mark exemption, the CAD frozen annuli, the half mesh and the fixed
   mirror plane, the absolute stress limits and four named load cases, the VTK renders, the `eval2` re-run (the ratchet is the judge), the
   `RM_PARAMS` tables and the chain script (the ratchet is the chain), the pinch split of `stl_clean` (`apply_marks` splits pinches).
10. Stress facts need `verify/fields.npz` for this `final.stl`; with none, `stress` is `null` and the order by stress is unknown.
11. A SMOOTH candidate asks for a `tube`, which can fall back to `iso` (part 5).
12. The candidates are found on one part. After an accept the hash `source_sha256` is stale and the `marks:` source applies the later
    marks to the new parent with `allow_stale` (36.7). A location that was rejected can be listed again by a new list on the new parent.
13. The applicability note has no trigger number; the reference values are two parts.
14. Time (Linux x86_64, load average 5 to 11 from other jobs): the list takes 6.1 s on the full hook at 0.5 mm (2.24 M voxels, 0.35 GB
    peak), 11.6 s at 0.3 mm (10.19 M voxels, 0.85 GB), 8.7 s on the ladle at 0.5 mm (9.29 M voxels, 0.84 GB). One judged candidate on
    the hook takes 21.7 to 32.0 s (apply 6.4 to 11.8 s, printcheck 3.1 to 5.4 s, verify 9.5 to 18.9 s); the whole ratchet of four candidates took 113.8 s.

## 30. Case file, brief and the soft gate of `run_topopt` (added with D2)

Code: `topopt/case.py` (the logic; it imports `topopt.config` and `topopt.runinfo` only) and, in `topopt_mcp/server.py`, the tools
`record_brief` and `case_status` and one gate call in `run_topopt`. No new dependency. Nothing here is specific to macOS or to Linux. **The CLI writes no case.**
`topopt run` is unchanged, so a run from the CLI is bit-equal to the run before D2. The engine files are not changed. (Since P9-7a the part card, section 9.2, reads the case
file, read only, when `topopt run` ends and when `topopt report` runs, to show the brief. It writes nothing there. A run does not change because of it.)

**A case.** One problem YAML, the region STL files that it names, one brief and many runs. The case folder is the folder of the
YAML, inside the work folder. The case has two files beside the YAML, named after the YAML stem:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `<stem>.case.json` | JSON, written with `runinfo.write_atomic`. The brief, the input hashes of the brief and of each run, one entry for each run. |
| `<stem>.case-log.jsonl` | One JSON line for each event. It only grows. |

Two YAMLs in one folder are two cases. Two YAML names with one stem (`hook.yaml` and `hook.yml`) have the same case file name, so they
cannot be two cases: `case.json` holds the YAML file name (`yaml`). `record_brief` for another file name writes nothing and gives a fact
and an option (rename one YAML); `case_status` and the gate treat that YAML as a YAML with no case. A case exists when its `case.json` exists. `record_brief` makes it. A YAML outside the work
folder (a relative path that only the code folder has, such as an example, or any path outside `TOPOPT_WORKSPACE`) has no case:
`record_brief` writes nothing there and gives the fact and the options (copy the YAML and its STL files into the work folder, or
use `build_regions`). A file in the code folder is replaced by a plugin update, so a case file cannot live there. A source checkout
with no `TOPOPT_WORKSPACE` has the code folder as the work folder: a YAML there (not under `runs/`) is recorded, with a fact (git
does not list a case file by default, an update can replace the folder) and an option (copy the YAML and the STL files into a work
folder; the option ends with how to change the work folder, in the words of the surface, section 10.1). `.gitignore` lists `*.case.json`, `*.case-log.jsonl` and `*.case.json.bad*`.

**`case.json`.** `format` (1), `yaml` (the YAML file name), `created_at`, `brief_count`, `brief` (null or the object below), `runs`
(a list of run entries). Every path in it is relative. No absolute path and no user name is written.

- `brief`: `id` (1, 2, ... one more for each `record_brief`), `recorded_at` (ISO time with the offset, to the second), `mode`
  (`state`: say it and go on; a `confirm` mode that waits is later), `text`, `assumptions` and `criteria` (lists of
  `{"text": str, "origin": "user" | "inferred" | "default"}`), `inputs`.
- `inputs` (in a brief and in a run entry): `yaml` (SHA-256 of the YAML bytes), `yaml_content` (a digest of the parsed YAML as
  canonical JSON, or null if the YAML does not parse; it is not a file hash; an integer and an equal float are one value, so `1`
  and `1.0` are not a change), `files` (`{"<role>:<path>": SHA-256 or "missing"}`). The `inputs` of a **brief** also hold the split of the
  parsed YAML by the kind of each key (P9-4b, "Method keys" below): `yaml_requirements` (a digest of the parts that are not `method`),
  `requirement_keys` (`{"<key path>": 12 hex characters}`, the start of the digest of each such part) and `method_values`
  (`{"<key path>": value}`, the method parts that the YAML sets, in JSON form). They are absent when the YAML did not parse at the time of
  the brief, and in a brief from before P9-4b. The `inputs` of a run entry hold none of them.
- Run entry: `run_dir` (the run folder relative to the YAML folder, or null when the folder is outside the work folder, with
  `run_dir_name` then: `<outside>/<12 hex>`, the same form as the key of an outside file, and no folder name), `started_at`, `pid` (the process that `run_topopt` started), `brief` (the `id` of the current brief, or null
  when the override was used), `inputs` (the hashes when the run started).
- `run.json` `assumptions` stays a list of strings (the YAML `assumptions` key, section 5). The brief holds the same facts with an
  origin. `case_status` compares the texts and gives a fact when they differ. It blocks nothing.

**Input hashes.** `topopt.runinfo.sha256_file` for every file (the hash is of the content). The files are the YAML and every region
file that `config.regions` holds. No second file-hash function exists. A file that is not there has the hash `missing`; that is a
fact, not an error. The keys come from `topopt.runinfo.region_files` (section 24.1) with the work folder as `root` and the YAML as
`yaml_path`; the checkpoint of D1b uses the same function, so a case record and a checkpoint give one key for one file:
- The key holds the path as the YAML names it, so a symbolic link keeps its own name and not the name of its target. A link that
  points to a new target with the same bytes is not a change. A link inside the work folder to a file outside it keeps its name and
  gives a fact (the case keeps the hash of the content).
- A file outside the work folder (an absolute path in the YAML) has the key `<role>:<outside>/<12 hex>/<file name>`. The 12 hex
  characters are the start of the SHA-256 of the resolved path text. No folder name of the outside place is written to `case.json`,
  the log or a reply; a fact names the role and the file name. (The parsed YAML of a checkpoint and `run.json` `region_files` still
  hold a path string that the YAML itself holds.)

A YAML that does not load (a syntax error, a missing STL, the test stub `name: x`) still has its hash and the fact `<yaml> does not
load as a problem (...)`. The region files then come from the file names in the YAML text. If the text gives none, they are the keys
that the record holds (the brief, or that run entry), and the fact says that only these files are checked. The hashes are taken in `run_topopt` before the process starts. The process can hash again later (the checkpoint), so a
file that changes between the two gives two records.

**Stale.** `compare` gives the list of changed files; each has a fact that names it.
- A region file is stale when its hash differs, when it is missing, when it is not in the record (a new file of the problem), or when
  the YAML no longer names it. Each record (the brief, a run entry) is compared with its own files. When the YAML gives no file list,
  a file that only another record holds is not reported as new.
- The YAML is stale when its bytes differ and its parsed content differs. A change of a comment or of the format only (the same
  `yaml_content`) is a fact and not stale. A YAML that does not parse any more is stale. **For a brief** (not for a run entry) a change
  of the values of method keys only is not stale either (see "Method keys").
- A brief or a run entry is stale when one of its input files is stale. A stale entry is a fact. It does not stop a tool by itself.

**Method keys (P9-4b).** The lever cards (section 41) give every YAML key a kind. The brief gate ignores a change of `method` keys, because
the rule of section 41.2 lets the agent change a method setting without asking, with a report. Without this, an agent that follows the
advice of `environment` (`settings.solver: gpu-mg`) or of a lever card (a larger `settings.voxel_size`) after `record_brief` would get
`awaiting_user` for a setting that is not a user requirement.
- The kind of a key path comes from `topopt.levers_cards` at run time, in `topopt.case.key_kind`: the card with the longest key path that
  starts the path of the key gives the kind (`settings.voxel_size` before `settings`). `[]` in a card matches every list item, and a `<name>`
  token matches any name of a mapping. A key with no card takes the kind of the nearest card above it (`settings.no_such_key` is `method`,
  like `settings`); a key with no card above it is a `requirement`. A card key listed in `also` has the kind of its card.
- `both` counts as a `requirement` in this version: the record does not say which origin a value has, so a change of
  `settings.volume_fraction`, `settings.objective` or `settings.min_member_mm` is stale. The gate does not read the origin of a value either:
  a `settings.voxel_size` that the user stated is a `method` key here, so a larger voxel size passes the gate with a fact. The agent still asks
  the user first, as section 41.2 says.
- A **part** is one value with no mapping inside: a number, a text, a list of numbers or texts (a force, the beta schedule), or an empty
  mapping or list. A mapping is opened, and so is a list that holds a mapping (`load_cases[0].name`). The key path of a part has the list numbers.
- `record_brief` records the split (see `inputs` above). The gate and `case_status` compare the brief with the YAML now (`compare` with
  `method_free=True`):
  - the same `yaml_requirements`, other method values: not stale. One fact for each changed method key, with both values in back quotes (`not set`
    for a key that is not there): "`settings.solver`: a method key changed from `amg` to `gpu-mg`; the brief stays current". The words are "a method key" for every
    method key, also for `name` or `assumptions` (they are keys of kind method, but they are not settings of the method).
  - another `yaml_requirements`: stale, as before (`stale_files` holds the YAML). The facts are the YAML change, one fact that names the changed
    requirement key paths (with "(new)" or "(removed)"), and the method facts without "the brief stays current".
  - a brief with no split (from before P9-4b, or recorded when the YAML did not parse): stale on any change of the content, as before, with one
    fact that says that `record_brief` again gives the rule.
  - `run_topopt` with a method change only starts the run. The method facts are in `brief_facts` of the reply (the agent reports them to the
    user), in the facts of `case_status`, and in the facts of a stop for another reason. They repeat on each call until the next `record_brief`.
- The run entries are not changed. A run entry is compared with the whole content (`compare` with `method_free=False`, the default): a run
  that started before a solver change is stale after it, because another solver is another run. `case_status` shows that in `runs[].stale`.
- `compare` is called in three places: the run view of `case_status` (whole content), the brief of `case_status` and the gate of `run_topopt`
  (both `method_free=True`).

**Writes.** `case.json`: `write_atomic` (a `.tmp` file in the same folder, then `os.replace`). If the write fails, the last valid
file stays, the `.tmp` file is removed, and the tool says so. A left-over `.tmp` file is ignored by the readers. The log: one whole
line for each event (JSON and `\n`, one write, then `flush`; the rule of `history.jsonl`, section 24.1). If an earlier write left a
part line, the next event starts on a new line, and a reader skips the part line. There is no lock. Two servers on one work folder
can lose a run entry of `case.json` (read, change, write). The log keeps every event, and `case_status` gives a fact when the log has
`run_started` events that `case.json` does not hold (same `pid` and `started_at`). A case file that cannot be read is moved to
`<name>.case.json.bad1` by the next `record_brief` (`.bad2`, ... when that name exists; an earlier file is never replaced). The next
brief `id` is one more than the highest of `brief_count` and of the `brief_recorded` events of the log, so an `id` is not used twice.

**Log events.** Each line has `ts` and `event`.
- `brief_recorded`: `brief` (the whole brief), `replaced` (the earlier `id` or null).
- `run_started`: the run entry, and `method_facts` (a list of the facts about method keys that differ from the brief at this start; always
  there, an empty list when none; the entry in `case.json` does not hold it).
- `gate_returned`: `state` (`awaiting_user`), `reason` (`no_brief` or `stale`), `stale_files`.
- `override_used`: `override` (`proceed_without_brief=true`), `reason`, `stale_files`. It comes before `run_started` of the same run.

**`record_brief(yaml_path, text, assumptions=None, criteria=None)`.** Makes the case or replaces its brief. A wrong shape of the
arguments gives `{"error", "recorded": false}` and writes nothing. Reply: `recorded`, `case` (path relative to the work folder),
`yaml_rel`, `brief`, `replaced`, `facts`, `options` (empty, or the option for a YAML in the code folder). For a YAML outside the work
folder, or a YAML whose name differs from the `yaml` of the case file: `recorded: false`, `case: null`, `facts`, `options`.

**`case_status(yaml_path)`.** Changes nothing. Reply: `yaml_rel`, `exists`, `case`, `log`, `brief` (null or the object above),
`brief_stated` (a current brief exists), `brief_stale`, `stale_files`, `inputs` (the hashes now), `runs`, `gate` (what `run_topopt` does
now), `facts`, `options`. `runs` lists the run entries newest first. The run data is read from the run folder (no copy):
`run_dir_rel`, `started_at`, `pid`, `brief`, `state`, `iteration`, `stale`, `stale_files`, `facts`. `state` is the `state` of
`status.json`, or `missing` (no folder), `replaced` (another run holds the folder), `not_written` (the folder holds only older data
than the start of this run: an earlier run, or this run stopped before it wrote) or `unknown`. `job.json` is the job of a run entry
when its `pid` is equal and its `started_at` is within 120 s of the entry (a `pid` can be used again). A folder holds another run
when `job.json` is not the job of this entry and (a) it is the job of a later entry of this case with the same folder, or (b) it
started after this run. A later entry replaces an earlier one only when the folder shows data of the later run: its `job.json`, or
(no job file) a `status.json` or `run.json` newer than its `started_at`. A later run that wrote nothing replaces nothing. Without
`job.json` the file times of `status.json` and `run.json` are compared with `started_at`. The default folder `runs/live` is reused by
each run, so the run before the last one is `replaced` when the last one wrote into it. Without `job.json` (the fake child of the
tests, a run from before `runjob`), a run that stops less than one second after the earlier run ended can show the state of the
earlier run: the file times cannot tell the two apart. The reply has the same keys for a YAML outside the work folder (`log`,
`inputs`, `brief` and `case` are null; `runs` and `stale_files` are empty; `brief_stated` and `brief_stale` are false).

**The gate in `run_topopt`.** `run_topopt(..., proceed_without_brief=False)` (after `stop_rules`). The gate reads the case and writes one log line when it
stops. It sits before the check for a running verify job and before `_alive_run()`, so a stop closes no dashboard and starts nothing.
- No case file, or a YAML outside the work folder: the run starts as before. The reply adds `brief_stated: false` and `brief_facts`
  (`no case for this YAML; record_brief makes one`). Nothing is written.
- A case with a current brief: the run starts. `brief_stated: true`. `brief_facts` has the notes (for example a changed comment, or one
  fact for each changed method key: "Method keys" above).
  One run entry goes to `case.json` and `run_started` to the log, after the process has started.
- A case with no brief, or a stale brief: the reply is `{"state": "awaiting_user", "facts": [...], "options": [...], "override":
  "proceed_without_brief=true", "case": <path>, "yaml_rel": <path>}`. It has no `error` and no `pid`. The log gets `gate_returned`.
- A call with `resume=true` (section 24.2) goes through the gate too. A resume has its own stop for changed inputs (override
  `allow_changed_inputs=true`), and a changed input file is also a stale brief. So the stop of the gate has one option that names both
  overrides (`resume=true`, `proceed_without_brief=true`, and `allow_changed_inputs=true` if an input changed since the checkpoint). The
  reply keeps `override: "proceed_without_brief=true"`. The gate stops before the resume refusal is read, so a refusal of the resume is
  seen after the gate passes.
- The same case with `proceed_without_brief=true`: the run starts, the reply has `brief_stated: false` and `brief_facts` (the facts
  of the stop), the run entry has `brief: null`, and the log gets `override_used` and `run_started`. A current brief with the
  override is not an override: `brief_stated: true` and no `override_used`.
- If the case code fails (an unexpected error), the run starts and `brief_facts` says that the check failed. The gate is a fact and
  an override, not a block.
The reply of `awaiting_user` is a third shape for a client: refusals have `error`, a start has `pid`.

**Limits.** Facts, not proof: a hash taken in `run_topopt` is not the hash that the process computes later. No lock (see Writes).
`confirm` mode, role folders (`cases/<name>/`), a tool to read and write other case files, and a log viewer are not in D2. Keep the STL
files beside the YAML: a file outside the work folder is hashed, but it is easy to lose when the work folder moves.

## 31. Displacement and alignment limits (added with A5)

Two kinds of limit in the YAML: the displacement of a region, and the relative shift and tilt of two regions.
Each limit is a constraint row of the A1 API (section 13). The code is `topopt/rows_motion.py` (rows, node sets, rigid fit,
report block), with the keys read in `topopt/config.py`.

### YAML keys

```yaml
regions:
  design: design.stl
  fixed: [plate.stl]
  load: {tip: tip.stl}
  measure:                        # optional. A name to STL mapping, like regions.load.
    probe: probe.stl              # A probe: a set of nodes. No label, no force. It changes the model in no way.
    collar_a: collar_a.stl
    collar_b: collar_b.stl

limits:                           # optional.
  displacement:                   # a list of rows
    - name: tip_drop              # optional. Default: the region name. The pair (sense, name) is unique in this list.
      region: tip                 # a regions.measure name or a regions.load name
      limit_mm: 1.5               # float > 0, mm. A limit of 0 ("must not move at all") is not allowed: the row is g = value / limit - 1.
      direction: [0, 0, -1]       # optional. Any non-zero vector (it is normalised). Without it: the norm of the mean vector.
      sense: abs                  # optional, only with direction. abs (default) | max | min
      cases: [hang]               # optional. One case name or a list. Default: every load case.
      price: 1000                 # optional. float > 0. The MMA price of a violation. Default 1000.
  alignment:
    - name: collars               # optional. Default: <region_a>-<region_b>.
      region_a: collar_a          # two different regions (measure or load)
      region_b: collar_b
      axis: [0, 0, 1]             # required. Any non-zero vector (it is normalised). Shift and tilt are measured across it.
      shift_limit_mm: 0.05        # float > 0, mm. One row per case.
      tilt_limit_rad: 0.001       # float > 0, rad. One row per case. At least one of the two limits is needed.
      cases: [pull_off]           # optional, as above
      price: 1000                 # optional, as above
```

- The loader checks the keys as in section 2. Unknown keys are an error. A number that YAML 1.1 loads as text
  (`5e-3`) is read as a number in `limit_mm`, `shift_limit_mm` and `tilt_limit_rad`.
- Messages (one line, with the file name): `'limits.displacement[0].region' is 'nope', not a measure or a load region (known: ...)`,
  `'limits.displacement[0].sense' needs a 'direction'. Without a direction the row limits the norm of the mean displacement vector, and a norm has no sign`,
  `'limits.alignment[0]' compares region 'a' with itself; name two different regions`,
  `'limits.alignment[0]' needs 'shift_limit_mm' or 'tilt_limit_rad' (or both)`,
  `'regions.measure.tip' has the name of a load region; a row names a region, so the names must differ`.
- A row with no `cases` key makes one row per load case.
- The pair (`sense`, `name`) must be unique in `limits.displacement`: a `max` row and a `min` row may share a region (and a default name),
  because their row names differ (`displacement_max:...` and `displacement_min:...`). Two rows with the same sense and name stop with
  `'limits.displacement[1]' has the name 'mid' and the sense 'max', as an earlier row; give each row its own 'name'` (for `abs`: `has the name 'mid', as an earlier row; ...`).
  The same rule holds for `limits.alignment` (the name only).

### Regions

- A measure region is an STL (closed, in the same frame, as every region). Its voxels are the voxels whose centre is inside the STL
  (the test of section 3). Only voxels inside the grid count. A measure STL does **not** extend the grid (the grid comes from
  design, fixed, keep-out and load). Its voxels get no label and no density.
- A load region as the `region` of a row is the voxels with the label LOAD and the id of that region (a fixed or keep-out voxel
  has priority and is not in it).
- The node set is the nodes of all voxels of the region (the 8-corner rule of section 5, `build_forces`). A node that no active voxel
  touches has no dof. It is left out. The facts below name the count.
- A fixed node stays in the set. Its displacement is 0 and it counts in the mean and in the fit.
- Per-dof supports: a row reads the displacement of every free dof and uses 0 for a fixed dof. It needs no change for that.

### Displacement row

`y` is the mean over the nodes of the region of `u . d` (with `direction`) or the mean vector `(mean ux, mean uy, mean uz)` (without).

| `sense` | value of the row | met when |
|---|---|---|
| `abs` (default; and with no direction) | `sqrt(|y|^2 + eps^2)` | `|y| <= limit` (about; see eps; the report says `g_end <= 0.005`, below) |
| `max` (direction needed) | `y` | `y <= limit` |
| `min` (direction needed) | `-y` | `y >= -limit` |

The row is `g = value / limit - 1 <= 0` (the linear form, the A1 default `scale = limit`). The limit must be above 0: a limit of 0 ("must not
move down at all") has no scale; use a small limit instead.

The report says "met" for `g <= 0.005` (`NOT_MET`, the rule of section 13 for every row), not for `|y| <= limit`: a row that is 0.5 % over its
limit is met in `metrics.json` `met` and in the run log. The `value` of a `min` row is `-y`: it is positive when the region moves against
`direction` (the motion that the row limits) and negative when it moves along it. The `constraint not met` line of the run log and `history.jsonl` print the
`value` of the table (with the guard for `abs`); `metrics.json` `rows` print the physical value (`|y|`, `y`, or `-y`, without the guard). The two
differ only near zero (`eps = 0.01 * limit`).

- **eps.** `eps = 0.01 * limit`, in the unit of the row. The plain norm has no slope at `y = 0` (KB `norm-constraint-nonsmooth-at-zero`).
  The guard makes the row smooth. It changes the value by `eps^2 / (2 |y|)` or less: 5e-5 of the limit at `|y| = limit`, `eps`
  at `y = 0`. The limit is met for `|y| <= limit * sqrt(1 - 1e-4)`. `max` and `min` have no guard.
- **Units.** mm. A displacement is the linear small-strain displacement of the voxel model.
- **Name.** `displacement:<name>:<case>` (`abs`), `displacement_max:<name>:<case>`, `displacement_min:<name>:<case>`.
- **Sign use.** `direction: [0, 0, -1]`, `sense: max`, `limit_mm: 2` means: the displacement down is 2 mm or less (up is free).
  The same with `sense: min` means: the displacement up is 2 mm or less.

### Alignment row

Each of the two regions gets a least-squares rigid fit of its node displacements: `u_k ~ t + theta x r_k`, with `r_k` the node
position minus the mean `c` of the node positions, equal weights. `t` (mm) is the mean displacement. `theta` (rad) is the small
rotation, `M theta = sum(r_k x u_k)` with `M = sum(|r_k|^2 I - r_k r_k^T)`. With `d = c_A - c_B`, `omega = (theta_A + theta_B) / 2`
and two unit vectors `e1`, `e2` across `axis` (the choice of the pipeline: `e1` from the x axis, from the y axis if `axis` is
within 26 degrees of x; `e2 = axis x e1`):

- shift (mm): `y = (e1 . s, e2 . s)` with `s = (t_A - t_B) + skew(d) omega`. This is the relative displacement of the two rigid
  motions at the midpoint of the two centres, across `axis`.
- tilt (rad): `y = (e1 . (theta_A - theta_B), e2 . (theta_A - theta_B))`.
- The value is `sqrt(|y|^2 + eps^2)` with `eps = 0.01 * limit` and the row is `g = value / limit - 1`, as above.
- A rigid motion of the whole body gives shift 0 and tilt 0 (to round-off). The shift along `axis` and the twist about `axis` are not
  limited. Swapping A and B changes the sign of `y`, not the value. The rotation is linear in `u` (small rotations).
- Names: `shift:<name>:<case>` and `tilt:<name>:<case>`. An `alignment` entry with both limits makes two rows for each case.
- This ports the method of `pipeline/lib/alignment_constraints.py` and `lug_loads.py` (`rigid_motion_rows`): the same rows. The
  centre is the node mean (the pipeline takes a typed centre), the rows are built sparse, the limit is absolute (no reference part),
  and the rank of the fit is checked.

### Gradient

One adjoint solve for each row and each case: `K lam = G^T w`, with `y = G u` and `w` the slope of the value with respect to `y`.
The gradient is `- lam^T (dK/d rho) u`, from `DesignPoint.solve_adjoint` and `stiffness_derivative`. The factor or hierarchy of the
forward solve is reused. A row has no explicit density term. A row whose `w` is exactly 0 (a region of fixed nodes, or `y = 0`) does
no solve and has the gradient 0. The gradient is with respect to `"rho_stiff"` (section 22b): the same as `"rho"` in a default run (bit for bit),
and the slope of the eroded projection in robust mode.

### Rows in the run

- Order: the volume row, then the compliance limits (section 13), then the displacement rows (YAML order, cases in the order of
  `cases`), then the alignment rows (each `alignment` entry: shift for each case, then tilt for each case).
- Price: 1000 by default, the A1 default of a custom linear row; `price` sets it. A limit that the design cannot meet at the volume
  is a fact, not an error. At price 1000 the volume row and the limit row share the miss. With `price: 100` (as the compliance limits)
  the volume stays at its target and only the limit row is unmet.
- Cost: each row and each case is one adjoint solve in each pass. With a direct solver (PARDISO, Cholesky) it adds about 3 % of a pass
  (hook, 115,836 dofs: 0.18 s against 6.2 s). With `amg` it adds about one third of a pass (2.35 s against 7.20 s for the forward solve).
  The time estimate of `topopt check` does not count the rows.
- `history.jsonl`: each row is in `constraints` like every row (section 13). `value` is the value of the table above (with the guard);
  `limit` is in the unit of the row; `g` is the dimensionless row.
- `run.log`: at the end, `constraint not met: displacement:tip:hang  value ...  limit ...` for a row with `g` above 0.005, with the
  hint `options: raise settings.volume_fraction, relax the limit, or move the region onto the load path`.
  At the start, one line `fact: ...` for each fact below.
- `result/metrics.json` gets the key `rows` (a list, empty when the YAML has no A5 limit and no perimeter bound):

```json
"rows": [{"name": "displacement:tip_drop:hang", "kind": "displacement", "unit": "mm", "limit": 1.5,
          "value_start": 3.21, "value_end": 1.49, "g_end": -0.0067, "met": true}]
```

  `kind` is `displacement`, `displacement_max`, `displacement_min`, `shift` or `tilt`, or `perimeter` (the row of section 26.3, unit
  `mm2`, values as the history has them). `value_start` is the value of iteration 0
  (the even start density) and `value_end` the value of the last pass. Both are physical: `|y|` without the guard for `displacement`,
  `shift` and `tilt`, `y` for `displacement_max`, `-y` for `displacement_min`. `met` is `g_end <= 0.005`, the rule of the run log.
  In robust mode (section 22b) `value_end`, `g_end` and `met` are of the nominal design and `value_end_eroded` is the eroded value.
  `run.json` `constraints` keeps name and limit only (section 13).

### Facts and errors

A fact is one line that gives the cause and the options. It does not stop the run. It is a `fact:` line in `run.log` and
a `limits: ...` entry in the `warnings` of `topopt check`. The plain-text `topopt check` prints it as `warning: limits: ...`, as `--json` lists it.

- `region 'probe': 10 of 18 nodes touch no solid or design voxel and have no displacement; they are left out. Options: to measure them, put the region on solid or on a load part; otherwise no change`
- `region 'plate_probe': 4 of 36 nodes are fixed; their displacement is 0 and it counts in the mean and in the fit. Options: to leave them out, cut the region away from the fixed part; otherwise no change`
- `displacement row 'x': every node of 'probe' is fixed, so the value is always 0 and the row cannot steer the design. Options: move the region off the fixed region, or drop the row`

A stop (`UserError`, one line with the file name, at `topopt check` and at the start of `topopt run`, before any solve):

- `alignment row 'collars' cannot work: the rigid fit of region 'collar_a' has rank 5 of 6 (two nodes). A rotation needs nodes that are not on one line. Options: a larger region, a region that is not on one line, or a displacement row in its place`
  (rank 3: one node; rank 5: two nodes, or nodes on one line). The rank is that of the fit matrix, not a count of nodes.
- `displacement row 'x' cannot work: region 'probe' has no node that carries a dof (N nodes, all of them outside the model). Options: move the region onto the part, or make it larger`
- `measure region 'probe' has no voxel inside the grid at voxel_size 2.0. Use a smaller voxel_size, make the region larger, or put it on the part`

### Combinations (facts)

- With mirror (A4a, section 26): the gradient of a row is symmetric by the transposed average of the library. A component that is
  antisymmetric under the mirror is exactly 0 for a symmetric load (for example, the displacement across the plane of a region on the
  plane). The smooth norm then has the gradient 0 and the value `eps`. A region that is itself mirrored (one of a pair) has a mirrored
  displacement, not an equal one.
- With robust mode (A3b, section 22b): `U` belongs to the eroded design. The rows are linear in `U`, so the optimizer sees the
  displacement of the eroded design, as the alignment rows of the pipeline, and the `history.jsonl` values and the `unmet` lines are
  eroded. In `metrics.json` `rows`, `value_end`, `g_end` and `met` are of the nominal design, the part that you print (the rule of
  `compliance_final`): `robust.finish_run` solves the nominal design once and stores `rows_nominal` in `robust.json`. `value_end_eroded` is
  the value that the optimizer saw at the end, and `value_start` is the eroded design of iteration 0 (as `compliance_initial`). The
  displacement of a point is not monotone in the density (section 22b, "The 3-design worst case"), so the nominal value can be above or
  below the eroded one: a nominal `met: false` is possible with an eroded `g` at or below 0. The 3-design mode is the tool for that.
- With the stress step acceptance (A2, section 17): the step acceptance of the stress limit does not check displacement and alignment
  rows. On the way to the limit, MMA can let these rows rise for some passes, mostly after a beta step. The run log and `metrics.json`
  `rows` give the end values. The join is a decision, not a gap: it was built and measured, and the rule holds an active row so close to
  its limit that the design stops moving (compliance 36.5x to 56x of the run without the join with three rows; 1.6 % to 3.7 % higher with
  one kind of row). A tolerance of 1e-2, a floor of the move limit and a check of the violated rows only did not fix it. The rows are `stage_aware` (the run log
  notes a beta stage that ends with a row not met). A stage-aware row with no `measure` is not checked by the rule, and these rows have none.
- With the mass objective (A2, section 17): a displacement or alignment row on a probe region does not hold material. The optimizer can
  remove the material between the load and the probe. Add a `compliance_limit` or a stress limit. A `max` or `min` row is also met when
  the region moves the other way. A row on a load region holds material (the load moves it; for an alignment row, one load region of the two is
  enough). A mass run that has no compliance limit, no stress limit and no row on a load region gets the fact "No row holds material"
  (`problem_facts`, in `topopt check` and in the run log). The run goes on with the rows and no volume ceiling. Each `max` or `min`
  displacement row gets a fact that the other motion meets it (plan, section 7). An unmet row says "the other rows are met, and this
  limit is not met at the end of the run" (not "does not fit at this volume") and, under the mass objective, has no volume option.
- A measure region inside the design space has the displacement of its nodes at the density that is there. A node that no active voxel
  touches (only void voxels or keep-out) has no displacement and is left out (a fact, see Facts and errors). Put the region on a solid
  or a load part for a stable value.
- Springs (B-067) add dofs to the system. A row reads only the dofs of the grid and needs a change then.
- `topopt verify` (B2) reads the YAML with the same loader. Since B3 it computes these rows on the tet model (see "In `topopt verify`" below).

**In `topopt verify` (added with B3).** When the YAML of the run has `limits.displacement` or `limits.alignment` rows, `topopt verify` computes them
from the P2 displacement of the printed STL, with the code of the optimizer (`MotionSet.bind_nodes` of `topopt/rows_motion.py`: the same rigid fits, rank checks,
signs and units). No flag is needed. The optimizer does not change (`MotionSet.bind` is the voxel part of the same code; a test and a hook run are bit-equal). The result is the
key `motion` of `verify.json`. The rows are facts: there is no `met` flag in the record and no exit code. With `topopt verify --gate` (section 16, "The gate"), the gate compares each
`tet_value` with the `limit` of its row (at most the limit, strict) and gives `met` in the key `gate`; a skipped or error record then has `met: null` and fails the gate. The ratchet rules `displacement` and `alignment` (section 36) read the rows in the same way.

- *Node rule.* A region is the set of P2 nodes (vertices and edge midpoints) whose signed distance to the region STL is at least `-band` (the region rule of section 16;
  the role of a measure region is `measure`, a load region keeps its role). The displacement of a region is the equal-weight mean over these nodes. The voxel model uses the grid nodes
  of the voxels of the region. The two sets of points are not the same, and the edge midpoints are most of the P2 nodes, so the two means can differ for the same displacement field.
- *Record.* `kind`, `status` (`done` or `skipped`), `reason` (`rows_cannot_work` for a skip), `rule` (the node rule and the signs, in words), `voxel_value_source`, `band_mm`,
  `regions` (for each region: `role`, `nodes`, `vertices`, `fixed_nodes`, `centre_mm`), `rows`, `facts`, `options`, `seconds`. A row: `name`, `kind`, `unit`, `case`, `limit`, `tet_value`,
  `voxel_value` (`value_end` of the key `rows` of `result/metrics.json`: the value of the optimizer density of the last pass, or `null` if the file does not name the row),
  `difference` (tet minus voxel), `tet_over_voxel`, `tet_over_limit`. The sign rule is the one of the optimizer: `displacement_max` is `y`, `displacement_min` is `-y`, the other rows are `|y|`.
- A row that cannot work on the tets (a region with no P2 node, an alignment fit with a rank below 6) gives `status: skipped` with the fact and the options, and `topopt verify` goes on.
  A row that has no voxel value gives a fact and an option.
