- Measured on the hook (one Linux host): the A5 design with the row `displacement:tip_pull:pull_off` (limit 0.021 mm) has the voxel value 0.020998 mm. The tet value is 0.02575 mm
  (1.23 times the limit, +23 percent) on the `sdf` `final.stl` that this revision makes (tip region: 3,292 P2 nodes, 521 vertices), and 0.03425 mm (1.63 times, +63 percent) on the `blur` `final.stl`
  of the same optimizer design (the older run: 80,170 triangles against 55,712). On the hook design of the recorded run (`blur` STL) the tet tip displacement is 36 to 41 percent above the voxel one.
- The value of a row is a mean over the P2 nodes of the region, so it depends on the mesh size. It moved by 5 to 6 percent between the mesh sizes 1.55 and 1.78 mm (the `limits3` row: `sdf` STL 0.025748 mm at 1.776 mm
  and 0.027247 mm at 1.553 mm; `blur` STL 0.036117 mm at 1.776 mm and 0.034253 mm at 1.553 mm; one shape). The load factors moved by less than 0.5 percent over the same sizes. With `--levels`, the `levels` block has
  `motion_tet_value` for each row, so you can see the change for your design. (A mean weighted by volume would converge with the mesh; it is not built.)

## 32. Print check (added with E1a)

The print check measures a finished part for printing. For each check it gives the value, the limit with its source, a state
(`pass`, `fail` or `unknown`) and a reason. It is geometry only: no solve, no optional package (numpy, scipy and trimesh are core;
the rays use the pinned `rtree`), no GPL extra. It changes no file. By default it only reports; the gate is opt-in and no run stops on it.
Code: `topopt/printcheck.py`.  The numbers of the overhang, the support volume,
the plate contact, the bed fit and the thickness come from `topopt/print_report.py` (section 18), which is not written again.

**After every run** (added with E1c). The post step (`post.finish`) calls `printcheck.write_for_run(run_dir)` last, after `metrics.json` is
written and before the status `done`. That is also so with `write_done=False` (the buckling check, section 33) and in a post-only resume
(`run_topopt` with `resume=true` and `allow_changed_inputs=true` on a finished run, section 41.8: the post step repeats, so a changed `print`
key gives a new report in seconds). The call is `check(run_dir, contain_errors=True)` with the `print` block of `run.json` and the voxel size
`h` of the run (no YAML is read), and it writes `result/print_check.json`. The file is the report of this section, the same keys as `--json`
(`input.stl` is the path at the time of the run). It reports and gates nothing: the run ends `done` whatever the checks say. A fault gives
`{"ok": false, "error": "<Type>: <text>"}` in the file, as the V2 `print` section does (section 18), and the run still ends `done`; a report that JSON cannot write (any exception in the dump) gives the same record; a file that
cannot be written is not an error of the run. The old file is removed before the check and the `.tmp` file after a failed write, so `run_result` never shows an old report as current. `metrics.json` and `final.stl` do not change; the file is new. The hook golden file (27.4)
compares `compliance_final`, `volume_fraction_final`, `volume_final_mm3` and `mass_final_g` with the tiers of 27.5 and does not read this file.
A direct `print_check` or `topopt printcheck` call is unchanged. It is for other limits (`print_settings`, `--set`), another build direction, or an
STL file.

The states are shown in two places. `run_result` has the key `print_check` (absent for a run from before E1c): `ok`, `pass`, `fail` and `unknown` (counts),
`failed` (the ids of the failed checks), `unknown_with_limit` (the ids of the `unknown` checks whose limit has a value: the limit is set and the tool cannot
say), `partial`, `file` and `file_rel`; for `ok: false` it has `ok`, `error`, `file` and `file_rel`. The run log and the screen of `topopt run` get one line
`print check: P pass, F fail, U unknown[; failed: ...][; unknown with a limit: ...] (print_check.json)`, or `print check: not made (<error>); ...` when
`ok` is false. The code is `printcheck.summary_of` and `printcheck.summary_line`. The dashboard result panel does not show it.

The check reads `final.stl` again (float32, as a slicer reads it), so it does not reuse the numbers of the V2 `print` section in `metrics.json`.
Time cost (Linux x86_64, 1 thread, CPU, a shared host; the check's own time is `elapsed_s` and `timing_s` of the report). Hook at 2 mm (19,762 triangles):
the check took 3.64 to 3.77 s (mesh health 0.09 s, V2 numbers 0.5 s, thickness 3.1 s) beside a `finish` of 21.3 to 23.6 s without it and 25.0 to 25.8 s with it
(3 pairs on copies of a finished run; the call replaced by a no-op for the run without it). A second host measured 1.5 to 1.8 s of the check in a `finish` of 9 to 12 s.
Hook at 0.5 mm (313,946 triangles, 564,298 active voxels): the check took 12.7 s (1.7 s, 5.9 s and 5.0 s). The two `finish` times of that run (277 s and 207 s)
are not comparable, because the host load changed between them, so no share is stated for it. The check has capped sample counts (60,000 thickness samples), so its time
grows slowly with the mesh: 3.7 s at 19,762 triangles and 12.7 s at 313,946. It is about the cost of the V2 section that the post step already runs.

**Command**

```
topopt printcheck <STL file or run folder> [--yaml FILE] [--set KEY=VALUE ...] [--resolution-mm MM] [--strict] [--json]
```

- The input is an STL file with any name (`final.stl`, a C2 `nominal.stl`, a C3a `edited.stl`), or a run folder (it has `result/final.stl`; `run.json`
  gives the `print` block of the run and the voxel size `h`). `metrics.json` and the YAML are not needed.
- Settings: the defaults of section 18, then `run.json` `print`, then `--yaml` (its `print` block; the file may have nothing else), then each `--set KEY=VALUE`
  (a key of the `print` block; VALUE is read as YAML: `1.2`, `[250, 210]`, `lpbf`). The later source wins. `settings.from` lists the sources.
- `--resolution-mm`: the size of the smallest member that the mesh holds. Default: `h` of `run.json` (not less than the median mesh edge), else the median mesh edge.
  Use 0 for an exact CAD mesh with big flat triangles.
- Output: text lines, or with `--json` the report below. Line 2 of the text is the `partial:` line (TC-2, section 44).
- Exit code: 0 for any check result. 1 when the input cannot be read (a missing file, a folder with no `result/final.stl`, a file that is not an STL, a bad
  `--set` or YAML `print` block; a file that is not an STL, an STL that is cut off or damaged, or an STL with a NaN or infinite coordinate): one `error:` line,
  as the other commands. 2 for an internal error. With `--strict` and a failed check: 4
  (`printcheck.GATE_EXIT_CODE`; the codes 0 to 3 are taken by `topopt run` and `topopt verify`).
- The MCP tool is `print_check(path=None, yaml_path=None, print_settings=None, resolution_mm=None, strict=False)`. `print_settings` is a dict with the keys of the
  `print` block. With no `path` the last run is used. It returns the same report as `--json` (`elapsed_s` and `timing_s` differ from run to run).
  On an input that cannot be read: `{"ok": false, "error": "<one line>"}`. A failed check is data, not an error; `gate.exit_code` is the code that the CLI returns.

**New keys of the `print` block** (all optional; section 18 has the others). A limit is a number that the YAML gives. A limit with no default has no value
until the YAML gives it: the check then reports the fact and its state is `unknown`. The two defaults are labelled "assumed".

| Key | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `min_wall_mm` | the thinnest wall or member that the printer makes (> 0) | none |
| `min_wall_area_pct` | the share of the surface area (0 to 100) that may have a chord under `min_wall_mm` before the check fails | 0.5 (assumed) |
| `max_closed_void_mm3` | the largest closed void that is allowed; 0 allows none | none |
| `max_bodies` | the number of separate bodies that is allowed (a whole number, 1 or more) | 1 (assumed) |
| `max_overhang_area_mm2` | the overhang area for the build direction and the angle | none |
| `max_support_volume_mm3` | the support estimate (an upper bound) for the build direction | none |
| `min_plate_contact_mm2` | the area that rests on the plate | none |

`load_config` checks them (an unknown key, a wrong type or a value out of range is a one-line error with the key). `PrintSettings.limits` holds the keys that the YAML
gave; `PrintSettings.limit(key)` returns the value or the default; `limit_source(key)` returns `yaml`, `assumed` or `none`. `run.json` `print` gets a key `limits`
only when the YAML gave one (a run with none keeps the old file). A number may be written in exponent form (`1e5`, `5e-1`; YAML 1.1 reads it as text, so
`load_config` and `--set` read the text as a number, as for `compliance_limit`). The report names the real source of each value: `run.json`, `yaml` or `option`
(`--set`, `print_settings`), the last source that gave the key. `PrintSettings.from_dict` (the `print` key of a hand-edited `run.json`) uses the same ranges and
drops a value that is out of range.

**Three measures of a thin member** are three different things. `tools/check_part.py --min-thick` is an opening test on the volume (0.5 % of the volume).
`settings.min_member_mm` (A3a, #30) is a request to the optimizer (a filter radius for the design). `print.min_wall_mm` is a limit on the chord of the finished
STL, and `topopt printcheck` reads only this one. A part can pass one and fail another; the report does not convert one into another.

**Report** (the JSON of `--json` and of the MCP tool). Keys, in this order:

- `ok` (true).
- `partial` and `coverage` (TC-2, section 44).
- `input`: `kind` (`stl` or `run`), `stl` (the absolute path), `run_dir` (or null), `sha256` and `bytes` of the STL file, `triangles`, `total_area_mm2`.
- `settings`: `build_direction`, `build_direction_label`, `bed_mm`, `printer_type`, `self_supporting_angle_deg`, `angle_source`, `limits` (each key of the table:
  `value` or null, and `source`: `run.json`, `yaml`, `option`, `assumed` or `none`), `assumed` (the keys of `build_direction`, `bed_mm`, `printer_type` that nothing
  gave) and `from` (the sources). With a `printer_model`: `printer_model`, `printer_name`, `catalog_version`, `printer_origin`, `profile_from`,
  `build_height_mm` and `derived`, and the `source` of a key that the profile filled is `profile:<id>` (section 18.7).
- `checks`: a list in this order: `mesh_closed`, `bodies`, `closed_voids`, `bed_fit`, `overhang`, `support_volume`, `plate_contact`, `wall_thickness`. Each has
  `id`, `state`, `reason` (one text), `value` (a mapping of facts), `limit` (`value`, `key` and `source`: `run.json`, `yaml`, `option`, `assumed`, `none` or
  `definition`; some have more keys), `method` and `estimate` (true for a check that is an estimate).
- `summary`: `pass`, `fail` and `unknown` (counts), `failed` and `unknown_ids` (lists of ids).
- A check that stops with an exception (the command and the MCP tool call `check(contain_errors=True)`; the default keeps the exception, because the ratchet reads it as a failure of the tool)
  is a record with the state `unknown`, no value, no limit, and the key `error` (TC-2). The other checks go on. `summary` counts it as `unknown`, and `gate` ignores it as for any `unknown`.
- `gate`: `strict`, `state` (`off`, `pass` or `fail`), `exit_code`, `failed` (the ids of the failed checks), `override` (the text that names the way on; null unless the
  gate failed), and `note` (when `state` is `off`).
- `definitions` (a text for each check), `note`, `warning` (an inside-out mesh), `timing_s` (`mesh_health`, `v2_numbers`, `thickness`) and `elapsed_s`.

**States.** `pass`: the check found nothing against its limit. `fail`: a check that has a limit is over it. `unknown`: the tool cannot say. The cases of `unknown`
are named in the reason: no limit, a limit under 3 x the resolution (thickness), a mesh that is not closed (thickness), a limit above the chord cap. A check with no
limit still passes when its number is zero (no overhang, no closed void, no support needed). A `pass` is not a promise that a print works.

**Checks** (the rules; the numbers of the V2 checks are for the configured build direction):

- `mesh_closed`: the STL is read as float32 and the vertices that are equal join. A face with two equal corners has no area: it is left out of the edges and the shells
  and counted in `zero_area_faces`. (`mesh.stl_roundtrip` of C1, section 19, keeps such a face, so for a file that has one the two can give another count of bodies and
  of non-manifold edges; for example 2 faces of the hook at 0.3 mm, and of the ladle at 1.625 mm, read as 2 bodies there and as 1 closed body here. E1b item 5, one shared
  helper, takes the rule of this check.) Closed: every edge has exactly 2 faces, the winding agrees across each edge, the volume is positive, and no closed shell is inside out.
  `value`: `triangles`, `vertices`, `watertight`, `winding_consistent`, `open_edges`, `nonmanifold_edges`, `winding_conflicts`, `zero_area_faces`
  (a fact, not a limit), `degenerate_shells` (shells with no area; a fact), `volume_mm3`, `inside_out` (the total volume is negative as written: the mesh is turned) and
  `inverted_shells` (closed shells with inward normals that lie in no other shell). The limit is the definition (source `definition`, no key). This check runs on the file, so it shows a pinch that the
  float32 rounding makes (two faces that touch) and the mesh in memory does not have.
- `bodies`: a shell is a set of faces joined along edges that have exactly 2 faces (the rule of `trimesh.split`). A shell is a body if its area is above 1e-12 mm2 (a shell of a
  collinear sliver is not: `degenerate_shells` in `mesh_closed`). A closed shell with a negative volume that lies inside a closed shell with a positive volume (the test is the
  winding number of the centre of its largest face) is a void, not a body. A closed shell with a negative volume that lies in no such shell is a body that is written inside out:
  it counts as a body, and `mesh_closed` fails with "N shell(s) inside out". `value`: `count`, `shells` (bodies, voids and shells with no area), `largest` (up to 10:
  `triangles`, `volume_mm3`, `closed`, `inside_out`). Limit `max_bodies` (default 1, assumed): `fail` above it. A body inside a void counts as a body.
- `closed_voids`: closed shells with a negative volume that lie inside a closed shell with a positive volume (a cavity with no opening). `value`: `count`, `total_mm3`, `largest_mm3`, `voids` (up to 10). Limit `max_closed_void_mm3`,
  compared with the largest void. No void: `pass`. A void and no limit: `unknown`, and the reason says what the process does with a closed void (`fdm`: a hollow; `sla`: resin stays;
  `lpbf` and `sls`: powder stays). The process is a note and not a limit: the state is `fail` only when the YAML sets the limit. A cavity that two bodies enclose together is not found.
- `bed_fit`: V2 `bed_fit`, `bed_turn_deg`, `bed_footprint_mm`, `bed_margin_mm`, `extents_mm`, `height_mm`. Limit `bed_mm` (`yaml`, `assumed` or `profile:<id>`).
  With a printer profile that states a build height (section 18.7) the value also has `height_fit` and `height_margin_mm`, `bed_fit` is false when
  the part is too tall, the limit has `build_height_mm` and `build_height_source` (`profile:<id>`), and the reason names both heights. Without a
  profile, or with a null build height, the height is not limited and these keys are absent.
- `overhang`: `area_mm2`, `fraction`, `angle_deg`, `angle_source`. Limit `max_overhang_area_mm2`: `fail` above it. No limit: `pass` for 0, else `unknown`.
- `support_volume`: `volume_mm3` (null for `sls`), `rays`, `support_needed`. An upper bound of the space under the overhangs (an estimate). Limit `max_support_volume_mm3`. No support needed: `pass`.
- `plate_contact`: `area_mm2`. Limit `min_plate_contact_mm2`: `fail` below it. No limit: `unknown`.
- `wall_thickness`: the V2 chord estimate (60,000 surface points, a chord along the inward face normal to the first wall, at most 12 mm). `value`: the V2 `thinnest_member` numbers
  (`thinnest_member_mm` is the 1st percentile, `min_mm`, `percentiles_mm`, `area_below_mm2`), `area_below_limit_mm2` and `area_below_limit_pct` (the area whose chord is under `min_wall_mm`),
  and `resolution` (`resolution_mm`, its `source`, `voxel_size_mm`, `mesh_edge_median_mm`, `resolves_from_mm` = 3 x the resolution). Limit `min_wall_mm` with `tolerance_pct`
  and `chord_tolerance_mm` (1e-4). When the state is `unknown` only because of the 3 x rule (the measured share is within the tolerance), `value` has
  `pass_needs`. Its key `resolution_mm_at_most` is the limit divided by 3, rounded DOWN to 4 decimals. A value rounded up gives `unknown`
  again: 2.0 mm gave 0.6667, and 3 x 0.6667 is over 2.0. The text uses the same value (the stored number, not a 4-digit rounding).
  For a run folder whose voxel size sets the resolution, `pass_needs` also has `voxel_count_factor`. That is an estimate:
  (voxel size / `resolution_mm_at_most`)^3, the number of voxels of the finer grid against this one.
  The reason gives the resolution and the factor. It says that a run at that voxel size makes a new shape.
  So the state is pass there only if its measured share stays within the tolerance.
  It says that the option `resolution_mm` replaces the voxel size or the mesh edge, and that the state of this STL is then pass.
  The option is for a mesh that holds members that thin (P4, F4-3; review M2).
  The text for a run folder is used when the voxel size is not under the median mesh edge, the rule of `resolution_of` (review L6).
  A chord is under the limit if it is shorter than `min_wall_mm - 1e-4` mm: a wall that is exactly at the limit reads a few 1e-6 mm short after the float32 rounding (it
  depends on the position and the turn of the part), and it is not thinner than the limit. (The V2 `area_below_mm2` thresholds compare without this tolerance: a note for #23.)
  Order of the rules: the mesh is not closed: `unknown`. No limit: `unknown` (the facts are in the reason). `min_wall_mm` above 12 mm: `unknown`. The share of the area under the limit
  is above `min_wall_area_pct`: `fail`. The limit is under 3 x the resolution: `unknown`. Else `pass`. This is a rule of this check, not a fact of the mesh: a pass needs a limit of
  at least 3 x the resolution (the pitfall `mesh-coarser-than-members` is about the stiffness of members in the voxel model: at least 3 voxels across, h <= d_min / 3), and a
  wall that is measured thin fails at any resolution. For a run folder the resolution is the voxel size of the analysis, so a member under 3 voxels was under-resolved there; the
  reason says so. `--resolution-mm 0` says that the mesh is exact. The share has a sampling error of about sqrt(f (1 - f) / samples) (60,000 samples): `value` has it in points
  as `area_below_limit_sampling_error_pct`, and the reason says so when the share is within 2 errors of the tolerance (another sample can then give another state). The result is the
  printed shape; it says nothing about the stress or about whether the voxel stress was valid for a thin member (a print pass is not a structural pass).

**Gate.** `--strict` (MCP `strict`) sets `gate.state`: `fail` if at least one check has `state` `fail`, else `pass`. An `unknown` never sets it. On `fail` the exit code is 4 and
`gate.override` names the failed checks and the way on: run without `--strict`, or change the limit key in the `print` block (a failed `mesh_closed` has no key: "mesh_closed has no
print key; to go on, run without --strict, or repair the mesh"). A failed `mesh_closed` (its limit is the definition) and the two assumed limits (`bed_mm` 220 x 220 and `max_bodies` 1)
can set the gate: this is by design. Nothing else changes: no run, no file and no other command stops because of the gate. Without `--strict`, `gate.state` is `off` and the exit code is 0.

**Not in E1a (E1b, after the MVP):** the overhang filter in the optimizer loop (B-063 phase 4), a screw-path check with a `kind` key on the keep-out regions (replaces the "hole" file-name
rule of `tools/check_part.py`), an orientation pick over the six axis options, the check of material in the load boxes, the mass check and the reference compare. `tools/check_part.py` stays as it is.

**Measured** (hook `final.stl`, 85,610 triangles, Linux x86_64, 1 thread): the numbers are measured on that file.

## 33. Linear buckling check (added with A6a)

The check gives the lowest linear buckling load factors of the final design for each load case. It is a voxel
estimate, not a verdict (it has no pass or fail). It is **off by default**. Then nothing changes: the optimizer, the
snapshots, `final.stl` and `metrics.json` are the same as without this section. The code is `topopt/buckling.py` (the eigen solve, with no element
code, shared with `topopt verify`) and `topopt/buckling_voxel.py` (the hex8 voxel part and the check of a run).
`topopt verify` does the same check on the P2 tet model (B3, "In `topopt verify`" below).

**Switch.** The YAML block `buckling` (all keys optional) or the flag of `topopt run`:

```yaml
buckling:
  check: true          # default false
  modes: 6             # integer >= 1. How many of the lowest load factors for each case. Default 6.
  density: printed     # printed (default) | gray
  max_seconds: 120     # number > 0. Time budget of the eigen solve of one case. Default 120.
  max_gb: 8            # number > 0, in GB (1e9 bytes). Memory budget of the check. Default: the RAM of this machine.
```

```
topopt run <file.yaml> --out <dir> [--buckling | --no-buckling]
topopt buckling <run_dir> [--modes N] [--density printed|gray] [--max-seconds S] [--max-gb G] [--yaml FILE]
```

**Memory unit.** Every memory number of the check is in GB (1e9 bytes), the unit of `max_gb`: the facts, the options and
the `topopt check` line. The `*_bytes` keys are in bytes.

**In a run.** `--buckling` turns the check on, `--no-buckling` turns it off, and without a flag the YAML decides. Unknown
keys and wrong values are errors of the YAML (section 2). `topopt.config.Buckling` holds the values in `Config.buckling`.
With the check on, `topopt run` calls `post.finish(run_dir, write_done=False)`, then
`topopt.buckling_voxel.run_check(run_dir, problem, log=...)`, then it writes the status `done`. The status is
`postprocess` with the message `buckling check` from the end of the post-process to the end of the check. So a reader that
waits for `done` (the dashboard, `run_status` and then `run_result`) always finds the key `buckling` in `metrics.json`
(a result, a skip or an error record). With the check off, `post.finish` writes `done` itself, as before.
`run_time_s` of `metrics.json` is made by the post-process and does not include the check.

- A failure of the check logs one `warning: buckling check failed: ...` line and the run ends with exit code 0.
  `metrics.json` gets the record `status: error`, `reason: exception`.
- Ctrl+C during the check: the record is `status: error`, `reason: interrupted`; `run.log` has one
  `warning: buckling check interrupted (Ctrl+C)` line; the run goes on to `done` (a finished run, with `final.stl`
  and the refine page). A second Ctrl+C stops the refine step as before.
- A kill during the check (the process is gone): the status stays `postprocess` with the message `buckling check`.
  `final.stl` and `metrics.json` are complete, and `metrics.json` has no `buckling` key (or the key of an earlier check).
  `topopt buckling <run_dir>` repairs this: it writes the key and sets the status `done`.

**The command `topopt buckling <run_dir>`.** It repeats the check on a finished run. It rebuilds the problem from the YAML
named in `run.json` (a changed YAML or STL is an error, as for `topopt refine`; `--yaml FILE` gives the YAML at its new place,
as for `topopt verify`), compares it with `run.json` (one `note: the YAML differs from run.json: ...` line for each difference,
in the log and in `run.log`; a fact, not a stop; the material is not compared, section 5), reads the last snapshot, and writes the key
`buckling` of `result/metrics.json` like `topopt run --buckling` does (the old key is replaced, the new one is last).
The YAML block `buckling` gives the defaults (the check does not need to be on in the YAML); the options override them for
this call only. It appends its log lines to `run.log` and prints them. It changes nothing else, except a status that a kill
left at `postprocess` / `buckling check`: that becomes `done`. Exit code 0: the check ran (`status: done`, with or without
facts). 3: it wrote a fact and no load factors (`status: skipped` or `error`). 1: bad input, for example no `run.json`, no
`result/metrics.json`, a state `starting`, `running` or `postprocess` with another message, or a wrong number. Do not call it
while the check of the same run is still running in another process (the status is the same as after a kill). There is no
MCP tool for it in this version.

**Method.** For each load case: the stiffness K of the design and one direct factor of K; the static solution; the
stress at the centre of each voxel, `D0 B_c u` with the full modulus; the geometric stiffness
`Kg = sum_e rho_e^p Kg_e`, with `rho^p` and no `E_min` (a void voxel adds no geometric stiffness); then
`eigsh(-Kg, M=K, Minv=<K factor>.solve, which="LA")` (ARPACK regular inverse mode, no shift, no second factor) for the
`modes` largest `mu = 1/lambda`. `lambda` is the multiplier on the load case as the YAML gives it (the weights of the
objective do not apply). A `mu` of zero or below gives no load factor. `tol` 1e-8, at most 100 restarts, a time budget
`max_seconds` for each case. K is assembled once for the factor and the eigen solves.

**Density.** `printed`: design voxels with a density of 0.5 or more are solid and the others are void (the
threshold of the post-process), K with `E_min` for void. `gray`: the density of the last snapshot as it is. The result
says which density it used. Both densities can have a low mode that is not a buckling mode of a solid member (see "Where the
lowest mode lives").

**Solvers.** The check uses the solver of the run (`settings.solver` as `resolve_solver` resolves it) when it has a direct
factor: `cholesky` (macOS arm64) or `pardiso` (Linux x86_64, extra `pardiso`). With another solver (`amg`: an inexact solve;
`gpu-mg`: no matrix) the check is skipped with a fact (see below), and the run goes on. No SciPy fallback exists.
Only one factor is alive at a time. The memory estimate is `estimate_memory_bytes` of the run model plus K, Kg and the
Lanczos vectors (`topopt.buckling_voxel.estimate_bytes`).

**The optimizer row.** The key `buckling.min_factor` (and `ks_q`) turns on a row that holds the lowest factor in the optimizer: section 39.

**`topopt check` with the check off.** When `buckling.check` is false and `buckling.min_factor` is not set, `topopt check` and MCP `check_problem` give
one fact line, so that a reader who did not turn the check on sees that it exists: `buckling: off (check and row). A part with members in compression can
buckle: buckling.check true gives the load factors (memory estimate about N GB; the time budget of each eigen solve is S s; the tool has no estimate of the
time).` `N` is `estimate_bytes` of the check for this grid and these free dofs (the budget code of this section, in GB of 1e9 bytes). `S` is `buckling.max_seconds`.
The tool has no model of the time of the check (only a budget for each eigen solve), so the line says so. If `preflight` says that the check would skip now, a
sentence follows (`With the solver of this run the check would skip: it needs a direct solver (cholesky or pardiso).` or `... (reason: <reason>)`).
The key `buckling_off` of the JSON has `check`, `row` (both false), `modes`, `max_seconds`, `memory_estimate_bytes`, `would_run` and `reason`. It is not there when the check or the row is on (then the line `buckling check: on in the YAML ...` or the
row lines of section 39 are printed, as before). The default does not change: the check stays off, and no run output moves.

**Where the lowest mode lives (facts, not verdicts).** A low load factor can come from a mode that a solid member of the
printed part does not have: a loose piece that only the stiffness of void voxels (`E_min`) holds, a hinge between voxels
that touch only on an edge or a corner, or a thin gray member of the gray density. For the lowest mode of each case the
record has:

- `lowest_mode_energy_share_rho_lt_half`: the share of the strain energy in voxels with a density below 0.5 (void voxels,
  or gray voxels of the gray density).
- `lowest_mode_motion_share_loose`: of the squared nodal motion of the solid voxels (density 0.5 or more), the share that is
  in the loose solid voxels. A loose solid voxel is not face-connected to a fixed region through solid voxels
  (6-neighbours, on the printed geometry: the optimizer density at 0.5). `null` if the model does not know them.
- `lowest_mode_energy_center_mm` and `lowest_mode_energy_box_mm`: the energy-weighted centre of the mode, and the box
  (`[[x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1]]`, voxel centres) of the voxels that hold 90 percent of its strain energy. They tell where to
  look.
- `shares_of_mode`: `lowest`, or `lowest converged (not always the lowest)` for a case that did not converge.

When the first share, or the second, is **0.5 or more**, the case has facts and options (and `run.log` has them as
`warning: buckling: <case>: ...` and `buckling: option: ...`): the percent of the strain energy in voxels below 0.5, with the
possible causes; the number of loose solid voxels and the share of the motion in them; the box. The options say: look at the
part in the box (`topopt refine <run_dir>`, `result/final.stl`), and run `topopt buckling <run_dir> --density <the other
density>` to compare. The load factor stays in the record: the level is a signal, not a rule that removes it. The level 0.5
is in the gap of the measured cases: the energy share is 0.0005 on the hook and
0.003 for a column in a box that is 98 percent void, and 0.94 to 1.0 for a loose piece, an edge-only strut and a thin gray
member. A gray neck of 0.45 has an energy share of 0.09, and the printed geometry has a loose piece there (motion share 0.97).

**Result.** The key `buckling` of `result/metrics.json`, always the last key. `result/buckling.json` has the same dict if
`metrics.json` does not exist. A reader ignores unknown keys. No key is written when the check is off.

```json
"buckling": {
  "kind": "linear buckling of the voxel model (hex8 elements). A voxel estimate, not a verdict: ...",
  "status": "done",                  // done | skipped | error
  "reason": "solver_not_direct",     // skipped: solver_not_direct | solver_unavailable | voxel_guard | memory.  error: exception | interrupted
  "message": "...",                  // only when status is error
  "meaning": "load_factors are multipliers on the load case as the YAML gives it ...",
  "density": "printed", "threshold": 0.5,
  "solver": "pardiso",               // the backend of the K factor
  "eigen_solver": "arpack regular inverse mode (scipy eigsh, which=LA, M=K, Minv=K factor)",
  "modes": 6, "tol": 1e-08, "maxiter": 100, "max_seconds": 120.0,
  "active_voxels": 39944, "free_dofs": 115836, "solid_voxels": 12452, "gray_voxels": 1543, "loose_solid_voxels": 0,
  "memory_estimate_bytes": 2083924573, "memory_budget_bytes": 68719476736,
  "factor_seconds": 11.5, "seconds": 54.2,
  "peak_rss_before_mb": 302, "peak_rss_mb": 1880, "peak_grew": true, "peak_note": "...",
  "cases": [{"name": "hang", "status": "ok", "load_factors": [1276.37, 1604.65, ...],
             "near_repeated": false, "near_repeated_rel": 0.01, "min_rel_gap": 0.016, "near_repeated_modes": [],
             "modes_requested": 6, "modes_converged": 6, "residual_max": 1.4e-08, "solves": 40,
             "kg_seconds": 1.2, "eigen_seconds": 17.2, "seconds": 18.4,
             "lowest_mode_energy_share_rho_lt_half": 0.0004, "lowest_mode_motion_share_loose": 0.0,
             "lowest_mode_energy_center_mm": [x, y, z], "lowest_mode_energy_box_mm": [[x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1]],
             "shares_of_mode": "lowest", "facts": [], "options": []}],
  "lowest_load_factor": {"case": "pull_off", "value": 120.9},   // null if no case has a load factor
  "facts": [], "options": [],
  "yaml_vs_run": {"matches": false, "differences": ["case hang, region tip: force [0.0, 0.0, -1.96] in run.json, ..."],
                  "note": "..."}   // only when `topopt buckling` rebuilt the problem (not from `topopt run`)
}
```

- `yaml_vs_run`: the result of the comparison of the YAML that `topopt buckling` read (the stored one, or `--yaml`) with `run.json`
  (`matches`, `differences`, `note`; no path). The load factors are multipliers on the load cases of THAT YAML: if it has other forces,
  the factors are for those forces, and the differences say so. `E`, `nu` and `penal` are not compared (`run.json` does not hold
  them): a YAML with another material gives no difference.
- Keys of the model. `active_voxels`: the design, fixed and load voxels (not keep-out). `solid_voxels`: the active voxels
  with a density of 0.5 or more in the density used (fixed and load voxels are always solid). `gray_voxels`: the design
  voxels with an optimizer density between 0.05 and 0.95 (the optimizer density, also when `density` is `printed`: it counts
  what the print rounds). `loose_solid_voxels`: see above. `memory_budget_bytes`: `max_gb` in bytes, else the RAM.
- `seconds` is the whole check (model, factor, static solves, all cases). `peak_rss_mb` is the peak of the whole process
  (`ru_maxrss`). When `peak_grew` is false, the check stayed below an earlier peak, the one of the run.
- Case `status`: `ok` (at least one positive load factor; `load_factors` are the positive ones, lowest first),
  `no_positive_factor` (every `mu` is zero or below: no compression that can buckle), `not_converged` (ARPACK did not
  converge in `maxiter` restarts: the case may have no compression, or the modes are not separated; the converged values
  are in `partial_load_factors` and they are not always the lowest ones), `time_budget` (`max_seconds` was used).
  These are facts with `facts` and `options`, not errors.
- `residual_max` is the largest relative residual `|(-Kg) phi - mu K phi| / (|Kg phi| + |mu| |K phi|)` of the pairs. A normal case
  has 1e-8 to 1e-10. Above 1e-6 (100 times `tol`) the case has a fact, also when the factors are returned. A part that is held
  only by void stiffness gives it.
- `near_repeated` is true when two of the reported factors differ by less than 1 percent (`near_repeated_rel`).
  `near_repeated_modes` lists the pairs (1-based). A square column has an exact double factor.
- A skipped check has `status: skipped`, the `reason`, `facts` (what is wrong, with the memory estimate of a direct factor
  for `solver_not_direct`) and `options` (for example `settings.solver: pardiso` or `cholesky`, `buckling.max_gb`,
  a larger `voxel_size`), and `cases: []`. The run is not stopped. The same lines go to `run.log` as `warning: buckling: ...`
  and `buckling: option: ...`. An `error` record has `reason`, `message`, `facts`, `options` and `cases: []`.
- **Joints (section 38).** A run with joints is checked, not skipped. The run holds the factor of the bordered matrix
  `[[K + Kb, C], [C^T, D]]` (`C`, `D` and `Kb` do not depend on the density). Its grid block of the inverse is `S^-1`, `S = K + Kb - C D^-1 C^T`, so the eigen problem is
  `S phi = lambda (-Kg) phi`. The call is `eigsh(-Kg, M=S, Minv=<grid block of the bordered solve>)`, where `S` is a `LinearOperator` (`joints.CondensedStiffness`: matvec
  `(K + Kb) v - C (D^-1 (C^T v))`, with a cached solve of `D`). `S` replaces `K` everywhere: the static solution (`S u = f`), the residuals, the K-normalisation, the strain energies of
  the mode and the dense path of a small problem (`S` is built dense there). A run without joints does not change: `K` stays a sparse matrix, and the output is the same as before.
  The beams have no geometric stiffness in this model (`Kg` has the grid dofs only), so the load factors are for buckling of the part and not of the beams (the tubes or the
  rods that the joints stand for). The record has the key `joints` (`joints`: the count, `stiffness`, `beams_have_geometric_stiffness: false`, `meaning`), the fact (also in `topopt check` and `run.log`) and
  the option to check a beam with its own load of buckling (for example its Euler load). `eigen_solver` names `M=S`. The reason `joints` of the old skip is gone.
  Checked against the dense generalized eigenproblem of the whole bordered matrix (relative difference 1e-14, `tests/test_buckling_joints.py`).
- Voxel guard: the check is skipped when the model has more active voxels than `settings.max_active_voxels`.
  Memory guard: it is skipped when the estimate is above `buckling.max_gb`, or above the RAM of the machine.

**`topopt check`.** When the YAML turns the check on, `topopt check` (and `check_data`, key `buckling` of the JSON) says now
if the check will run: the memory estimate of the check, or the warning `buckling check: it is on in the YAML, but it will be
skipped (<reason>). ...` with the facts and options of the skip (`solver_not_direct`, `solver_unavailable`, `voxel_guard`,
`memory`). With the check off, the JSON has no `buckling` key, and `topopt check` gives only the one fact line "`topopt check` with the check off" (below).

**In `topopt verify` (added with B3).** `topopt verify --buckling` (or `buckling.check: true` in the YAML of the run) does the same check on the P2 tet model of the printed STL.
The method is the one above, with other elements: for each load case, the stress of the static solve at the 14 points of the order-5 rule of every tet gives
`Kg = Ks (x) I3` (`P2Model.geometric_stiffness`; the test agrees with an independent scikit-fem assembly to round-off), and
`topopt.buckling.buckling_modes` gets the plain factor of the matrix that verify already holds (not the refined one; no second factor is made; with springs that matrix holds the spring matrix, with joints it is the condensed stiffness `S = K + Kb - C D^-1 C^T`, section 16). `lambda` is the multiplier on the load
case as the YAML gives it (the traction of the load region, the case weights do not apply). `buckling.modes` and `buckling.max_seconds` of the YAML are the settings; `buckling.density`
and `buckling.max_gb` are not used (the record lists them in `not_used_keys`). The check runs on every level of `--levels`. Memory and the skip: section 16, "Memory of the buckling check".
The result is the key `buckling` of `verify.json`. Everything is a fact: no pass or fail, no exit code, no `met` in the record. With `topopt verify --gate` (section 16, "The gate"), the gate turns the check on when the YAML has
`buckling.min_factor`, compares the lowest load factor of each case (`load_factors[0]`, the measured value) with it (at least `min_factor`, strict) and gives `met` in the key `gate`; a `skipped` or `error` record (or a case with no load factor, other than a case with no compression) then has `met: null` and fails the gate.
The ratchet rule `buckling` (section 36) reads the same factors (`load_factors[0]` of each case). The rigid-body rule below adds a projected value as a fact next to them; neither the gate nor the ratchet reads it (see "Rigid-body test").

```json
"buckling": {
  "kind": "linear buckling of the P2 tet model of the printed STL ...", "meaning": "...", "factor": "...", "stress": "...",
  "status": "done",                  // done | skipped | error
  "reason": "memory",                // skipped: memory.  error: exception
  "message": "...",                  // only when status is error
  "solver": "pardiso", "eigen_solver": "arpack regular inverse mode (...)", "modes": 6, "tol": 1e-08, "maxiter": 100, "max_seconds": 120.0,
  "not_used_keys": ["buckling.density", "buckling.max_gb"],
  "loose_piece": {"applicable": false, "reason": "..."},
  "models": "tet_over_voxel is the difference of two models ...",
  "mode_rule": "A mode is local when the tets that hold 90 % of its strain energy ...",                 // K1-C: the text of the rule of kind and region
  "rigid_body_rule": "The test runs when the part has joints or springs and no fixed node ...",         // K1-C: only with joints or springs; or why the test did not run
  "supports": {"joints": 2, "stiffness": "S = K + Kb - C D^-1 C^T ...", "beams_have_geometric_stiffness": false, ...},   // K1-A: only with joints
  "free_dofs": 77967, "threads": {"MKL_NUM_THREADS": "4", ...}, "threads_note": "...",
  "memory": {"term_bytes": ..., "estimate_without_check_bytes": ..., "estimate_with_check_bytes": ..., "limit_bytes": ..., "limit_source": "...", "model": "..."},
  "cases": [{"name": "hang", "status": "ok", "load_factors": [808.32, 994.72, ...],
             "near_repeated": false, "near_repeated_rel": 0.01, "min_rel_gap": 0.15, "near_repeated_modes": [],
             "modes_requested": 6, "modes_converged": 6, "residual_max": 4.4e-09, "solves": 40, "eigen_seconds": 2.8, "kg_seconds": 0.6, "seconds_per_solve": 0.052,
             "lowest_mode_energy_center_mm": [x, y, z], "lowest_mode_energy_box_mm": [[x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1]],
             "stiffness_over_optimizer": 0.764,
             "voxel": {"lowest": 1276.367, "status": "ok", "density": "printed", "solver": "pardiso", "source": "result/metrics.json, key buckling"},   // null: no voxel value
             "tet_over_voxel": 0.633,                                                                                                            // null: no voxel value
             "mode_facts": [{"load_factor": 808.32, "kind": "global", "energy_volume_share": 0.4156, "largest_motion": {"region": "tip", ...}}],   // K1-C: one entry for each load factor
             "rigid_body": {"applied": true, "status": "ok", "load_factors": [3.87, ...], "mode_facts": [...], "lowest_over_unprojected": 30.0, ...},   // K1-C: only when the rule ran
             "facts": [], "options": [], "seconds": 3.5}],
  "lowest_load_factor": {"case": "pull_off", "value": 74.10},   // null if no case has a load factor
  "facts": [], "options": [], "seconds": 8.1, "peak_rss_before_bytes": ..., "peak_rss_bytes": ..., "peak_grew_bytes": ...
}
```

- *Voxel value.* `voxel.lowest` is the lowest load factor of the key `buckling` of `result/metrics.json` (written by `topopt run --buckling` or `topopt buckling <run_dir>`), with its density and
  solver. If the file has no such key, or its status is not `done`, the case has `voxel: null` and `tet_over_voxel: null`, and the record has a fact and the option to run `topopt buckling <run_dir>`.
  The voxel energy centre and box of the lowest mode are copied when the voxel record has them.
- *`tet_over_voxel`* is the difference of two models (P2 tets of the printed STL against hex8 voxels of the optimizer). It is not an error or a bias of one of them. The text says so. It has three parts
  that were measured on the hook (section 33 "Limits": the element, the geometry and region rules, the load model). `stiffness_over_optimizer`
  (the static stiffness of the case, tet over the optimizer stiffness of the last pass) is in the case as context.
- *Statuses.* The case statuses and the facts for no compression, no convergence and the time budget are those of the voxel check, with texts that name no voxel and no refine page. A failure of one case
  gives `status: error` in that case (with `message`, `facts`, `options`) and the other cases go on. A failure of the whole check gives `status: error`, `reason: exception`. A skip for memory has
  `cases: []`, `size_mm`, `memory`, and options: a larger `--max-gb` or `--force`, a larger mesh size, a factor that needs less memory, or the check off.
- *Mode facts (added with K1-C).* The record has the key `mode_rule` (the text of the two rules below), and each case with `status: ok` has the key `mode_facts`: a list with one entry for each load
  factor of `load_factors`, in the same order. A plain run with the buckling check on gets these keys. A run without the check has no `buckling` key, so its key sets do not change. An entry has:

  ```json
  {"load_factor": 808.3, "kind": "global", "energy_volume_share": 0.4156,
   "largest_motion": {"region": "tip", "position_mm": [0.0, 5.0, 100.0], "region_rms_over_peak": {"clamp": 0.0, "tip": 0.9988, "design": 0.4789}},
   "rigid_body_fraction": 0.98, "support_energy_share": 0.0017}      // the last two keys: only for a run with joints
  ```

  `kind` is `local` when the tets that hold 90 % of the strain energy of the mode (taken by strain energy density, highest first) fill at most 25 % of the part volume, else `global`; `energy_volume_share`
  is that volume share (`null` and `kind: null` if the mode has no strain energy). `local` is relative to the part volume: a slender member that is a small share of the part gets `local` for its own mode, so `local` means small against the part and not small in itself.
  `kind` is also `null`, with a `kind_note`, when the supports hold half of the energy of the mode or more (`support_energy_share >= 0.5`): the tets hold only the rest, and `kind` would describe that rest.
  `largest_motion.region` is the named region that holds the node of the largest displacement (the fixed, load, joint, spring and measure regions of the YAML; a measure region is named when a row of `limits.displacement` or `limits.alignment` uses it),
  else `design`. A joint or spring region that also carries a force is one name. `position_mm` is that node. `region_rms_over_peak` gives the root-mean-square displacement of each named region and of the whole part (`design`) divided by the peak. With joints or springs and no fixed
  node, the displacement is the mode without its rigid-body part (a least-squares fit of the 6 rigid motions).
  The two keys of a run with joints or springs: `rigid_body_fraction` is the share of the squared mode (all dofs) that a rigid motion of the part reproduces; `support_energy_share` is the share of `phi^T S phi` that is not
  strain energy of the tets, so it is the energy of the bonds, the beams and the springs. They are facts about the shape of the mode, not a limit.
  The three values 90 %, 25 % and 0.5 are first values from the author's measurements on two test parts (a column with an energy volume share of 0.416, and a fin on a block with 0.096; nothing is measured between them). They are module constants of
  `topopt/verify/buckling_p2.py` (`MODE_ENERGY_SHARE`, `LOCAL_VOLUME_SHARE`, `SUPPORT_ENERGY_SHARE`), not YAML keys and not options. The texts `mode_rule` and `rigid_body_rule` are built from them, and a test ties the texts to the constants.
- *Rigid-body test (K1-C).* The bordered stiffness `S` is positive definite, and a part that only soft joints or springs hold still has modes that are a motion of the part on its supports at a very small load factor
  (`Kg` of the stress state acts on a rigid motion; `tests/test_verify_buckling_modes.py`). So `topopt verify` tests this. The rule is in the record (`rigid_body_rule` for a run with joints or springs). The test runs when joints or springs hold the part,
  it has no fixed node (`free` is all dofs), and the supports hold at least half of the strain energy of its lowest mode (`support_energy_share >= 0.5`). The `rigid_body_fraction` is not in the trigger: it was 0.98 to 0.9999 on every part that was measured, so it decided nothing.
  The trigger decides only whether the projected value is computed as a fact. Then the case is solved again with
  `Kg' = P Kg P`, `P = I - R (R^T R)^-1 R^T` (`R` the six rigid motions of the P2 nodes), and the case has the key `rigid_body`: `applied`, `rule`, `status` (`ok`; the status of a solve that gave no factor; or `error` when the solve raised, and then the measured factors of the case stay), `load_factors`, `solves`, `eigen_seconds`,
  `residual_max`, `mode_facts`, `lowest_over_unprojected`, and one fact and one option are added to the case. The option says: the part itself buckles at X; the lowest mode is a swing on the supports.
  `load_factors` and `lowest_load_factor` of the record stay the result without the projection, and they are the numbers that the gate (`topopt verify --gate`) and the ratchet rule `buckling` read. `rigid_body.load_factors` is a fact next to them; the gate record shows it as `projected_value` with its reason (section 16).
  The reason: the projected factor does not see the support. The review of PR 137 forced the projected solve on a floating column with six beams from stiff to soft (mesh 2 x 2 x 24, one part, one host): it was 3.867 for all six beams (3.866 for the stiffest), while the lowest load factor fell from 1.0 to 0.13. A gate on it passed the soft joints and failed the stiff ones. `test_the_gate_value_does_not_rise_when_the_support_gets_softer` (`tests/test_verify_gate.py`) checks that the gate value falls with the beam.
  A higher number in place of the measured one also loosens `buckling.min_factor`, a requirement, and that needs the consent of the user. The pipeline that this check comes from gates on the unprojected value too.
  The projection is a test of the part and not a model of the supports: the beams have no geometric stiffness, so neither result is a buckling load of the whole assembly. The projector `P` weights all nodes alike; another valid projector (volume weights) gives
  another value on a graded mesh: 2.7 % and 4.2 % higher on an 8-cell column that is graded with the power 2 and 3 (review of PR 137, one part, one host). So the projected value depends on the mesh grading by about 3 to 4 %.
  In `rigid_body.mode_facts` the `rigid_body_fraction` can be far from zero (0.94 on the column of the review): the projected modes are orthogonal to the rigid-body motions in the inner product of `S`, and the fraction is measured without weight.
  A part with a fixed node does not run the test (`rigid_body_rule` says "The rigid-body test did not run"). A part that springs alone hold runs it as a part that joints hold. A mode is not removed from a result by this key. The dense generalized eigenproblem with the same projector agrees (relative difference 1e-6).
- *Loose piece.* The loose-piece fact of the voxel check does not apply on tets: a body with no fixed node and no joint or spring facet makes K singular, and verify stops with exit code 1 before the solve (section 16); a body that a joint or a spring holds is held. A part with no fixed node that joints or springs hold runs (K1-A, section 16): K is not singular then. The record says so.
- *Threads.* With `pardiso` the seconds of a solve depend on the MKL thread count and on the load of the machine, the load factors do not. The record has `threads` and `threads_note`.
- Measured on the hook (one Linux host). On a recorded hook run of an older build (a `blur` run; mesh 1.5 mm, 139k dofs): tet 808.32 (hang) and 74.10 (pull_off) against voxel 1276.37 and 120.91 (`tet_over_voxel` 0.633 and 0.613; static stiffness 0.764 and 0.583).
  On a new run of the same design (the same voxel result; the `sdf` `final.stl` of this revision; mesh 1.75 mm, 97k dofs): tet 1003.70 and 86.22 (`tet_over_voxel` 0.786 and 0.713; static stiffness 0.869 and 0.718). So the ratio depends on the mesh method of the run (section 16), not only on the voxel design.
  Times: 9 s for the check with pardiso and 10 s with SuperLU, which agree to about 1e-12; the check added 0.12 to 0.13 GB to the measured peak. A Euler column (tensor mesh) agrees to 0.3 percent, and a gmsh column with 2 or more
  elements across to 1.5 percent (tests).

**Limits (facts).**

- Hex8 voxels with full integration are too stiff in bending, so the factor reads **high**, and it converges from above.
  The bias depends on the stress state and on the voxels across the thinnest member:

  | Voxels across | Column buckling (Euler column, against the formula) | Lateral-torsional buckling (a deep cantilever, against a P2 model) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | +59 % | +29 % |
  | 2 | +15 % | +9 % |
  | 3 | +7 % | +4 % |
  | 4 | +4 % | +2 % |
  | 6 | +1.8 % | +1 % |

  The hook has members of about 2.5 voxels. The earlier estimate for the hook was roughly 5 to 12 percent above a converged model of the same voxel geometry. B3 measured it (one Linux host, the recorded hook design, last snapshot): hex8 voxels against P2 tets on the same voxel solid
  (6 tets for each voxel, same loads and supports) read +22.6 percent (hang) and +22.4 percent (pull_off) higher. So the estimate was too low for this design. The whole difference
  between the voxel factor and the tet factor of the printed STL depends on the mesh method of the run. On the `blur` STL of the recorded run it is 1.58 (hang) and 1.63 (pull_off), and the element is 45 and 41 percent of
  the log difference. On the `sdf` STL of the same design it is 1.27 and 1.40, and the element is 85 and 60 percent. The `blur` method thins the members of 2 to 3 voxels (it drops 1,408 of 12,452 voxel-solid
  centres of the hook, in clusters along members; `sdf` drops 535, in small clusters at the surface). All numbers are facts of one host and one design.
  The check applies no knock factor.
- Every load of a case is a fixed (dead) load: the check does not see imperfections, nonlinear effects or follower loads.
  After PR #38 (moments, remote forces, pressures) this includes them: a pressure keeps its direction when the part
  deforms in the real world and does not here, and a remote force has no lever geometry in the buckled shape.
- A case that has no compression can still give positive factors from local compression (for example the Poisson effect at a
  clamp): a column in tension gave factors in the thousands. They come from the stress state of the model, and the check does not judge them.
- It does not use the keep-out cut or the smoothing of the final mesh. The load factors are for the voxel model of the chosen
  density.

## 34. Configs for other agent clients (added with E2)

This section names the client config files that the repo ships, the launch command that they depend on, and the checks.
The user text is `docs/clients.md`. The engine (`topopt/`) and the server (`topopt_mcp/`) do not change.

### 34.1 The launch

- Every client config starts the server as `sh scripts/topopt-env.sh mcp`. This is the launch of the Claude Code plugin
  (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: `sh ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/topopt-env.sh mcp`). The launcher finds the repo root from its own
  path, so the working folder of the client does not matter for the launch.
- The path of the script is `${workspaceFolder}/scripts/topopt-env.sh` where the client expands that variable (Cursor, VS Code).
  The Cursor user entry (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`, section 34.2) is the exception: it serves every folder, so it has full paths.
  Codex CLI and Gemini CLI have no such variable, so their config has the relative path `scripts/topopt-env.sh`, and the client
  starts in the repo root. (The Codex docs say that a relative path in a project config is taken from the `.codex/` folder.
  They do not name the MCP `cwd`, so the file sets none. The human checklist tries `cwd = ".."`.)
- The work folder (runs, relative YAML paths) is `TOPOPT_WORKSPACE`, else `TOPOPT_DEFAULT_WORKSPACE`, else the current folder of the server
  (`topopt_mcp/server.py` `workspace()`, rule in section 10.1). A config sets `TOPOPT_WORKSPACE` where the client does not start the server in
  the workspace folder (Cursor).
- `EVAL_TOPOPT_NO_WAIT=1` adds `--no-wait` to the `topopt run` command of `run_topopt`: the job process ends when the run is done,
  and no dashboard stays on. `claude plugin eval` passes only `EVAL_*` variables to the plugin; the e2e eval sets it.
- The environment of the server is `<repo>/.plugin-env/` (`TOPOPT_ENV_DIR` changes it). The first start downloads about 205 MB
  (63 to 77 s on a fast link, measured on 2026-10-20). `sh scripts/topopt-env.sh sync` makes the environment before the first client start.
- **`plugin-sync` (#357).** `sh <plugin folder>/scripts/topopt-env.sh plugin-sync` runs `sync` with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` set to the folder
  that Claude Code gives the plugin server: `<plugins>/data/<id>`. `<plugins>` is `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`, else
  `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/plugins`; `<id>` is `<plugin>@<marketplace>` (the first `name` of `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and
  of `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` of that copy), with each character other than a letter, a digit, `_` and `-` replaced by `-`
  (read in Claude Code 2.1.293). `TOPOPT_ENV_DIR` and `EVAL_TOPOPT_ENV_DIR` still come first, as for the server. Then it runs `status`
  with the same folder: `topopt: ready ...` and exit 0, else exit 1. It stops with exit 1, before any download, when
  `<plugins>/installed_plugins.json` does not name the id, or when the copy has no plugin manifests. The stamp names the root, so it
  is run from the folder that Claude Code starts (`claude plugin list --json`: `readFromFolder`, else `installPath`). The install prompt
  (`docs/reference/install.md`, "The install prompt") runs it after the install and before `/reload-plugins`, so the first start of the server finds a ready environment.
- **The uv of the launcher (REL-9).** `uv` is no prerequisite. `scripts/topopt-env.sh` picks the uv in this order and uses it everywhere by its
  full path (the variable `UV`): (1) `TOPOPT_UV`, a full path; if it is set and does not run (no file, not a full path, no `uv ` line from
  `--version`), the launcher says so, exits 1 and tries no other uv; (2) a `uv` on `PATH` (the folders that the script adds at the end of `PATH`
  count); (3) a copy that the launcher downloaded before, `<env dir>/uv/<version>/uv`, if it runs and its `--version` names the pinned version;
  (4) a new download. The download happens only in the setup, under the setup lock (`sync`, `python`, `topopt`, and the background setup
  that the first `mcp` start begins); `status` and `doctor` never download and change nothing. One pinned release (constants at the top
  of the script: `PINNED_UV_VERSION`, `PINNED_UV_URL_BASE`, `PINNED_UV_SHA256_MACOS_ARM64`, `PINNED_UV_SHA256_MACOS_X86_64`,
  `PINNED_UV_SHA256_LINUX_X86_64`, `PINNED_UV_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT_S`; none is read from the environment). The asset follows `uname -s -m`: Darwin arm64
  gives `aarch64-apple-darwin`; Darwin x86_64 gives `x86_64-apple-darwin`, but `aarch64-apple-darwin` when `hw.optional.arm64` is 1 (an Apple silicon
  Mac under Rosetta, as the official installer does); Linux x86_64 gives the static `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`; any other platform gets no
  download. The URL is `https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/<version>/uv-<asset>.tar.gz` only. The tool is `curl`
  (`--proto =https --proto-redir =https --tlsv1.2 --fail --silent --show-error --location --max-time <limit>`), else `wget`
  (`--https-only --tries=1 --timeout=<limit>`); `sha256sum` or `shasum -a 256` checks the file BEFORE `tar` runs; a wrong sum deletes the
  file, unpacks nothing and says so. The archive is unpacked into `<env dir>/uv/.tmp-<pid>`, the unpacked uv runs once (`--version` must name the pinned
  version), and the folder `<version>` is moved into place in one rename; a cut download leaves only a `.tmp-*` folder, which the next download removes
  and step 3 never takes. Nothing is written outside the env dir; no `PATH`, shell profile or `sudo` change. A failure (offline, a wrong
  sum, an unknown platform, no `curl` or `wget`, no tool for the sum, an unpack error) prints the old message (`uv is not installed. Install it with:
  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`), one line `The automatic download of uv did not work: <reason>` and `Then start this again.`, and exits 1.
  When the uv is a downloaded copy, the launcher exports `TOPOPT_UV=<its full path>` to its children, and the Python side
  (`topopt/uv_command.py`, `uv_command()`) puts that path, shell-quoted, in front of `pip install ...` in every repair command (doctor,
  `environment`, solver choice, the extras, `topopt step`, `topopt verify`, `gpu-check`); with no `TOPOPT_UV` that names an executable file the text is `uv`.
  **The oldest uv (#390).** `MIN_UV_VERSION` (0.6.8) is a constant next to `PINNED_UV_VERSION`, not read from the environment. Step 1 of the setup
  passes `uv venv --managed-python`, a flag that came with uv 0.6.8 (uv 0.6.7 stops with "unexpected argument", exit 2); the comment at the
  constant says how to raise it. The version is the X.Y or X.Y.Z after `uv ` in the first line of `--version`, compared part by part as numbers.
  A `TOPOPT_UV` older than the minimum stops like one that does not run (`TOPOPT_UV is set to '<path>', but it is uv <X>, and topopt needs uv
  <MIN> or newer.`). A `uv` on `PATH` older than the minimum is skipped and the search goes on with (3) and (4): the setup says once
  `the uv on PATH is too old (<path> is uv <X>; topopt needs uv <MIN> or newer)` (stderr, so `setup.log` for the background setup), with
  `: downloading uv <version> ...` or `: the setup uses <copy> instead. The uv on PATH is not changed.`; `status` says it before the plan of the
  download, and `doctor` says it in the row `uv` (`not found: the uv on PATH is too old (...); ...`) or, once a copy is in use, in the row
  `uv on PATH` (`skipped: <path> is uv <X>, older than uv <MIN>, which topopt needs`). The uv on `PATH` is never changed. A `uv` on `PATH` whose
  line has no version is taken, as before. If the download then fails (or cannot be made on this platform), the message says to update that uv with the tool that
  installed it (`brew upgrade uv`, `pip install --upgrade uv`, or `uv self update` for a uv from the install script; `uv self update` of a uv
  from pip or brew stops and names those) instead of the install command: a new uv from the install script can come after the old one on `PATH`.
  The launcher asks every uv that it could take for its version (in the plugin folder), so a start of a ready environment now also runs
  `uv --version` of the uv on `PATH` (about 6 ms measured; a downloaded copy or `TOPOPT_UV` was asked before too, so a ready start with an old
  uv on `PATH` and a copy makes two calls); a downloaded copy is then exported as `TOPOPT_UV` also when an old uv is on `PATH`.
  Tests: `tests/test_plugin_launcher.py` (section REL-9: a fake `curl`, the pinned constants rewritten in the copy of the script, no switch in the
  script; section #390: an old fake uv that says `uv 0.5.0` and exits 2 on `--managed-python`) and `tests/test_uv_command.py`.
- The setup runs in a background process that the launcher detaches from the server (L1a). The command is a subshell, so that the
  setup is no child of the launcher at once (its parent is process 1, or the subreaper of the system, for example `systemd --user`
  or a container): `( nohup setsid sh SELF sync >>LOG 2>&1 </dev/null & )` when `setsid` exists (Linux);
  else `( nohup perl -MPOSIX -e 'POSIX::setsid() or warn ...; exec @ARGV' sh SELF sync ... & )` when `perl` exists (macOS); else
  `( nohup sh SELF sync ... & )` (no child of the launcher, but still in the process group of the server). A `POSIX::setsid` that
  fails is written to the setup log (`topopt: setsid failed: <reason>`), and the setup goes on in the session of the launcher. With `setsid` or `perl` the setup also has a
  session and a process group of its own. So a client that ends the process group of the server (Codex does, each time it closes
  the server, also after `mcp` has exited) or the process tree of the server (VS Code does) does not reach the setup. With neither
  tool, a client that ends the group stops the setup: run `sync` once in a terminal first. The variable `TOPOPT_DETACH=setsid|perl|plain`
  forces one way (a knob for tests and diagnosis; a way whose tool is missing is ignored). The lock folder holds the pid of the
  setup shell in all three ways. A waiter removes the lock of an owner that is gone only inside a mutex, the folder `.setup-lock.break`, and reads the owner
  again inside it (and, when the pid is not running, reads the pid once more and takes the lock for stale only if it is the same pid: the owner can end and a new
  owner can take the lock between the read and `kill -0`; F3 review m1) (F3, review m-4 of L1a: with one `rm -rf` on the name, a late waiter removed the new lock of the waiter that had broken the stale one, and two
  setups ran; 8 of 60 rounds of 4 `sync` at once on a stale lock, none after the change). A signal removes the mutex; only a kill that cannot be
  trapped, inside those few commands, leaves it, and then the stale lock is not removed and `sync` waits (no time limit); `doctor` names the folder. Tests (`tests/test_plugin_launcher.py`): the own session and the survival of a group kill for `setsid` and `perl`
  (after the launcher has exited, and while it still waits; the `plain` way dies with the group, as documented), the tree kill for each way, the pid in the lock, the choice of the way with and without the tools. The `perl` and `plain` ways
  ran on Linux only; nothing ran on a Mac.
- A kill that cannot be trapped (SIGKILL, a power loss) in the install part of the setup can leave a package with its `.dist-info`
  and without its files, and uv then counts it as installed. So step 2 writes the marker `<env dir>/venv/.topopt-step2` before
  it starts, and the setup removes the marker after it wrote the stamp. If the marker is there at the next setup (a cut, or a clean
  uv error), the install calls of step 2 (the lock, or the pins of `pyproject.toml`) and of step 3 get `uv pip install --reinstall`
  (9 to 21 s for a warm cache on one Linux host with a load average of 20 to 50; a new venv has no marker, because `uv venv --clear`
  deletes the folder). `--reinstall` implies `--refresh` in uv: the repair needs the network to check the index, but it downloads no
  wheel that the uv cache has. With no network the setup fails with the network message and the marker stays. `UV_OFFLINE=1` makes the
  repair work when the uv cache has every file. While the marker is there,
  `status` and the start of `mcp` call the environment not ready, even if a stamp matches. After step 3 and before the stamp, the
  launcher imports `numpy, scipy.ndimage, scipy.sparse.linalg, numba, yaml, topopt_mcp.server` in a child Python that runs in the
  folder `/`. If an import fails, the launcher prints the Python error, keeps the marker, writes no stamp and exits 1; its stdout stays
  the path of the Python only. A fast start (a ready environment) runs no import check. Tests: a cut by SIGKILL in step 2
  (`test_a_setup_cut_in_step_2_is_not_ready_and_the_next_sync_installs_again`), the marker after a clean uv error, the import check
  (`test_import_check_failure_keeps_the_marker_writes_no_stamp_and_keeps_stdout_clean`).
- **The link of step 3 (#397).** Step 3 runs `uv pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e <root>`: uv builds topopt with the
  setuptools of the environment, not with one that it gets from the index for an isolated build. Both lock files pin setuptools (the
  package of `[build-system] requires`), so step 2 installs it; the fallback of step 2 installs the pins of `pyproject.toml` together with
  the setuptools line of the lock (`build_backend_pin`; a lock without the line gives `setuptools>=77`, the requirement of
  `[build-system]`). So a plugin update (a new root, the same lock) runs steps 2 and 3 with no network call, except the update that changes the Python of the launcher (#422, the update to Python 3.13): that one makes the environment again, downloads Python 3.13 and the packages (about 180 MB) and needs the network. An update that changes the
  lock downloads the new pins in step 2, as before. Tests: `tests/test_plugin_launcher.py` (the calls of step 3 and of the fallback, and
  the flags against `uv pip install --help` of the real uv) and `tests/test_locks.py`
  (`test_both_locks_pin_the_build_backend_at_a_version_that_build_system_allows`).
- `sh scripts/topopt-env.sh doctor` prints the facts of the setup on stdout, then the next command. It reads only: it installs nothing,
  changes no setup file (Python can write `.pyc` files while it imports), makes no network call and works with a broken or a missing environment. `mcp` never calls it, so the MCP channel
  stays clean. The rows are `script`, `system` (`uname -s -m`), `uv` (which uv and where: `system` (path, version), `TOPOPT_UV` (path, version), `downloaded by topopt` (path, version), `not found: the setup downloads uv <version> (<asset>) into <path>`, `not found: the setup cannot download it here (<reason>)`, or a `TOPOPT_UV` that does not work; a `not found` row names a uv on `PATH` that is too old first), `uv on PATH` (only when a uv on `PATH` was skipped as too old and another uv is in use), `env dir` (and which of `TOPOPT_ENV_DIR`,
  `EVAL_TOPOPT_ENV_DIR`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` or the default chose it), `venv Python` (runs or not, with its version; when it is not the Python of the launcher the row says that the next `sync` makes the environment again), `stamp` (when it does not match, the row names the Python as the reason if the stamp holds another one or none), `setup marker`, `setup running` (the pid in
  the lock), `setup lock` (`none`, or the facts of the lock folder: the pid and whether it is alive, for a live pid the command that it runs
  (`ps -p PID -o command=` when `ps` exists, else `/proc/PID/cmdline`, else the row says that the command is not known), when the lock was taken and when `setup.log` last changed
  (each as seconds and minutes, or `not known` when `date -r` is missing; only a background setup writes `setup.log`, and the row says so); no limit is applied to any of them, so a person sees a pid that another program has taken), `lock mutex` (only when the folder
  `.setup-lock.break` is there), `imports` (the list above, in a child Python; not run when the Python does not run or a setup is running), `lock file`
  (`requirements.lock`, or the Intel lock of an x86_64 Python on a Mac), `start method` (`setsid`, `perl` or `plain`) and the last 5
  lines of `setup.log`. If the Python runs and no setup is running, it then runs `<env Python> -m topopt doctor` in the folder `/` (so a
  folder `topopt` of the user cannot take the place of the code of the environment) and prints the output (the Python side, added
  with L1b, section 8). Before it, the launcher prints one line that says what the step does and the two limits: the self-test of gpu-mg
  up to 60 s (`PROBE_TIMEOUT_S`) and each import check up to 90 s (`IMPORT_TIMEOUT_S`); a test pins both numbers. The line gives
  no time that was not measured ("usually a few seconds"). The output reaches the terminal as it comes (stdout
  and stderr of the Python side together, through `tee` into a folder that `mktemp -d` makes under `$TMPDIR`, with the exit code in a
  file; POSIX sh has no `pipefail`); the folder is removed at the end and by INT, TERM and HUP. After the removal the launcher ends by the same signal (the trap is reset
  and the signal is sent again), so a calling shell sees 130 for Ctrl+C, as before. The shell runs the trap when the pipeline ends:
  Ctrl+C reaches the whole foreground group, so it ends at once; a signal sent to the pid of the launcher alone (a client that does not
  signal the group) waits until the Python step ends, because a POSIX shell defers the trap of a signal until its foreground command
  ends (a background job would ignore SIGINT and could not be stopped by Ctrl+C). If `mktemp` fails, the output comes
  at the end, as before. A topopt without that command (the error `invalid choice: 'doctor'`) shows its usage error lines first,
  then one line of the launcher that says so. The last
  lines are `Result:` and, when something is wrong, `Next command:` with one command that has the right `TOPOPT_ENV_DIR`: `sync`
  for a missing or old environment, a cut setup or a Python that does not run; `touch <marker> && sync` when the stamp is current
  and an import fails (the marker makes `sync` install the packages again; an older launcher can leave such an environment);
  `sync` while a setup runs (it waits for that setup and returns when the environment is ready; the path of the log is in the row
  `setup log`). `rm -rf '<env dir>/.setup-lock.break' && <the command above>` when a lock is stale (its pid is not running) and the mutex `.setup-lock.break` is there
  too and the environment is not ready: no `sync` removes the lock while the mutex stays, so `sync` alone would wait with no end (F3 review m2; the `setup lock`
  row and the waiter message say so, and there is no healing and no time limit). The command is not offered when the lock belongs to a live pid, when there is no lock folder,
  or when the environment is ready. **Exit code:** 0 when the environment is ready and every import works; 1 when a command is needed. The exit code of
  `topopt doctor` does not change it. When it is not 0, the printed report says so, and the last line says "the launcher environment
  is ready, but the Python report above lists a problem (exit code N)" instead of "Result: ready". Tests: `test_doctor_*`.
- `TOPOPT_MCP_WAIT` is the time in seconds that the launcher waits for the first setup before it answers. When it is set, it wins. When it
  is not set, the default is 0 if stdin is not a terminal (a client: the status server answers at once from the snapshot, so a client start
  does not wait and the 30 s limit of Claude Code does not matter), and 24 if stdin is a terminal (a person who runs `mcp` by hand and
  reads the stderr lines). A config that sets it (the Codex file: 180) makes that client wait that long for the real server; it must be
  shorter than the start timeout of the client. A setup that stops at once is not seen by a launcher that does not wait: the status text
  of a tool call gives the cause (`mcp_cause`). For 3 s after the launcher started the setup, the cause is `running` (the setup shell may
  not have written its lock yet; the 3 s are the early-stop check of the wait loop). `need_uv` does not download in the foreground: it only
  looks for a uv or plans the download, which the background setup does.
- **The status server of `mcp` when the environment is not ready (#370).** When the wait (`TOPOPT_MCP_WAIT`, above) is over and the environment is
  not ready, `mcp` does not fail and does not exit: it writes its stderr lines as before, and then it is a small MCP server in sh
  (`serve_status`) until the client closes stdin. It reads one JSON-RPC message in each line. The era comes from the first request with an id:
  `server/discover`, or a request whose `params._meta` has the key `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`, is the modern era (protocol
  2026-07-28); anything else is the legacy era; an `initialize` makes the era legacy. The id and the method are the top-level keys of the line
  (a number or a string, printed as the client sent it; the same keys of an inner object are not read); a line that is not a request or a
  notification is skipped.
  - **The lists are a snapshot of the real server.** `server/discover` (modern) or `initialize` (legacy), `tools/list`, `prompts/list`,
    `resources/list` and `resources/templates/list` are answered with the `result` of the real server, from the files
    `topopt_mcp/launcher/{modern,legacy}.{discover,initialize,tools,prompts,resources,templates}.json`. Each file is one line of JSON (no
    newline inside, ASCII). The modern files hold what the server sends (`resultType`, `ttlMs`, `cacheScope`, `_meta`); the legacy files
    hold none of them. The legacy `initialize` file holds the text `@PROTOCOL_VERSION@`, and the shell puts the version that the SDK
    picks for the request: the requested version if it is in `HANDSHAKE_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` of `mcp_types.version`, else
    `LATEST_HANDSHAKE_VERSION` (the lists `HANDSHAKE_VERSIONS` and `HANDSHAKE_LATEST` in the script are compared with the SDK by a test).
    The files are made by `python -P -m topopt_mcp.snapshot`, which starts the real server over stdio, once for each era. A change of a tool,
    a prompt, a resource or the instructions needs a new snapshot: `tests/test_launcher_snapshot.py` fails with "the launcher snapshot is
    out of date: run python -P -m topopt_mcp.snapshot" until the files are made again. Many clients (Codex CLI, Cursor, Claude Desktop, the
    Code tab of the Claude desktop app) do not ask for the lists again after `list_changed`; that is why the first answer has the full lists.
  - `subscriptions/listen` gets the acknowledgement with its id as `subscriptionId`, and no result. In the legacy era `ping` gets an empty result; in the modern era it
    gets `-32601`, as the Python server. Any other method with an id gets `-32601`. A notification gets no answer. The method must be
    plain text: a method with JSON escapes (`tools\/list`) is not read and gets `-32601`. Legacy: `listChanged` stays false, as the Python
    server says; the notifications of the safety net go without the capability.
  - **A call of a tool** gets a tool result with `isError` true (the modern result also has `resultType` and `_meta`, as the server's). The
    text is one line. While the setup runs it gives the step of `setup.log`, the seconds that the setup has run (the lock folder holds
    `started`), the usual total (the figures of the README: 1 to 3 minutes, about 200 MB), and ONE next step: tell the user that topopt is
    still setting up, about <wait> more, wait that long, and do not call a tool again at once. Every text of a running setup names a wait
    and has that rule (#399). The wait (`mcp_wait`): in step 2, from the progress that uv writes to `last-step.log`
    (`Downloading <name> (<size>)` and ` Downloaded <name>` for each large package; the text then says how many of them are downloaded
    and their MB in all): the bytes so far are taken as the sum of the done packages plus, for each other one, the size of the smallest
    one that is not done (with its default settings uv starts them at once, and they end in the order of their size); the rest at the
    rate since step 2 began (the lock folder holds `step2`; `install_all` empties `last-step.log` before it writes that time), plus
    `SETUP_TAIL_S` (10 s: the install, step 3 and the import check), at most `SETUP_MAX_WAIT_S` (180 s). Without progress (step 1, no
    package done yet, no step-2 time, or a `Downloading` line after a ` Downloaded` line: uv did not start them at once) it is
    `SETUP_RECHECK_S` (30 s); in step 3 it is `SETUP_TAIL_S`. Under 2 minutes it is said in steps of 5 s ("about 95 s", rounded up), else
    in whole minutes (the nearest). The three are constants of the launcher, not environment variables.
    In the first 3 s after the start, when the setup has no pid in the lock yet, the text says that the setup is starting, to call again in about 10 s, and not to call again at once. After 180 s it says that the setup takes longer than usual (a slow link) and that it goes on in the background, with the same wait.
    For a setup that stopped or was cut, for no uv, a `TOPOPT_UV` that does not run or is too old, or a folder that cannot be made, it gives the cause and
    the command that fixes it (`sync` for the same environment folder, or the official uv installer, to be run only if the user agrees; for a uv on
    `PATH` that is too old and a failed download, the update of that uv);
