    the next step is to show that command. `prompts/get` and `resources/read` get `-32603` with the same text as the message.
  - **The hand-off.** The first request with an id that comes after `is_ready` is not answered by the shell. The shell writes the lines to
    replay to the file `<env dir>/.mcp-handoff.<pid>` (mode 0600; a file, not an environment variable: a line can be longer than one environment string,
    and the client text stays out of the environment of the child processes), sets `TOPOPT_MCP_HANDOFF` (the file),
    `TOPOPT_MCP_HANDOFF_ERA`, `TOPOPT_MCP_HANDOFF_LISTEN_ID` (the JSON id of the acknowledged listen request, if any) and, in the legacy era,
    `TOPOPT_MCP_HANDOFF_DROP_ID` (the id of the `initialize` that the shell answered), and replaces itself with
    `python -P -m topopt_mcp.server` (exec). The open stdin goes with it: the shell reads with `read`, one line at a time. Replayed lines:
    modern, the pending line; legacy, the `initialize` line, `notifications/initialized` (the one of the client, else a plain one) and the
    pending line (if the pending line is the first `initialize`, only that line and no drop id). `topopt_mcp/handoff.py` reads and deletes
    the file and removes the variables from the environment, serves the SDK a stdin with the replayed lines first, drops the one answer to
    the replayed `initialize` (the id is compared as JSON with its type), and claims fd 0 and fd 1 as `stdio_server()` does, so a stray
    `print()`, a write to fd 1 or a child process cannot write into the protocol stream. With no hand-off variable, `main()` is as before.
  - **The safety net.** Before the SDK takes the stream, `handoff.py` compares the live tools, prompts, resources, templates and the
    instructions with the snapshot of the era. If they differ, it writes the three `list_changed` notifications as raw lines (modern: with
    `_meta` `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId` = the listen id, and only if a listen request was acknowledged; legacy: plain, and only
    if the shell answered `initialize`) and logs one line to stderr. If they are equal it writes nothing.
  - The shell is the only writer to stdout until the exec: no watcher, no lock. If stdin is a terminal, `mcp` reads nothing. The exit code
    is 1 when the client closes stdin and the Python server never ran. A ready environment starts the server as before.
  - **Checked live** (2026-10-27, Linux): Claude Code 2.1.293, install from the `/plugin` screen, cold first start (connect in 81 ms, the
    status in a tool result, the real tools after the setup, no list_changed). **Not checked:** the Code tab of the Claude desktop app,
    Codex CLI, Cursor, VS Code and Gemini CLI. The Claude Desktop chat extension starts the same launcher (#206, section 25.5); its command
    was run on Linux on the unpacked zip (2026-10-27), not in the app. Tests: `tests/test_plugin_launcher.py`,
    `tests/test_mcp_handoff.py`, `tests/test_launcher_snapshot.py` (the lines of the real client are in
    `tests/data/mcp_client_lines_claude_code_2.1.293.jsonl`).

### 34.2a The guide for any MCP client (added with #418)

- `docs/reference/any-mcp-client.md` is the one setup guide for any MCP client. Its parts, in order: what to have, the automatic setup, a manual setup,
  the server on its own, the config, typical problems, tips per client.
- Its part 5 has two templates, marked `<!-- template: any-client.json -->` and `<!-- template: any-client.toml -->`: the server name `topopt-local`
  (not `topopt`, which the project files of the repo use), `type` `stdio` (JSON), `command` `sh`, `args` the launcher at the placeholder path
  `/full/path/to/topopt` and `mcp`, `env` `TOPOPT_WORKSPACE` at the same placeholder; the TOML sets `startup_timeout_sec` and `tool_timeout_sec`,
  and keeps the `TOPOPT_MCP_WAIT` and the `startup_timeout_sec` of the committed `.codex/config.toml` (the wait is shorter than the start timeout).
  A key is a key that the clients document. The tests replace the placeholder with the repo root, start the server with a generic MCP client and list the tools.
- The numbers in the guide that live in code follow the code: the minimum uv (`MIN_UV_VERSION`), the pinned uv (`PINNED_UV_VERSION`), the number

- `docs/clients.md` keeps the status table, the shipped configs and snippets, the short quirks, roles, skills and limits.

### 34.3 Skills

- The source of `start-here` is `skills/start-here/SKILL.md`. The source of `part-to-topopt` is `.claude/skills/part-to-topopt/`.
- `.agents/skills/start-here/` and `.agents/skills/part-to-topopt/` hold a copy of every file of the source (`SKILL.md`, the shim
  `build_regions.py`, the two example specs and the two files of `references/` for `part-to-topopt`). Codex, Gemini, Cursor and VS Code read `.agents/skills/`.
  No file is a symlink. A test fails when a copy differs from its source by one byte, or has another set of files.
- `scripts/sync_agent_skills.py` makes the copies (`python3 scripts/sync_agent_skills.py`) and checks them (`--check`, exit 1 on a
  difference). The test uses the same check. A file counts when git tracks it or would track it (not ignored), so a `.DS_Store` does not count.
  Run it after each change of a source skill and after a merge that changes one.
- Every `SKILL.md` meets the Agent Skills spec: the required fields are `name` and `description`; the optional spec fields
  (`license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`, `allowed-tools`) may appear and no other field; `name` equals the folder name
  (lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, 64 characters or fewer); `description` has 1 to 1,024 characters; the body has fewer than 500 lines.
- A path in a skill text starts at the repo root, or (the Agent Skills rule) at the folder of the skill, and the file exists there.
  `part-to-topopt` names its script, its example specs and its `references/` files "in the folder of this skill", and both copies hold them.
  `references/patterns.md` and `references/blind-test.md` are read on demand: `SKILL.md` says when to read each one. The plugin ships
  the whole skill folder (`skills` in `plugin.json` names the folder), so no file list needs them. A plugin user adds
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/` in front of a repo-root path. The skills do not use `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, because only Claude Code fills it in.

## 35. Spring supports (added with A7a)

Backlog B-067, the spring part. Section 35 comes after section 34 (E2) on `main`.
Do not renumber other sections. Code: `topopt/springs.py`.

**YAML.** The top-level key `springs` is a list of entries. Each entry has `region` (a name of `regions.load`) and exactly one of:

| Key | Form | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `stiffness` | `[kx, ky, kz]`, N/mm | The total stiffness of the region in the global axes. It is spread over the exposed faces by count (every face has the same area). |
| `stiffness_per_area` | a number or `[kx, ky, kz]`, N/mm3 | The stiffness of each unit of face area (the `bond_k` form of the pipeline). One number is the same on all three axes. |

A region may have a spring and no force, or a spring and a force. One entry for each region. An entry stops before the run, with the
fact and a `(file: <yaml>)` suffix, when it has both keys or neither, names a region that is not in `regions.load`, has a negative number,
has all numbers zero (a zero on one axis is valid), has a rotational key (`krx`, `rotational_stiffness`, `moment`, `torsion`, ...) or 6 numbers,
or has an unknown key. A region with no exposed face is refused when the problem is built. `regions.fixed` may be missing or empty. A YAML with
neither a fixed region nor a spring stops with a `UserError` that names the six free modes and the options (add a fixed region, or a spring).
`Config.uses_extended_loads()` is True when the YAML has a spring.

**Faces and matrix.** The faces are the pressure faces of section 26.2: a face of a voxel of the region whose neighbour is EMPTY or KEEP_OUT,
or lies outside the grid. A spring acts on all of them, also on the side faces of a pad (a face toward the design, a fixed voxel or another load
voxel gets no spring). Shape the region so that only the wanted face is free. Each face gets, on each axis `d`, the matrix `k_face,d * U`.
`U` is the consistent Q1 face matrix of a unit area: the entries are 1/9 (same node), 1/18 (edge neighbour) and 1/36 (diagonal); they sum to 1.
`k_face = k_total / n_faces` (the form `stiffness`) or `k_per_area * h^2` (the form `stiffness_per_area`). The face matrices of a region sum to the
stiffness on each axis (audit 1e-12). The count of faces gives the area of the voxel surface (a staircase), not the area of the STL surface.

The sparse term `Kb` is added to `K` in place after the assembly (`K.data[pos] += vals`), in the same index arrays, so the caches of the
solvers stay. A term on a fixed dof is dropped. A spring adds no dof and does not depend on the density, so the sensitivities do not change.
A config without springs runs the old lines (bit-equal).

A lumped rule (a quarter of `k_face` at each node) is not used: it makes the rotation of the support too stiff by the factor `1 + 2 / n^2`
for `n` voxels across. Measured (cantilever 40 x 8 x 8 mm on a face spring of 2 N/mm3, tip deflection against beam theory with a Winkler
root, `tools/spring_check.py`): the consistent matrix gives -0.095, -0.027 and -0.007 percent at 2, 4 and 8 voxels across; the lumped rule gives
-33.06, -11.01 and -3.00 percent. A series spring (a bar with a spring at one end) is exact to round-off for both.

The voxels of a spring region are LOAD voxels: solid, with full E, and in `final.stl`. The region carries load and adds its own stiffness to the
part (the same fact as for a per-axis support, section 26.2). A spring on a thin pad is a spring in series with the pad.

**Rigid-body test.** A spring with `k > 0` on an axis counts as a support on the dofs of that axis at the nodes of its faces. The test of
section 26.2 runs on the fixed dofs and the spring dofs together (always, when the YAML has a spring; also with a full clamp). Facts: `spring_dofs`.
A spring on one axis only blocks the modes that move along it: `[k, 0, 0]` on a pad leaves the translations along y and z and the rotation about x free,
and the run stops before the first solve with their names. The test is geometric: it does not weigh `k`. A very small `k` passes it and makes `K`
nearly singular. `check` adds a warning when the smallest `k` of a region is below `1e-6 * E * h` (the fact `relative_to_Eh`). A direct solver
can stop with a pivot error then, and AMG needs many iterations. It is a fact, not a refusal.

**Solvers and readers.** pardiso, cholesky (macOS) and amg take `K + Kb`: the pattern is the pattern of `K`. AMG keeps its 3 x 3 blocks when no
support is per-axis (`triplets_aligned`, section 26.2): a full clamp, a spring and no fixed region all keep them; a per-axis support makes AMG scalar.
`gpu-mg` has no matrix and takes springs since P2b (section 20): `Kb` is a Galerkin product on every level of the multigrid, and it is in the smoother
blocks, the dense coarsest matrix, the FP64 residual and the operator of the backward-error rule; the reactions come from the displacement as for the other
solvers (`GpuModel.kb` is the border of its solver, because `GpuModel` has no assembler). `gpu-mg` takes a per-axis support too since P2c
(section 20). `topopt verify` takes a spring since K1-A (section 16).
The refine step (`refine/stress.py`) and the linear buckling check (section 33, `buckling_voxel.check_problem`) solve with the same `K + Kb`; the
geometric stiffness has no spring term (a spring has no prestress).

**Readers of "the part is held".** `springs.support_mask(problem)` is the FIXED voxels and, with springs, the voxels of the spring regions. These readers use it:
`interfaces.voxel_facts` (a union piece with no support makes `K` singular; section 23), `stress_report` (the load path of the thresholded design and of
`final.stl`; the set `used` of the peak scope also holds the spring regions, but `used_by` does not: a spring is not a load of a case), the loose
pieces of the buckling check (section 33), `topopt check` and the part builder (the pieces and the "touches a design voxel" warning).

**Reactions.** The record of the last pass in `history.jsonl` (the pass `iterations`, or the pass of a stop rule) and `result/metrics.json` have `reactions`
(only with springs; a robust run has them in `robust.json` and `metrics.json`, for the nominal design):
`{"moment_about_mm": [..], "cases": [{"name", "applied", "clamp", "springs", "sum_force_n", "sum_moment_nmm", "force_error", "moment_error", "residual_rel"}]}`.
`Model.reaction_facts(U, rho)` takes the density `rho` of the stiffness that gave `U` (`Model.element_E`), not a state of the model.
Each of `applied`, `clamp` and the entries of `springs` (region name -> entry) is `{"force_n": [x, y, z], "moment_nmm": [x, y, z]}`,
the force on the part and its moment about the grid origin. `applied` is the sum of the nodal forces of the case (also the lost force on
fixed dofs). `clamp` (only if there are fixed dofs) is `(K u)_i + (Kb u)_i - f_i` on the fixed dofs `i`: the element forces at the fixed dofs, less
the load that sits on them. A spring region has `-Kb_r u`. The sum of the three is zero; `sum_*` is the sum, and `force_error` and `moment_error` are its
largest component over the sum of the sizes of the terms. With the clamp defined as above, the sum is the net force and moment of the residual of the solve on the
free dofs. For a direct solver that is round-off. For AMG it can be far below the residual of the solve (AMG leaves a residual that is nearly orthogonal to
the rigid-body modes), so it does not bound the error of the displacement. `residual_rel` is the norm of the residual of the solve on the free dofs over the
norm of the load on them: it does. A reaction that was made with another density than the solve shows in both. `topopt run` writes a `reactions:` line for each
case to `run.log`, with the prefix `warning:` when `force_error` or `moment_error` is above 1e-6.

**Output.** `run.json` has `springs` (`regions`: `region`, `faces`, `area_mm2`, `nodes`, `stiffness_n_per_mm`, `stiffness_per_area_n_per_mm3`,
`relative_to_Eh`, `audit_rel`, `faces_by_direction` (`{"+x": 100, "-z": 20, ...}`, the faces by outward direction: the side faces of a pad show here); and
`spring_dofs`) and `supports`. `check_data` has the same under `extended`, and `topopt check` and `run.log` have a `spring:` line. A spring below `1e-6 * E * h` gives a
line with the prefix `warning:` in `topopt check` and in `run.log` (the run goes on).
`stiffness_cases[].N_per_mm` keeps its rule: `|F|^2 / c` for plain forces. With springs `c` includes the deflection of the springs, so it is the
stiffness of the mounted part.

**Merge notes.** A7a was rebased onto `integration/mvp-1` (fix round 1), and the joins with these branches are in the code and tested
(`tests/test_springs_x_merge.py`): A6a buckling (K + Kb, loose anchor), D1b (the reactions in the record of the last pass and of a stop-rule pass; a
resume of a finished run), C2 interfaces and A2 stress report (`support_mask`), A3b robust (reactions of the nominal design), G1d gpu-mg (three refusals; the two for springs and joints lifted by P2b, the one for a per-axis support by P2c, section 20),
C3a `feedback.py` (`_settings` and `_yaml_vs_run` know `springs`). Left for later:

- Mirror (A4a, PR #36): no refusal. The label check of A4a sees a spring region as a LOAD label. A spring that is not symmetric gives the best
  symmetric design (the rule of a load). A spring asymmetry fact is a later option.
- A stiffness on one face direction only (a normal filter) is a later option; the facts `faces_by_direction` show what a region has.

## 36. The ratchet: keep a candidate edit only if the rules pass (added with D3)

Roadmap D3. Section 36 comes after section 35 (A7a) on `main`. Do not renumber other sections. Code: `topopt/ratchet.py` (the rule, the judge, the log, the runner, the script),
`topopt/ratchet_sources.py` (the sources), the `acceptance` block in `topopt/config.py`, and the tools `ratchet_run`, `ratchet_status` and
`ratchet_approve` in `topopt_mcp/server.py`. Script: `python -m topopt.ratchet` (no change to `cli.py`).

A finished part gets candidate edits (a mark of the Refine page, a part that another tool made). The ratchet judges each candidate with
`topopt printcheck` and `topopt verify`, and keeps it only if every rule of the case passes. A kept candidate is the new parent; the next
candidate is judged against it. Every record has the rule, the number, the limit and where the limit comes from. The ratchet has no number
of its own and no part name: every limit comes from the case YAML. The word for the outcome is `decision` (`verdict` is the convergence
verdict of the optimizer, section 24.2).

### 36.1 YAML: the block `acceptance`

An optional top-level block. A YAML without it loads as before, and the ratchet refuses to judge with it ("no rules"). Unknown keys, unknown
rules and a rule listed twice are errors (the message names the key and the file). A rule that is not listed is off.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rules` | A list, one entry for each rule: `{rule: <name>, ...options}`. Required. |
| `mesh_size_mm` | The mesh size of `verify`, for the baseline and for every candidate. Default: the size that `verify` picks for the baseline. |
| `percentile` | The volume percentile of the stress (default of `verify`, 99.9). |
| `owner_gate` | `true`: the runner stops before it promotes (36.6). Default `false`. |

A number in a rule has a source: `source: "text"` for the numbers of the rule, or `<key>_source` for one number. A number with no source prints
"source not recorded" in the record (value plus source, the pattern of the print block).

| Rule | Options | Needs | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| `watertight` | none | printcheck | The mesh is closed (`mesh_closed` of section 32). The fact must be `true` or `false`; any other value is `no_input`. |
| `bodies` | none | printcheck | The body count is at most `print.max_bodies` (the YAML limit, else the assumed default 1; the record names which). |
| `loose_island` | `max_mm3`; optional `relative_to_parent` | printcheck | The volume of the loose bodies (the sum over every body but the largest) is at most `max_mm3`; with `relative_to_parent` the increase over the parent is. The report of `printcheck` lists the 10 largest bodies only, so the judge adds up all bodies from the mesh health. If that fails, the number is a lower bound: a bound above the limit is a `fail`, and any other result is `no_input` (a lower bound is no pass). |
| `stress` | optional `margin` (0 to 1), `against_parent`, `cases`, `tolerance_pct` | verify | The p99.9 (or `percentile`) stress by volume of each case, against the limit of the case: `load_cases[].stress_limit`, or `allowable_mpa / safety_factor` (section 17), times `margin`. `tolerance_pct` (0 or more, with `tolerance_pct_source`): the rise over the parent that is allowed, for `not_worse` and for the parent branch of `cap_or_parent`. There is no default: with no tolerance every rise fails. The loader refuses it with `absolute`, and refuses `margin` with `not_worse`. |
| `stiffness` | `max_drop_pct`; optional `cases` | verify | The stiffness of each case drops by at most `max_drop_pct` percent against the parent. |
| `mass` | exactly one of `must_fall: true`, `max_rise_pct` | printcheck | The mass falls, or rises by at most `max_rise_pct` percent against the parent. The mass is the printcheck volume times `material.density`. |
| `print_gate` | none | printcheck | The strict print gate (section 32) does not fail, and no print check that has a limit is `unknown`. The strict gate fails only on `fail`; an `unknown` check (for example `wall_thickness` with a limit that the mesh resolution or the chord cap cannot decide) is `no_input`, with the check ids and the reasons. An `unknown` check with no limit stays a fact. |
| `symmetry` | `max_mm` | mirror | `mirror_error_mm` is at most `max_mm`. The YAML needs a top-level `mirror`. |
| `displacement`, `alignment` | optional `against_parent`, `cases`, `tolerance_pct` | verify | The tet value of each row of `limits.displacement` (or of `limits.alignment`: the shift and the tilt rows) in the key `motion` of verify.json (section 31) is at most the limit of its row (K1-B). The limit comes from the YAML row, as verify read it; the rule has no number of its own. `cases` keeps the rows of the listed cases. If the YAML has no such row, or verify did not compute the rows (a skipped or error record), the rule is `no_input` with the reason. |
| `buckling` | `min_factor` (required unless `against_parent: not_worse`); optional `against_parent`, `cases`, `tolerance_pct` | verify with the buckling check | The lowest tet load factor of each case (`load_factors[0]` of the key `buckling`, section 33: the measured value; the projected value of the rigid-body rule is a fact and is not read) is at least `min_factor`. The judge runs verify with the buckling check when this rule is listed (and only then; `buckling.check` of the YAML does not turn it on). A check that did not run (a skip because of memory, an error, a case with no factor) is `no_input` with the reason (K1-B). |

`against_parent` of `stress`, `displacement`, `alignment` and `buckling` has three forms. `absolute` (default): the value is at most the limit. `not_worse`: the value is at most the value of
the parent (plus `tolerance_pct`); no limit is needed. `cap_or_parent`: the value is at most the larger of the limit and the value of the parent (plus
`tolerance_pct`). At the baseline `absolute` and `cap_or_parent` read the limit alone, and `not_worse` is `off`.
For `displacement` and `alignment` (a value that must stay at or below its limit) the forms read as for `stress`, with the limit of the row. For `buckling` (a factor that must stay at or above its floor) the directions turn round:
`absolute` is at least `min_factor`; `not_worse` is at least the factor of the parent (less `tolerance_pct` of it); `cap_or_parent` is at least the lower of `min_factor` and that bound. The loader refuses `tolerance_pct` with `absolute`, refuses `min_factor` with `not_worse`
(it reads no floor) and refuses a `buckling` rule that has neither `min_factor` nor `not_worse`. `tolerance_pct` is the move to the worse side of the parent value that is allowed: a rise for `stress`, `displacement` and `alignment`, a fall of the factor for `buckling`. `margin` belongs to `stress` only. Two more forms belong to other rules:
`falls` is the form of `mass.must_fall`; `delta` is the form of a change in percent (`stiffness`, `mass.max_rise_pct`, `loose_island.relative_to_parent`).

A rule list must not be empty: the loader refuses `rules: []`, `make_rules([])` raises `UserError`, and `keep` raises `RatchetError` for a `Rules` with no rule
(an empty set would accept anything).

### 36.2 The rule `keep`

`keep(candidate_facts, parent_facts, rules) -> Outcome(decision, failed, checks)` is a pure function over plain dicts. It reads no file and runs no
solve. `parent_facts` is `None` for the baseline.

- Each check has `rule`, `case` (or none), `state`, `reason`, `value`, `parent_value`, `limit` (text), `limit_value`, `limit_source`, `input_source`, `form`,
  and, for a form that reads the parent, `delta` (the change) and `delta_pct` (the change in percent of the parent value; `null` if that value is 0). The `reason` of a
  parent form says how far the value moved.
- `state` is `pass`, `fail`, `no_input` or `off`. `off`: the check needs a parent and the part is the baseline.
- A rule that is on and has no input is `no_input`. It counts as failed, with the reason (a fact is missing, partial, stale, not a finite number or of the wrong
  type; a tool failed with its message; there is no limit and the options to add one; or there is no producer). The ratchet never skips a rule that is on, and
  a missing, partial, stale or unknown fact is never a pass.
- `decision` is `BASELINE` (no parent), `REJECT` (a check is `fail` or `no_input`) or `ACCEPT`. `failed` lists the rules, in the order of the YAML.
- A baseline that fails an absolute rule is a fact (`failed` is not empty and `decision` is `BASELINE`). The run goes on.
- The stress comparison uses the percentile by volume at one mesh size. The peak moves with the mesh (section 16). A comparison of two solved facts
  with two mesh sizes raises `RatchetError` (a mistake in the code, not a user input).

### 36.3 The judge and the facts

`judge_facts(shadow_dir, parent_dir, ctx) -> facts` builds the facts of one candidate. The input is a run-shaped folder (36.5), so the tools read it as a run.

- `topopt printcheck` runs always, with the strict gate on. Facts: `watertight`, `open_edges`, `nonmanifold_edges`, `volume_mm3`, `bodies`, `loose_mm3`,
  `loose_lower_bound`, `closed_voids`, `print_gate`, `print_failed`, `print_unknown` (the checks that are `unknown` and have a limit, with the reason) and `mass_g` when
  the material has a density. `loose_mm3` is the sum over all bodies but the largest (from the mesh health); if that fails it is the lower bound of the report.
- `topopt verify` runs in the process, only when a listed rule needs it (`stress`, `stiffness`, `displacement`, `alignment`, `buckling`), at the mesh size of the baseline, with
  `load_sensitivity` and `bore_checks` off (a `bore_checks` block of the YAML does not turn on the bore checks of section 40) and `buckling` off, except that a listed rule `buckling` turns it on (`buckling.check` of the YAML does not). Facts: `mesh_size_mm`, `percentile` and, for each case, `stiffness_N_per_mm`, `compliance_Nmm`, `max_displacement_mm`,
  `p_by_volume_MPa`, `peak_qp_MPa`. K1-B adds: for each case `buckling_lowest_factor` (when verify ran the check; `null` if the case has no factor), `buckling_problem` (text: the status, reason and message of a check that did not run), `motion_rows` (`{row name: {kind, case, limit, value}}`,
  the `tet_value` of each row of the key `motion`) and `motion_problem` (the same text for the rows). With a rule `buckling`, `topopt ratchet check` also reports the memory estimate with the check.
  When verify welded the input (section 14, weld retry) or cleaned the refused surface (section 14, clean retry), the facts also have
  `notes`: the one line of the verify text for the reader. No rule reads it.
- `mirror_error_mm(stl, planes)` (the rule `symmetry`): the largest distance from a mirror image of a vertex of the surface to the surface, over the
  planes. A symmetric part gives about the size of the triangles, not zero. With no plane the function raises `UserError` (the rule is then `no_input`).
- `sources` names where each fact comes from. `errors` has `{step: {exit_code, message}}` for a tool that failed (1 bad input, 2 could not run). A tool
  that fails does not raise: the rules that need it are `no_input`, and the record has the message.
- The record also has `tools`, `timing_s` and `peak_rss_bytes` of the judge (the block `judge`).

One mesh size for the whole ratchet. The baseline is judged first, at `acceptance.mesh_size_mm` or the size that `verify` picks; every candidate is
judged at that size (kept in `ratchet.json`). The size is a pin: a root with another size is refused (36.5).

### 36.4 The log and the state

`ratchet.jsonl` in the root is append-only. One JSON line for each record, written whole with one `os.write` and then `fsync`. The reader is
`runinfo.read_history(strict=False)`: a partial last line is skipped and named as a fact; the next record starts on its own line. The record keys:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `format`, `seq`, `at`, `type` | Format 1; the record number (from 0); the UTC time; `baseline`, `candidate` or `approval`. |
| `id` | `c` and the three digits of `seq` (`c000` is the baseline; an approval record uses a number, so ids can skip). |
| `decision`, `failed`, `parent` | As in 36.2. `parent` is the folder name (`acc_01`), `null` for the baseline. |
| `promoted` | The `acc_NN` folder that this record made (or `null`). It is written before the folder moves. |
| `owner_approval` | `not_required`, `pending`, `given` or `declined`. |
| `source` | `{kind, ref, note, facts}`: `ref` names the candidate in the source (`marks.json#3`, `part_b.stl`); `note` is the reason when there is no candidate; `facts` are the facts of the source. |
| `inputs` | SHA-256 of the candidate STL, the parent STL, the YAML, `inputs_sha256` (one hash of the YAML, every region file and `run.json` of the start run), the rules (all limits resolved), and the marks file. |
| `facts`, `checks`, `judge`, `errors` | 36.3 and 36.2. `errors` is `null` when no tool failed. |

A source that makes no change (a mark off the part) is a record with `decision: REJECT`, `failed: ["no_candidate"]` and the reason in `source.note`.
A judge that raises is a record with `errors.judge` and a REJECT. Neither is a crash. The log is the truth: a source skips every `ref` that the log holds
with the same content (the hash of the marks file or of the STL file), so a restart goes on with the next candidate. A `ref` with other content (a marks
file or an STL file of the same name) is a new candidate: it is judged, and its record has `source.facts.same_ref_as_earlier` and a note. When nothing is new,
the run says so and counts what the log holds.

A `baseline` record that has `rebase_of` (the parent folder) is a re-baseline (36.5): the parent was judged again under new inputs. `derive` takes its facts as the
facts of the parent, so later candidates are compared with it. The earlier records stay as they are.

`ratchet.json` is a copy of the state for a reader that does not parse the log: `state` (`running`, `finished`, `waiting_for_owner`,
`baseline_failed`, `stopped_after_approval`), `parent`, `next_seq`, `next_acc`, `mesh_size_mm`, `pending`, `counts` and the pins (`start_run`,
`start_final_sha256`, `rules_sha256`, `yaml_sha256`, `inputs`, `owner_gate`, `source`, `with_labels`). `inputs` holds the YAML hash, the hash of every region file,
the hash of `run.json` and the leaves of the YAML (`values`, so that a difference can be named). The job files of section 24 (`job.json`, `job.DONE` or
`job.FAILED`, `job.guard`) are in the root, so a second runner gets `JobHeld`, and a process that is killed leaves `job.FAILED`, never `job.DONE`. `approve` has its
own job folder (`approve_job/`), so it does not replace the job record of the run.

The state that a reader sees (`rt.status`, the tool `ratchet_status`, the script `status`) is derived from the state file and the job files for a runner of any kind:
a live job lock means the process runs (a final state in the file waits for the process to end). A last job that failed with an exit code (a refused start, an error,
Ctrl+C) means `failed`: the file holds the state of an earlier call, and the text of the error is in the job record (`error` in `job.json`, written when the call
ends) and in the status (`last_error`: `exit_code` and `message`, also inside `summary`). A file that says `running` with no live lock and no exit code (a kill, for
example for lack of memory) also means `failed`, and then the summary says that the process can have been killed. `promotions_open` names a folder that the log
promotes and the root does not hold yet.

### 36.5 Folders, promotion and restart

The root (default `<run folder>-ratchet`) holds: `acc_00` (a copy of the start part, run-shaped), `acc_NN` (each promoted candidate), `shadow_NNN` (a
judged candidate; a promoted one is moved to `acc_NN`), `cand_NNN` (what a source wrote), the log, the state and the job files. The STL of a candidate folder (`cand_NNN/edited.stl`) and the STL of its judged folder
are one file (a hard link; a file system without hard links gets a copy), so the root stores it once. `acc_NN` is a run-shaped
folder: `run.json` (a copy of the start run, with the YAML path made absolute and a key `ratchet`: `{format, id, parent, kind}`), `result/final.stl`, and
the `verify/` folder of its own judge. It has no `result/metrics.json`, so `verify` finds no optimizer stiffness to compare with. It has `labels.bin` when the
source reads the frozen regions (`needs_labels`) and for `acc_00`. The number of `acc_NN` is an integer: `acc_99` is followed by `acc_100`.

The start run is never written (a test compares the hash of the whole tree). The root must not be inside a run folder. The parent must have
`run.json` and `result/final.stl`, must not have `result/nominal.stl` (machining stock: `verify` reads `nominal.stl`, so the candidate and the parent would be
different parts; version 1 refuses it with the reason), and must have `labels.bin` for a marks source.

Order of a promotion, so that a kill at any point is safe: (1) the log line with `promoted`; (2) the move of `shadow_NNN` to `acc_NN` (with the
labels copied first); (3) the state file. On the next start, `recover` finishes step 2 for every promoted record whose folder is not there (`approve` calls it too,
so a kill after the approval line is finished by the next `approve` or `run`). One log line, one promotion.

A promotion never lands on a folder that the log does not name. A new parent takes the next free `acc_NN` number (a stray folder is reported as a fact and is never
used or changed). `acc_NN` that is there next to its shadow, or that holds another candidate than the record (`run.json` id, hash of `final.stl`), stops the run with
the facts. The folders of a candidate that no record names (a kill during the judge: the candidate is judged again) are moved to `unlogged/<UTC>/`, not deleted;
the same holds for an unfinished `acc_00`. The only file the ratchet deletes is a `.tmp` file of an interrupted write (it holds no result).

A root that holds a ratchet goes on with it only when the start part (`result/final.stl`), the rules, the mesh size and the inputs of the judge are the same. The
inputs are the YAML (material, loads, settings, print block), every region file that it names and `run.json` of the start run; they are pinned by hash in
`ratchet.json`. They are checked at the start, before and after each judge call, and by `approve`. A difference stops the run with the facts (old and new sha256, and the
YAML keys or region files that differ) and the options: a new root; `rebaseline` (`--rebaseline`: judge the current parent again under the inputs, rules and mesh size of
now, append a `baseline` record with `rebase_of`, keep the log, and go on; refused while a candidate waits for the owner); or `overwrite` (`--overwrite`: move the
files into `earlier_NN` and start again). A change that happens while the ratchet runs raises `RatchetError` (exit code 2) and logs nothing for the candidate in hand.
`overwrite` moves the files into `earlier_NN.tmp` and renames the folder once, so a kill leaves a `.tmp` folder that the next `overwrite` finishes. A root with other
files is refused in the same way. A `rebaseline` whose judge fails keeps the old pins, so it is asked for again.

### 36.6 The owner gate

Opt-in: `--stop-before-promote` (or `stop_before_promote`), or `acceptance.owner_gate: true`. The runner stops after the first ACCEPT, before it
promotes: the record has `owner_approval: pending` and `promoted: null`, the state is `waiting_for_owner`, and the exit code is 3 (the job is `DONE`: a pause is
not a failure). A call with a waiting candidate judges nothing. `python -m topopt.ratchet approve ROOT [--id c007] [--decline]` (the tool
`ratchet_approve`) appends an `approval` record (`given` or `declined`) and, for `given`, promotes the candidate. A candidate that was judged against an old
parent is not approved: judge it again. `approve` also stops when the inputs of the judge changed since the ratchet started (a decline does not need them). It finishes a
promotion that a kill left, and it stops while a runner holds the root. Run the ratchet again to go on with the next candidates. The gate is a recorded fact; the tool decides nothing.

### 36.7 Sources

A source makes candidates and decides nothing. The interface (`topopt/ratchet_sources.py`): `kind`, `needs_labels`, `describe()`, and
`propose(parent_dir, out_dir, history) -> Candidate | None`, where `history` is the list of log records (the source skips what it finds there).

- `marks:FILE`: one candidate for each mark of a marks file (section 29), in file order, made by `apply_marks` on the current parent. After the first
  promotion the hash `source_sha256` of the file does not match the parent: the source applies the mark with `allow_stale` and the record says so
  (`source.facts.source_sha256_stale`).
- `marks:FILE` where the file is the output of the list command (29.3): each mark has the keys `remove_mode` or `smooth_mode`, so the
  source (which passes no `per_mark` option) applies the operator that the list chose (29.1: the order of the keys). The extra key
  `cleanup` is ignored by the source; the ratchet log names the mark as `marks.json#<id>`. The order of the file is the order of judging.
  The later marks keep their points after an accept: a mark whose feature the earlier accept changed can fall back to the plain boolean
  seam, and `verify` can refuse that surface (the `errors.verify` case below). A file that holds loose bodies has the body marks only
  (29.3 part 7: two roots).
- `stl:FOLDER`: each `.stl` file of the folder is a candidate (a part that another tool made), in natural name order.

Marks candidates and `verify` (the C3a fix, section 29): `apply_marks` sews the new surface into the part (`seam.method: sewn`), and `topopt verify` meshes the
result. A `stress` or `stiffness` rule on a marks candidate is judged like on any other candidate. The rules that need `printcheck` only (`watertight`, `bodies`,
`loose_island`, `mass`, `print_gate`) do not need a solve. `symmetry` needs no solve either, but it needs the top-level `mirror` of the YAML (36.1). If the step
falls back to the plain boolean (`seam.method: boolean`, with `why_not_sewn`), the surface can have fold edges (read `totals.surface_quality` of the candidate), and
`verify` can still refuse it. The record then has `errors.verify` with the message of `verify`, the check of the `stress` or `stiffness` rule is `no_input`, and the
decision is REJECT. Measured (hook short, mesh 3.27 mm, one `remove` mark of radius 3 mm, a sewn seam): `verify` exit 0 in 3.4 s, `printcheck` 1.8 s, the mark 0.9 s,
peak memory 0.65 GB. With `against_parent: not_worse` and no tolerance the cut is REJECTED: p99.9 stress `hang` 0.0793 MPa against 0.0779 MPa of the parent (+1.9 %),
`pull_off` 1.673 against 1.636 MPa (+2.3 %). With `cap_or_parent` and a limit of 1.25 times the stress of the parent it is ACCEPTED. The tests are
`test_t6_stress_on_a_marks_candidate_is_judged_by_the_stress_rule_like_any_other` and `test_t6_cap_or_parent_with_a_limit_above_the_parent_accepts_the_same_cut`
(`tests/test_ratchet_e2e.py`). The box-cut source of `tests/ratchet_helpers.py` (not in the engine) still makes the candidates of the hook and ladle tests.

### 36.8 Script and exit codes

```
python -m topopt.ratchet check   RUN_DIR [--yaml F] [--source SRC] [--json]   rules, what each needs, what is missing; no solve
python -m topopt.ratchet judge   STL --parent RUN_DIR [--yaml F] [--out DIR] [--mesh-size MM]    one judge call; no promotion
python -m topopt.ratchet run     RUN_DIR --source marks:FILE|stl:FOLDER [--root DIR] [--yaml F] [--max-candidates N]
                                 [--mesh-size MM] [--stop-before-promote] [--overwrite] [--rebaseline] [--override-lock]
python -m topopt.ratchet status  ROOT [--json]
python -m topopt.ratchet approve ROOT [--id c007] [--decline]
```

Exit codes: 0 finished (any mix of ACCEPT and REJECT); 1 bad input, a usage error, inputs that differ from the pins at the start, or a second runner (`JobHeld`); 2 could not run (the baseline could not
be judged, or the inputs changed while the ratchet ran: the log has the record with `errors` or nothing for the candidate, and the job is `FAILED`); 3 stopped at the owner gate. 130: Ctrl+C (the log is kept).

### 36.9 MCP tools

`ratchet_run(run_dir, source, marks, root, estimate_only=True, yaml_path, max_candidates, mesh_size_mm, stop_before_promote, overwrite, rebaseline, override_lock)`:
with `estimate_only` (the default) it returns the `check` (the rules, what each needs, what is missing, the number of candidates, the verify time) and starts
nothing. A real start is a detached process (`python -m topopt.ratchet run`, a lock file `.topopt-ratchet.lock` in the work folder, the output in
`<root>.stdout` beside the root, in a folder that the tool makes) and returns at once. `ratchet_status(root, last)` gives the state, the counts, the parent, the last records with the reasons,
`pending`, the facts of the job and the process. The state file is written before the process exits, so a final state (`finished`, `waiting_for_owner`,
`baseline_failed`) shows only after the process has ended; while it lives the status says `running` and holds the file state in `file_state`. Then the next
call (`ratchet_approve`, `ratchet_run`) is never refused as busy for a state that the status showed. `ratchet_approve(root, id, decline)` is the gate. The one-job guard counts a ratchet: `run_topopt`,
`verify_run` and `ratchet_run` refuse a start while any of the three works (an estimate is not a job). Test hook: `TOPOPT_MCP_RATCHET_CMD`.

### 36.10 Facts and limits of version 1

- Version 1 judges against the parent one candidate at a time. It makes no candidate of its own: a generator is a later source (the interface above).
- `displacement`, `alignment` and `buckling` have a producer since K1-B (36.1): the tet rows of `verify` (B3) and the tet buckling factor. A rule that is listed and has no input (no rows in the YAML, a skipped check, a case with no factor) is `no_input` with the reason.
- A marks candidate can use `stress` and `stiffness` (36.7). Only a `boolean` seam of `apply_marks` can still give a surface that `verify` refuses; the
  ratchet records that as `errors.verify` and REJECTs, and does not hide it.
- Since K1-A the verify step of the judge takes a YAML with a joint or a spring (section 16, "Joints and springs"): before, such a part gave `errors.verify` and the `stress` and `stiffness` rules had no input. `verify_facts` reads the same keys as for a clamped part (`tests/test_verify_supports.py` checks that a part with two joints gives them). The supports are the YAML as it is; the judge adds no support of its own. A full judge call with a joint YAML is not tested here.
- `run_history` (section 21.1) lists the `acc_NN` folders as runs with the problem "result/metrics.json is missing". `verify/verify.json` in an `acc_NN`
  folder names the `shadow_NNN` path of the judge in its `run` block (the folder moved after the judge).
- The percentile by volume is a number of the mesh. Two parts are compared at the mesh size of the baseline; a stress margin is the number of the user, with a source.
- A judge call on the examples took 21 to 28 s (hook 1.2 mm, ladle 3.25 mm) and 4 to 5 s on the short fixtures; the peak memory was 0.7 to 1.2 GB.
- Disk: each judged candidate keeps its judged folder. On the full hook it is 3.9 MB: the copy of the STL in `result/` is 3.0 MB and `verify/` is 0.85 MB
  (`mesh.npz` 0.22, `fields.npz` 0.63). The STL is the large part, not `verify/`. A marks candidate also has `cand_NNN/edited.stl` (about 7 MB with the copy); the two names are
  one file now (a hard link), so the root stores it once. (Measured by the independent review at commit 4e25add.)
- The judge is deterministic: the same STL at the same mesh size gives bit-equal facts. A changed surface gives a new mesh, and the numbers move a little even for a harmless edit.
  Measured for a cut of 0.05 mm3 far from every region: on the full hook (mesh 1.75 mm) the p99.9 stress moved +0.09 % and -0.21 % and the stiffness +0.008 % and
  -0.012 %; on the short hook (mesh 3.27 mm) the stress moved -2.0 % and +2.2 % and the stiffness -0.36 % and -1.37 %. The noise grows with the mesh size. So `stress` with
  `not_worse` and no `tolerance_pct` is strict: the check says how far the value moved, and the owner may set `tolerance_pct` with a source. The same holds for a
  `stiffness.max_drop_pct` near zero. These numbers are facts for the owner; the engine has none of its own.

## 38. Joints: a beam from a load region to a fixed point (added with A7b)

Backlog B-067, the beam part. This section is number 38. Sections 35 (A7a) and 36 (D3) are in main, and this section follows them. The number 37 is not used in this file. Do not renumber other sections. Code: `topopt/joints.py`. Check against closed forms: `tools/joint_check.py`.

**What a joint is.** A joint bonds the exposed faces of one load region to a rigid body with 6 dofs `q = (t, w)` (a translation and a rotation about a
reference point), and an Euler-Bernoulli beam joins the body to a fixed far point. The far end of the beam is fixed. The beam sees the region as one
rigid body, so the region carries the load to the ground through the beam. Use it for a part that hangs on a rod, a pin or a tube that is not
in the voxel grid. The beam adds 6 dofs for each joint to the stiffness matrix (a bordered matrix, below).

**YAML.** The top-level key `joints` is a list. Each entry:

| Key | Form | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `region` | a name of `regions.load` | The faces that are bonded. One joint for each region. The region may have a force, a spring (section 35) or neither. |
| `to` | `[x, y, z]`, mm | The far point. The beam runs from the reference point to it. Any direction. |
| `section` | `{kind: round, d}`, `{kind: tube, od, id}`, `{kind: rect, b, h}` or `{kind: props, A, Iy, Iz, J}` | The beam section, mm and mm2/mm4. `rect`: `b` runs along the section y axis and `h` along the section z axis. The torsion constant of a rectangle is the usual series `J = a t^3 (1/3 - 64/pi^5 (t/a) sum tanh(n pi a / 2t) / n^5)`, n = 1, 3, 5, ... (a the longer side, t the shorter one; a square gives 0.140577 a^4). |
| `origin` | `[x, y, z]`, mm, optional | The reference point of the rigid body and the start of the beam. Default: the area centroid of the bonded faces. |
| `orient` | `[x, y, z]`, optional | The section y axis, with its part along the beam removed. Default: the global axis least parallel to the beam. It matters for a section that is not round. |
| `bond_stiffness_per_area` | number, N/mm3, optional | The stiffness `k_a` of the bond. Default: `c E / h` with the module constant `c = 30` (`joints.BOND_C`), `E` of the run material and `h` the voxel size. |
| `E`, `nu` | numbers, optional | The material of the beam. Default: the run material. |

An entry stops before the run, with the fact and a `(file: <yaml>)` suffix, when `region` is not a load region, a key is missing or unknown, a region
has two entries, `to`, `origin` or `orient` is not a list of 3 numbers or `orient` is the zero vector, a section value is not above 0, `id` is not
less than `od`, `E` or `nu` is out of range, `bond_stiffness_per_area` is not above 0, the beam has length 0 (`to` equals the reference point), or `orient`
is parallel to the beam axis. The last two are found when the problem is built, because the default reference point comes from the faces. The zero-vector
test uses the tolerance `1e-9` of the other vector keys (`DEGENERATE`); it is not a physical limit. A region with no exposed face is refused when the
problem is built. `Config.uses_extended_loads()` is True when the YAML has a joint, and `Config.has_joints()` tells it. `regions.fixed` may be missing or empty
when the YAML has a joint. `L/d` of the beam (`d` is the diameter, `od`, the longer side of a rectangle, or the diameter of the circle of equal area for
`props`) is a fact: the beam is Euler-Bernoulli, and the shear flexibility of a short beam is not in the model. The size of the missing shear: for a transverse force at the free end, the shear deflection over the bending deflection is `3 E I / (kappa G A L^2)`; for a solid round section (Cowper `kappa = 6 (1 + nu) / (7 + 6 nu)`) it is about `0.57 (d/L)^2` at nu 0.35, that is 0.6 percent at L/d 10, 2.3 percent at 5, 6.3 percent at 3, 14 percent at 2 and 57 percent at 1. Axial load, torsion and a pure moment have no shear term.

**Faces and the bond.** The faces are the same as for a spring (section 35: a face of a voxel of the region whose neighbour is EMPTY or KEEP_OUT, or
lies outside the grid); all of them are bonded. The bond energy is `1/2 k_a int |u - R q|^2 dA` with `R = [I, -skew(x - ref)]`. With the consistent Q1 face matrix
`U` of section 35 this gives three blocks: `Kb = k_a h^2 U` on each axis (added to `K` in place, as a spring, in the same index arrays), a coupling `C` (grid dofs x 6) and
a block `D_bond` (6 x 6, summed over the faces pairwise: a plain sum has a rounding error that grew to 1.5e-2 in a bending case). `D_bond` equals the 2 x 2 Gauss rule to 3e-14;
a lumped rule is 1.2 percent off in the rotation block. A joint region and a spring region may be the same region: the two face matrices add.
The voxels of the region are LOAD voxels (solid, full E, in `final.stl`), as for a spring.

**Beam.** `L = |to - ref|`. The frame `Q = [axis, y, z]` is right-handed and orthonormal. The 6 x 6 matrix at the joint end (far end fixed) has `EA/L`,
`GJ/L`, `12 E I/L^3`, `6 E I/L^2` and `4 E I/L`; the plane (axis, y) uses `Iz` and the plane (axis, z) uses `Iy`, with the sign of the coupling flipped,
and it is turned into the global axes with `diag(Q, Q)`. The bordered matrix is

```
[[ K + Kb ,   C           ],
 [ C^T    ,   D_bond + B  ]]
```

The supports do not depend on the density, so the sensitivities are the same formula as without a joint, and the force vector has zeros on the border. The problem is
self-adjoint: the factor of the solve serves the adjoint. `C` rows on fixed dofs are dropped.

**Solvers.** `joints.BorderedSolver` (a `LinearSolver`) factors the bordered matrix and returns vectors with `n_free` rows: `solve(B)` pads `B` with zeros on the border and cuts the
border from the result, so no caller changes (`formulation.py` and `checkpoint.py` are the same; the warm start of AMG has the bordered size and the same class restores it).
pardiso, cholesky (macOS) and amg take it. AMG keeps its 3 x 3 blocks (the augmented near-null space has `6 m` more rows: the rigid-body modes of the grid and
the bodies that move with them). A run without joints builds the old `LinearSolver` (bit-equal; `Model.kb` is None without springs and joints). Measured (hook grid, 115,836 free dofs, one
joint, pardiso, 4 threads): the bordered matrix is built again in each pass (`sps.bmat`, 0.09 to 0.13 s), and a pass costs 0.45 s more (+24 to 38 percent of the factor); the peak memory of a factor and solve is +305 MB with pardiso and +138 MB with amg.
`topopt check`, the run log and `build_regions` count the bordered copy of `K` in the memory estimate (`joints.bordered_copy_bytes`: 28 bytes for each stored entry of `K`, 242 MB on the hook; `memory_estimate.bordered_copy_bytes` in `check`). With `gpu-mg` they count none: it is matrix-free and makes no copy of `K` (the `check` number `memory_estimate.cholesky_bytes` is the Cholesky number for comparison and keeps it).
AMG needs 11 to 40 iterations with a clamp and 9 to 138 on a floating part, with the lowest count at `c = 30`. `history.jsonl` has `amg_iterations` (a list with the CG iterations of each load case in the main solve of the pass)
for amg, and `metrics.json` has `joints.amg_iterations` (`passes`, `last`, `max`).
cholesky is tested on Linux with a fake Accelerate library (the Python side: the lower triangle, the refactor of the same pattern, the padding); the Accelerate factor
itself runs on a Mac only: `pytest tests/test_joints.py` (the whole file: on a Mac `solver: auto` is cholesky, so `test_gradient_matches_finite_differences_with_a_joint[auto]` also runs the real Accelerate factor of a bordered matrix, and `-k cholesky` would leave it out). `gpu-mg` takes joints since P2b (section 20): the term `- C D^-1 C^T` (rank `6 m` for `m` joints) is in the operator of every level, with `C_l = P^T C_{l-1}`,
and in the smoother blocks, the dense coarsest matrix, the FP64 residual and the operator of the backward-error rule; `q = -D^-1 C^T u` and the wrenches come from the
displacement on the host. A part held by joints only runs there. Case C (32-bit float on the device) computes the joint term in
32-bit float and removes the rigid modes of each body and the harmonic columns of each bonded patch from its inner PCG (P2d and P2d-D3h, section 20): the ratio of the beam to the bond stiffness (`GpuSolver.facts()["border"]["beam_over_bond_min"]`) is printed by `topopt check` and `run.log` with the cases that were measured
(section 20), and a run that stops gives the ratio and the options, with no threshold. A per-axis support runs on `gpu-mg` since P2c (section 20), also next to a joint.
`topopt verify` takes a joint since K1-A (section 16, "Joints and springs"): the bordered matrix on the P2 dofs, with the 6 resultants of each bond.

**Rigid-body test.** The test of section 26.2 is skipped when the YAML has a joint (also when it has a spring): the beam blocks all six modes. The fact is in `supports.rigid_body_test`
(`"skipped: a joint blocks all six rigid-body modes ..."`), in `run.json`, `check_data` and the `supports:` line of `topopt check`. A part on joints only is valid. The check of the voxel
buckling (section 33) and the buckling row (section 39) run with joints (PR 4, H1): the stiffness of their eigen problem is the condensed matrix
`S = K + Kb - C D^-1 C^T`, the Schur complement of the bordered matrix, because the grid block of the bordered factor is `S^-1` and not `K^-1`. The beams have no geometric stiffness
in this model, so the load factors are for buckling of the part and not of the beams (the tubes or the rods that the joints stand for). The refine step (`refine/stress.py`) solves with the same `K + Kb` and the bordered solver.

**Readers of "the part is held".** `springs.support_mask(problem)` includes the joint regions (the readers of section 35: `interfaces.voxel_facts`, `stress_report`, the loose pieces of the
buckling check, `topopt check`). `regions_builder` counts a region with a joint as used, and `feedback._yaml_vs_run` knows `joints` (`joints[<region>]`, `.to`, `.section`).

**Facts.** For each joint (`run.json` `joints.joints[]`, `check_data` `extended.joints.joints[]`): `region`, `faces`, `faces_by_direction`, `area_mm2`, `nodes`, `reference_mm` and
`reference_from`, `to_mm`, `length_mm`, `axis`, `section` (as given), `section_area_mm2`, `iy_mm4`, `iz_mm4`, `j_mm4`, `depth_mm`, `length_over_depth`, `beam_E_mpa`, `beam_nu`, `beam_G_mpa`,
`beam_material_from`, `frame` (`x`, `y`, `z`, `y_from`), `bond_stiffness_per_area_n_per_mm3`, `bond_stiffness_from`, `c_equivalent` (`k_a h / E`), `bond_diagonal` and `beam_diagonal` (the six
diagonal entries of `D_bond` and `B`), `rho` (the smallest `D_bond_ii / B_ii` of the six dofs) and `bond_share_max` (the largest share of the joint flexibility that the bond holds, over all wrenches:
the largest eigenvalue of `B x = lambda (B + D_bond) x`; this is the share of the joint flexibility, and it does not bound the error of the compliance), `beam_min_translation_over_Eh` (the smallest eigenvalue of the translation block of `B`, over `E h` of the run material) and
`beam_min_rotation_over_Eh3` (the smallest eigenvalue of the rotation block of `B`, over `E h^3`). `joints.bordered_dofs` is `6 m`; `joints.bond` is `{"c": 30, "source": <text>}`: the source of `c` (from measurements on the hook grid).
The bond stiffness is a fact and a field, not a threshold: nothing refuses a small `rho`. `rho` is the bond over the beam, so a softer beam gives a larger `rho`: it does not show a nearly free part.
The two `beam_min_*` facts do. When one is below `springs.NEAR_SINGULAR` (1e-6, the constant of the spring facts of section 35), `topopt check` adds the warning `joint on '<region>': its smallest beam stiffness is ... below 1e-06: the part is nearly free on that axis ...`
(with the options: raise the section or E, shorten the beam, or add a fixed region), and `run.log` has the same text with the prefix `warning:` (the function is `joints.near_singular_lines`, the pattern of `springs.near_singular_lines`). Nothing stops the run.
Measured (pad case, no clamp, round d 0.5 mm in the run material, `E h` with h 1 mm): L 100 mm gives 3.7e-8 (residual 3e-4, a visible `warning:` reaction line); L 1,000 mm gives 3.7e-11 (pardiso gives no error, residual 0.38; amg stops at 10,000 mm with `did not converge`).
The same facts are in the lines `joint:`, `joint frame:`, `joint beam:`, `joint bond:` and `joints:` of `topopt check` and `run.log`.

**Reactions.** The record of the last pass in `history.jsonl` and `metrics.json` have `reactions` (section 35) with, for a joint region, an entry in `joints` (region name -> entry) in each case; its `nodal` is the term of the balance. The body motion comes from the grid solution, `q = -D^-1 C^T u` (no stored border state, so `Model.reaction_facts(U, rho)` stays a function of `U` and `rho`); the nodal force of the bond is `g = Kb u + C q`.
The entry has `part` (the wrench on the part: the force `-(B q)[:3]` and the moment `-(B q)[3:]` about `about_mm`, the reference point), `ground` (the reaction of the fixed end: the same force with its moment about
the far point, `-(B q)[3:] - (ref - to) x (B q)[:3]`, `about_mm` = the far point), `translation_mm`, `rotation_rad` (`q`), `nodal` (`{"force_n", "moment_nmm"}`, the moment about the grid origin: the sum of `-g` over the nodes, the force of the bond on the part, which is the term of the balance) and
`bond_energy_share` (the energy of the bond `1/2 (u^T g - q^T B q)` over `c/2` of the case: the share of the strain energy that sits in the bond; it is the first-order error that the finite bond stiffness puts in the compliance: 0.8 percent for a round d 10 mm, L 5 mm steel beam on the pad case, where `bond_share_max` is 0.41; for a very stiff bond the difference of the two energies cancels and the value is of the size of the round-off, for example -1.1e-6 at `bond_stiffness_per_area` 1e9). The sum of `applied`, `clamp`, the `springs` entries and the `nodal` terms of the `joints` entries is zero;
`force_error` and `moment_error` and `residual_rel` are defined as in section 35 (the same balance with the bond forces as one more term). `topopt run` writes, for each case, a `reactions:` line with the joint nodal sum and a line
`reactions: <case>: joint '<name>': on the part ..., ground reaction ..., ... percent of the strain energy in the bond` to `run.log` (the prefix `warning:` when an error is above 1e-6).
`stiffness_cases[].N_per_mm` keeps its rule `|F|^2 / c` for plain forces; with a joint `c` includes the deflection of the beam, so it is the stiffness of the mounted part.

**Checks (tests).** `tests/test_joints.py`. Closed forms (`tools/joint_check.py`: a stiff cube of 4 to 8 voxels, one load region, a round beam of the same material, `c = 100`): axial, bending in both planes, torsion, and a force
with a moment (the cross term `F M L^2 / (E I)`), for the x axis and an oblique axis (1, 2, 2), with splu, amg and pardiso, all within 1e-3 of the cantilever. Measured: axial +2.9e-4 (the flexibility of the block and of the bond in series with the
beam; it falls as `E_block / E_beam` grows), bending, torsion and the cross term 3e-7 to 2e-6 with 8 voxels (up to 5e-6 with 4 voxels), the same for splu, amg and pardiso. The bordered solve equals the dense Schur form (1e-10 relative in the compliance with splu); `q` from `-D^-1 C^T u` equals the border slice of the
bordered solution; a finite-difference check of the gradient with a joint (a stiff beam, `E = 210000`) agrees to 1e-5 (direct) and 1e-4 (amg); a joint with no fixed region and no spring runs, and its ground reaction of a transverse tip force is
`-F` with the moment `F L` about the far point.

**Merge notes.** `Problem.joints` and `Config.joints` are tail fields with a default; `Regions` has not changed. Mirror (A4a): no refusal, as for springs (a joint that is not symmetric gives the best symmetric design; a run with a symmetric joint keeps its symmetry; `tests/test_joints.py`). Left for later: a beam between two load regions (a separate backlog item); the stress in the beam section (the joint reaction gives the forces);
the shear flexibility of a short beam (Timoshenko; `L/d` is a fact, and the size of the missing shear is above); a bond on one face direction only (the facts `faces_by_direction` show what a region has).

## 39. Buckling row in the optimizer (added with A6b)

An opt-in row of the optimizer: the lowest linear buckling load factor of each load case is held at or above `buckling.min_factor`.
It is **off by default**. Then nothing changes: the optimizer, the snapshots, `history.jsonl`, `labels.bin`, `final.stl` and `metrics.json`
are bit-equal to a run without this section (at 1 thread, a direct solver). The code is `topopt/buckling_row.py`. The section number is a working number (36 is taken, 38 is the beam section, and 37 is not used in this file).

**Switch.** The YAML block `buckling` (section 33) gets two keys. The row is on when `min_factor` is set. `topopt run` has no flag for it.

```yaml
buckling:
  min_factor: 150     # number > 0. Turns the row on. The lowest load factor must be at least this multiplier on the load case. No default.
  ks_q: 40            # number > 0. KS sharpness of the row. Default 40. A value without min_factor has no effect (a fact in `topopt check`).
  modes: 6            # integer >= 1. Modes in the KS (also the modes of the check). Default 6.
  max_seconds: 120    # number > 0. Time budget of one eigen solve (also of the check). Default 120.
  max_gb: 8           # number > 0, GB (1e9 bytes). Memory budget for the fact of the row (also of the check). Default: the RAM.
  check: true         # the check of the final design (section 33). It is independent of the row.
```

Unknown keys and wrong values are errors of the YAML (section 2). `buckling.density` belongs to the check: the row uses the gray density of
the optimizer. `Config.buckling.min_factor` and `.ks_q` are `None` when the key is absent.

**The row.** One row `buckling:<case>` for each load case, in the order: volume, compliance rows, stress rows, buckling rows, then the rows of
section 31. The row is `KS_q(F mu_j) - 1 <= 0` over the `modes` lowest factors, with `F = min_factor`, `mu_j = 1 / lambda_j` and
`(-Kg) phi_j = mu_j K phi_j`. `limit` 1, `scale` 1, price 1000, `stage_aware`, no `measure` (step acceptance of the stress rows does not run the row).
`S >= max_j F mu_j`, so a met row has a lowest factor of at least `F`. `S <= max_j F mu_j + ln(k)/q`: a row that is just met has a lowest factor between
`F` and `F / (1 - ln(k)/q)` (4.5 percent for 6 modes and q 40). The history reports it as `ks_offset`.
The gradient is exact for the optimizer density (`wrt` `rho_stiff`; the chain rule of the formulation goes through the projection, the filter and the mirror).
It has three parts: the explicit part of `Kg`, the K part, and the stress part through `u`. The stress part needs one adjoint solve for each load case.
It is 80 to 95 percent of the gradient norm, so it is not optional. A mass run with only buckling rows has these rows and no volume ceiling.

**Solvers.** The row needs a direct factor of K with a solve call at every evaluated pass: `cholesky` (macOS arm64) or `pardiso` (Linux x86_64, extra `pardiso`).
With `amg` (also what `auto` gives without PARDISO or the Accelerate shim) or `gpu-mg`, `topopt run` stops before the model is built with a `UserError`:
the facts, and the options from `backend_availability()` (for each direct solver: "set settings.solver", or its note with the install command and the license
note; "remove buckling.min_factor and use the check" only when a direct solver is available here, because the check skips without one). The setting
`gpu-mg` is refused by its name, before `backend_problem` (no OpenCL loads). A `BucklingRow` that a script builds by hand checks `model.solver_name` at its first
evaluation and raises the same text. There is no SciPy fallback. `topopt check` prints the same text as a warning and does not stop (also for `gpu-mg` on a host without OpenCL).
`settings.robust: eroded` or `wall` with `buckling.min_factor` stops at the start in the same way (the row would hold the eroded design, and no test covers this);
`topopt check` has the text as a warning.

**Joints (section 38).** The row runs with joints. The stiffness of the eigen problem is the condensed matrix `S = K + Kb - C D^-1 C^T` of the bordered matrix that the run holds (section 33,
"Joints"). The eigen solve, the K-normalisation (`phi^T S phi = 1`), the adjoint solve (`S lam = s`, the grid block of the bordered solve) and both residuals (`residual_u`, `residual_adjoint`, the
factor check) use `S`. The three parts of the gradient do not change: `dS/drho = dK/drho`, because `Kb`, `C` and `D` do not depend on the density. The beams have no geometric stiffness in
this model: the row holds the buckling of the part, not of the beams. `topopt check` has this as a fact (`buckling_row.facts`), and the other refusals (a solver with no direct factor, `gpu-mg`)
stay. The old refusal text for joints (`joints_refusal`, reason `joints`) is gone. Checked against central differences of the full chain with a joint (`tests/test_buckling_row_joints.py`).

**Which passes run (the skip rule).** An evaluation is one eigen solve for each load case. A pass evaluates when the first of these reasons is true:
`no_pass_number` (a point that a script built by hand), `unknown` (fewer than 2 evaluations with a result since the row was last unknown: passes 0 and 1 always
run), `stage_start` (the beta changed), `last_pass`, `near` (the last lowest factor is at most 1.5 `min_factor`), `every` (5 passes since the last evaluation).
A skipped pass returns the last value and a zero gradient: its `g` is at most `1/1.5 - 1 + ln(modes)/q` (-0.2885 for 6 modes and q 40), and MMA gives such a row a
multiplier of 0. The constants are `SKIP_FACTOR` 1.5 and `EVERY` 5 in `buckling_row.py` (the pipeline values). The rule can miss a fall of the lowest factor of
more than 33 percent within 4 passes. In the measured runs the only fall above 5 percent was the hook `hang` case, -43 percent from pass 0 to pass 1, and the two
evaluations at the start cover it. In loop runs on a column the rule gave the same design as the every-pass run (largest change of a density 1.02e-4) with 31 to 84
percent of the evaluations.
A failed evaluation (`not_converged`, `time_budget`, `factor_mismatch`) gives the last value (0 if none) and a zero gradient, and the row is unknown again: the next
pass evaluates. **The back-off:** after `KNOWN_EVALUATIONS` (2) failures in a row, the row has no known lowest factor and stops evaluating at every pass. It evaluates at a
`stage_start`, at the `last_pass`, and `every` `EVERY` (5) passes since the last try (the try counts whether it gave a result or not), and it has no `near` reason, until one
evaluation gives a result; then the row is unknown with one result, so the next pass evaluates, and the skip rule above applies again. The back-off adds no constant.
The first failure writes one fact line to `run.log`; its options go with the status: `not_converged` says "the case may have no compression" and gives the options to remove
`buckling.min_factor` or to look at the load case (the row is on for every load case and there is no key to choose the cases; raising `buckling.max_seconds` does not help
there), `time_budget` gives "raise `buckling.max_seconds`", `factor_mismatch` says it is a fault of the tool. It is not a stop of the run.
A row with no result at the last pass (the last entry has `evaluated` false and a failure status, or no value at all) is **not judged** in the verdict (section 24.2): `verdict.json`
`measures.max_g` names the row with `judged` false and `met` false, so `feasible` is false. The end of the run has the line "constraint not judged: ..." and a fact with the status, the pass of
the value that the row holds, and options. A last pass that the skip rule skipped holds a value that is a result, and the row stays judged. The run does not add an evaluation at a pass where a stop rule fires: it would cost
one eigen solve for each case, and the bound of the skip rule covers that pass.

**Warm start of the eigen solve (#155).** After an evaluation with a result, the row keeps the start vector `v0 = sum_j c_j / sqrt(c_j^T K c_j)` over all columns `c_j` of the
eigen solve (`modes + 1`, before the cut to `modes`; `K` is the matrix of that solve, with joints the condensed `S`). The next evaluation of the same row passes it as `v0` to ARPACK.
The row starts cold (`v0=None`: the fixed seeded random vector of `buckling_modes`) at its first evaluation; when no vector is kept; when the kept vector has not the length of `K`, is not
finite, or is zero (it is dropped); and after a state of other settings (below). A failed evaluation (`not_converged`, `time_budget`, `factor_mismatch`) keeps the last vector of
an evaluation with a result and does not replace it. `buckling_modes`, the voxel check (`topopt buckling`) and the `verify` check do not change. The factors, the value and the gradient
stay the same to the solver tolerance (on the hook at 2 mm, 41 passes, 4 threads: the lowest factors differ from the cold solve of main by 4e-12 relative or less at the last pass, the design by 4e-9 or less);
the number of solves falls by 12 to 14 percent (3541 to 3101 and 3316 to 2869 eigen solves at `min_factor` 150 and 100). The vector is in the row state `v0`, so it is in the checkpoint: an array
`rowvec_<n>` of the `.npz` (float64, exact; section 24.2), also for `rows_before`. A resume and a continuation then do the same solves as the run that was not stopped (the same bytes at 1 thread).
A checkpoint of an older topopt has no vector: it loads, and the first evaluation after it starts cold.
The eigen tolerance of the row is the module constant `ROW_TOL` (`= buckling.TOL`, 1e-8): one place in `buckling_row.py`. It is in the row state (`tol`; a state without it was solved at `buckling.TOL`).

**The factor check.** The eigen solve and the gradient use `model.solver`, the factor of the last solve before the row. At each evaluated pass the row solves the adjoint
`K lam = s` with the K of the point and tests `||K lam - s|| / ||s||` against `RESIDUAL_FACT` (1e-6, section 33). A normal pass reads 3e-15 to 4.6e-13 (4.6e-13 is the largest of the 99 evaluations of the E3 hook run). A factor of
another pass reads 1.5e4 (hook). Above the level the status is `factor_mismatch`: no usable result. A wrong factor can also stop the eigen solve first (no convergence, or no
time left): then the row solves `K x = b` with the factor, for `b = K v` with a fixed random vector `v` (`buckling_row.CHECK_SEED`), and tests the same residual, so a failed
eigen solve with a wrong factor is `factor_mismatch` too, not `not_converged` or `time_budget`. The right-hand side is not the load: the residual of the load is `residual_u`, which
reads 1e-6 to 5.6e-6 on a valid near-singular design (a 60 mm column with void layers), while `b = K v` reads 2e-16 to 5e-16 there with the right factor (also with a joint), and
0.06 to 0.9 with the factor of another density (0.06 with a joint).
`residual_adjoint` and `adjoint_seconds` of a failed evaluation hold this check, and its first-failure fact names the check solve. `residual_u` (the residual of the static solve) and `residual_max`
(the eigen residual) are data only: the first does not see a wrong factor, and a valid near-singular design reads 1e-7 and 1e-3.
A blind spot of the adjoint residual: a factor that differs from the factor of K only in the void stiffness (a 0/1 design with the factor of `rho + 0.01`) gave an adjoint residual of 7.8e-7, below the level,
so the status is `ok`; the lowest factor was 9.49e-5 against the true 4.75e-5, and `residual_max` was 0.55 (3.4e-7 with the right factor). Only a lowest mode in the void is affected (low-density share 0.9995):
read `low_density_energy_share` and `residual_max` for it. The check after a failed eigen solve has the same blind spot: such a factor reads 8.1e-7 to 8.6e-7
(a column and a loop), below the level, so the status stays `not_converged` or `time_budget`; the factor of `rho + 0.1` reads 7.7e-4. The load as the right-hand side would
see it (1.2 to 1.75), but it gives a false `factor_mismatch` on a valid near-singular design (above).

**History.** Each pass adds these keys to the entry of the row in `constraints[]` of `history.jsonl`: `evaluated`, `reason`, `status` (`ok`, `no_positive_factor`,
`not_converged`, `time_budget`, `factor_mismatch`, `skipped`), `min_factor`, `ks_q`, `modes`, `lowest_factor`, `last_eval`, `load_factors`, `near_repeated`, `min_rel_gap`,
`cluster_cut`, `ks_share_last`, `ks_offset`, `low_density_energy_share`, `n_pass`, `n_eval`, `n_fail`, `solves`, `eigen_seconds`, `kg_seconds`, `adjoint_seconds`,
`residual_u`, `residual_adjoint`, `residual_max` (`buckling_row.INFO_KEYS`). A skipped entry has the same keys, repeats the values of the last evaluation, and has zero cost and
null residuals. Its `status` is `skipped`, or the status of the last failed evaluation while the row is in the back-off (no value is known there). The state of the row
(`n_known`, `last_value`, `last_lowest`, the counters, and for the back-off `streak`, `last_try`, `fail_status`; `logged`: the first-failure line was said, so a resume does not say it again; `tol`, `v0`: the eigen tolerance and the start vector) is in the checkpoint. A resume with the same YAML does the same passes. A resume with a
changed `min_factor`, `ks_q` or `modes` (it needs `--allow-changed-inputs`), or with a checkpoint of another `ROW_TOL`, evaluates at once and starts the eigen solve cold. `result/metrics.json` has no new top-level key. Its `constraints` list is the list of the last history entry, so the entry of the row there has the keys above (the `*_seconds` keys too). The end of the run says, as facts, the last
evaluation, the count of failed passes with options, `cluster_cut` with `ks_share_last`, a low-density share of 0.5 or more, and a last pass that was not evaluated.

**`topopt check`.** With the row on, `check_data` has the key `buckling_row` (`min_factor`, `ks_q`, `modes`, `will_run`, `reason`, `memory_estimate_bytes`, `memory_extra_bytes`,
`budget_bytes`, `evaluations_low`, `evaluations_high`, `facts`, `warnings`), and `topopt check` prints one line `buckling row: on in the YAML (...)` and the warnings. Without the row there is no key. The memory estimate is the
estimate of the check (section 33, `buckling_voxel.estimate_bytes`, K, Kg and the Lanczos vectors) on top of the run. Above the budget it is a fact with options, and the run goes on.
The time estimate of `topopt check` does not include the row. It gives these facts instead (no threshold; nothing warns or refuses on them): the count of evaluations,
`evaluations_low` to `evaluations_high` (`buckling_row.evaluation_range`: one eigen solve for one load case; the high count is every pass, the low count is the skip rule far from the limit: the passes that
always run, that is the first two, each beta stage start and the last pass, plus one evaluation for each 5 passes between them; the `near` reason lies between the two); the measured cost of one evaluation on the hook
(9.3 s for `hang`, 12.2 s for `pull_off`, "one machine, 4 threads, E3", 5.5 to 7.2 times the median pass without the row); and the worst case, `buckling.max_seconds` for each evaluation that fails.
There is no time in seconds for another model: the hook ratio is not applied to it. The same lines go to `run.log` at the start of a run. `checkpoint.effective_settings` has the key `buckling_row`
(`min_factor`, `ks_q`, `modes`) only when the row is on, so the hash of the inputs of any other run does not change.

**Cost (measured, Linux x86_64, PARDISO, a shared host).** The eigen solve is the cost: 85 percent of the time of the example run below. The hook at 1.2 mm
(two cases, 115,836 free dofs, 4 threads, `examples/hook/hook_buckling.yaml`, `min_factor` 150): one evaluation of one case takes a median of 9.3 s for `hang` (51 solves of the factor)
and 12.2 s for `pull_off` (66 solves); the first two passes take 26 to 31 s and 110 to 193 solves for a case. One adjoint solve takes 0.13 s (research). The whole run took 1469 s (81 passes,
median pass 17.2 s) against 170 s for `hook.yaml` in the same hour on the same host (median pass 1.7 s; load average 8 to 13). `pull_off` was evaluated at all 81 passes (its lowest factor stayed within 1.5 times
`min_factor`), `hang` at 18 (the skip rule). The ratio to a run without the row depends on how fast that run is: an earlier measurement of a run with the row at every pass gave 3.5 times a base run of 568 s.
At 1 thread the eigen solve is about 2.4 times slower (research). The memory estimate of the row is 0.3 GB on top of the run at the hook; the example run peaked at 2.0 GB (VmHWM) against 1.8 GB for `hook.yaml` (+0.2 GB).
`topopt check` does not include the row in its time estimate: it gives the evaluation count, this measured cost and the worst case as facts.

**Limits (facts).**

- The voxel estimate reads high for thin members (section 33): 5 to 12 percent on the hook, 59 percent at one voxel across a column. The row applies no knock-down factor. B3
  (PR #55, one host, one mesh method) measured on the hook the tet factor over the voxel factor: 0.786 (`hang`) and 0.713 (`pull_off`) with the sdf STL (0.61 to 0.63 with the `blur` STL).
  A part that must hold a tet factor `F_true` needs `min_factor` of about `F_true / 0.71` to `F_true / 0.79` on the hook. `min_factor` is a multiplier on the voxel model, and the tool
  does not change it.
- The row sees the gray density of the optimizer. The check of section 33 sees the printed density (0.5 threshold) by default. The two can differ.
- The KS offset `ln(k)/q` is accepted: a met row has a lowest factor up to 4.5 percent above `min_factor`.
- Repeated factors. The KS over a complete cluster has the exact gradient at every gap. A cluster that is cut at mode `k` has a gradient error of 0.23 to 1.8 times `ks_share_last`
  (measured on a square column 2 x 2 x 40 voxels with `modes` 1: 0.23 at 4 threads and 0.93 at 1 thread with share 1, and 1.8 in an earlier review): the error depends on the basis
  that ARPACK picks inside the cluster, so there is no single factor. When the share is near 0 (2e-16 at `modes` 3 and 5 on that column) the cut mode has no weight and the error is the
  1e-5 level of the K-normalised FD (3.9e-5 there). The history has `cluster_cut` and `ks_share_last`; `modes: 1` has a wrong gradient at a repeated factor (a fact in `topopt check`).
  **Limits of the flag `cluster_cut`.** It is true when the row holds `k + 1` finite factors and the gap between factor `k` and factor `k + 1` is below `NEAR_REPEATED_REL` (1e-2).
  It does not see: a partner of mode `k` that ARPACK did not return (a Lanczos method can miss a member of a repeated factor; not observed, on the square column ARPACK found both
  members of each pair at every `k` from 1 to 6), a mode `k + 1` that is not finite or a mode `k` with `mu` at or below 0, and a cluster whose gap is just above the level (such a gap still gives some error).
