  The option is to raise `buckling.modes`.
- `low_density_energy_share` is about 1 in the first passes of every run (all design voxels start gray). Read it for the final design.
  A lowest mode in voxels below the density 0.5 can be a false mode (section 33, "Where the lowest mode lives"): a share of 0.5 or more is a fact at the end of the run.
- The row value `F / lambda` has no upper bound: a near-mechanism gave `lambda` 1.2e-4. MMA wants rows of order 1; the pipeline has the same form.
- A load case with no compression has no buckling load. The row then holds no material for that case. A tension column still has small positive `mu` from the stress state of the model,
  and the row can need many solves or not converge; this is a status of the pass, not an error. Measured (`tension_loop.py` of the A6b review: a 3 x 3 x 30 column, 1500 N in tension, F 1, 12 passes,
  one beta, 4 threads, Linux x86_64): every evaluation gave `not_converged` (1298 to 1380 solves, 2.0 to 2.2 s each). Without the back-off 13 of 13 passes evaluated, 27.2 s for the run
  (load average 12.3 at the start; 0.21 s without the row); with it 5 of 13 (passes 0, 1, 6, 11, 12), 10.8 s (load average 16.7). The verdict does not judge the row (`feasible` false).
  The same column with a lateral 75 N converges and the skip rule works (5 of 13 passes evaluated, 2.3 s).
- A stress row together with a buckling row can need more passes than each row alone. Measured on a column with a lateral load, step acceptance on: at 60 passes the stress row ended
  at g +0.26 (the buckling row met); at 120 passes at g +0.0128 and falling, with +24 percent compliance and 82 s against 14 s. The tool does not change prices or passes: the user decides.
- A step-acceptance trial does not run the row: a trial design can have a lower factor than the row holds. The row meets its target at the passes that ran it.
- The numbers above are from one Linux host. Apple silicon has no measurement of the row.

## 40. Bore checks: Goodman and press fit (added with B4)

`topopt verify` can check the bores of a part: the stress of each load case at the wall of the bore, and the Goodman fatigue factor with the mean stress of a press fit.
Both checks are general. The YAML names the bores, the strengths and their sources. The code holds no material, no heat treatment, no interference and no cup.
They give facts, not verdicts: there is no pass or fail, no limit and no exit code.
The code is `topopt/verify/bore.py` (facets and statistics), `topopt/verify/fatigue.py` (the Goodman function and the record), `topopt/verify/pressfit.py` and the block in `topopt/config.py`.
Built in B4a: the YAML block (all keys), the bore facts and the Goodman check. Built in B4b: the press-fit check (40.5); it gives the mean stress `sm` of the Goodman rows.

### 40.1 Switch

The optional top-level YAML block `bore_checks` turns the checks on. `Config.bore_checks` is None when the block is absent, and then the output of every command is the same as before this section.
`verify_run(..., bore_checks=None)`: None follows the YAML (on when the block is there); False is off; True is on and needs the block, else the error E13. The CLI flags are
`--bore-checks` and `--no-bore-checks` (section 16). The MCP tool has no argument for them; the card `verify_run` names the keys. The block is read by `load_config`, so `topopt check`, `topopt run` and `topopt verify`
stop early on a wrong block (40.2). `run.json` does not hold the block.

### 40.2 The YAML block

```yaml
bore_checks:                        # absent: the checks are off
  radius_tolerance_mm: 0.35         # optional facet knobs; each has a default (below) and takes an optional <key>_source
  end_margin_mm: 0.35
  normal_limit: 0.35
  sample_band_mm: 1.2
  bores:                            # required, one entry or more
    - name: upper                   # unique
      point: [390.0, 0.0, 617.0]    # mm; the centre of the first end face of the contact range
      axis: [0.3007, 0.0, -0.9537]  # from `point` along the bore (made a unit vector)
      radius_mm: 21.9875            # the finished radius
      length_mm: 8.5                # the contact range goes from `point` along `axis` for this length
      diametral_interference_mm: 0.10          # with press_fit only (E10)
      diametral_interference_mm_source: "..."
    - name: lower
      interface: lower_bore         # shorthand: point, axis, radius_mm, length_mm of this `bore` entry of `interfaces` (section 23)
      diametral_interference_mm: 0.05          # with press_fit only (E10); the shorthand does not change this rule
      diametral_interference_mm_source: "..."
  goodman:
    materials:                      # one entry or more; the label is free text
      H1025: {su_mpa: 1100, sy_mpa: 1000, se_mpa: 350, source: "..."}
  press_fit:                        # the cup variants (40.5)
    cups:
      - {name: rigid, k_mpa_per_mm: 1.0e6, k_mpa_per_mm_source: "..."}
      - {name: cup_al, e_mpa: 70000, nu: 0.33, wall_mm: 2.0, source: "..."}
```

- `bores[].mean_stress_mpa` (MPa, optional, with `_source`) is the mean stress `sm` of the Goodman rows of that bore when there is no `press_fit` block (E11 forbids it with one).
  Without it `sm` is 0.
- A block needs `goodman` or `press_fit` or both (E2). The names of bores, materials and cups are free text. They appear in the report and in the ids of the rows.
  Bores and cups are lists, and a repeated name is an error. The materials are a YAML mapping, so a repeated material label is not seen: YAML keeps the last entry and drops the first with no message
  (as for any repeated key of the problem YAML). Use one label for each material.
- `interface: <name>` takes `point`, `axis`, `radius_mm` and `length_mm` from the entry `<name>` of `interfaces` (it needs `kind: bore`); the four geometry keys are then not allowed.
  The C2 `length_mm` is the cut length of the bore. The shorthand takes it as the contact length, and the report says so. The record says `geometry_from: interface:<name>`; a bore with its own keys says `yaml`.
  `stock_mm` has no effect: `topopt verify` meshes the finished part (`nominal.stl` when the run has stock).
- **Knobs and defaults.** The four knobs are optional. They are not physical data, so their source is optional too. The defaults are the module constants of `topopt/config.py`, with the pipeline
  line in the comment: `DEFAULT_RADIUS_TOLERANCE_MM` 0.35 and `DEFAULT_END_MARGIN_MM` 0.35 (the one `TOL` of `s9_print/final/pressfit.py:45`, used at `:50`), `DEFAULT_NORMAL_LIMIT` 0.35 (`:50`),
  `DEFAULT_SAMPLE_BAND_MM` 1.2 (`:127`). Ranges: `radius_tolerance_mm` and `sample_band_mm` above 0; `end_margin_mm` 0 or more; `normal_limit` above 0 and at most 1. The report gives the value used and its origin (`yaml` or `default`).
- **Sources (decision D7).** A physical number needs its source: `su_mpa`, `sy_mpa`, `se_mpa`, `k_mpa_per_mm`, `e_mpa`, `nu`, `wall_mm`, `diametral_interference_mm`, `mean_stress_mpa`. The source is the text of
  `<key>_source`; a `source` key in the same entry covers the numbers of the entry that have no own source of that kind. A source of a number that the entry does not have is an error (E12).
  The tool does not check the content of a source. The report copies each source next to its value.
- `se_mpa` is the endurance limit as the user gives it: fully corrected. The tool applies no factor and has no preset.
- Cup: `k_mpa_per_mm` (the spring stiffness for each unit of area, above 0), or all three of `e_mpa` (above 0), `nu` (0 up to, not including, 0.5) and `wall_mm` (above 0, at most the bore radius).
  YAML 1.1 reads `1e6` as text; the loader reads a text that `float()` accepts as a number, as for the other blocks.

Errors (`UserError` from `load_config`; the text ends with `(file: <path>)`, names the key path, gives the facts and the options):
Every text of this block has an option: a missing key ("add the key 'bores'"), an unknown key (the known keys, and "remove the key"), a wrong type or range (the range in words), a wrong name or source ("give a non-empty text"),
and each text of the table below. The options of the key, type, range, name and source texts end with `see CONTRACTS.md section 40.2`. The other YAML blocks keep the texts they had (the block calls the shared checks and adds its option).

| # | Condition |
|---|---|
| E1 | The block is not a mapping, or has an unknown key. |
| E2 | The block has neither `goodman` nor `press_fit`. |
| E3 | `bores` is missing, empty, or two bores have one name. |
| E4 | A bore has neither `interface` nor the four geometry keys, or has both. |
| E5 | `interface` names no entry, or an entry that is not a `bore`. |
| E6 | A geometry number or a knob is out of range, or the knobs leave no contact range (`length_mm` not above 2 `end_margin_mm`). |
| E7 | A physical number has no source. |
| E8 | A material has not all three of `su_mpa`, `sy_mpa`, `se_mpa`. |
| E9 | A cup has both forms, neither form, or a part of the `e_mpa`/`nu`/`wall_mm` form; or `wall_mm` is above the bore radius. |
| E10 | `press_fit` is present and a bore has no `diametral_interference_mm`; or the key is given and `press_fit` is absent. |
| E11 | `mean_stress_mpa` is given and `press_fit` is present. |
| E12 | A `_source` key names a number that the entry does not have. |
| E13 | `--bore-checks` (or `bore_checks=True`) and the YAML has no block. Raised in `preflight`, as a `UserError` with the YAML path. |

Not errors, because the input is valid: no facet for a bore, an empty sample set, a negative mean stress, no `n`, a variant with no press-fit result. They are facts with options in the records.

### 40.3 The bore: facets, sample set, statistics (`bore.py`)

For a bore with point c, unit axis a, radius R and length ell: `s = a . (x - c)`, `r` = the distance from the axis. A boundary facet of the tet mesh is a **wall facet** when all four tests hold.
(1) All three vertices have `|r - R| <= radius_tolerance_mm`. (2) The centroid has `end_margin_mm <= s <= ell - end_margin_mm`. (3) The unit normal has `|n . a| < normal_limit` and the area is above 0.
(4) The outward normal (away from the fourth vertex of the tet that owns the facet) points toward the axis at the centroid. Test 4 has no constant: a boss or a shaft of the same radius is not taken.

The **sample set** of a bore is the set of the 14 quadrature points (order `STRESS_ORDER`) of the tets that own the wall facets (one tet layer) with `|r - R| < sample_band_mm`. The weight is the quadrature weight times the tet
volume. Statistics of the von Mises stress and of the hoop stress `e_t . sigma . e_t` (`e_t = a x e_r`): `p99_9` by volume (`BORE_PERCENTILE = 99.9`, the step rule of `stats.py`), `max`, `median`, `min`, and `n_qp`
(names as in `pressfit.json`: `vm_p99_9_MPa`, `hoop_max_MPa`, ...). The stress is not smoothed: it is the P2 stress at the points, and it scatters from point to point;
the p99.9 and the max take the top of that scatter, and the median does not (the measured size is in 40.7).

`bore_facts` has one entry for each bore: `name`, `status` (`ok` or `empty`), `geometry_from`, `funnel` (`boundary`, `radius`, `axial`, `normal`, `side`: the count of the facets that pass the tests in order), `facets`, `area_mm2`,
`analytic_area_mm2` (`2 pi R (ell - 2 end_margin_mm)`), `analytic_area_full_mm2`, `area_over_analytic`, `vertex_radius_mm`, `largest_vertex_deviation_mm`, `vertex_s_range_mm`, `mean_facet_edge_mm`, `largest_angular_gap_deg`,
`largest_facet_width_deg`, `closes_cylinder`, `near_miss` (`facets`, `area_mm2`, `deviation_mm`: the facets that pass tests 2 to 4, lie within `sample_band_mm` of R and fail test 1), `sample_set` (`tets`, `points`, `volume_mm3`, `band_mm`),
`facts`, `options`. A bore with no wall facet or no sample point is dropped with the funnel as a fact, and the other bores go on.
A bore that raises an exception, in the build of its facets and sample set or in the statistics of a load case, is dropped in the same way: its entry has `name`, `status: error`, `geometry_from`, `stage` (`build` or `stats`),
`message` (the error type and its text), `facts` (they name the bore, the error type and the text) and `options`, and none of the funnel keys. The Goodman record has no row for it, `missing_rows` names it with the reason `error`
(a bore that fails at the statistics has no value for the earlier cases either), and the text has the line `bore <name> (<geometry_from>): stopped at the <stage>: <message>`. The note "the facets do not close a cylinder" prints when the largest gap between neighbouring facet centroids
is larger than the largest angular width of one facet (no constant).
The set depends on the mesh and on the knobs: on the two-joint part (2.5 mm tets) a radius tolerance of 0.2 mm removes the first facet row at the bore mouth (21 % of the area). The report gives the numbers that show why a value moves, and does not decide for the user.

### 40.4 Goodman (`fatigue.py`)

For a material (Su, Sy, Se), a bore, a statistic (`p99_9` or `max`) and a load case:
`n = 1.0 / (sa / Se + sm / Su)` when the denominator is above 0, else null; yield ratio `(abs(sm) + sa) / Sy`. The order of the operations is that of the pipeline check (`goodman.py:17`), so a row of the pipeline is reproduced bit for bit.
`sa` is the von Mises statistic of the load case at the sample set of the bore (each case is solved alone, with no cup spring, and is taken fully reversed about `sm`).
`sm` is the hoop statistic of the press fit of the same variant, bore and statistic (40.5), or the `mean_stress_mpa` of the bore (`yaml_mean`), or 0 (`zero_mean`, only when the YAML has neither `press_fit` nor `mean_stress_mpa`).
The worst case of a row has the smallest `n` among the cases whose `n` is not null (the first wins a tie). If every case has `n = null`: `n_goodman` is null, the worst case has the largest yield ratio, and a fact says so.
The rows go in the order: material, variant, bore, statistic (the YAML order). The row id is `<material>/<variant>/<bore>/<statistic>`.
The function `fatigue.goodman_row` is pure (no numpy, no extra, no name of a part); the level-2b converter of the acceptance case calls the same function.

Record `goodman`: `kind`, `status` (`done`, `skipped` with the reason `no_bore`, or `error`), `reason`, `rule`, `statistics`, `mean_stress` (`from`, `note`), `materials` (the strengths with their sources), `service_stress`
(`{case: {bore: statistics}}`), `rows` (`id`, `material`, `variant`, `bore`, `statistic`, `worst_case`, `sa_MPa`, `sm_MPa`, `n_goodman`, `peak_over_yield`, `all_n_none`, `cases`; a row with `sm` below 0 also has `n_goodman_at_sm0` and `worst_case_at_sm0`, see 40.7), `missing_rows`
(`variant`, `bore`, `reason`, `options`: a bore or a variant that has no row), `lowest_n`, `facts`, `options`, `seconds`. The rule string, the mix of a von Mises `sa` and a hoop `sm` (the method of the pipeline check, not a signed equivalent stress),
the strengths of the YAML and the cases solved alone are facts in the record. One more fact says that `n` uses the p99.9 or the max of the sample set, that these two statistics carry the point scatter of the
stress that is not smoothed, and that the scatter depends on the mesh realization (40.7). `n` below 1 in a row is a fact that lists the ids: 1 is the Goodman line, not a limit of topopt. A compressive `sm` is applied as it is, with a fact, and the row also gives the `n` for `sm = 0` (40.7).
An exception of the check gives `status: error` with the message, and `topopt verify` goes on. The same holds for one bore: an exception in its build or its statistics drops that bore (40.3), and the other bores and the rest of the report go on. With the `--percentile` of the command not 99.9, the base key `bore_checks` has `percentile_note`: the bore statistics stay p99.9 and max.

### 40.5 Press fit (`pressfit.py`)

The cup of a bore is a **linear two-sided Winkler spring** on the wall facets of the bore (40.3). The contact pressure is `p = k (d_r - u_r)`: `k` is the spring stiffness (MPa/mm for each unit of area),
`d_r` the radial interference (half of `diametral_interference_mm`: the key says its kind, and the half is a conversion), `u_r` the radial displacement of the wall. The spring acts along the **radial unit vector from the axis**
at each facet quadrature point (not along the facet normal), and it can pull as well as push: `p` is below 0 where the wall lifts off the cup. There is no contact iteration.

Assembly (scikit-fem, imported inside the functions): `FacetBasis(mesh, ElementVector(ElementTetP2()), facets=<wall facets>, intorder=FACET_QUAD_ORDER)`, with `FACET_QUAD_ORDER = 4` (a module constant of `topopt/verify/pressfit.py`: the facet quadrature of the
topology pipeline, its `pressfit.py:63`; the facet rule of the pipeline, not an exact rule: the radial unit vector is not a polynomial). `Ks = sum over the bores of int k (u . n)(v . n) dA` and `f = sum over the bores of int k d_r (v . n) dA`. The dof numbering of
`P2Model` is that of `ElementVector(ElementTetP2())`, and the pattern of `Ks` is inside the pattern of `K`. One linear solve for each cup variant: `(K + Ks) u = f` on the free dofs of the static solve, with the supports of the static
solve (the clamped fixed regions), the factor of `make_factor` and `RefinedFactor(steps=REFINE_STEPS)`. The load cases are solved with no cup spring, so the Goodman `sa` (the case) and `sm` (the press fit) come from two solves.

**The cup.** A cup is `k_mpa_per_mm` (the same `k` for every bore), or `e_mpa`, `nu` and `wall_mm`: then `k = 1 / c` with `c = R / E ((R^2 + ri^2) / (R^2 - ri^2) - nu)`, `ri = R - wall_mm` and `R` the radius of the bore. It is the
radial compliance at the outer radius of a thick cylinder with a free inner surface under an outer pressure (plane stress), and the expression of `pressfit.py:55-58` of the pipeline (`cup_k`: the same bits).
`wall_mm = R` is a solid disc. There is no rigid mode and no built-in large `k`; a rigid cup is a `k` that the YAML gives with its source.

**Statistics at the bore.** For each variant and bore: `vm_*` and `hoop_*` (`p99_9`, `max`, `median`, `min`) at the sample set of the bore (40.3), and `n_qp`. The hoop p99.9 and max of a variant at a bore are `sm` of the Goodman rows of
that variant and bore (`fatigue.build_record(..., hoop=...)`). A part with a `press_fit` block never has a row with `sm = 0`: a skipped or failed stage gives `missing_rows` with its reason and options.

**Contact pressure, two forms.** `area_mean` is `int p dA / A` on the facet basis of the assembly: the radial spring force over the area, the primary value, reliable for every `k`. `mean`, `max`, `min` (with `nodes`,
`negative_nodes`, `mean_radial_displacement_mm`) are `p` at the vertex nodes of the wall facets, the numbers of the pipeline. The vertex values of a stiff spring are differences of near-equal numbers and are not a stress measure:
on thick steel rings with `k = 1e6` MPa/mm the vertex mean was 4.5 % to 20 % above the Lame closed form and the vertex max 45 % above it, and on the one measured part the vertex mean was 2.9 times the area mean. The area mean was within
0.4 % of the closed form on every ring mesh for every `k`. The hoop p99.9, the statistic that feeds `sm`, was +0.5 % to +2.7 % above the closed form on eight ring meshes (+1.2 % to +1.5 % on the two meshes of the tests) and
+5 % to +7 % on a ninth, where the top points were at the bore mouths (40.7): it is a point statistic of the P2 stress at the surface and it moves with the mesh. No threshold decides "very stiff": the text is in the record of every run.

**Forces.** `net_spring_force_N` is the force of the spring on the part, `int p n dA` over the wall facets: the sum over the bores is minus the reaction of the clamps (`solve.clamp_reaction_N`; a test checks it on a half ring).
`load_vector_net_N` is the net of the load vector `k d_r n` (the `net_force_N` of the pipeline); for a large `k` it is not a force on the part (the research run had load-vector nets of (-196, 487, -62) kN and (532, 140, 168) kN against a clamp reaction of (10.5, 0.0, 3.3) kN).

Record `pressfit`: `kind`, `status` (`done`, `skipped` with the reason `memory` or `no_bore`, or `error`), `reason`, `rule`, `statistics`, `cups`, `model` (`text`, `facet_quadrature_order`, `solver`, `refinement_steps`), `memory`,
`variants`, `dropped_bores`, `facts`, `options`, `seconds`, and `combined` when the stage has the stress of the cases. A variant has `name`, `k_form` (`k` or `lame`), `sources` (the source texts of the cup), `e_mpa`, `nu`, `wall_mm` (the Lame form),
`bores` (`name`, `k_mpa_per_mm`, `diametral_interference_mm`, `radial_interference_mm`, `facets`, `area_mm2`, `net_spring_force_N`, `load_vector_net_N`, `contact_pressure_MPa`, the statistics above, `n_qp`) and `solve`
(`relative_residual`, `backward_error`, `refinement_steps`, `assemble_seconds`, `factor_seconds`, `solve_seconds`, `seconds`, `max_displacement_mm`, `clamp_reaction_N`). A bore with no wall facet or no sample point is not in the stage
(`dropped_bores`; the fact names each bore with its reason, `no_facets`, `no_sample_set` or `error`, and the funnel is in `bore_facts`), and if no bore is left the record is `skipped` with the reason `no_bore`. An exception of the stage gives `status: error` with the message, and `topopt verify` goes on.
`combined` is `{variant: {bore: {case: {vm_p99_9_MPa, vm_max_MPa, hoop_p99_9_MPa, hoop_max_MPa}}}}`: the stress of a load case plus the stress of the press fit at the sample points (linear superposition, as the pipeline check does).
The cup spring does not act in the solve of the case, so the sum is not a solve of the assembled problem; the record says so. It is a fact, not an input of the Goodman check.

**One factor at a time, and memory.** `run_level` frees the factor of the static solve (`fac.free()`) and drops `rf` and `Kff` before the stage; the stage frees the factor of each variant before the next. A test counts the live
factors with a spy on `make_factor`. The memory rule of section 16 is for one factor, so the stage adds only the arrays it holds on top of it. Before meshing, each entry of `estimates_before_meshing` has the key `pressfit`
(`variants`, `factorizations`, `estimate_bytes` equal to the estimate of the entry, `estimated_seconds` = variants x (`memory.factor_seconds` + one solve and stress at `memory.TIME_CASE_PER_1E5_S`; None where the fit has no value,
for example `cholesky`), `note`). After meshing and before the first press-fit factor, `memory.extra_bytes` is the `nbytes` of the spring matrix of the largest variant (data, indices, indptr), its load vector, the arrays of the springs,
the stress of each load case at the sample points, and the stress array of one variant at the quadrature points of every tet (`stress_array_bytes`), counted from the real arrays and shapes (no model and no constant). The decision is `estimate_after_meshing_bytes + extra_bytes` against the limit of the run (the smaller of the available RAM
and `--max-gb`): above it, and without `--force`, the stage is skipped (`status: skipped`, `reason: memory`) with the numbers and the options (`--max-gb`, `--force`, a larger `--mesh-size`, a factor with a smaller footprint, the check off),
and the Goodman check has no row for a variant. The record has `peak_rss_before_stage_bytes` and `peak_rss_after_stage_bytes` (the running peak of the process).

### 40.6 Keys, text and levels

With the checks on, `verify.json` has (the file has none of them with the checks off, `format` stays 1, and a reader ignores unknown keys):
`bore_checks` (`on`, `source`: `bore_checks in the YAML of the run` or `the flag --bore-checks`, `checks`, `statistics`, `knobs` with `value`, `origin`, `source` or `default_source`, `bores` with the resolved geometry and the sources,
`percentile_note`), `bore_facts` (40.3), `goodman` (40.4) and, with a `press_fit` block, `pressfit`. `timing_s` has `bore_s`, `goodman_s` and `pressfit_s` (each when its work ran). The result does not change any other number: the stress of each case is computed once and
the bore statistics read it before it is freed. The text of `topopt verify` has `bore checks:` lines (with the knobs and their origin), a line for each bore (wall facets, the area over the analytic area, the sample points) with one line under it for each
load case (the von Mises p99.9, max and median of the sample set of that bore; the median is `service_stress[case][bore].vm_median_MPa`),
a line for each Goodman row (worst case, `sa`, `sm`, `n`, yield ratio), a line for each press-fit variant and bore (`k`, hoop p99.9, max and median, the contact pressure, the net spring force), and the `fact:` and `option:` lines. `--estimate-only` and the head of a run print the `pressfit` estimate of each size. With several levels (`--levels`), the checks run on every level; each row of the `levels` block has `goodman_n`
(`{row id: n_goodman}`), and with a press-fit result `pressfit_hoop_p99_9_MPa` (`{"<variant>/<bore>": value}`); the relative changes have both too.

### 40.7 Documented limits

`sa` is a von Mises value and `sm` is a normal stress; the mix is the method of the pipeline check. The load cases are solved alone and taken fully reversed. The statistics are p99.9 and max of the sample set only. The facets and the
sample set depend on the mesh and on the knobs (40.3). `topopt verify` keeps its refusal of pressures, moments and remote forces (section 16), so the `sa` of a case with such a load is a model gap, not a number of the part. Springs and joints are modelled since K1-A. The press-fit stage runs with springs and is skipped with a joint (section 16).
The interference is a number of the YAML with its source; the diametral reading is the default of the pipeline session. The cup is a linear spring with no contact iteration, so `p` can be below 0; the vertex values of its pressure are not a stress measure for a stiff spring (40.5). The hoop stress at the surface is not smoothed, so its p99.9 depends on the mesh (a ring of the research meshed with two builders at 2 mm: +1.4 % and +5 % to +7 % above the closed form; the median was 1.6 % to 1.8 % below it on both). The cause of the +5 % to +7 % is the P2 surface error at the bore mouths (the edge between the bore wall and the end face), not the supports: all the top 0.1 % points of that ring are at z below 1.25 mm or above 29.4 mm (the bore is 30 mm long), and the points with 2 mm < z < 28 mm give +1.4 % to +1.5 %, as on the other ring; three sets of supports move the p99.9 by about 1 point.

**Levels.** The ids of `goodman_n` in the `levels` block are the row ids of the last level (the finest). A row that exists at an earlier level only (for example a bore that is dropped at the finest mesh) is not in
`goodman_n`; the `goodman` record of its own level has it. A row that exists at the last level and not at an earlier one is there with a null value and a null change.

**A negative `sm`.** The Goodman line of the rule is applied as it is for `sm` below 0, so `n` is larger than `Se / sa`: the usual rule for a compressive mean stress is a flat line (`n = Se / sa`). A row with `sm` below 0
therefore has two more fields, so that no second run is needed: `n_goodman_at_sm0` (the `n` of the same rule for `sm = 0`, which is `Se / sa` of the worst case at `sm = 0`; null when `sa` is 0 in every case) and
`worst_case_at_sm0` (the case with the smallest `n` at `sm = 0`, the largest `sa`). A row with `sm` of 0 or above has neither field. Example (the numbers of the review): `sa` 150, `sm` -400, `Se` 350, `Su` 1100 gives `n` 15.4 and
`n_goodman_at_sm0` 2.33; `sa` 100 and `sm` -100 gives 5.13 and 3.5. The text line of the row shows `(n at sm = 0: ...)`, and the record has a fact that names the fields. Only a negative `mean_stress_mpa` in the YAML reaches this;
the `sm` of the pipeline data is 0 or above (its smallest stored value is 47.67 MPa).

**The scatter of the bore statistics (measured).** The p99.9 and the max of the sample set carry the point scatter of the P2 stress. The scatter depends on the mesh realization, not only on the mesh size: a mesh of 2 mm
gave +18 % on a ring of 60 mm and +3 % on a ring of 120 mm. It is not a defect of the bore sampling: the hoop stress of an injected uniform field equals the tensor product to 2.3e-13 MPa, and the von Mises p95 of the whole ring volume of the same runs shows the same
scatter (+2.3 %, +19.8 % and +7.5 % at 3.0, 2.0 and 1.5 mm).
It is not an effect of the ends only: it is in every 10 mm slice of the ring. The measurement is on a thin steel ring (inner radius 21.9875 mm, outer radius 25.25 mm, one load case: an axial force F). Away from the ends the
stress is the closed form `F / (pi (b^2 - a^2))` = 2.0654 MPa. The bore is the middle third of the ring. The columns are the difference of the statistic of the von Mises sample set from the closed form (band 1.2 mm):

| Ring length, mesh size | tets | median | p99.9 | max | min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 mm, 3.0 mm | 6,321 | +0.39 % | +4.78 % | +5.80 % | -2.94 % |
| 60 mm, 2.0 mm | 14,617 | +1.43 % | +18.23 % | +18.80 % | -18.03 % |
| 60 mm, 1.5 mm | 33,020 | -0.01 % | +8.32 % | +8.83 % | -5.61 % |
| 120 mm, 2.0 mm | 27,608 | -0.29 % | +3.02 % | +3.31 % | -2.47 % |

- At 2.0 mm on the ring of 60 mm, the slices of 10 mm at z 10 to 20, 20 to 30, 30 to 40 and 40 to 50 mm give the median +3.9, +1.9, +0.7 and -1.9 %, the p99.9 +18.1, +16.1, +18.3 and +20.6 %, and the min -14.7, -14.4, -18.0 and -25.0 %.
  The scatter is symmetric (min -18 %, max +19 % in the middle bore). The two end slices (clamp and load slab) are not a test of the closed form: the median is -15.5 % and -9.0 %, the p99.9 +11.0 % and +91.6 %.
- A sample band of 0.5 mm in place of 1.2 mm gives the same picture (p99.9 +5.0 %, +16.4 % and +8.5 % at 3.0, 2.0 and 1.5 mm).
- At sm = 0 a Goodman `n` is `Se / sa`, so +18 % on `sa` gives an `n` that is 15 % low. The p99.9 and the max take the top of the scatter, so the error is one-sided (a low `n`), and its size depends on the mesh.
  On the two-joint part the size is not known: the context rows of level 2b cannot separate it from the difference of the models.
- The median moves little with this scatter (within 1.5 % of the closed form at the three sizes of the ring of 60 mm), and the text lines give it next to the p99.9 and the max. The option "a smaller mesh size" is not a sure cure:
  the mesh of 2 mm is worse than the mesh of 3 mm. The first option of the record is `--levels`, which shows how `n` changes between meshes.

## 41. Levers: cards for YAML keys and engine tools (added with P7)

A user says "too heavy" or "extra film here". The agent needs to know which key or tool changes it, what a try costs, and who decides the change. Each YAML key and each engine tool has one **lever card**.
The cards are guidance for agents. They give facts, estimates and options. No tool refuses a change because of a card, and no card adds a limit, a tolerance or a wait to the product.
The code is `topopt/levers_cards.py` (the table: data only, no logic in a row), `topopt/levers.py` (the text and the lookup) and the key lists of `topopt/config.py` (41.6).

### 41.1 The card

`Card` (a frozen dataclass of `topopt/levers_cards.py`) has these fields.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `key` | A key path of the YAML (`settings.penal`, `load_cases[].forces[].force`; `[]` is one entry of a list; `<label>` is a free name), or an engine tool: the name of the MCP tool or of the CLI subcommand (`verify_run`, `buckling`, `refine`), or `<tool>:<argument>` (`run_topopt:resume`). |
| `group` | `yaml` or `tool`. A key may appear once in each group (`buckling` is the YAML block and the CLI command). |
| `kind` | `requirement`, `method` or `both` (41.2). |
| `kind_note` | For `both` only: when the key is which. A card of another kind has none. |
| `layer` | 1 to 4, the cost of one try (41.3). |
| `effect` | One sentence: what the lever does. |
| `values` | Type, unit, default, range or typical values, interactions. |
| `cost`, `call` | The cost and the call, when they are not the text of the layer. A card of layer 3 has both. |
| `symptoms` | `Symptom(words, detect, facts, when)`: the words that a user says (comma-separated) and the fact in the result that detects the symptom (41.7). Where no fact exists, `detect` says "no fact yet" or names the error text, and `facts` is empty. `when` is an optional text: which value of the facts makes the symptom true (a flag that is set, a list that is not empty, a value that is not null). It names the key of a fact and needs `facts`; the reference prints it as "Present when: ...". A symptom with no `when` is read from `detect` alone. |
| `evidence` | `Evidence(change, effect, price, part_class, runs)`: measured rows. A row is a fact about its part class only (`PART_CLASSES`). |
| `confidence` | `measured` (at least one evidence row with run ids and a part class), `code` (from the code or from this file only; nobody measured the effect on a part) or `untested`. A card that is not `measured` has no evidence row. |
| `also` | More key paths that the same card covers because they have the same effect (the `<number>_source` keys of a block; `buckling.max_gb` with `buckling.max_seconds`). |
| `price_note` | Empty or one text: how to read the price of the evidence rows of this card (41.9). Only a `measured` card has one. |

A number in a card is one of three kinds: a row of the phone stand series, of the E1 series on the hook (run ids `E1/<id>`), of the E2 series (54 runs, run ids `E2/<id>`, and the tool calls `E2/T-...`), of the E3 series on the bracket and the ladle: 62 runs, run ids `E3/<id>`) or a run of the PR that made the table (a measured row, with run ids), a fact that this file or the code records (the card names the section), or nothing.
The part classes (`PART_CLASSES`) are `phone stand`, `hook` (`examples/hook/hook_short.yaml`: voxel 2.0 mm, 40 passes, CPU), `hook fine` (`examples/hook/hook.yaml`: voxel 1.2 mm, 80 passes), `hook_stress` (E2, `examples/hook/hook_stress.yaml`: voxel 2.4 mm, 220 passes, `objective: mass`; its base is the mean of 6 runs that do not repeat), `hook_buckling-2mm` (E2, a coarse copy of `hook_buckling.yaml`: voxel 2 mm, 40 passes), `bracket` (E3, `examples/interfaces/bracket.yaml`: voxel 1.0 mm, 40 passes; its base BR-B0 is a grey design that ends at beta 2), `bracket-fitted` (E3, the same file with the beta schedule scaled to the 40 passes), `ladle-4mm` (E3, a coarse copy of `examples/ladle/ladle.yaml` at 4.0 mm, because the run at 3.25 mm took 401 s), `ladle` (E3, the example grid of 3.25 mm; filter rows only), `bracket example`, `larger part` (a part that this repository does not ship) and `not printed (CONTRACTS)` (round 3: the numbers of section 9.1 that P4b-2, P4b-3 and P4b-6 recorded, on the hook example with `regions.not_printed` or the bar of `tests/test_part_only.py`; P7 read them and did not run them again); each is a fact about that part only.
A field that no source fills says "not measured" or "no fact yet". The table held 147 cards at the first version: 130 for YAML keys (they cover the 214 key paths that the loader accepted) and 17 for engine tools. After round 3 (the keys that main added) it holds 151 cards: 131 for YAML keys (215 key paths) and 20 for engine tools (`run_topopt:continue_from`, `run_topopt:more_iterations`, `verify_run:part_only` are new). After the E2 evidence (P7-5) it still holds 151 cards; 30 cards changed, 13 turned from `code` to `measured`, and the table has 65 `measured` and 86 `code` cards (52 and 99 before). `limits.displacement` is a list card that stays `code` and points to `limits.displacement[].limit_mm`, which holds the E2 rows. After the E3 evidence (P7-6) it still holds 151 cards, 65 `measured` and 86 `code`: 12 cards changed, 9 of them hold E3 rows (8 keys and `check_problem`; all were `measured` by the E1 rows already, so none turned), and `settings.stop_rules.grayness_max` stays `code` (its symptom text cites E3/LAD-IT40; it has no row). With #90 (main d48371f: `interfaces[].full_surface`, a `code` card) it holds 152 cards: 132 for YAML keys (216 key paths) and 20 for engine tools, 65 `measured` and 87 `code`; `export_step` (#103) is in the list of tools that change no design. With I7 (`settings.target_mass_g`, kind `requirement`, confidence `code`) it holds 153 cards: 133 for YAML keys (217 key paths) and 20 for engine tools, 65 `measured` and 88 `code`. With PM-1 (`print.printer_model`, kind `requirement`, confidence `code`) it holds 154 cards: 134 for YAML keys (218 key paths) and 20 for engine tools, 65 `measured` and 89 `code`; `find_printer` and `save_printer` are in the list of tools that only report. With K1-B it holds 156 cards: 134 for YAML keys (218 key paths) and 22 for engine tools (`verify_run:gate` is a `method` card and `verify_run:allowable_mpa` a `requirement` card, both `code`), 65 `measured` and 91 `code`. With PM-2 (`material.filament`, kind `requirement`, confidence `code`) it holds 162 cards: 135 for YAML keys (219 key paths) and 27 for engine tools, 68 `measured` and 94 `code` (the five cards `run_topopt:fine_from`, `fine_pass`, `fine_voxel`, `fine_passes` and `fine_tol` of the fine pass, section 24.6, are in the 27); `find_material` and `printer_materials` are in the list of tools that only report, and `save_material` is in the list of tools that only write the work folder (like `save_printer`). With the YAML key `settings.fine_pass` (a `code` card) and `settings.fine_pass.objective_change` (a `measured` card), both kind `method`, it holds 164 cards: 137 for YAML keys (221 key paths) and 27 for engine tools, 69 `measured` and 95 `code`. With F4-55 (`settings.envelope_fill`, `auto | on | off`, kind `method`, confidence `code`) it holds 165 cards: 138 for YAML keys (222 key paths) and 27 for engine tools, 69 `measured` and 96 `code`.

### 41.2 Kinds and the rule for agents

- `method`: a setting of the method (penal, beta schedule, move limit, solver and tolerances, voxel size, iterations, robust, mesh method, smoothing). The agent changes it without asking and reports what, why and the price.
- `requirement`: a user requirement (loads, supports, keep-outs, interfaces, material, stress limits and safety factors, a stated mass or volume target, print limits, symmetry). The agent may tighten one without
  asking, with a report and its measured price. It loosens one only with the user's consent, and it brings the facts.
- `both`: a key that can be either (for example `settings.min_member_mm`: a print rule or a look lever; `settings.volume_fraction`: a stated target or a method choice). It follows its origin in the brief record
  (`record_brief`): origin `user` is a requirement; `inferred` and `default` are the agent's (a method setting). The `kind_note` of the card says it.
- The two voxel guards, `settings.max_active_voxels` and `settings.max_grid_voxels`, are `method` cards (the agent decides each guard override, not the user). The agent decides with the facts and reports what, why and the price. The facts: `check_problem.memory_estimate` (`bytes` against `ram_bytes`) and the RAM that `environment` gives. The risk: a run above the RAM can freeze the machine (a 0.5 mm whole-domain grid did on a 16 GB Mac). The card says the facts and the risk and gives no cap. `settings.voxel_size` is `method` too, unless the user stated it (its origin in `record_brief`: then a larger voxel is a loosening of a requirement).
  By kind the table holds 72 `method`, 82 `requirement` and 11 `both` cards (`settings.stress_scale` is `both` since the E2 evidence).

This is guidance. The tools give facts, estimates and options; the agent decides. One check in the code reads the kind: the brief gate ignores a change of `method` keys (section 30, "Method keys"; `both` counts as a requirement there). No tool refuses a change because of the kind. The rule is in the reference text, in Step 6 of the skill `start-here`,
in the description of `run_topopt`, and in the lead design role.

### 41.3 Layers: the cost of one try

| Layer | Meaning | Cost | Call |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A global setting. | A new run: the run time of the problem (`check_problem.derived.time_estimate_s` gives it). | Edit the key, `check_problem`, then `run_topopt` with a new `out_dir`. |
| 2 | Continue or branch a run. | A part of a run. | `run_topopt` with `resume=true` on a stopped run. |
| 3 | The post step only. | Seconds, no new pass. | Edit the key; `run_topopt` with the same `out_dir`, `resume=true` and `allow_changed_inputs=true` (CLI: `topopt run <yaml> --out <run> --resume --allow-changed-inputs`); or the tool that the card names. |
| 4 | A local edit or judgement of the finished part. | Seconds to minutes (and a verify). | The tool that the card names (`apply_marks`, `cleanup_list`, `ratchet_run`, `print_check`, ...). |

Layer 3 was measured on a finished run of `examples/hook/hook_short.yaml` (voxel 2.0 mm, 40 passes, CPU; the base run took 27.0 s) and on the bracket example:
`--resume --allow-changed-inputs` on a finished run runs the post step only (section 24.2: a checkpoint with `complete: true` has no pass left, and the resume only runs the post step again; the run log says "No pass is left to run. The post step runs again."). `history.jsonl`, `checkpoint.npz` and the snapshots stay equal by sha256; the files of the
post step (`result/`, `verdict.json`, the labels) are made again; each resume appends one entry to `metrics.verdict.resume_points`. It took 6.1 to 16.9 s on the hook example (longer with the buckling check).
A key has layer 3 only when the post step reads it: `settings.mesh_method`, `print.build_direction`, `print.printer_type`, `print.bed_mm`, `print.self_supporting_angle_deg`, `regions.not_printed`, `settings.part_only_min_film_mm` (round 3: the post step reads it from `run.json`; no pass does, and a test pins it in `topopt/optimize.py`), `material.density` (the mass numbers),
the three thresholds of `settings.stop_rules` (`objective_change`, `window`, `grayness_max`: the verdict), the check keys of `buckling` (`check`, `modes`, `density`, `max_seconds`, `max_gb`; the card says that `modes`, `max_seconds` and `max_gb`
are layer 3 only when the YAML has no `buckling.min_factor`), `interfaces[].stock_mm`, `load_cases[].allowable_source` (a free text that the report and the ratchet show; the passes do not read it), `name` and `assumptions`.
A key that the passes read (measured: `settings.penal` and `settings.volume_fraction`; the others, such as `settings.move_limit`, by the code) is accepted by the same call, but no pass runs, so the design does not change
(`run.json` records the new value; `settings.penal` also changes the stress display `stress.npz`): layer 1 is the layer of such a key. The resume says so as a fact, with the options (41.8). A changed `regions.keep_out` file moves the labels and the saved density is mapped
onto the new voxels (measured: `labels.bin`, `final.stl` and `stress.npz` are made again); no pass adapts the design to it, so a new run is the layer of that key. The refusal "This version does not make a finished run longer" is the answer to `settings.iterations` on a finished run. The limit keys of `print` are not read by the post step: a
change is judged by `print_check` (layer 4). A change of `interfaces[].stock_mm` or `radius_mm` makes the labels and the meshes again, but the design is not adapted to the new shapes; the card says it.

The cost of one try on the hook (the reference prints it in the layer list; the numbers are those of the E1 series and of the layer 3 runs above): layer 1 is a run of 40 passes at voxel 2 mm, 15 to 37 s wall (median 21 s over 47 runs; the load of the host changes the same run by a factor of about 2), 0.40 s per pass for 7651 free design voxels, 3.09 s per pass at 34220 (`hook.yaml`: 261 s);
layer 2 (round 3, `run_topopt` with `continue_from` and `more_iterations` on the finished base run) is 14.3 to 25.7 s wall for 10 or 20 more passes in 4 runs, against 34.0 s for a new run of the 40 passes in the same hour (host load 29 to 42 on 22 cores): the fixed part of a run (start, build, pass K again, the post step, the refine page) is of the size of the passes, so 10 and 20 passes are not told apart; layer 3 is the post step alone, 4.5 to 5.6 s at 2 mm and 10.5 to 13.8 s at 1.2 mm, or 6.1 to 16.9 s for the resume call; layer 4 is seconds (`print_check` 5.5 s, `cleanup_list` 3.0 s, `topopt verify` 12 s, `topopt verify --no-sensitivity` a median of 4.7 s). E2 (P7-5), on a loaded host (load average 12 to 43 on 22 cores): a stress run (2.4 mm, 220 passes) 45 to 105 s; a run with the buckling row (2 mm, 40 passes) 177 to 235 s, 10.4 to 13.8 times a plain run; `print_check` 3.2 to 3.9 s, `cleanup_list` 3.1 s, `apply_marks` 2.4 to 3.1 s, `compare_runs` 0.12 to 0.67 s, `ratchet_run` 15.5 s (rule `mass`) and 23.3 s (rule `stiffness`) for one candidate, `topopt buckling` 6.8 to 16.6 s at 2 mm and 47.3 s at 1.2 mm.

### 41.4 The reference: the MCP resource and the CLI

One function, `topopt.levers.reference(query=None)`, makes the text (Markdown). It holds the header (the kinds and the rule, the layers, the confidence values, the part classes that the evidence uses), a symptom index (a word of the user and the keys of its cards),
then the cards by block, then the cards of the tools, and the list of the tools that only report (`READ_ONLY_TOOLS`: they have no card because they change and judge nothing).

- MCP resource `topopt://levers` (name `levers`, title "Levers: YAML keys and engine tools", `text/markdown`): `reference()` with no query. The server registers it in `_add_levers_reference()`, as the material reference is registered.
- MCP resource template `topopt://levers/{query}` (name `levers_cards`, `text/markdown`; registered in the same function): `reference(query)`, the cards of one key path, tool name or word, as `topopt levers <query>` prints them. The query is one URI segment: the client encodes a space and the signs `[`, `]`, `<` and `>` (`topopt://levers/load_cases%5B%5D.weight`), and the server decodes them. A query with no match gives the same message as the command (the options), not an error of the transport. `topopt://levers` stays the full text.
- CLI: `topopt levers` prints the same text. `topopt levers <key or word> [<word> ...]` prints the cards that match (`reference(query)`): a word that is exactly a key (or a key in `also`) gives that card; any other word
  matches a key, a key in `also`, a symptom word, a `detect` text or a fact path (not the effect text). No match: exit code 1, and the message names `topopt levers` and the options. Without `--run` the command reads no run and no YAML (`--run` is 41.10).
- Size: about 265,700 characters (227,264 before the E3 evidence of P7-6, which added about 38,400; 171,560 before the E2 evidence of P7-5). A client that wants less reads `topopt://levers/{query}` or calls `topopt levers <word>`.

### 41.5 The test

`tests/test_levers.py` holds the checks. `topopt.levers.problems()` returns the faults of the table itself (a bad field, a repeated key, a bad fact path); the test asserts that it is empty.

- Every key path of `config.accepted_key_paths()` has exactly one card (as `key` or in `also`), and no card names a key that the loader does not accept.
- Every card has a valid `kind`, `layer`, `confidence` and `group`; a `measured` card has an evidence row with run ids and a known part class; a `both` card has a `kind_note`; a layer 3 card has a `call` and a `cost`.
- Every card of a tool names an MCP tool or a CLI subcommand (and, after `:`, an argument of the tool). Every MCP tool and every CLI subcommand has a card or an entry in `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`.
- The reference holds every card once and no habit word (`must`, `never`, `always`). The resource is listed and read (in process and through a stdio client). The CLI prints the reference, finds a card by key and by a symptom word, and exits with 1 for no match.
- The unknown-key error names the known keys and the reference in each of the 27 blocks (41.6).
- The template resource is listed as a template; it gives the cards of a key path (also one with `[]`, in the encoded form `%5B%5D`) and of a word (`%20` for a space), says so for a query with no match, and is listed and read through a stdio client.
- The hook rows have run ids of `E1/`, `P7-1/l3/` or `P7-1/r3/`; a `hook` row is marked `inside the noise` exactly when its three optimizer values are inside the bands of 41.9; the five keys whose optimizer price misleads (`settings.penal`, `settings.min_member_mm`, `settings.filter_radius`, `settings.mesh_method`, `settings.voxel_size`) give the P2 ratio next to the optimizer ratio and a `price_note` that says to read P2; the `penal` rows of the phone stand are labelled as optimizer values; the filter symptoms hold no `thinnest_member` fact; the keep-out finding is on both cards; `iterations` and `beta_schedule` hold the unscaled and the scaled rows; the layer costs and the text of 41.9 are in the reference.
- The E3 rows (P7-6, 41.9): the run ids are `E3/BR-...` or `E3/LAD-...` and the part class is one of `bracket`, `bracket-fitted`, `ladle-4mm`, `ladle`; each row with ratios gives the optimizer ratio and the P2 ratio; a row is marked `inside the noise` exactly when all its values are inside the band of its class; a `bracket` row says that its base is grey; the class texts give the base values and the bands; each of the eight keys has the sentence across parts; the facts of F4-19, F4-25 and F4-22, the blur row of the ladle, the grayness text of the three symptoms and the time rows of `check_problem` and `voxel_size` are pinned; the pair facts of F4-22 are on `settings.iterations` only (a summary and a pointer on `beta_schedule` and `stop_rules.objective_change`), and `beta_schedule` holds the scaled-schedule rows. `tests/test_levers_run.py` pins the entry of a grayness under the verdict test with the last beta stage not met.
- The flags of the engine (41.7) are facts of the matching cards, each with a `when` text that names the key of the fact; a `when` without facts is a fault of `problems()`; the reference prints "Present when: ...".
- The resume fact (41.8): the keys of the passes of a finished run are named in the run log and in the reply of `run_topopt`; a key of the post step gives no fact; the keys come from the layer of the cards; the fact refuses nothing and writes no file.
- Round 3 (the keys that main added): `settings.part_only_min_film_mm` is a layer 3 card with `RESUME_COST` and `RESUME_CALL`, and a test pins that the passes do not read it (in `topopt/optimize.py` only `problem_facts` names it; the post step reads it from `run.json`); `run_topopt:continue_from` and `run_topopt:more_iterations` are layer 2 cards with measured rows (run ids `P7-1/r3/<name>`; a test checks that the ratios of the rows follow from the measured values) and `LAYER_COSTS[2]` is a measured text; `verify_run:part_only` is a layer 4 card whose rows are CONTRACTS-recorded (part class `not printed (CONTRACTS)`, run ids `CONTRACTS 9.1: ...`). The description of `run_topopt` fits in 4,096 characters with the text of `continue_from` (4,072; the details are in the cards).
- The layer 3 route is pinned for `settings.mesh_method` (a short run: no pass, the three sha256 sums equal, the mesh method changed) and for a key of the passes (accepted, the part unchanged).
- Every fact path (41.7) is in the one path form, and every `metrics`, `run`, `history` and `check_problem` path is a key that the code writes: it is a key of the documents of a short real run, or (for the keys of a joint, which the short
  run does not have) every plain segment of the path stands as a quoted string in the writer files that the test names.
- The text pointers: Step 6 of the skill `start-here` (and its copy in `.agents/skills`), the key guide of `run_result` (since #174; the description of `run_result` names the guide), `run_topopt`, `check_problem` and the three roles name `topopt://levers` (since #380 the server `INSTRUCTIONS` name the `levers` block of `run_result` only, for the limit of 2,048 characters).

**A new key gets a card.** A new key of the YAML is added to its constant in `topopt/config.py` (41.6). Then `test_every_accepted_key_path_has_exactly_one_card` fails until `topopt/levers_cards.py` has the card (or `also` names the key).
A new engine tool (an MCP tool or a CLI subcommand) fails `test_every_mcp_tool_and_cli_command_has_a_card_or_is_listed_as_read_only` until it has a card, or an entry in `READ_ONLY_TOOLS` if it only reports. Write only what the code, this file
or a measured run says. A measured row has run ids.

### 41.6 The key lists of the loader

Each block of the YAML has its known keys as named constants in `topopt/config.py` (`SETTINGS_OPTIONAL`, `PRINT_KEYS`, `INTERFACE_KEYS`, ...), and `KEY_BLOCKS` maps the block path (`settings.stop_rules`, `load_cases[].forces[]`, ...; the top level is `""`)
to its required and optional keys. `accepted_key_paths()` gives the 221 key paths from `KEY_BLOCKS`. The loader (`_check_keys`, `_bc_keys` and the checks of the mirror, the interface and the joint section) reads these constants, and no call holds a list typed
at the call (a test reads the source to check it). A block whose keys depend on a kind (an interface kind, a joint section kind, an acceptance rule) lists all keys in `KEY_BLOCKS`, and the loader checks the keys of the kind.

An unknown key gives `UserError` with the key path, the known keys (`none` when the block or the kind takes no key), the options, and `LEVERS_HELP`: "The cards of all keys: the MCP resource topopt://levers, or the command 'topopt levers'".
The texts of the other errors are as before.

### 41.7 The fact paths of a symptom

`Symptom.facts` is the machine-readable form of `Symptom.detect`: the exact key paths of the facts that detect the symptom, so that a later tool (the `run_result` that names the cards whose fact is present in a run) can read them. One form:

`<source>.<key path>`

| Source | The document |
|---|---|
| `metrics` | `result/metrics.json` of the run (what `run_result` reads), for example `metrics.filter.min_feature_note`, `metrics.print.thinnest_member.thinnest_member_mm` |
| `run` | `run.json` of the run folder |
| `history` | one record of `history.jsonl` |
| `check_problem` | the reply of the tool `check_problem` (the output of `topopt check --json`), for example `check_problem.solid_pull.share_above` |
| `print_check` | the reply of the tool `print_check` |
| `verify` | the result that `verify_status` gives for a finished verify job |
| `ratchet` | a record of the ratchet log that `ratchet_status` gives |

- `.` goes one level down in a mapping. `[]` after a name takes every entry of the list (`metrics.stiffness_cases[].N_per_mm`). `<name>` stands for any key of a mapping (a case, a region, a measure: `metrics.reactions.cases[].joints.<region>.bond_energy_share`).
- A bare tool name (the key of a tool card, or a tool of `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`) says that the tool gives the fact (`cleanup_list`, `verify_run`, `environment`). The tool gives the fact when it is called; nothing is read from a run.
- `when` (41.1) says which value of the paths means the symptom. It is set for the symptoms that read a flag: `metrics.filter.facts` (not empty: the warning of `min_member_mm` under 2 voxels, and the lines for a derived radius not above 1 voxel and for both keys set; a `filter_radius` alone gives no line, so that card also reads `metrics.filter.size.radius_voxels`),
  `check_problem.warnings` (a line that starts with "fact: settings.iterations": the passes end before the last stage of `settings.beta_schedule`; P7-4 gives it in `topopt check`, `check_problem` and `run.log` before the run),
  `check_problem.derived.load_cases[].applies_load` and `run.derived.load_cases[].applies_load` (false: the case applies no load, U21), and the same two paths with `load_reaches_free_dofs` (false: no free dof gets a load from the case, F4-37; `load_reach` says which cause: the nodal forces cancel, or every force lands on fixed dofs),
  `metrics.stress.cases.<case>.relaxed.met` (false), `metrics.stress.cases.<case>.relaxed.peak_above_limit` (true: F4-34), `metrics.load_paths.regions.<region>.final_stl.connected_to_fixed` (false: I6; `final.stl` does not join the load region to a support), `metrics.mesh.fallback` (not null: the SDF step did not run), `metrics.mesh.extra_bodies_removed` (above 0; sdf only), `metrics.interfaces.error` (not null), `metrics.verdict.notes` (not empty: the verdict was made from the history with the default thresholds) and `verify.bore_facts[].status` (`empty` or `error`).
  The other symptoms have no `when` yet.
- A path has no space and no backtick, and a symptom does not repeat a path. `facts` is empty where no fact exists ("no fact yet"); 4 symptoms of the first version have no fact: the keep-out wall (`regions.keep_out`), the width of the rear trunk under the force of a load case
  (`load_cases[].forces[].force`), `settings.penal` (sheets) and `settings.gpu_tol` (an error text). The same force card has a second symptom with facts since U21 (a case that applies no load).
- What the test checks. The form of every path. For `metrics`, `run`, `history` and `check_problem` paths: that the path is a key of the documents of a short real run (it has a mirror, a displacement limit, the buckling check with a limit, a stress limit, a
  bore with stock, a spring and a perimeter bound), or that the plain segments of the path stand as quoted strings in the writer files of the block (the keys of a joint: `metrics.reactions.cases[].joints.<region>.*`, `run.joints.*`, `check_problem.extended.joints.*`).
  The `verify`, `ratchet` and `print_check` paths need a tet mesh or a ratchet: the test checks their form only, and the table was read against the code that writes them.

### 41.8 A resume of a finished run with a changed key that acts in the passes

`--resume --allow-changed-inputs` on a finished run (the checkpoint has `complete: true`) runs the post step again and no pass (section 24.2, 41.3). A key that the post step reads takes effect. A key that the passes read is accepted, the design stays as the old values
made it, and the record can name the new values. Since P7 this is a fact, not a surprise. The fact refuses nothing, writes no file and holds no number.

- Which keys. `topopt/resume_fact.py`, `pass_key_note(changes, complete, labels_compared=False)`, reads the change lines of `ResumePlan.changes` (the lines of section 24.2: `settings.penal: 3.0 -> 3.5`). A line is named when the key path has a YAML card of layer 1 in `topopt/levers_cards.py`
  (a key of `also` counts, an index `[0]` is `[]`, a path with no card takes the card of its parent). A card of layer 3 or 4 is not named. A changed region file, voxel labels or design voxels are named as `regions`, with one rule from round 3: the passes read the voxel labels and not the files, so a region file with other content is named only when the plan compared the labels with the checkpoint (`labels_compared`: the problem is built and the checkpoint holds the labels hash) and they moved (a `the voxel labels are not the same` or `the design voxels are not the same` line), or when the labels were not compared; a file under another path with the same bytes is never named. A not-printed region is no case of its own: the entries of `regions.not_printed` are files of a fixed, load, solid or keep_out region (section 2), the change line has that role (`region file fixed:plate.stl has other content`; there is no `not_printed:` line, because the entries are not in `Regions`), and a file that moves labels is named, one that moves none (measured: a plate that moves by 0.01 mm at voxel 1 mm) is not. The table of cards is the one source: a new key with a card is covered.
  A run that is not finished has its passes to run, so it gets no fact.
- Limits. (1) The function reads the layer of the card only. A key whose cards say "layer 3, but layer 1 with `buckling.min_factor` set" (`buckling.modes`, `buckling.max_gb`, `buckling.max_seconds`) is not named, also when the row reads it in the passes. (2) The stop rules (`settings.stop_rules` and its keys) and the two voxel guards (`settings.max_active_voxels`, `settings.max_grid_voxels`) are `checkpoint.SOFT_KEYS`: a change is a note on a resume, not a change of the inputs, so the fact never sees it (the thresholds act in the passes when the rules are on). (3) The reply key `resume` of the MCP tool compares the YAML keys and the region files only: the server builds no problem before the run. A change that moves only the voxel labels or the design voxels (for example `interfaces[].stock_mm`, layer 3) is in the run log line, where the CLI plan has the problem, and is not in the reply. The cards of these keys say it. For a region file the reply cannot tell whether a voxel label moved: it names the file and says `(this reply does not compare the voxels that it fills)`.
- Where. `plan_resume` (`topopt/checkpoint.py`) adds one line to `facts` after the line "the inputs changed since the checkpoint". The line is `resume: the run is finished, so no pass runs again, and the design stays as the old values made it. The changed inputs that act in the passes: <key (old -> new); ...>. ...`,
  and `run.log` shows it. `run_topopt(resume=true, allow_changed_inputs=true)` returns the key `resume`: `{"facts": [<the same sentence>], "options": [...], "pass_keys": [<card keys>]}`. Without a changed key of the passes, or for a run that is not finished, the reply has no `resume` key. The reply is made before the process starts and reads the checkpoint only.
- Options (four since round 3): a new run with the new values (`run_topopt` without `resume`, with a new `out_dir`; the cost is a whole run, and `check_problem` gives `derived.time_estimate_s`); `run_topopt` with `continue_from=<this run folder>`, `more_iterations=N`, `allow_changed_inputs=true` and a new `out_dir` (a new folder that links to this run, which is only read; the passes go on from its last checkpoint with the new values; a changed grid is refused; the cost is the N passes and a fixed part, and the card `run_topopt:continue_from` has a measured row); give the old values back and resume (the record then agrees with the part); keep this resume for a key that only the post step reads (layer 3 on its card).
- Test: `tests/test_levers.py` (the keys of the passes and no other key; the layer of the cards decides; the log line of a real short run with no pass and equal sha256 sums; the reply of `run_topopt`; round 3: the four options, the call of the option on a real run (refused without the override, with it the new value acts and the parent is only read), a region file that moves labels and one that does not, on a run with `regions.not_printed`).

### 41.9 The hook evidence and how to read a price

The cards hold the 60 runs of the E1 series (part class `hook` for `hook_short.yaml`, `hook fine` for `hook.yaml`; run ids `E1/<id>`, the folders are not in this repository). The rows are facts about that part. The reference (header, "How to read a price") defines the three measures:
`optimizer` is `stiffness_cases[].N_per_mm` (the voxel field, with the `penal` of the run itself), `P2` is `topopt verify <run> --no-sensitivity` on `final.stl` (section 16: quadratic tets, independent of the voxel model; the printed part is the P2 model), and `mass` is `mass_final_g`.

- Noise of the base (`hook_short`, B0 and four runs that change one input by 0.05 to 0.1 %): the optimizer stiffness moves at most 0.12 % (`hang`) and 0.17 % (`pull_off`), the mass 0.078 %, 0.72 % of the design voxels change state, and P2 moves 0.7 % and 3.3 %. A `hook` row is marked `inside the noise` when its three optimizer values
  are inside +-0.3 % (stiffness) and +-0.1 % (mass). The bands are the observed maximum with a margin, taken from the report; they are not tolerances of the product, and no code reads them. A normal step of `move_limit`, `penal` or the filter radius flips 5 to 21 % of the design voxels and moves the optimizer stiffness by up to about 2 %:
  one run for each setting cannot tell that from a lever effect, so the cards call a difference below about 2 % "small, unproven" and a P2 difference below about 4 % "inside the P2 noise".
- Five keys give a price in the optimizer that misleads: `settings.penal`, `settings.min_member_mm` and `settings.filter_radius` (a radius of 1 voxel or less is "no filter"), `settings.mesh_method` (`blur` leaves the optimizer value unchanged and has P2 x0.571 / x0.784) and `settings.voxel_size`. The `price_note` of these cards says to read P2. The `penal` rows of the phone stand are optimizer values.
- The estimate `metrics.print.thinnest_member.thinnest_member_mm` did not follow the filter radius on the hook and moved 4.8 % between the noise runs: the filter symptoms do not list it as a fact (the card of `print.min_wall_mm` keeps it, as the estimate of the print check).
- `settings.volume_fraction` is the mean density of the free design voxels. The `regions.keep_out` and `settings.volume_fraction` cards hold the formula that keeps the mass (the volumes come from `check_problem`), the blocks K1 to K3v, and the fact that `metrics.mass_saved_pct` hides the loss (its "before" mass falls too).
- `settings.iterations` and `settings.beta_schedule` hold the rows of 20 and 80 passes with the schedule unchanged and scaled with the passes.
- The cost of one try by layer on the hook is in 41.3 and in the layer list of the reference.

**The E2 series (P7-5; 54 runs, run ids `E2/<id>`, the folders are not in this repository).** The cards of the stress keys, the buckling keys, `mirror`, `eta_eroded`, `perimeter_max_mm2`, `regions.solid`, `limits.displacement` and the local tools hold its rows.
- Noise of the stress case (part class `hook_stress`): 6 runs of the unchanged `hook_stress.yaml` gave 6 different designs (the cause was not isolated), and a change of 0.1 % in one key moved the end state as much. The base of a stress row is the MEAN of the 6 runs (mass 33.09 g; optimizer 874.3 and 1079.7 N/mm; P2 770.5 and 813.3 N/mm).
  A stress row is marked `inside the noise` when its hang, pull_off and mass ratios are inside the range of the 6 runs (hang x0.989 to x1.013, pull_off x0.986 to x1.014, mass x0.983 to x1.009). The range is the observed one; no code of the product reads it, and `tests/test_levers.py` (`STRESS_BAND`) pins the marks.
  The hook family and the buckling copy repeat byte for byte, so the bands of `hook` (+-0.3 %, +-0.1 %) apply to them.
- `relaxed.met` is the relaxed measure of the optimizer: the P2 p99.9 stress of `pull_off` stayed 2.45 to 2.67 times the limit (0.5 MPa) in the 6 base runs, and with `stress_scale` 0.5 the relaxed peak was 0.957 MPa and the row said met. The card of `settings.stress_scale` has kind `both`: the number moves the user's limit
  (1 or more tightens it, below 1 loosens it), `topopt check` prints no fact for it, and the origin of the number does not change that.
- The buckling row costs 10.4 to 13.8 times a plain run at 2 mm, also when it is slack (`min_factor` 100: 11.4 times). The P2 `pull_off` stiffness fell about 8 % in 4 designs (150, 150.15, 250 and 150 with `ks_q` 80), also in the 250 run where the row was slack at the last pass, while the optimizer showed none (the cause was not isolated). `mirror` with `align: centre` at 2 mm left 570 orphan voxels and a mirror error of 3.36 mm against 0.462 mm for `auto`.
- `confidence` is `measured` only for a card with a run row; a key that E2 did not run keeps `code`.

**The E3 series (P7-6; 62 runs and 62 P2 checks on `examples/interfaces/bracket.yaml` and `examples/ladle/ladle.yaml`, run ids `E3/<id>`, the folders are not in this repository).** The cards of `filter_radius`, `min_member_mm`, `iterations`, `beta_schedule`, `stop_rules`, `penal`, `volume_fraction`, `mesh_method` (P2 only: `blur`) and `check_problem` hold its rows; `voxel_size` holds the ladle times.
- Part classes and bands: `bracket` (base BR-B0, grey: grayness 0.129, beta 8 not reached), `bracket-fitted` (base BR-BS40s), `ladle-4mm` (base LAD-D0, three load cases and an `objective` that is the weighted compliance sum) and `ladle` (3.25 mm, the three filter rows). Each class gives its base values and the noise band it uses (the class `ladle` has no noise set of its own and uses the bands of `ladle-4mm`); the engine repeated byte for byte on both parts.
  A row is marked `inside the noise` when every value of its price is inside the band of its own class (`tests/test_levers.py`, `E3_BAND`, pins the marks). These bands are the observed maximum of the noise runs of each class; no code of the product reads them, and the 2 % / 3.5 % sign rule of the report is the report's reading aid, not a rule of the cards.
- Across parts: each of the eight keys has one sentence in its `price_note` with the sign on the hook, the bracket and the ladle (outside the band of that part) and "same sign on the three parts" or "differs" with the numbers. The cards say "on three parts" and give no general law.
- Facts for the open questions of the report, as facts only (no decision, no default change, no new warning): F4-19 (the 2-voxel member on five rows with mass and grayness, the 1-voxel member inside the P2 band, which settings get the 2-voxel warning) on `min_member_mm`; F4-25 (a radius of 1 voxel: 1 entry per row, no warning, P2 below the optimizer, islands removed) on `filter_radius`; F4-22 (the gain of double passes with and without the last beta stage, the 0.0017 contrast) on `iterations` only, with a one-line summary and a pointer on `beta_schedule` and `stop_rules.objective_change`, and `stop_rules: true` at pass 78 and 79 on `stop_rules`; the blur on the ladle (P2 x0.009, one run, cause not isolated) on `mesh_method`; the grayness 0.085 of LAD-IT40 in the symptoms that name the grayness (`iterations`, `beta_schedule`, `stop_rules.grayness_max`); the time of the ladle and the bracket against the estimate of `topopt check` on `check_problem` (rows) and `voxel_size`.
- The levers block (41.10) has no new fact path: the E3 facts are in the evidence rows, the `price_note` texts and the `detect` text of three symptoms. `tests/test_levers_run.py` pins that a grayness under the verdict test with the last beta stage not met lists the stage and not the grayness (E3/LAD-IT40).

### 41.10 The levers of a run: the block `levers` of `run_result` and `topopt levers --run` (added with P7 PR-3)

A run shows many facts, and most of them are plain numbers (a mass, a stiffness, a grayness). A list of all the symptoms of the cards in every reply would be noise. This subsection is the
diagnosis step of the loop: it names the lever cards of the facts that the ENGINE flags in THIS run. The code is `topopt/levers_run.py` (it reads files, writes nothing, needs no solver).

**What is read.** `result/metrics.json` (a run that stopped has none: then `verdict.json`, which holds the document of `metrics.verdict`), `run.json`, `history.jsonl`, `status.json`, `verify/verify.json`
(the result of `verify_run`; only when the folder has it) and the last record of the ratchet log in the default root beside the run folder (`<run folder>-ratchet/ratchet.jsonl`).
Notes (`notes` in the result; a problem with a file is a note and never an error):
- A file that is not there is a note for `result/metrics.json` ("is not there: the run has no result"; `verdict.json` is read instead), `run.json` and `history.jsonl`. `status.json`, `verify/verify.json` and the ratchet log are optional:
  a missing one gives no note (most runs have no verify result and no ratchet; an old run has no `status.json`).
- A file that is there and does not parse (not JSON, not a JSON object, or not readable as text) is a note that says "does not parse" for `result/metrics.json`, `run.json`, `status.json`, `verify/verify.json`, `history.jsonl` and the ratchet log.
  A `metrics.json` that does not parse is read as a missing one: the verdict comes from `verdict.json`.
- A line of `history.jsonl` or of the ratchet log that does not parse is skipped (the lines before and after are read), and one note for the file gives the number of lines: "history.jsonl: 2 line(s) do not parse and were skipped".
- A `verify.json` that is for an older `result/final.stl` (the sha256 of the mesh file named by `run.verified_file` differs from `run.final_stl_sha256`: the check of `verify_status`) is read, and a note says that its facts describe the older mesh.
  `run.verified_file` is used only when it is text; anything else is the default, `final.stl`.
The print check is a reply of a tool that no file of the run folder holds, so its facts are not read.

**Which facts are listed.** A fact path of a card (41.7) is listed only when the engine already flags it. The module has no threshold, tolerance or number of its own (a test reads its source).
A row of `FLAGS` has a fact path, a rule and the place in the engine where the flag comes from (`anchor`). The rules: `false` (the value is the boolean false), `text` (a text, or a list or mapping with
something in it: a note, a warning, a refusal, options), `in S` (one of the states S that the engine names as an end that needs a look), `not_in S` (none of the good states S that the engine names) and
`above C` (a number above a constant C that the engine already has), and `true` (the value is the boolean true: a fact that the engine sets true when it holds, F4-34). A value that is null is no fact. `joined` paths are the numbers that the flag judges: they are shown with the hit, and the cards that name them join
the entry (a grayness test that is not met brings the cards that name the grayness value). `shown` paths (F4-29) are shown with the hit in the same way but judge nothing: no card joins by them, and they need not be a fact path of a card.
The two stress flags (`relaxed.met` false, `relaxed.peak_above_limit` true) show `independent_check.found`, `independent_check.p2_p99_9_by_volume_MPa` and `independent_check.p2_over_limit` of the case: the P2 value of `topopt verify` and its ratio to the limit,
read from `verify/verify.json` when the run folder is read (`stress_report.refresh_from_verify`); `found` false means that verify has not run, and the `says` text gives the option.

| Fact path | Rule | Where the flag comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `metrics.verdict.state` | not in `converged`, `stopped_by_rule` | `verdict.STATES`: `converged` = the objective tests and every row met at the last pass; `stopped_by_rule` = the tests of a stop rule ended the run. The pass limit, a request and an unfinished history are listed |
| `metrics.verdict.measures.grayness.met` (+ `value`) | false | `grayness` is above `settings.stop_rules.grayness_max` |
| `metrics.verdict.measures.objective_change.met` (+ `value`, `threshold`) | false | the change is above `settings.stop_rules.objective_change`, or not judged |
| `metrics.verdict.measures.last_beta_stage.met` | false | the run ends before the last stage of the beta schedule |
| `metrics.verdict.facts.load_path.not_joined` | text | the text of the verdict names a load region that is not joined (`stage_facts.verdict_sentence`) |
| `metrics.load_paths.regions.<region>.final_stl.connected_to_fixed` (+ `touches_a_body`, `bodies_with_the_region`) | false | `stress_report._stl_connectivity`: no body of `final.stl` holds a point of the load region and a point of a fixed region (I6: every run has `metrics.load_paths`; before I6 only a run with a stress row had it). The region name is in `of` |
| `metrics.verdict.notes` | text | `verdict.verdict_for_post`: the run folder has no matching `verdict.json`, so the verdict was made from the history with the default thresholds (`metrics.verdict.source` is `history`) |
| `metrics.stress.cases.<case>.relaxed.met` | false | `stress_report.relaxed_numbers`: met is `g <= NOT_MET` at the last pass; the row is the relaxed measure of the optimizer, not the stress of the part (`met_means`); joined: `relaxed.peak_MPa`, `stress_limit_MPa` |
| `metrics.stress.cases.<case>.relaxed.peak_above_limit` (+ `relaxed.peak_MPa`, `stress_limit_MPa`) | true | `ks_stress.peak_above_limit`: the relaxed peak is above the limit by more than `PEAK_ABOVE_TOL` (= `formulation.NOT_MET`), whether the row is met or not; the test of the run log line `stress peak above the limit` (F4-34). The cards of the stress limit and of `settings.stress_scale` name it |
| `metrics.constraints[].g` (+ `verdict.feasible`) | above `formulation.NOT_MET` | the run log calls a row not met above this g |
| `metrics.verdict.feasible` | false | `verdict.measures` `max_g`: met is false when the largest g is above `FEASIBLE_TOL`, or a row has no result (listed once with the rows when a row is above `NOT_MET`) |
| `metrics.rows[].met` (+ `value_end`, `limit`, `g_end`) | false | `rows_motion.rows_block`: met is `g_end <= NOT_MET` |
| `metrics.mesh.fallback` (+ `requested`) | text | `post._mesh_method`: the SDF step did not run (the grid guard, or an error) and the blur path made the mesh; the log warns |
| `metrics.mesh.extra_bodies_removed` (+ `extra_bodies_volume_mm3`) | above 0 | `smooth_sdf.make_mesh_sdf`: the log warns when the step removed bodies that do not touch a frozen region |
| `metrics.mesh.stl_roundtrip.watertight` | false | `post._mesh_record` warns when the STL file, read again, is not a closed manifold |
| `metrics.print.configured.bed_fit` | false | `print_report.bed_fit_turn`: the bed margin of the part is negative |
| `metrics.filter.facts` | text | `members.member_facts`: the warnings about `min_member_mm` below 2 voxels, both keys set, or a derived radius not above 1 voxel; the run log prints each as `warning: ...` |
| `metrics.buckling.status` (+ `facts`, `options`) | not in `done` | `buckling_voxel`: status `done`, `skipped` or `error` |
| `metrics.buckling.facts` (+ `options`) | text | the run log prints each fact of the buckling check as a warning (listed once with the status) |
| `metrics.interfaces.error` (+ `applied`) | text | `interfaces.write_outputs`: the record has the error text when the exact step did not apply (`applied` is then false) |
| `metrics.interfaces.applied` | false | `interfaces.write_outputs`: the exact step did not apply (listed once with the error when there is one) |
| `metrics.interfaces.items[].as_printed.measured.<measure>.within_tolerance` (+ `deviation_mm`, `coverage`, `measured_mm`, `expected_mm`) | false | `interfaces.measure`: the test of a feature against its tolerance and coverage |
| `metrics.verdict.interface_tests[].met` (+ `full_coverage`) | false | `interfaces.full_surface_tests`: an interface with `full_surface` whose full coverage is below `FULL_COVERAGE_MIN` (check D of section 23; #90) |
| `metrics.interfaces.warnings` | text | `interfaces`: the warnings of checks C, D and E of section 23 (`run_result` key `interface_warnings`; #90) |
| `metrics.part_only.pinches_left` | above 0 | `part_only.make`: the record has `pinches_left` only with `settings.part_only_min_film_mm`; above 0 it has a note that `topopt.tet` refuses a surface that touches itself at a vertex |
| `metrics.part_only.watertight` | false | `part_only.make`: the run log warns when `part_only.stl`, read again, is not one closed manifold |
| `verify.bore_facts[].status` (+ `funnel`, `facts`) | not in `ok` | `verify.bore.build_bore`: `ok` when the bore has a sample set, else `empty`; `verify.bore._error_entry`: `error`; the bore is not checked |
| `run.lost_force.max_lost_percent` | above 0 | `loads.lost_force_warning` warns when a case loses force (above 0) |
