| `run.derived.load_cases[].load_reaches_free_dofs` (+ `applies_load`) | false | `loads.reaches_free_dofs` (F4-37, `problem.build_problem`): false for a case whose load vector is exactly 0.0 on every free dof (the nodal forces add up to 0.0 at every node, or all its force lands on fixed dofs; also false for a case with a YAML zero); `loads.no_load_lines` writes the fact at the start of `run.log`. `applies_load` joins it, so a YAML zero case is one entry (the hit shows `applies_load` in `with`) |
| `run.derived.load_cases[].applies_load` | false | `config.LoadCase.applies_load` (U21): false for a case in which every force and moment is exactly 0 and no pressure is other than 0; `loads.no_load_lines` writes the fact at the start of `run.log`. The entry of a `run.json` that has no `load_reaches_free_dofs` (an older run); a newer one lists it under the row above |
| `history.step_acceptance.accepted` (+ `tries`) | false | `optimize.StepAcceptance`: all tries were rejected and the step was taken; a history fact has one hit with `passes`, `first_pass`, `last_pass` |
| `run_status` | in `stopped`, `error` | the `state` of `status.json` (the card of `run_topopt:resume` and `stop_run` name this tool fact) |
| `ratchet.decision` | in `REJECT` | `ratchet.Outcome.decision` of the last record |
| `ratchet.checks[].state` | in `fail` | `ratchet.Check.state` of the last record |

A fact path of the cards that is not in this table is not listed. `NOT_FLAGGED` in the module gives the reason for each of them (the "needs an engine fact" list), and `decisions()` assigns one of
`flagged`, `joined` or a reason to every fact path of the cards; the test asserts that no path is left out, so a new fact path in a card fails until a row or a reason is added here (as a new key
fails until it has a card). The reasons are of these kinds: the value is a plain measurement and the engine sets no limit for it (a mass, a stiffness, an overhang area, the thinnest member); the asked value of a requirement, on which
the engine sets no test (`run.derived.volume.target_mass_asked_g` and `metrics.mass_asked_g`, I7); the
stage facts of the volume are, by their own text, "not a test, a limit or a warning rule"; the Goodman number and the stress of `verify` are reported with no pass or fail; the print check is a
reply of a tool; `check_problem` facts are of the time before the run; the engine warns about a filter radius not above 1 voxel only when it derives the radius from `min_member_mm`, so
`metrics.filter.size.radius_voxels` of a `filter_radius` alone is a number with no flag; the islands that the mesh step removes and its local loss are numbers with no warning; `metrics.threshold_stability.levels[].volume_mm3` and `.bodies` (I6) are a fact only, with no limit for how far they move between the levels 0.4, 0.5 and 0.6, so they are not listed. Round 3 (the cards of the part-only file and of `continue_from`): the contact numbers of a removed body (`area_below_voxel_mm2`, `thinnest_wall_mm`) are written in every cut, and the note that compares them with the voxel size is
written only when the film setting is off, so no flag is in the record; `metrics.part_only.applied` and `.file` are named by the card of `verify_run:part_only` for a run that has the file, and an `applied` that is false is an
error record that no card names; `verify.part_only.yaml_vs_run` is a mapping in every check (its flag is the key `matches`, and no card names that key); `verify.part_only.file` is the name of the mesh that the check used. The layer order
`(3, 4, 2, 1)` needs no change: the new layer-2 cards come after the cheaper layers of an entry and before the layer-1 cards (a run that ended at its pass limit lists `run_topopt:continue_from`, then `run_topopt:more_iterations`, then `settings.iterations`).

**The entry.** `run_levers(run_dir)` returns `{run_dir, read, notes, order, entries}`. An entry has `fact` (the path as the cards write it), `flag` (what the engine says), `hits` (where it holds: `at`
the concrete path, `value`, `of` the name of the row or feature, `with` the values of the joined paths for the same row) and `cards`. A card has `key`, `group`, `kind`, `layer`, `words` (the words of
the symptoms of that card that name the fact), `when` (the `Symptom.when` text of those symptoms, 41.1 and 41.7: which value of the fact the symptom means; the key is there only where a symptom has one),
`cost` and `call` (the card's own, else the text of its layer). The cards of an entry are the cards that name the fact path or a joined path in a symptom.
**The order** is the cheapest layer first: 3 (the post step only, seconds), 4 (a local edit or judgement, seconds to minutes), 2 (continue or branch a run, a part of a run), 1 (a new run), from the cost
texts of the layers (41.3); the layer numbers are names, not a scale. The cards inside an entry have this order, and the entries are ordered by their cheapest card (a tie keeps the order of the table above).
The kind of each card (`requirement`, `method`, `both`) is in the entry, so the agent sees which cards are the user's; the rule of 41.2 is not repeated.

**Limits to read.** A card names the facts of a symptom, and only the symptoms that have a `when` text say which value they mean. A card can come with the mirrored symptom: `settings.stop_rules`, "runs after it has settled",
comes with an objective change that is not met, because it names the same value (that symptom has no `when`). The words and the `when` text are in the entry so that the agent can tell: for `metrics.filter.facts`
the card `settings.filter_radius` says that its own fact is `radius_voxels`, and that `facts` is empty for a `filter_radius` alone. `metrics.constraints[].g` and `metrics.verdict.feasible` name the cards of the compliance
rows, and a row of another kind (stress, perimeter, buckling, a displacement limit) is told by `of`, the name of the row (a displacement row that is not met has the card `limits.displacement[].limit_mm` in its entry: E2/LDc); a stress row that is not met has also its own entry (`relaxed.met`) with the cards of the stress limit and of `settings.stress_scale`; its hit shows `peak_MPa` and `stress_limit_MPa` of the same case (joined paths). A row that is met is listed through `relaxed.peak_above_limit` when the relaxed peak is above the limit (E2/SS05: peak 0.957 MPa, limit 0.5 MPa, `met` true): the engine sets this flag (F4-34, `ks_stress.peak_above_limit`), and the block adds no threshold of its own. A row that is both not met and above the limit has the two entries.
The block is a list of facts and options: the agent decides.

**Where it shows.**
- MCP `run_result`: `levers` = `compact(run_levers(run_dir))`: `{entries, order, cards[, notes]}`, where each entry has `fact`, `flag`, `hits` (without `at` when it equals `fact`) and `cards` with `key`
  (and `tool: true` for the card of a tool), `kind`, `layer`, `words`; no card text, no cost, no call. `cards` is one line that points to the resource `topopt://levers`, to the resource template `topopt://levers/{query}` (41.4) and to `topopt levers <key or word>`. A card has `when` where the symptom has one.
  A clean run has `entries: []`. The reply for a run that a request stopped has the block too (the verdict, `run_status` and the cards of the resume).
- CLI: `topopt levers --run <run folder>` prints `format_text`: the entries with their cards (key, kind, layer, words, and the line `Present when: ...` where a symptom has a `when` text), then the full text of each distinct card (`levers.render_card`, the text of
  `topopt levers <key>`), cheapest layer first. It takes no key or word with `--run` (exit code 1). A folder that is not there gives exit code 1; a folder with no run file gives the notes. It reads files only.

**The test.** `tests/test_levers_run.py`: one real short run and copies of its folder with edited files. One case for each row of `FLAGS` (an entry when the flag holds, none when it does not), the
two engine constants at their edge, the null value, the order of the layers, a run with no `metrics.json`, a damaged folder, every path that the module reads is a fact path of a card, a decision for
every fact path of the cards, no float and no number of its own in the module, the `when` text of the cards, the `verify.json` of the folder (a note for an older mesh, for a damaged file, and no crash for a file name that is not text), a file that is not there against a file that does not parse, the skipped lines of `history.jsonl` and of the ratchet log, the compact block, the text, `run_result` (clean, stopped, with a fault in the block) and the command.

## 42. Faceted STEP file of a finished run (added with P8-1)

Code: `topopt/step.py` (all OpenCASCADE calls are in this file; `_import_ocp()` is the only place that imports it). Command: `topopt step`.
MCP tool: `export_step`. Extra: `step` (`cadquery-ocp-novtk`, pinned).

**What the file is.** The STEP file holds the triangles of `result/final.stl` (or `part_only.stl`) as planar faces of closed solids, in mm. It is
a faceted solid, not a CAD model with cylinders and fillets: a CAD program can measure it, cut holes in it, join it to other parts and
mirror it, and it cannot edit the surfaces of the optimizer shape (there are none: the shape is a mesh). The faces of the fixed and load
regions are true planes after the merge (below). No optimizer pass runs. The input files do not change. Nothing here changes the stress, the
mass or the stiffness of the run: the file is the shape of the STL, to the distance in the report.

**Extra and install.** OpenCASCADE is not a core dependency. `pyproject.toml` has the extra `step = ["cadquery-ocp-novtk==7.9.3.1.1"]`
(OCCT 7.9.3; wheels for macOS arm64, macOS x86_64, Linux x86_64 and aarch64, Windows; the install is about 250 MB on disk). `topopt/step.py` imports
nothing of OpenCASCADE at module level, so `import topopt`, `topopt run` and the MCP server never load it (a test asserts this
in a fresh Python). Do not install the packages `cadquery-ocp` and `cadquery-ocp-novtk` together: both write the folder `OCP/`.
Without the extra, `topopt step` and the MCP tool give one message, no traceback, exit 1:

```
OpenCASCADE (the optional extra `step`, the package cadquery-ocp-novtk) is not installed in this Python, so topopt cannot write a STEP file.
Install it (macOS with Apple silicon, and Linux x86_64; about 250 MB on disk). In the topopt folder:
    uv pip install -e ".[step]"
With no checkout of topopt:
    uv pip install "cadquery-ocp-novtk==7.9.3.1.1"
Keep the quotes: zsh reads [...] as a pattern. Then run this command again.
```

A package that is installed and does not load gives the same text with `installed but does not load` and the import error. `topopt doctor`
(section 8.1) lists `OpenCASCADE (OCP)` with `extra step`. The licence of the wheel: `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (the extra `step`). The wheel bundles
native libraries: LGPL (OpenCASCADE, LibRaw) and libraries that are GPL or have a GPL option (libjbig, FreeImage, FreeType, zstd, libgomp with the GCC exception). The package was accepted as the optional
extra `step` on 2026-10-23 (option 1: the rule of gmsh and cholespy of 2026-10-19: it is installed from PyPI on the machine of the user, never vendored, never imported by the core). `scripts/ci/license_policy.toml` has
the `allow` and the `override` entry, and every CI leg installs the extra (section 27.2).

### 42.1 Command

```
topopt step <run_dir> [--part-only] [--out FILE_OR_FOLDER] [--tolerance-mm X] [--no-merge-planes] [--schema AP214|AP242] [--estimate-only] [--json]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `run_dir` | A finished run folder (the `--out` of `topopt run`). It is only read. A run that is `starting`, `running` or in `postprocess` gives an error with the state. |
| `--part-only` | Wrap `result/part_only.stl` (section 9.1) and write `result/part_only.step`. Without `regions.not_printed` there is no such file: the error says so. |
| `--out` | The STEP file. A file path, or an existing folder (the file name is then `final.step` or `part_only.step`). Default `<run_dir>/result/final.step`. An existing file is replaced only when it is a `.step` or `.stp` file; the input STL and any other existing file give an error (exit 1) with the options: a new file name that ends in `.step`, or a folder. The report is next to the STEP file and has its name plus `.json` (`result/final.step.json`, `result/part_only.step.json`, `<file>.step.json`), so with `--out` elsewhere the run folder gets no file. |
| `--tolerance-mm X` | The simplification tolerance in mm (42.2). `0` = none: every STL triangle is a face. Default: the voxel size of the run / 20 (`run.json` `h`, else `verify/verify.json` `run.voxel_size_mm`); a folder that holds neither gets 0 (no simplification), and `simplify.note` names the option `--tolerance-mm`. A value that removes every triangle (the part is smaller than the tolerance, or the STL is not in mm) is an error, and no file is written. |
| `--no-merge-planes` | Keep one face for each triangle. Default: coplanar faces are merged (42.2). |
| `--schema` | `AP214` (default; `AP214IS`) or `AP242` (`AP242DIS`). The case and a hyphen do not matter (`ap-242`); the command, the MCP tool and the Python function read the name the same way. |
| `--estimate-only` | Simplify and count, then print the expected faces, file size, time and memory (42.5). Writes no file. It works without OpenCASCADE (the report has `ocp: null`). |
| `--json` | Print the report as JSON on stdout (the text report otherwise). Without `--json`, one progress line for each phase goes to stderr. |

Exit codes: `0` the file is written and every check passed (or `--estimate-only`); `1` a usage error or a wrong input (a message on stderr, also the missing
extra, a target that would replace another file, a folder without write access, a tolerance that removes every triangle); `3` the file is written and at least one check failed (a fact, 42.4).
The folder of the STEP file and its report is tested for write access before the work starts; a write error later is also exit 1 with the path, not a traceback. Exit 2 is an internal error, as for every command. Exit 3 means what it means for `topopt verify` (section 16): the result is made and one fact is flagged.
A run folder is the same before and after, except the new files `result/final.step` (`part_only.step`) and its report `result/final.step.json` (`part_only.step.json`), or no new file with `--out` elsewhere (a test hashes the whole tree).

### 42.2 Method

1. Read `result/final.stl` (`printcheck.load_stl_float32`, 32-bit float). The facts of the mesh come from `printcheck.mesh_health` (`input` in the report).
2. Simplify with manifold3d, `Manifold.simplify(tolerance_mm)` (a core dependency; the same call as the post step). It removes vertices and
   flips edges while the surface moves less than the tolerance. A mesh that manifold3d refuses (not a manifold) is wrapped as it is, and
   `simplify.note` says so. `simplify` in the report: `applied`, `tolerance_mm`, `triangles_before`, `triangles_after`.
3. Build the solid directly: one `TopoDS_Vertex` for each mesh vertex, one `TopoDS_Edge` for each mesh edge (shared by the 2 faces), one planar
   face for each triangle, so the shell is closed by its topology. No sewing is used: `BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing` took 6.6 times longer on the
   same mesh in the prototype. The shells are found by edges (`mesh_shells`). A closed shell is a void when it lies inside an odd number of other closed shells, and a body otherwise,
   whatever the winding of the shells is. A body is written with its faces outward and a void with its faces inward, so a shell with the other winding is turned
   (`build.inside_out_bodies`, `build.inside_out_voids`). The volume of the mesh (`input.volume_mm3`, `volume.wrapped_mm3`) is the volume of the bodies minus the volume of the voids, counted after the
   orientation. A void is an inner shell of the body that holds it with the smallest volume; several bodies are one compound of solids. A shell with an edge of 1 face or of more than
   2 faces is not manifold (`build.shells_not_manifold`); it is written as it is, and the checks of 42.4 show what follows. Zero-area triangles are left out and counted
   (`build.degenerate_triangles_left_out`). An edge shorter than 1e-7 mm (the OpenCASCADE point tolerance) stops with an error that names the option
   `--tolerance-mm 0.00001`.
4. Merge coplanar faces (`ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain` with its default tolerances; `merge_planes` in the report has `faces_before` and
   `faces_after`). The faces of the fixed and load regions are flat, so each becomes one planar face. The curved part keeps its facets. Larger
   tolerances than the default merged curved facets into invalid solids in the measurements, so no tolerance option exists: the merge is on or off.
5. Check the model in memory (42.4, `before_write`), then write with `STEPControl_Writer`: `write.step.schema` as asked, `write.step.unit` `MM`, `write.step.product.name` = the run name (`(part only)` is added; OpenCASCADE adds a number to it, and the report gives the name that the file holds),
   `write.surfacecurve.mode` 0 (no pcurves: they only repeat the planes; the file is half the size). The file goes through a temporary file in the
   same folder, then `os.replace`. OpenCASCADE prints progress to the C stdout, which is the protocol channel of the MCP server; the message printers
   are removed in `_import_ocp`, and the MCP tool runs the command in a child process in addition.
6. Read the file back with `STEPControl_Reader` and check it (42.4), then sample the distance to the STL (42.3).
7. Write the report next to the STEP file (`result/final.step.json`, atomically).

**Default tolerance (a method setting, measured).** Without the option, the tolerance is the voxel size / 20. Reason: the mesh comes from marching cubes of a density
field with a voxel size `h`, so its surface is known to a fraction of `h` only. A tolerance of `h/20` moves the surface by at most 0.10 to 0.16 mm
(1.6 to 2.2 times the tolerance) on the two public parts (`B0`, the short hook with `h` 2.0 mm, and `H0`, the T-shirt hook with `h` 1.2 mm), removes 55 and 70 percent of the triangles, and changes the volume by -0.21 and -0.07 percent.
A smaller tolerance gains little (`h/200`: 4 to 14 percent fewer triangles); a larger one is the option for a faster file: `h/10` gives 77 to 85 percent fewer
triangles, a largest distance of 0.24 to 0.33 mm and a volume change of -0.36 to -0.97 percent (table in 42.7). The volume change is small and, on the public parts, mostly a loss;
the report gives it in `volume.step_vs_stl_pct`. The distances are sampled (42.3.1), so they can be below a dense measure: a dense check of the same pairs gave 0 to 7 percent more (for `B0` at h/20: 0.159 mm sampled, 0.170 mm dense).
The cost of the default does **not** stay flat on every part: it follows the number of faces after the simplification, and that follows the part (42.7: a larger part A, not shipped, gave 85,103 faces and 102 s; a larger part B, not shipped, 355,585 faces and 613 s). The tolerance is a method setting, not a user requirement
(requirement vs method keys): a user can set any value with `--tolerance-mm`, the report gives the price, and a value of `0` keeps the exact triangles of the STL.

### 42.3 The report (`result/final.step.json`, `--json`, the MCP reply)

| Key | Content |
|---|---|
| `format` | 1. |
| `state` | `written` or `estimate`. |
| `run_dir`, `mesh` | The absolute run folder; `final.stl` or `part_only.stl`. |
| `input` | `path`, `bytes`, `sha256`, `triangles`, `vertices`, `volume_mm3`, `closed`, `bodies`, `voids`, `open_edges`, `nonmanifold_edges`, `zero_area_faces`. |
| `settings` | `tolerance_mm`, `tolerance_source` (`option`, or the text of the default), `merge_planes`, `schema`, `part_only`. |
| `simplify` | Step 2. |
| `ocp` | The version of the installed OpenCASCADE package (or null). |
| `estimate` | Only for `state: estimate` (42.5). |
| `output` | `path`, `bytes`, `schema` (`AP214` / `AP242` / ... read from the file), `schema_text` (the `FILE_SCHEMA` text), `unit` (the length unit that the file declares, from `STEPControl_Reader.FileUnits`: `mm`, else the name of OpenCASCADE such as `INCH`; null when the file names none), `product_name` (the name that the file holds: the run name and a number that OpenCASCADE adds), `notes` (texts: a setting that OpenCASCADE did not take, a product name with characters outside ASCII; `[]` when there is none). |
| `merge_planes` | `{"applied": false}` or `{"applied": true, "faces_before", "faces_after"}`. |
| `build` | `bodies`, `voids`, `shells_not_manifold` (shells with an edge of 1 face or of more than 2 faces), `inside_out_bodies`, `inside_out_voids`, `degenerate_triangles_left_out`, `edges`, and `in_memory`: the model before it is written (`valid` from `BRepCheck_Analyzer`, `solids`, `smallest_solid_mm3`, `invalid_parts`). |
| `invalid_parts` | About the file read back: `null`, or (when `BRepCheck_Analyzer` says not valid) `{vertices, edges, faces, statuses, smallest_face_area_mm2, first_faces}`: how many parts of each kind it flags, the status names (for example `BadOrientationOfSubshape`), the smallest flagged face in mm2 and the first 5 flagged faces with their area and statuses. |
| `model` | What OpenCASCADE reads back: `solids`, `shells`, `faces`, `planar_faces`, `edges`, `vertices`, `free_edges`, `overshared_edges`. |
| `volume` | `stl_mm3`, `wrapped_mm3` (after the simplification), `step_mm3` (the read-back model), `step_vs_stl_mm3`, `step_vs_stl_pct`, `roundtrip_error` (relative, `step` against `wrapped`; a number with no state, the measured range is in 42.4). |
| `deviation` | `method: "sampled"`, `step_to_stl` and `stl_to_step`, each `{max_mm, mean_mm, points}` (42.3.1). |
| `checks`, `checks_failed` | 42.4. |
| `options` | Texts: what the user can do about a failed check (facts and options, no refusal). |
| `timing_s`, `cpu_s`, `peak_rss_bytes`, `peak_rss_mb_after_phase` | Seconds for each phase (`read_stl`, `simplify`, `build`, `merge`, `check_before_write`, `write`, `read_back`, `check`, `deviation`, `total`), CPU seconds of the process, peak memory. |
| `report_path` | Only in the reply: where the report is saved (next to the STEP file). |

**42.3.1 Distance.** The distance of the two surfaces is sampled, not exact: the vertices of each mesh (an even pick of at most 20,000) and 20,000 random area-weighted
points on its surface go to the nearest point on the other surface, in both directions (the surface of the STEP model is the read-back faces: a face with 3 edges is its own triangle, and the merged polygons are meshed by OpenCASCADE in batches of 20,000 faces). `max_mm` is the largest
sampled distance, so the true largest distance can be a little larger than the number in the report (a dense measure of `B0` at h/20 gave 0.170 mm against 0.159 mm sampled; over `B0` and `H0` the dense value was 0 to 7 percent more); `mean_mm` is the mean over the surface points. It is a fact of the file, not a limit.

### 42.4 Checks

Each check is `{"state": "pass" | "fail" | "unknown", "reason": text}`. No check has a threshold: a count is equal or not, a sign is positive or not, a text is the one that was asked for or not.
`before_write` looks at the model in memory, before the file is written. The other checks look at the file as OpenCASCADE reads it back.

| Check | Pass when |
|---|---|
| `read_back` | OpenCASCADE reads the file and finds a shape. (Without it only `before_write` is reported.) |
| `topology` | The read-back counts equal the counts of the build: solids = `build.bodies`, shells = `build.bodies + build.voids`. It sees a body or a void that did not reach the file. |
| `before_write` | `BRepCheck_Analyzer` says the model in memory is valid, the model has at least 1 solid, and the volume of every solid is positive. The analyzer does not see a solid with its faces turned inward (it says valid); the sign of the volume does. |
| `valid_solid` | `BRepCheck_Analyzer` says valid on the file as OpenCASCADE reads it, and the file holds at least 1 solid (a shell that is not closed is not a solid). |
| `closed` | Every edge joins exactly 2 faces (`model.free_edges` and `model.overshared_edges` are 0). When zero-area triangles were left out of the model, the reason says that the free edges can come from them. |
| `units` | The length unit that the file declares (`STEPControl_Reader.FileUnits`) is mm. The reader converts the geometry to mm when it reads, so the read-back volume is the same for a file in inches; only this check sees the unit. |
| `schema` | The schema in the file is the one asked for. |

**The volume has no check.** The number `volume.roundtrip_error` (the read-back volume against the volume of the wrapped mesh, relative) stays in the report. It was 4e-14 to 5e-9 over the runs of 42.7, and
exact to 1e-12 on a box, so a user can judge a value outside that range; no limit stands behind it. The difference to the STL, `volume.step_vs_stl_pct`, is a fact of the simplification.
The defects that a volume limit caught are caught by exact checks: a lost body or void by `topology`, a turned triangle or an inside-out solid by `before_write`, and a hollow or mixed-orientation mesh is oriented in the build (42.2 step 3).

**What `valid_solid` means.** The OpenCASCADE reader turns faces that point the wrong way when it reads (a box with one turned triangle is not valid in memory and valid after the read-back; the file holds the turned face).
So `valid_solid` and `closed` say that OpenCASCADE reads a valid solid, and another CAD reader can differ. `before_write` is the check of the model that was built.

A failed check is data: the file stays written, `checks_failed` lists the names, exit code 3, and `options` names what to try (`--no-merge-planes`, a larger `--tolerance-mm`).
The reply of the MCP tool has `ok: true` and `exit_code: 3` in this case: the tool ran.

### 42.5 `--estimate-only`

Simplifies the mesh (it does not build or write, and it does not load OpenCASCADE: it works before the install, and the report has `ocp: null`) and reports `estimate`: `faces` (the triangles after the simplification; an upper bound, because the merge removes 0.7 to 4 percent more on the public parts),
`step_bytes`, `seconds` (the whole command), `peak_rss_bytes` and `basis` (the text with the coefficients). The model is a fit to the runs of the table in 42.7 (weights 1/measured, so a small file
counts as much as a large one): the file is `1,100` bytes for each face (measured 1,038 to 1,135); the time is `1.3 s + 1.08 ms` for each face `+ 17.7 us` for each STL triangle; the peak memory is
`526 MB + 15.5 KB` for each face `+ 0.26 KB` for each STL triangle. The largest error of the fit over the 21 measured runs is 32 percent (the median 8 percent for the time and 6 percent for the memory; the estimate for the 565,276-triangle raw run is 28 percent below its measured time).
**This error is in-sample**: the 21 runs are the data of the fit, from 2 hook shapes and one loaded host, and **the worst errors are estimates that are too low** (time -32 percent, memory -27 percent). Out of sample, the estimate against the two larger runs of 42.7 (parts that this repository does not ship) was
+1 percent (part A) and -34 percent (part B) for the time, and +9 and +8 percent for the memory. For a memory decision on a 16 GB Mac, the low side is the risk. The runs were on one Linux x86_64 host with a load average of 10 to 18 on 22 threads (2 threads for the libraries), so the time is
the weak number and a Mac differs. The fit was made before the check `before_write` was added to the pipeline. That check takes 0.8 to 1.8 times as long as the `check` phase of the file, which is 9 to 19 percent of the total time in five runs after the change, and it adds no memory (the analyzer is released before the write;
the peak memory of those runs was 0.06 to 0.4 GB lower than before). On the public meshes the estimate was -40 to +10 percent against their measured time (the -40 percent is a run that took 38.5 s against 23.2 s before, on a host with a load average of 19: every phase was slower) and -9 to +21 percent against their measured memory. The fit is not made again.
Constants in `topopt/step.py`: `ESTIMATE_*`. No limit follows from the estimate; the user decides.

### 42.6 MCP tool `export_step`

`export_step(run_dir=None, part_only=False, tolerance_mm=None, merge_planes=True, schema="AP214", out=None, estimate_only=False)`. `run_dir` defaults to the current run of the session.
The tool starts `python -m topopt step <dir> --json ...` in a child Python (the interpreter of `TOPOPT_PYTHON`, else the server's own) and returns the report of 42.3 with
`ok`, `exit_code`, `run_dir_rel`, `report_path_rel` and `output.path_rel`, paths relative to `TOPOPT_WORKSPACE` where they lie inside it. Exit 0 and 3 are `ok: true`. Any other exit is
`{"ok": false, "error": ..., "exit_code": N}`: for exit 1 (a usage or input error) `error` is the whole message of topopt with its options; for exit 2, another code or a signal it is the last line of stderr (for a traceback, the exception),
and `signal` names the signal when the child process was killed (`SIGSEGV` for `exit_code` -11); `stdout_first_line` is added when the child wrote to stdout (the reply of an exit 0 with no JSON has it too). A missing extra adds `missing_extra: "step"`, `install_command` and `install_command_no_checkout`.
**The call is synchronous**: it returns when the file is written, and a large export holds the call for minutes (part B of 42.7 took 613 s). `estimate_only` gives the time before the work starts. A detached job that returns at once
and is polled (the pattern of `verify_run`) is a follow-up item, not part of this one. The tool text is under the 4,096-character
bound of `tests/test_plugin_manifest.py`; `INSTRUCTIONS` did not grow.

### 42.7 Measured (Linux x86_64)

**How.** Each row is one `python -m topopt step <run> --json` in its own process (so the peak memory is the peak of the whole command), with `MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 OMP_NUM_THREADS=2`,
`cadquery-ocp-novtk 7.9.3.1.1` (OCCT 7.9.3), Python 3.12.13, on an Intel Core Ultra 9 185H (22 threads, 64 GB) that had a load average of 10 to 18 from other jobs: the times are noisy upper values
(`cpu_s` in the report is within 5 percent of the time). The meshes are public: `B0` (the short hook, `h` 2.0 mm) and `H0` (the T-shirt hook, `h` 1.2 mm), both finished runs of the lever series, and
`H0-up3`, `H0-up4`, `H0-up5`: the post step of `H0` run again with `post.UPSAMPLE` 3, 4 and 5 (the same shape with finer triangles; 172,188, 322,438 and 565,276 triangles). "raw" is `--tolerance-mm 0 --no-merge-planes`:
every STL triangle is a face. "h/20" and "h/10" are the tolerance of the voxel size of the run divided by 20 and by 10; "merged planes" is the default merge. The distance is the largest of the two sampled directions (42.3.1).
