The two private rows are numbers from a run with the default setting on parts that are not in the repository (the files are not available here; both are valid closed solids and every check passed). They were run with the code
before fix round 1, which has no `before_write` phase. For part B `timing_s` was: `read_back` 281 s, `merge` 147 s, `write` 76 s, `check` 45 s, `deviation` 29 s. They are out-of-sample checks of the estimate (42.5):

| Part | Triangles in | Faces | Time measured / estimate | Peak memory measured / estimate | STEP file |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| larger part A (not shipped) | 529,876 | 85,103 | 102 s / 103 s (+1 %) | 1.83 GB / 1.99 GB (+9 %) | 94 MB / 94 MB |
| larger part B (not shipped) | 925,248 | 355,585 | 613 s / 402 s (-34 %) | 5.79 GB / 6.28 GB (+8 %) | 402 MB / 391 MB |

**Reading the table.**
- With the default setting (tolerance h/20, merged planes) the cost follows the number of faces after the simplification, and that follows the part, not the input size. On the public meshes (one shape at different triangle sizes) 20,586 to 565,276 triangles give
  9,017 to 35,558 faces, 10 to 39 MB, 12 to 39 s and 0.6 to 1.1 GB; the STL and the simplification take 0.4 to 0.9 GB of that, and the STEP phases add 0.08 to 0.6 GB. The tolerance h/20 moved the surface by at most 0.16 mm and the volume by -0.21 to +0.05 percent.
  **The cost does not stay flat on every part**: a larger part A (not shipped, 529,876 triangles) gave 85,103 faces, 102 s and 1.83 GB, and a larger part B (not shipped, 925,248 triangles) gave 355,585 faces, 613 s (10 minutes) and 5.79 GB. Use `--estimate-only` first for a part you have not exported.
- With every triangle kept the file is 1.04 to 1.13 KB for each face, the time 0.9 to 1.5 ms for each face, and the memory about 0.5 GB plus 15.5 KB for each face. The 565,276-triangle file is 641 MB and takes 14 minutes and 9.2 GB (measured phases: build 23 s, write 95 s,
  read back 598 s, check 75 s, distance 44 s; the memory is 6.8 GB after the write and 8.9 GB after the check). The first version meshed the whole model for the distance and peaked at 19.1 GB for the same file; the triangles of the model are now read directly.
  Nothing refuses a large mesh and no limit exists: `--estimate-only` gives these numbers before the work, and a tolerance above 0 brings the cost down to the default row. Not measured on a Mac.
- The merge of coplanar faces removes 0.7 to 4.1 percent of the faces. With the default setting it takes 0.2 to 2.0 s. On raw triangles the merge phase takes 0.9, 8.3, 42 and 130 s (8 to 34 percent more time) and adds no memory.
- `H0-up3` raw (172,188 triangles, no merge): `valid_solid` fails in both runs, and `invalid_parts` says: 1 face of 1.08e-8 mm2, status `BadOrientationOfSubshape`. The solid in memory before the write is valid (checked face by face with the same analyzer), the read-back volume
  matches the wrapped mesh to 2e-10, all edges join 2 faces, and the same mesh with merged planes passes. The file is written. The source is a needle triangle of the unsimplified marching-cubes mesh: one edge of 1.9e-6 mm and an area of about 1e-8 mm2 (that mesh has 512 edges shorter than 1e-5 mm, the shortest 2.4e-7 mm). The flagged face has the same normal as its mesh triangle, so the
  reader did not turn it. The options are in the report: a tolerance above 0 (the default), or the merge of coplanar faces.



### 42.8 Tests

`tests/test_step.py` (77 tests) and `tests/test_step_mcp.py` (14 tests); the marker `needs_ocp` (`tests/helpers.py`) skips the tests that write a STEP file when OpenCASCADE does not import. Run time on the measuring host:
91 tests in 32 s with `-n 2` on the measuring host (the hook export of the module fixture takes 17 s). The tests of the missing-extra message (a child Python in which `OCP` cannot be imported), of the import rule (`import topopt`, `topopt.cli` and
`topopt_mcp.server` do not load `OCP`), of the extra pin, of the estimate without the extra, and of the argument checks run without the extra. They cover: the exact volume of a box (6,000 mm3 to 1e-12) and a round trip; the recorded hook (a valid closed solid, the distance
within 2.5 times the tolerance, the volume within 2 percent, fewer faces with merged planes); a cavity (an inner shell of one solid), a cavity and a body written the wrong way round (`hollow_inverted`, a cavity written outward, `one_body_inverted`), a body in a cavity, two bodies (two solids), an inside-out body, and an open mesh (failed checks,
the file is still written, exit code 3); the keys of the CLI and MCP reports; `--part-only` (its own report), `--out` (a file or a folder; the input STL, `run.json`, `status.json` and the report of an earlier export give an error and stay as they were; `.step`, `.stp` and `.STEP` files are replaced; the report next to the file),
a folder without write access (before the work), a run folder without write access with `--out` elsewhere, a write error and a report error (`UserError` with the path), a tolerance that removes every triangle, `--schema AP242` and `ap-242`, `--estimate-only` (no file is written; no OpenCASCADE needed);
the run folder unchanged except the new outputs (a hash of the whole tree); the unit check on files in INCH, FOOT and metres; a rejected setting and a product name outside ASCII; the reason of `closed` for left-out triangles; and the failure replies of the MCP tool (a killed child, no JSON, an internal error, a usage error, another exit code).
Tests that take a check out on purpose: a body lost on the way to the file (`topology`, and the distance in the other direction), a void lost (`topology`), a read-back that the analyzer flags (`valid_solid`), a model in memory that is inside out (`before_write`).
Mutants of `topopt/step.py` (one change each, a fresh copy of the tree, both test files run on it): 27 mutants, and each one fails at least one test. They include the four that passed every test in the review
(no orientation fix: 5 tests fail; the read-back replaced by the model in memory: 8; the distance in one direction: 1; the analyzer ignored: 2 for the model in memory and 1 for the file), the checks `topology`, `units` and the sign of the volume taken out
(3, 3 and 1 tests), a unit of INCH (23), a swapped schema (28), a void that is not turned (3), a shell parity that is ignored (1), and the `--out` rules, the empty result, the write errors and the voxel-size source taken out (1 to 4 tests each).
The mutant without the write-access check is killed by a test that skips when the user is root (a folder with mode 500 is writable for root).

`tests/test_doctor.py` names `OpenCASCADE (OCP)`. On f86ac04 the two new files fail to import (`cannot import name 'step' from 'topopt'`) and the doctor test fails.


## 43. The registry of live topopt servers (added with P9-14)

Two topopt servers on one machine (two chats, a chat and a Code tab, two clients) do not know about each other. Two heavy runs at the same time
can use all the RAM of a 16 GB Mac and freeze it. Each server writes one small file in a folder of the user. A server that reads the folder
knows the other servers and the run folders that they started. The registry gives a FACT to the agent and to the user. It is not a lock: nothing
waits and nothing is refused. (A machine-wide lock is a later item of its own; the name `locks/` is reserved for it, 43.2.) Code:
`topopt/registry.py`. The module uses the standard library, `topopt.runinfo` and `topopt.runjob`, and it makes nothing at import.

### 43.1 The folder

One path for each platform. There is no chain of folders: two processes with different environments must see the same folder.

| System | Root folder |
|---|---|
| Linux | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/topopt`; `~/.local/state/topopt` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is not set. As the XDG rule says, an empty or relative value is not valid and counts as not set. |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/topopt` (`XDG_STATE_HOME` is not read) |
| any | the env var `TOPOPT_STATE_DIR` replaces the root folder (tests, unusual setups). A leading `~` is replaced, a relative path starts at the current folder, and an empty text means not set. |

The `~` (of the Linux default, the macOS path and a leading `~` of `TOPOPT_STATE_DIR`) is the home folder of the account database,
`pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir`, and NOT the env var `HOME`: a client may start a server with another `HOME`, and the two processes must see the same
folder. `Path.home()` is the fallback when the system has no `pwd` module, the uid has no entry (a container user), or the entry has no absolute folder.
EVERY topopt process of a user must see the same `XDG_STATE_HOME` and `TOPOPT_STATE_DIR`, or the registry is split: a server that has another value
writes in another folder, and the servers of the two folders do not see each other.

- `TOPOPT_STATE_DIR` is also the override of the per-user folder of `topopt gpu-check` (`gpu_mg.check.state_dir()`, section 20). That folder has
  another default (`~/.topopt`), and it is not changed here. With the variable set, the calibration file and `servers/` are in the same folder.
  The names do not collide: `gpu-check` writes `gpu-constants.json` at the root of the folder (`gpu_mg.check.CALIBRATION_FILE`), and the registry uses the
  folders `servers/` and the reserved `locks/` (43.2). A test checks it.
- Folders are made with the mode 0700 and files with the mode 0600. A folder that is there already is not changed. `write_atomic(path, data, mode=...)`
  of `topopt/runinfo.py` gives the file its mode from the start. It removes a `<name>.tmp` that is there already (also a link: the link goes, not its target) and makes the new one with `O_EXCL` and `O_NOFOLLOW`, so the data never goes through a link.
- When the folder cannot be made or written, the registry is OFF for this server. The reply says so as a fact: `other_servers_note` of
  `environment` starts with "The registry of topopt servers is off" and names the cause. When the root folder cannot be made, the note names
  the root folder and, if the cause is a file where a folder must be, says "a part of the path is a file" (with the text of the OS). The server writes one line to stderr and goes on. There is no
  other folder to fall back to. A later write (the next run start) tries again.
- The module reads the platform with `sys.platform`; the macOS branch is tested with a patched platform and has not run on a Mac.

### 43.2 Names

- `<root>/servers/` holds the entries (43.3). This item writes it.
- `<root>/locks/` is RESERVED for the later machine-wide lock (a `flock` file and a record of the holder). This item does not make it, and nothing
  reads it.

### 43.3 The entry of one server

One file for each server process: `<root>/servers/server-<pid>.json`. JSON, format 1:

```json
{"format": 1, "kind": "mcp_server", "pid": 4242,
 "process_start": 1792800000.12, "process_start_ticks": 123456789, "boot_id": "7b0c...",
 "started_utc": "2026-10-23T22:30:11Z", "work_folder": "/Users/<user>/Documents/topopt",
 "topopt_version": "0.1.0", "code_folder": "/Users/<user>/topopt", "python": "/Users/<user>/topopt/.plugin-env/venv/bin/python",
 "run_dirs": ["/Users/<user>/Documents/topopt/runs/hook"],
 "run_processes": [{"run_dir": "/Users/<user>/Documents/topopt/runs/hook", "pid": 4310,
                    "process_start": 1792800100.5, "process_start_ticks": 123459999, "boot_id": "7b0c..."}]}
```

- `kind` is the kind of the start (`mcp_server` now). `pid` and the keys of `runjob.process_identity(pid)` (`process_start`; on Linux also
  `process_start_ticks` and `boot_id`) tell the process from another process that gets the same pid later. `started_utc` is the time that the server
  imported its module (the `server.started_utc` of `environment`).
- `run_dirs`: EVERY run folder that this server started a run in, in start order, with no cap (a server lives for a short time). It is rewritten at
  each run start. A run folder that was refused is not added.
- `run_processes`: for each run that this server started, the run folder and the process identity of the run process: `run_dir`, `pid` (the pid of the
  process that `run_topopt` started, `proc.pid`) and the keys of `runjob.process_identity(pid)`. It is an identity, not run state. It is rewritten at each
  run start, with no cap, and a process is listed once. It stays next to `run_dirs`, which is unchanged. A job in a run folder counts for an entry only
  when the process that holds its job lock is a process of that entry (`registry.same_process`: the same pid, and the same start ticks and boot id on
  Linux, else start times that differ by `START_TOLERANCE_S` at most). Two servers can name one folder (the default run folder is the same for the chats of
  one user); the job there is the job of the server that started it, and of no other.
- Written with `runinfo.write_atomic` (a reader sees the old file or the new file) at the start of the server (`main()`, after the work folder is
  known), rewritten at each run start, and removed at a clean exit (`atexit`) UNLESS a run process that this server started is still there (43.4). A process
  that ends by a signal or a crash leaves its file: a reader finds the process dead, and deletes the file when no run process of that server is there. A reused
  pid overwrites the stale file of the same pid. A forked child does not remove the file.
- The registry holds no run state. The state of a run is read from the job files of its run folder (section 24.1): one truth.

### 43.4 Liveness and the reader

`runjob.identity_state(rec)` gives the state of the process of an entry (24.1):

| State | Meaning | The reader |
|---|---|---|
| `live` | the pid exists and its start time is the recorded one | lists it |
| `unconfirmed` | the pid exists, but there is no start time to compare | lists it, with the note "may be stale" |
| `dead` | no such process | lists it, with the note "no longer running", while a run process that it started is still there; else deletes the file and does not list it |
| `reused` | the pid exists, but it is another process | the same as `dead` |

A run process lives on after the server that started it (it has its own session). So a closed chat can leave a heavy run that still uses the RAM.
The registry keeps that run in sight, with no number and no wait. The rule is about the PROCESS that the entry names (`run_processes`, 43.3), not about the
job files of a run folder:
- At a clean exit, the `atexit` function (`Registration.remove`) keeps the entry while a run process of this server is still there (`identity_state` of the
  recorded process is `live` or `unconfirmed`). Else it deletes the entry. This holds also before the run process has taken its job lock, so a server that
  ends just after the start of a run does not lose its run. If the system refuses a recorded pid, the entry is kept (not sure).
- The reader deletes the file of a server that is `dead` or `reused` only when no run process of that server is there. This also covers a server that a
  signal ended (`atexit` did not run). A server that has ended and has a run process that is there is listed with its state (`dead` or `reused`), and its
  running job counts for the fact of `run_topopt` (43.5).
- When the processes have ended, the next reader deletes the file. Nobody else deletes it. The rule is about the process, not about the job: a run that is done
  but whose process stays on (`topopt run --dashboard` serves the result until the process is stopped) keeps the entry of an ended server. The entry then shows
  the job state `done`, and there is no fact of a running job.
- A job in a run folder counts for an entry only if the holder of its job lock is a process of that entry (43.3). The state of the job still comes from the job
  files (`runjob.job_facts`), and the registry holds no run state. The `runs` item of a folder whose job is a job of another process has `job_state` null.

`registry.read_servers(own_pid=None, root=None)` returns `Others(servers, notes)` and never raises.
- It skips its own pid. It never says that a server is live when it cannot confirm it.
- It deletes the file of a server that is confirmed `dead` or `reused` and has no run process that is there, and nothing else. A file that a new server with the same
  pid has replaced since the read is kept (the inode and the modification time are compared before the delete).
- It reads only a regular file with the exact name `server-{pid}.json`, where `pid` is the pid in the file (the name that `Registration` writes). A name that
  looks like an entry but is not that name (a leading zero, non-ASCII digits), and a name that is not a regular file (a link, a folder), is a note and is never
  read through or deleted. A name that does not look like an entry (for example `.tmp`) is ignored.
- A file that cannot be read or parsed, that has another format, or whose pid is not the pid of its name is a note in `notes`, not an error; the other
  files are read. A missing folder is no note. The reader makes no folder.
- There is no TTL, no expiry and no other new number.

### 43.5 The reply keys

`environment` (the MCP tool, not `environment_data`) adds:
- `other_servers`: a list with one item for each listed entry; `[]` when there is none. An item has `pid`, `state` (`live`, `unconfirmed`, or `dead` /
  `reused` for a server that has ended while its run process is still there, 43.4), `kind`,
  `started_utc`, `work_folder`, `topopt_version`, `code_folder`, `python` and `runs`; an `unconfirmed` item also has `note` ("may be stale"), and a `dead` or
  `reused` item has `note` ("no longer running"). `runs`
  has one item for each absolute folder of `run_dirs`: `run_dir`, `job_state` (the `state` of `runjob.job_facts`: `running`, `done`, `stopped`, `failed`,
  `stale_lock`, `unfinished`; null if the folder has no job record, or if its job is not a job of a process of this entry, 43.3), `pid`, `started_at`, `summary`
  (for a job of another process: "the job record in this folder (pid P) is not a job that this server started") and `memory_estimate_gib` (for a running job: the
  `derived.memory_estimate_gib` of its `run.json`; null if the run has not written it yet, and for any other job).
- `other_servers_note` (only when there is something to say): the registry is off for this server (43.1), or a file was not read (43.4).

`run_topopt` adds `other_server_jobs` when a listed server (also an `unconfirmed` one, and a server that has ended) has a running job. It is a FACT in a reply
to a run that has started, not a stop: `fact` ("A job that another topopt server started is running now: pid P in RUN_DIR (started by server S, ...)", with
"(no longer running)" after the server when it has ended and "may be stale" for an `unconfirmed` one; the memory estimate if the run folder has one; the RAM of
this machine; "Two heavy jobs at the same time can use all the RAM, and the machine can freeze"), `jobs` (`server_pid`, `server_state`, `work_folder`, `run_dir`, `pid`, `started_at`, `memory_estimate_gib`),
`ram` (`total_bytes`, `available_bytes` as in `environment.ram`) and `options` (wait, stop the other job with `stop_run` and its `run_dir`, or run both).
The key is not in the reply when no other listed server has a running job. There is no new limit: the agent decides with the facts.

The tool texts: the key guide of `environment` (`topopt://replies/environment`, since #174) has the sentence for `other_servers`; the description stays at or under 4,096 characters. The description of `run_topopt`
does not name `other_server_jobs`: the key describes itself with `fact` and `options`, and the characters of that description are left to other items.

### 43.6 Not in this item

- A run that the CLI started (`topopt run` in a terminal) has no server, so the registry does not show it. The later route is the process scan of the
  host info (`hostinfo.topopt_processes`).
- A run that no registry entry names: a run of a server whose entry was lost (a reused pid that a new server took over overwrites the stale file of the same
  pid, with its own `run_dirs` and `run_processes`), and a run of a server that is killed in the moment between the start of the run process and the write of
  its entry. The process scan of the host info is the route. (The old gap of a run that has not taken the job lock yet is closed: the entry names the process.)
- A pid that another process takes: `same_process` and `identity_state` compare the start time, so they see it, except where the system gives no start time
  and the pid decides.
- The `locks/` folder and the machine-wide lock (43.2).

### 43.7 Tests

`tests/test_registry.py` (the folder rule on Linux and macOS, the override, a folder that cannot be written, the entry, the modes, the atomic write,
the states live, dead, reused and unconfirmed, the job state of the run folders, a server that has ended while its run process is still there: the entry stays at
the exit, also before the run takes its job lock, and the reader lists it, keeps the file and deletes it when the process has ended; two entries that name one folder, where the
job counts only for the server that started it; names that are not `server-{pid}.json` and links; the runner that sets `XDG_STATE_HOME`), `tests/test_registry_mcp.py` (the entry of the server, `environment.other_servers`,
the fact of `run_topopt`, two real servers over stdio, and a run that goes on after its server has ended, with the stand-in `tests/hold_job_fake.py`) and, in `tests/test_runjob.py`, `identity_state` and a test that `holder_state` gives the same
answers as before. `tests/conftest.py` sets `TOPOPT_STATE_DIR` for every test, also in the default environment of a server that a test starts over stdio
(the MCP SDK passes only a few variables to such a server), and removes `XDG_STATE_HOME` (a test of the XDG rule sets it itself), so no test reads or writes the
registry folder of the user.

## 44. Partial results and the list of checks that did not run (added with TC-2)

A report of several sub-checks writes the failure or the skip of a sub-check as a fact in the record of that sub-check, and the other sub-checks go on. That stays.
Before TC-2 no key of the whole report said that a sub-check had failed or had not run. A reader had to open every record, and a summary that quotes only the numbers
that exist read as clean. Three reports now have two keys: `topopt verify` (`verify.json`, section 16), the `print` section of `metrics.json` (section 18) and `topopt printcheck`
(section 32). One module builds them from the records that exist: `topopt/check_coverage.py`. It runs no check again. It adds no number, no limit, no exit code and no gate.

### 44.1 The two keys

- `partial` (true or false): true only when a sub-check that the inputs ask for failed or did not run.
- `coverage`, a mapping with three lists. Each sub-check is in exactly one of them, in the order of the report:
  - `ran`: the names of the sub-checks that ran.
  - `failed`: a list of `{name, reason}`: a sub-check that the inputs ask for and that stopped with an error.
  - `not_run`: a list of `{name, reason, asked}`: a sub-check that gave no result. `asked` is false when the inputs do not ask for it (for example, the YAML has no bore). It is listed, and it
    does NOT make the report partial. `asked` true makes it partial.
- `reason` is the text of the record: the `message` of an error, else the first fact of a skip, else the reason code. With several mesh sizes (`--levels`) the worst level decides, and the reason starts with `mesh size X mm:`.
- Place: right after `kind` in `verify.json`, right after `ok` in the `print` section and in the report of `topopt printcheck`. A report from before TC-2 has neither key, and a reader ignores a key that is not there. `format` stays 1.
- `partial` is a fact about the report. It does not change an exit code, the gate (`--gate`), the ratchet rules or any number. The other numbers of a partial report stand.
- `topopt verify --estimate-only` has neither key: nothing was checked.

### 44.2 The sub-checks

| Report | Sub-check | Asked when | `failed` when | `not_run` and asked when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| verify | `stress` | always | (a failure stops verify: `status.json` has the state `error` and there is no `verify.json`) | never |
| verify | `supports` | the YAML has a joint or a spring | (stops verify, as `stress`) | the result has no record |
| verify | `buckling` | `buckling.check` is on in the YAML, or the call turns it on | the record has `status: error`, or a load case has `status: error` or a rigid-body test with `status: error` | `status: skipped` (for example the memory rule), or a case that did not converge or ran out of time |
| verify | `motion` | `limits.displacement` or `limits.alignment` has a row | `status: error` | `status: skipped` |
| verify | `bore_facts` | the YAML has `bore_checks` and the call does not turn it off | an entry has `status: error` | an entry has `status: empty` (no wall facet or no sample point) |
| verify | `goodman` | `bore_checks` has a `goodman` block | `status: error` | `status: skipped` (for example no bore has a sample set) |
| verify | `pressfit` | `bore_checks` has a `press_fit` block | `status: error` | `status: skipped` |
| verify | `gate` | the call has `--gate` | never (a gate that fails is a verdict: the check ran) | the result has no `gate` |
| print report | `bed_fit`, `overhang`, `plate_contact` | always (one measure of the configured direction) | the whole report fails: see 44.4 | never |
| print report | `support_volume` | the printer type needs support | the whole report fails | never. `asked` is false for a printer type that needs none (`sls`) |
| print report | `thinnest_member` | always | `thinnest_member.error` is there | no chord could be measured on the mesh |
| print check | the eight checks of section 32 | always | the record has `error` | the state is `unknown`, the check has a limit, and it could not decide (a mesh that is not closed, a limit above the chord cap, a limit under 3 x the resolution), or no chord was measured. `support_volume` for a printer type that needs no support is `not_run` with `asked` false |

A check with the state `unknown` and no limit in the `print` block is `ran`: the value is a fact, and the inputs ask for no verdict. A sub-check that the inputs do not ask for is only counted in the text ("6 not asked"): its name and reason are in the record.

### 44.3 The text line

One line near the top of the text of `topopt verify` (line 2), of `topopt printcheck` (line 2) and of `tools/print_section.py` (line 2). It is made by `check_coverage.line`; the reason is cut at its first sentence (the whole text is in the record):

```
partial: no; 1 of 1 checks ran (stress); 7 not asked
partial: 1 of 2 checks failed (buckling: RuntimeError: phase 33 error -4); ran: stress; 6 not asked
partial: 1 of 2 checks not run (buckling: The memory estimate with the check is 9 GB, above the limit 8 GB); ran: stress; 6 not asked
```

When the verify result is partial, the same line is also the first `plain:` line. The line never names a sub-check that the inputs do not ask for.

### 44.4 Failure inside a report

- Print report: the thinnest-member estimate is isolated (`print_report.thickness_failed`). A failure gives the shape of a block with no chord plus `error`, and `coverage.failed` names `thinnest_member`; the other numbers stay.
  Any other failure gives `{"ok": false, "error": "<text>", "partial": true, "coverage": {"ran": [], "failed": [{"name": "print_report", "reason": "<text>"}], "not_run": []}}`, and the run goes on as before.
- Print check: `printcheck.check(..., contain_errors=True)` records a stage or a check that raises as a record with the state `unknown` and the key `error` (44.2). A stage that stops names all checks that read it:
  `mesh health` (`mesh_closed`, `bodies`, `closed_voids`, `wall_thickness`), `build-direction numbers` (`bed_fit`, `overhang`, `support_volume`, `plate_contact`, `wall_thickness`), `thickness estimate` (`wall_thickness`).
  The reason starts with the name of the stage. The default is `contain_errors=False`: the exception passes to the caller. The ratchet calls `check(strict=True)` and reads an exception as a failure of the tool, so its behaviour does not change.
  The CLI (`topopt printcheck`) prints the whole report and then exits with code 2 (an internal error) when a check has `error`, with and without
  `--strict`, as when such a check stopped the command before; stderr names the checks. The MCP tool `print_check` returns the report.
- Verify: a failure of a sub-check was and is a fact in its own record (`status: error`); verify goes on, and `exit_code` does not follow `partial`.

### 44.5 Where the record is quoted

- MCP `verify_status`: `partial` and `coverage` are keys of the reply (section 16). `run_result`: `metrics.print.partial` and `metrics.print.coverage`; `metrics.stress.cases.<case>.independent_check.verify_partial` and `verify_coverage`
  (only when the P2 value was found and `verify.json` has the keys), and one sentence in the `summary` of the case (section 17). `print_check` has both keys (section 32). `verify_run` (a real run) returns at once and has no result: its description lists the keys of the result.
- A reader of a file from before TC-2 (no `partial` and no `coverage`) gets the text and the keys as before.

### 44.6 Tests

`tests/test_check_coverage.py` (the module on made-up records), `tests/test_verify_coverage.py` (the recorded hook run: a clean run, a forced failure of the buckling check, of the motion rows and of a bore, a memory skip, the gate, two mesh sizes, `--estimate-only`),
`tests/test_printcheck_coverage.py` and `tests/test_print_coverage.py` (a clean report, a forced failure of one check, of a stage and of the whole report, a check that is not asked for, a limit that cannot decide, the text line, the command and the MCP tool),
and the cases in `tests/test_verify_mcp.py` (`verify_status`) and `tests/test_stress_report.py` (`independent_check` and the case summary).

## 45. find_features: the holes, bosses and flat faces of an STL (added with I2, part 1 of #151)

Code: `topopt/features.py` (the engine), the MCP tool `find_features` (`topopt_mcp/server.py`), tests `tests/test_find_features.py`. There is no CLI command and no YAML key.

A user who has an STL of the part says "keep the screw holes". Today the agent has to find the holes by hand. `find_features(stl)` reads the STL and lists what a person
sees: the cylindrical holes (axis, radius, length, through or blind), the convex cylinders (bosses) and the flat faces (outward normal, area). It is a read:
the file is not changed, nothing is written and no work folder is made. It repairs nothing (a mesh that is not closed gives a fact). It gives facts and options; the
agent decides what a hole is for. All values are mm (an STL has no unit; the engine reads every STL as mm, as everywhere in topopt) and unit vectors.

**Call.** The tool is `find_features(stl_path)`. A relative path starts at the work folder (as `render_part` and `print_check`). The Python function is
`topopt.features.find_features(stl, *, smooth_angle_deg, flat_angle_deg, fit_residual_frac, axis_normal_deg, arc_min_deg, flat_min_area_mm2, flat_soft_share_max)`: `stl` is a path
or a `trimesh` mesh, and each number is a keyword argument whose default is the module constant of the same name in capitals. The tool passes none of them; a tool
argument for a number is one more name in the signature of the tool and one more line in the dict `options` of the tool function. A file that is not there, a folder, a
file that is not an STL (the check of the bytes is the one of the print check), an empty mesh, and a number that is not valid give `UserError`; the tool returns
`{"ok": false, "error": "<one line>"}`, with the work folder and the way to change it added to "file not found".

**Reply.**

| key | content |
|---|---|
| `ok` | `true` |
| `mesh` | `source`, `source_rel` (tool only; relative to the work folder when inside it), `faces`, `vertices`, `unit` (text), `watertight`, `winding_consistent`, `normals_flipped`, `zero_area_faces`, `bounds_mm` (min, max), `size_mm`, `volume_mm3` (null when not watertight) |
| `holes` | the cylindrical holes (below), ordered by `radius_mm`, then by the centre (x, y, z), both rounded to 0.001 mm. Ids `H1`, `H2`, ... in that order |
| `bosses` | the convex cylinders, the same keys as a hole without `depth` and `ends`. Ids `B1`, ... |
| `flat_faces` | the planar regions (below), the largest `area_mm2` first, then by the centroid. Ids `F1`, ... |
| `method` | `numbers` (every number of the detection and the value that was used), `counts` (smooth regions, candidates, cylinders, rejected, arcs and flat regions that are not listed), `text` |
| `facts` | plain sentences: a mesh that is not closed, winding, inverted normals, a hole near a limit of the method, a stepped hole, regions that were left out and why |
| `timing_s` | seconds |

A **hole** has: `id`; `point` (the centre of the first end face), `axis` (unit vector from `point` along the cylinder), `radius_mm`, `length_mm` and `end_point` (`point + length_mm *
axis`); `diameter_mm`; `depth` and `ends`; `arc_deg` (the angle of the circle that the faces cover) and `closed_ring`; `segments` (the number of facets round the circle) and
`chord_sag_mm` (`radius * (1 - cos(pi / segments))`: a facet wall lies that far inside the radius); `area_mm2` and `faces` (the wall); `fit` (`rms_mm` and `max_mm`: the distance of the wall
vertices to the circle; `normal_deviation_deg`: the largest angle of a face normal to the plane across the axis); `coaxial_with` (the ids of the other holes on the same axis).
The keys `point`, `axis`, `radius_mm` and `length_mm` are the keys of an interface `bore` (section 23), with the same meaning and units: a hole is a `bore` with those four values. For a
`tube` (section 23) around a hole, `inner_radius_mm` is the `radius_mm` of the hole, `radius_mm` (the outer wall) is a choice, and `point`, `axis` and `length_mm` are the same. A **flat face** has `id`, `normal` (unit,
outward), `area_mm2`, `centroid` (the area-weighted centre of its faces), `offset_mm` (`normal . x` for a point `x` of the plane), `faces` and `max_normal_deviation_deg`.

**The axis direction.** A blind hole has its axis from the open end to the closed end (the direction of the drill). Any other cylinder has the sign that makes the largest
component of `axis` positive. `ends` has the state of the end at `point` first.

**Method.** (1) The STL is read as the file holds it: float32 vertices, equal vertices joined, no repair. Neighbour faces share an edge. A face with an area under 1e-12 mm2 has no normal and is left out. The
normals are made outward by the sign of the volume of the mesh. (2) A *smooth region* is a set of faces that neighbour angles of at most `smooth_angle_deg` join. (3) A smooth region is a
*cylinder* when every face normal is within `axis_normal_deg` of the plane across one axis (the axis is the direction of the smallest normal scatter, area weighted) and the vertices
projected on that plane lie on one circle: the RMS distance to the least-squares circle is at most `fit_residual_frac` of the radius. The radius is the radius of the wall vertices. (4) The
faces cover an angle of the circle (the union of the angular spans of the faces). A cylinder is listed when it covers at least `arc_min_deg`. A smaller one is an arc (a fillet, the end of a slot); it
is counted in `method.counts.arcs_not_listed` and the facts. (5) *Hole or boss*: the sum of the area times the face normal along the direction away from the axis is negative for a hole (the
normals point to the axis, the material is outside the cylinder) and positive for a boss. (6) A *flat region* is a set of faces that neighbour angles of at most `flat_angle_deg` join, and each
face is within `flat_angle_deg` of the region normal. It is a flat face when no listed or unlisted cylinder owns it, its area is at least `flat_min_area_mm2`, and at most `flat_soft_share_max` of its
boundary length joins a neighbour by a soft edge (an angle above `flat_angle_deg` and at most `smooth_angle_deg`). The facets of a sphere are soft on all sides; the faces of a box are hard on all sides.

**Through or blind.** For each end of a hole wall, the faces across the rim edges vote: the sum of the edge length times the face normal along the axis direction that leaves the hole (the
direction away from the wall at that end). A positive sum: the surface leads away from the hole and the end is `open`. A negative sum: the surface closes the end (`closed`: a flat or cone bottom, a step).
`depth` is `through` for two open ends, `blind` for one closed end, `closed` for two closed ends (a cavity), `unknown` for an end with no vote (the mesh is open there). This reads the rim only. A stepped
hole (a counterbore) is two cylinders on one axis. The big one has a closed end at the step and reports `blind`. The small one reports `through`. Each names the other in `coaxial_with`
(parallel within `axis_normal_deg`, and the axis lines closer than `fit_residual_frac` of the smaller radius).

**The numbers.** Each is a module constant in `topopt/features.py` with a comment, a keyword argument of the function and a key of `method.numbers`. The effects below were measured on plates
built with manifold3d and on the recorded hook (`final.stl` of the recorded run, 85,610 faces).

| number | value | meaning and measured effect |
|---|---|---|
| `smooth_angle_deg` | 30 | Neighbour faces up to this angle are one smooth region. A ring of `n` segments has 360/n degrees between wall facets, so 30 finds `n >= 12`; at 15 only `n >= 24`, at 10 only `n >= 64`. The edge wall to plate (90 degrees) and a 45 degree chamfer split at 30 and merge at 45 or more (then the hole is lost). A concave fillet at the mouth (steps of 11 degrees) merges at every value from 10 up: that hole is not found |
| `flat_angle_deg` | 1 | A flat region stays within this angle of its normal. A plane with vertex noise of 0.001 mm on 2 mm facets (0.04 degrees) is flat at 0.5 and more; with 0.02 mm (0.8 degrees) it needs 5. A panel with a radius of 500 mm over 40 mm width (2.3 degrees) is flat at 5 and not at 1 |
| `fit_residual_frac` | 0.01 | RMS distance of the wall vertices to the circle, as a share of the radius. A tessellated wall has 0 (below 1e-5 mm). Radial vertex noise of 0.3 percent of the radius gives 0.27 percent; 1 percent noise gives 0.9 percent and 1.7 degrees of normal deviation; 3 percent noise splits the wall into regions (not found at any value) |
| `axis_normal_deg` | 2 | Largest angle of a face normal to the plane across the axis. A taper (draft) of 0.25 degrees on a 10 mm deep hole is a cylinder; 0.5 degrees is not (the fit residual fails first: 1.4 percent of the radius at 0.5 degrees) at any value up to 10; with `fit_residual_frac` 0.1 a draft of 1 degree needs 1 and 3 degrees needs 5 |
| `arc_min_deg` | 180 | Smallest angle of the circle that the faces cover. A closed ring covers 360. A half-round notch on a plate edge covers 180: listed at 180 and less, an arc above it. Corner fillets that join the straight sides tangentially are not separate regions |
| `flat_min_area_mm2` | 1 | Smallest flat face that is listed. On the recorded hook: 237 flat faces at 0, 131 at 0.1, 15 at 1, 8 at 10, 0 at 100. The count and the area of the left-out regions are in `facts` |
| `flat_soft_share_max` | 0.5 | Share of the boundary of a flat region that may be soft. A ladle bowl of 3,360 faces: 1 flat face at 0.5 or less, 81 at 0.75, 2,841 at 1 (every facet of the curved bowl). The recorded hook: 2 at 0, 15 at 0.5, 99 at 1 |
| `near_limit_share` | 0.5 | Only for a fact: a value above this share of its limit is named as near the limit. It changes nothing that is found |
| `angle_eps_rad` | 1e-6 | Rounding of an angle: a ring of 12 segments has exactly 30 degrees between facets and passes the limit 30. It also closes a gap of the angular cover. Not a user number |
| `zero_area_mm2` | 1e-12 | A face with a smaller area is left out (the number of the print check) |

There is no smallest hole radius: a hole of any size is listed with its radius and fit, and the agent filters. On the recorded hook (free form, 85,610 faces) the method lists 1 hole and no
boss, and on a sphere of 1.3 million faces none.

**Accuracy** (measured, STL as a float32 file). The wall vertices of a tessellated cylinder are on its radius, and the fit returns that radius: within 5e-5 mm (the rounding of the reply is 1e-4 mm) for a radius from 0.1 to 50 mm, with 32
segments or the interface rule of section 23, at the origin and at 1000 mm from it. A plate rotated by a random matrix: the axis within 5e-5 degrees, the centre within 7e-5 mm, 40 cases. A mesh with a facet wall
of fewer segments reports the radius of the vertices, so the area of the hole is smaller than the cylinder by `chord_sag_mm` at most.

**Limits of the method.** (1) A hole whose wall joins a fillet or a shallow chamfer (all neighbour angles within `smooth_angle_deg`) is one smooth region that is not a cylinder: the hole is not found, the flat
faces next to it may be missing, and `facts` counts the smooth regions that are neither a cylinder nor flat. (2) A tapered hole, a slot (planes and half cylinders that meet tangentially) and a rounded
outline are not cylinders. (3) The sign of the normals decides hole or boss: a mesh whose faces do not agree (winding not consistent) can give a hole as a boss; this is a fact. (4) `through` is a
statement about the rim of the wall, not about the line of sight along the axis. (5) A flat face that is a single smooth region with a curved neighbour that joins it tangentially is not listed. (6) The mesh is not
repaired: an open edge in a wall can hide the hole.

**Time and memory.** There is no limit on the number of faces. A perforated plate of 925,212 faces with 900 holes took 3.7 s (peak 0.83 GB) with the read of the file; a sphere of 1,310,720 faces took 4.4 s (1.1 GB); the recorded hook 0.24 s. The memory is about 0.9 KB for each face. The tool runs in the server process and holds the call while it works. The reply grows with the number of holes: about 350 bytes for each hole (900 holes: 330 KB).

**Tests.** `tests/test_find_features.py`: the plate with two holes, the box, the faces of the plate, a blind hole, a boss, a stepped hole, a plate rotated by a general rotation, 16, 24 and 128 segments, radius from 1 to 20 mm,
a far part, what is not a hole (a taper, a sphere, a notch, a wall with a small chamfer), the limit of the angle between wall facets, a curved face and `flat_angle_deg`, an order that does not depend on the face order, an open mesh, inverted normals, wrong files, the numbers (constant, keyword default, key of the reply, valid range), the MCP tool
(a relative path, read only, the error form, the text within the bound and with no habitual cap, the mock equal to the server) and the entry in `READ_ONLY_TOOLS` (section 41).

### 45.1 The `stl` kind of `build_regions` (part 2 of #151)

Code: `topopt/regions_builder.py` (`make_stl`, `_plug_holes`, `_check_plugs`), tests `tests/test_stl_region_kind.py`. This kind is a solid in the **region spec** of `build_regions`. It is not the `stl` kind of the YAML block `interfaces` (section 23): that one
unites or cuts a finished solid after the run and is not read by `build_regions`.

A user who has an STL of the part says "here is my part, keep the screw holes, make it lighter". The spec item gives the part as a region, with its holes plugged where the
user wants the optimizer to add material.

**The item.** `{stl: {path: <file>, plug_holes: [H1, H3] | all}}` is one item of a region, like `box` or `cylinder`. It works in every role (`design`, `fixed`, `load`, `solid`,
`keep_out`), it joins the other items of its region (union: a growth box is one more item, for example `[{stl: ...}, {box: ...}]`), and it can stand inside `subtract`
(`{subtract: {stl: {path: cutter.stl}}}`). The keys are `path` (required, text) and `plug_holes` (optional), and, since section 45.2, `screw_holes` and `ring_mm` (optional). Any other key is a `SpecError` (a misspelled key is not dropped
without a word). The shape walk of section 10 (`check_spec_shape`) checks the types before anything is read: a `path` that is not text, a `plug_holes` that is not a list of
texts or `all`, an `stl` that is not a mapping.

**The path.** An absolute path is used as it is. A relative path starts at the **work folder** for the MCP tool `build_regions` (`build_in_workspace`), at the **folder of the spec
file** for the CLI (`regions_builder.main`; the YAML loader reads a region path the same way), and at the **current folder** for a caller of `build_spec` or `build_all` that gives
no `base`. The STL is read as the file holds it (float32 vertices; equal vertices are one vertex), in mm: an STL has no unit and the report line gives the size in mm, so a part in
metres shows as a tiny size.

**A mesh that cannot be used.** The builder does not repair a mesh (that is #159). A file that is not there, a folder, a file that is not an STL, an empty file, a mesh that
is not a closed solid (open edges, edges with more than 2 faces), a mesh whose neighbour faces do not agree on the winding, a mesh with inward faces (negative volume), a mesh
that `manifold3d` refuses and a mesh with no volume give a `SpecError`. The text is one line: the key path in the spec, the file as the spec gives it, and the cause, for example
`regions.design[0].stl.path: plate.stl: the mesh is not a closed solid (2 open edges, 0 edges with more than 2 faces). The builder does not repair a mesh`. For a file that is not
there, the cause names the place that was looked at and where a relative path starts. Through the MCP tool the reply is `{"ok": false, "error": <that line>}`; the CLI prints
`SPEC ERROR: <that line>`.

**Plugging holes.** `plug_holes` names holes of `find_features` (section 45) on the same file, with the default numbers: a list of ids (`H1`, ...) or `all` (every hole in the
list of `find_features`, also an arc and a cavity). The ids are stable for one file and one set of numbers, so the agent calls `find_features` first and reads the ids there. An
unknown id is a `SpecError` that lists the known ids with their size (`H1 (d 4 mm, 4 mm long, through)`). A repeated id plugs once; `[]` plugs nothing. Without `plug_holes` the
builder does not run `find_features` (the cost is the cost of the read).

The **plug** of a hole is the convex hull of its wall vertices. A wall vertex is a vertex of the mesh on the cylinder of the hole (axis, radius, `point`, `length_mm` from the
reply of `find_features`) between its two ends. The part is united with the plugs (`Manifold.batch_boolean`, one call). Why the hull and not a cylinder of the builder:
the plug has the same vertices as the wall, so (1) no thin skin of void stays at the facets of the wall, (2) the ends of the plug lie in the faces of the part, so no material is
added outside the part, and (3) the plug takes the facets of the file as they are, for any number of segments and any phase. A cylinder with the radius of the hole and its own
segments leaves 0.04 to 1.17 mm3 of void in a hole of radius 5 mm (16 to 128 segments; with the phase of the facets turned by half a facet, up to 3.0 mm3); the hull leaves
0 to 1.2e-5 mm3 (the float32 rounding of the file). A cylinder with a radius above the hole (R / cos(pi / n)) closes the skin, but it needs the plane of each end from the
rounded `point` and `axis` of the reply, so it does not meet the faces of a rotated part.

The **tolerance of the wall test** has no number of its own. It is the largest fit distance of the hole (`fit.max_mm`) plus the rounding of the reply of `find_features`:
`WALL_ROUND_MM = 2 * 10^-MM_DIGITS` (the `point` and `radius_mm` are rounded to 0.1 micrometre, at most 0.14 micrometre together) plus `WALL_AXIS_PER_MM = 10^-UNIT_DIGITS` for each mm of
`length_mm` (the unit `axis` has 6 digits). Measured (plates of 16, 24, 64 and 128 segments, at the origin, rotated and moved, and rotated at 300 mm): all wall vertices are found from
this tolerance up to 500 times more (0.1 mm); at a quarter of it a rotated part at 300 mm (64 segments) loses 1 of 256 vertices, at a tenth 76 (table in the report).

**What stays.** The plug fills the cylinder wall from `point` to `end_point`. A hole that is not a prism with flat ends is filled to the end of its wall only: a chamfer or a
countersink at the mouth stays as a dimple, and the cone of a drill point stays as a closed cavity inside the part (the report has a `WARNING:` line with the volume of each new inner
void). A blind hole keeps its bottom. An arc (a notch, `closed_ring` false) is filled up to the chord of the arc: flush with the face when the chord lies in it, and the report has a
`note:` line with the angle. A cavity (`depth` closed) is filled and the report has a `note:` line.

**Checks after the plug.** (1) A face that part 1 would call wall (all vertices within `FIT_RESIDUAL_FRAC` of the radius from the cylinder, normal across the axis within
`AXIS_NORMAL_DEG`) and that stays in the part gives a `WARNING:` line with the count: the hole is not filled to its wall. (2) New inner voids give a `WARNING:` line. (3) The plugged
mesh must be a closed solid on the float32 write (the test of `write_outputs`). When it is not, the item is a `SpecError` with the key path: `regions.design[0].stl.plug_holes: the plugged
mesh is not a closed solid (H1: wall faces stay in the part). The wall or the rim of a hole is not an exact cylinder with flat ends in this mesh ...`. This happens with the recorded
hook (`final.stl` of the recorded run, an optimizer result): its one recess has vertices at 84 different depths (to 1 micrometre) and no flat floor, so the hull of the wall vertices is
6 percent smaller than the prism of the hole and the surface pinches. A hole of an exported CAD part, or of a part built from a prism, is exact.

**The report.** One line for each `stl` item, before the `wrote ...` line, in `report` (and in the `report` of the tool; the lines that start with `WARNING:` are also in
`builder_warnings` and `warnings`). There is no new key in the reply. The line is `stl <key path of the item>: <file as given>, <faces> faces, closed solid, size <x> x <y> x <z> mm,
volume <v> mm3[, <n> bodies][; plugged <id> (d <mm> mm, <mm> mm long, <depth>), ...; open <ids>]`, for example

```
stl regions.design[0]: plate.stl, 276 faces, closed solid, size 40 x 20 x 4 mm, volume 3037.7 mm3; plugged H1 (d 4 mm, 4 mm long, through); open H2
```

**Time and memory.** There is no limit on the faces. A perforated plate of 925,212 faces: 3.1 s to read and build with no plug (peak 0.9 GB), 7.9 s with 10 plugs (1.4 GB), 14.8 s with all
900 plugs (2.1 GB; `find_features` is 4.3 s of it). The server holds the call while it works.

**Tests.** `tests/test_stl_region_kind.py`: the card (a plate with two holes as the design gives a YAML that `check_data` accepts, the report names the plugged holes), the volume of the
plugged part against a part built with no hole and `find_features` on the written `design.stl`, `all`, 16 to 128 segments, a rotated part far from the origin, a blind hole, a drill
point, a chamfer, a notch, many holes, a growth box, every role, `keep_out`, `subtract`, the path rules of the tool and the CLI, every error, the tolerance, a real mesh that cannot be
plugged, the tool and its text (within the bound, with no habitual cap) and the mock equal to the server.

### 45.2 Screw rings: `screw_holes`, `ring_mm` and the `screw_ring` item (part 3 of #151)

Code: `topopt/regions_builder.py` (`screw_rings`, `ring_thickness`, `make_ring_item`, `_add_screws`), tests `tests/test_screw_rings.py`. The skill route for a user who has an STL (part 4) is in `.claude/skills/part-to-topopt/SKILL.md` ("Your own STL"; the copy in
`.agents/skills/` is equal).

A part with screw holes is held at some holes and loaded at others. The optimizer must not cut the material round a screw. The `tube` interface of section 23 does this: a
frozen ring (label LOAD with id -1, no force) and a KEEP_OUT cut of the hole. The builder writes one `tube` interface for each screw hole, so the agent does not draw a ring with
`subtract`.

**The keys.** Both keys are keys of the `stl` item (section 45.1). The `screw_ring` item has its own `ring_mm` (see below).

- `screw_holes`: a list of hole ids of `find_features` on the same file, or `all` (every hole of the list). The shape rules are the rules of `plug_holes`.
- `ring_mm`: a number above 0 (every screw hole of the item), or a mapping `{H1: 2.5}` (one hole; the other holes keep the default). `ring_mm` with no `screw_holes` is a
  `SpecError`, and so is a mapping key that is not in `screw_holes`.

These are `SpecError` lines that name the key path: a `screw_holes` of the wrong type; an unknown id (the line lists the known ids); a hole in `plug_holes` and in `screw_holes`
(a hole is filled or it takes a screw); an arc (`closed_ring` false), because a ring needs the whole circle; a cavity (`depth` closed); a hole whose end `find_features` could not judge
(`depth` unknown); `screw_holes` in `keep_out` or inside `subtract` (a ring is a frozen shape of the part). A blind hole is allowed: the ring and the hole run along its depth.

**The thickness t.** t is a method setting with a default rule. The report gives t for each hole, so the agent can say it to the user.

- Default: `t = RING_PER_DIAMETER * d` with `RING_PER_DIAMETER = 0.5` and d the diameter of the hole (`diameter_mm` of `find_features`).
- Floor: at least `RING_MIN_VOXELS = 2` voxel sizes of the written YAML, so that the optimizer sees the ring as frozen voxels. The voxel size is known only when the YAML is written
  (`auto_voxel`, and up to 3 retries that make the voxel 8 percent bigger), so the builder builds the shapes again when the floor changes a `screw_ring` item, and computes the
  `tube` entries after the last voxel size is known.
- `ring_mm` from the spec is used as it is. It is a method setting: the agent sets it when the user asks for a thicker or thinner ring, and the report says `ring_mm from the spec`.
  A `ring_mm` under 2 voxels is used and gets a `WARNING:` line.

The two constants are named, with a comment, in one place. They are not physical limits. The table below shows what they do on a plate. Why 0.5 d: the ring is the wall that holds the
screw. At 0.25 d the wall is 1 to 1.5 mm (2 to 3 voxels at 0.5 mm), at 0.75 d it is 3 to 4.5 mm and the optimizer keeps more mass round the holes.

**What the builder writes.** For each screw hole, one entry of the `interfaces` block of the YAML (section 23): `kind: tube`, `name` = `<region>_<file stem>_<id>` (made of safe characters,
unique; a number is added to a name that is taken), `point`, `axis` and `length_mm` of the hole, `inner_radius_mm` = the radius of the hole, `radius_mm` = the radius of the hole + t
(6 digits). The values are the fit values of the reply of `find_features` (`point`, `axis`, `radius_mm`, `length_mm`, rounded to 0.1 micrometre), not the numbers of the report text:
the text rounds to 0.1 mm and could miss the faces of the part. The ring ends then lie in the faces of the part up to that rounding. The ring uses the facets of section 23
(`interfaces.segments`), so the ring and the hole have the same polygons as the `tube` interface that the run measures after it.

The spec can have its own `interfaces` list (a list of mappings; the YAML loader checks the entries). The builder copies it as given, and the screw rings come after it, so the
order of the boolean steps is the order of the user first. The written file has an `interfaces` block only when the spec has entries or a hole takes a ring.

**The ring item.** `{screw_ring: {path: part.stl, hole: H2[, ring_mm: 3]}}` is one item of a region, like `box`. It is the ring of one hole of the file, with the same polygons and the
same rule for t as the interface. It works in `fixed`, `load` and `solid`. In `design`, `keep_out` and `subtract` it is a `SpecError`. Use it to fix a screw hole (`fixed`) or to put the
load on the ring of a hole (`load`): the force acts on the voxels of the ring and not on the wall of the hole. The ring item has its own `ring_mm`. When the ring item and
the interface of one hole have two thicknesses, the report has a `WARNING:` line (give both the same `ring_mm`).

Labels (section 3): keep_out > fixed > load > solid > design. A union interface is LOAD with no load case, and a load region wins on overlap (section 23). So a `fixed` ring item wins over the
frozen ring of the interface in the same voxels, a `load` ring item keeps its force, and the hole of each ring is KEEP_OUT.

**The report.** In `report` and in the `report` of the tool, before the `wrote ...` line (the lines that start with `WARNING:` are also in `builder_warnings` and `warnings`). No new key
in the reply. If a retry changes the voxel size, the lines are said again.

```
screw ring regions.design[0].stl: H1 (d 4 mm), t 2 mm (default 0.5 x d); tube interface 'design_plate_H1'
screw ring regions.design[0].stl: H1 (d 4 mm), t 3 mm (raised to 2 voxels; 0.5 x d is 2 mm and the voxel is 1.5 mm); tube interface 'design_plate_H1'
screw ring regions.design[0].stl: H1 (d 4 mm), t 2.5 mm (ring_mm from the spec); tube interface 'design_plate_H1'
screw ring regions.fixed.wall[0].screw_ring: H2 of plate.stl (d 6 mm), t 3 mm (default 0.5 x d)
```

After them, when needed:

- `note: <key path>: the ring of H1 (t 2 mm) has <v> mm3 outside the part (<file>): the hole is near an edge or a face. The exact union adds this material outside your part`. The ring
  is in the YAML as it is; the volume is the part of the ring outside the item. The limit is the noise of the float32 file: `2 * end area * WALL_ROUND_MM + 2 * pi * r_in * L *
  interfaces.SAG_MM` for the ring (the rounding of the ends and the sag of the facets). There is no new number.
- `WARNING: <key path>: the ring of H1 (t 2 mm) overlaps the keep_out region '<name>' by <v> mm3. The keep-out region wins (CONTRACTS.md section 23): the ring is cut there`. The same limit.
- `WARNING: ....ring_mm: ... t .. mm is under 2 voxels ...`, and `WARNING: the ring of H1 of plate.stl has two thicknesses ...`.

**Measured on a plate.** The plate is 40 x 20 x 4 mm (276 faces), hole H2 (d 6 mm, at x 10) is fixed by its ring, hole H1 (d 4 mm, at x 30) takes a
force of 20 N along +x on its ring, voxel 0.5 mm, 80 iterations on the CPU, volume fraction 0.5 of the free voxels. In all runs `final.stl` is watertight, one body, and both holes have the
radius of the YAML to 0.001 mm.

| t | ring voxels (load H1 / fixed H2) | mass | compliance | wall at H2 in `final.stl` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25 d (1.0 / 1.5 mm) | 480 / 1152 | 2.00 g | 0.0364 | 1.50 mm |
| 0.5 d (2.0 / 3.0 mm) | 1248 / 2688 | 2.17 g | 0.0298 | 3.00 mm |
| 0.75 d (3.0 / 4.5 mm) | 2112 / 4832 | 2.40 g | 0.0242 | 4.50 mm |

The ring takes the mass, and the optimizer keeps the wall at the thickness of the ring where nothing else holds it (the side of H2 away from the load). The compliance is not a clean
measure of t: a thicker ring is also a bigger fixed and load area, so the same force acts on more voxels. With a fixed mass of 2.4 g the order is the same (0.0345, 0.0288, 0.0244). Voxel 1.5 mm
(the floor case): both rings are 3 mm, which is 2 voxels.

**Time and memory.** The ring adds one `find_features` call for each file (cached: one build reads the holes of a file once), one boolean step for each screw hole (the part of the ring outside the item) and one
for each screw hole and each `keep_out` region (the overlap). Measured with `screw_holes: all` on a plate of 30 x 30 holes (d 3 mm, voxel 1 mm, the build with `check_yaml`, CPU): 118,812 faces took 16 s (peak 0.9 GB), 1,846,812 faces took 75 s (peak 4.4 GB). The tool holds the call while it works.

**Tests.** `tests/test_screw_rings.py`: the entries against the plate (point, axis, radii, length, names), `check_yaml` on the written file, no entry without a screw hole, `all` and a list, a
blind hole, a rotated part far from the origin, the spec `interfaces` list first, every `SpecError` (type, id, plug and screw, notch, cavity, keep_out, subtract, no file), the report lines (default,
floor, `ring_mm`, note, keep-out warning), the default rule and the floor (the voxel of the YAML, auto voxel, a retry), `ring_mm` (a number, a mapping, under 2 voxels, every wrong form), the
ring item in `fixed`, `load` and `solid` and its errors, the same voxels as the interface, two thicknesses, the labels (a frozen ring and a KEEP_OUT hole, and no ring without the key), a short
run on the plate with the holes exact in `final.stl`, the tool reply, the texts within their bounds, the mock equal to the server, the skill route (two copies equal, each key named, the example
spec builds) and the eval case `evals/stl-own-part/`.
